title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試錄序
嘉靖丁酉秋制當鄉試先期
巡按江西監察御史陳〔褎〕謀
於藩臬之長聘〔倳〕及教諭葉
天榮爲考試官林〔應鳳〕孫〔憲〕
葉〔潤〕胡〔希定〕徐〔穀〕王〔臣〕唐〔魯〕
李〔仁〕李〔時暘〕鄧〔體靜〕以所專
===
經爲同考試官比至則御史
旣巳貞度集思愼簡諸執事
暨提調左布政使李〔崧祥〕左
叅政陳〔卿〕監試按察使劉〔士〕
奇副使陸〔堂〕各矢心以俟乃
合提學副使徐〔階〕所選士三
千七百人三試之〔倳〕獲縱觀
punctuated:
江西鄉試錄序

嘉靖丁酉秋，制當鄉試。先期，巡按江西監察御史陳〔褎〕謀於藩臬之長，聘〔倳〕及教諭葉天榮爲考試官，林〔應鳳〕、孫〔憲〕、葉〔潤〕、胡〔希定〕、徐〔穀〕、王〔臣〕、唐〔魯〕、李〔仁〕、李〔時暘〕、鄧〔體靜〕以所專經爲同考試官。比至，則御史旣巳貞度集思，愼簡諸執事，暨提調左布政使李〔崧祥〕、左叅政陳〔卿〕、監試按察使劉〔士〕奇、副使陸〔堂〕，各矢心以俟。乃合提學副使徐〔階〕所選士三千七百人，三試之。〔倳〕獲縱觀
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination

In the autumn of the dingyou year of Jiajing (1537), the Provincial Examination was due to be held under the established regulations. Beforehand, Chen Xiu [?], the Investigating Censor touring Jiangxi, consulted the heads of the Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions and invited me, Shi [?], together with Ye Tianrong, an Instructor, to serve as Examiners. Lin Yingfeng, Sun Xian, Ye Run, Hu Xiding, Xu Gu, Wang Chen, Tang Lu, Li Ren, Li Shiyang, and Deng Tijing were appointed Associate Examiners according to the Classics in which they specialized.

By the time we arrived, the censor had already deliberated carefully, gathered opinions, and judiciously selected the examination staff. Together with the Proctors, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Li Songxiang and Left Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner Chen Qing, and the examination monitors, Surveillance Commissioner Liu Shiqi and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Lu Tang, all had pledged their wholehearted commitment and awaited the examination. They then assembled the 3,700 candidates selected by Xu Jie, the Surveillance Vice Commissioner overseeing education, and examined them in three sessions. I, Shi [?], had the opportunity to survey …

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
其文麗而則辯而不誇深而
不鑿謹拜手言曰於戲此盛
世之文也
聖天子以身立教功效固然哉維
昔帝王觀文成化于時人士
之文渾渾噩噩舉足以徵德
樹業無容議矣秦漢而降世
===
無主張斯文之君本喪質窮
於是恠誕不經之書雕鏤絺
繪之技雜然竝出獨一二賢
人君子相與私正救之若八
代之衰得韓愈氏以興五季
之餘習得歐陽脩氏以振孔
孟仁義之旨得周敦頤氏程
punctuated: 其文麗而則，辯而不誇，深而不鑿。謹拜手言曰：「於戲！此盛世之文也。聖天子以身立教，功效固然哉！維昔帝王觀文成化，于時人士之文渾渾噩噩，舉足以徵德樹業，無容議矣。秦漢而降，世無主張斯文之君，本喪質窮，於是恠誕不經之書、雕鏤絺繪之技，雜然竝出。獨一二賢人君子相與私正救之，若八代之衰，得韓愈氏以興；五季之餘習，得歐陽脩氏以振；孔孟仁義之旨，得周敦頤氏、程
translation_en: …their compositions were elegant yet measured, persuasive without exaggeration, profound without forced interpretations. Respectfully bowing with hands clasped, I said: “Ah! These are the writings of a flourishing age. The sagely Son of Heaven establishes instruction through his own example: surely these are its fruits! In antiquity, emperors and kings observed cultural patterns and thereby brought about transformation. The writings of the scholars of that time were whole and uncontrived, all sufficient to manifest virtue and establish achievement; there was no room for criticism. From the Qin and Han onward, the world lacked a ruler who upheld this literary and cultural tradition. Its foundations were lost and its substance exhausted; writings full of strange absurdities contrary to the classics, and arts of elaborate carving and embroidered embellishment, consequently arose together in profusion. Only one or two worthy and noble men joined in efforts, in a private capacity, to correct and rescue it. Thus, after the decline of eight dynasties, Han Yu arose to revive it; amid the lingering habits of the Five Dynasties, Ouyang Xiu arose to reinvigorate it; and the teachings of Confucius and Mencius concerning benevolence and righteousness found exponents in Zhou Dunyi and Cheng…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
顓頊氏以發其微朱熹氏陸
九淵氏往復辯難以究其藴
雖功在斯文炳然不誣而復
古之盛卒不見於天下何也
其勢誠弗尊弗從也洪惟我
太祖高皇帝以
上聖之德續道統之傳表章六經
罷斥百氏學者旣曉然識其
所宗肆今
===
皇上敬一之學得之性成言發爲
經聲出爲律薄海内外人誦
習之蓋天之文也乃者病文
體之謬又特
詔有司正之所謂道兼
punctuated: 顓頊氏以發其微，朱熹氏、陸九淵氏往復辯難，以究其藴。雖功在斯文，炳然不誣，而復古之盛卒不見於天下，何也？其勢誠弗尊弗從也。洪惟我太祖高皇帝，以上聖之德，續道統之傳，表章六經，罷斥百氏。學者旣曉然識其所宗，肆今皇上敬一之學，得之性成，言發爲經，聲出爲律，薄海内外，人誦習之，蓋天之文也。乃者病文體之謬，又特詔有司正之，所謂道兼
translation_en:
…Zhuanxu [?] brought out its subtleties, while Zhu Xi and Lu Jiuyuan exchanged arguments and challenges to fathom its deeper meanings. Although their contributions to this cultural tradition were manifest and undeniable, the flourishing restoration of antiquity was ultimately never seen throughout the realm. Why? Their positions truly lacked the eminence to command a following.

We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao, through the virtue of a supreme sage, continued the transmission of the succession of the Way, exalted the Six Classics, and rejected the hundred schools. Scholars thus came to understand clearly what they should take as their guiding authority. Now His Majesty’s learning of reverent concentration on the One comes from his innate nature. His utterances become canonical standards; his voice becomes a rule. Throughout the lands within and beyond the seas, people recite and study his words: these are indeed the writings of Heaven. Recently, troubled by errors in literary style, he issued a special decree ordering the responsible officials to correct them. This is what is meant by saying that the Way unites…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
君師身任斯文之責萬物所共快
覩焉者士生斯時其有弗與
於文者非夫也況玆土韓周
程朱之所寓遊也歐陸之所
產也而其流風又有存者乎
然則諸士子以文鳴
國家之盛褎然爲天下先有以
===
也雖然韓歐諸君子固皆有
功斯文然其所造或至或不
至是故一以爲詞章一以爲
理學優劣則□別矣諸士子
於所嚮往可無擇乎必脩詞
立其誠反躬踐其實使藴之
爲德行措之爲事業斯眞無
punctuated:
君師，身任斯文之責，萬物所共快覩焉者。士生斯時，其有弗與於文者，非夫也。況玆土，韓周程朱之所寓遊也，歐陸之所產也，而其流風又有存者乎？然則諸士子以文鳴國家之盛，褎然爲天下先，有以也。

雖然，韓歐諸君子固皆有功斯文，然其所造或至或不至。是故一以爲詞章，一以爲理學，優劣則□別矣。諸士子於所嚮往，可無擇乎？必脩詞立其誠，反躬踐其實，使藴之爲德行，措之爲事業，斯眞無
translation_en:
…sovereign and teacher, personally assuming responsibility for this cultural tradition—a sight that all creation rejoices to behold. A scholar born in such an age who takes no part in this tradition is no true man. Moreover, this land is where Han, Zhou, Cheng, and Zhu sojourned and travelled, and where Ou and Lu were born; how much more is this so when their enduring influence still survives here! Thus there is good reason for you scholars to proclaim the flourishing of the state through your writing and stand pre-eminent in the realm.

Nevertheless, although Han, Ou, and the other gentlemen all contributed to this cultural tradition, some attained its fullest realization, while others did not. Hence one approach became literary composition, the other the learning of principle; their relative merits are thus distinguished [?]. Can you scholars fail to choose carefully what you aspire to? You must refine your words to establish your sincerity, examine yourselves and put into practice what is substantial, so that what you nurture within becomes virtuous conduct and what you put into action becomes achievement. This would truly leave no …

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
賀於
聖敎也已否則直藝焉耳豈所望
於今日哉〔偉〕不敏敢因成事
遂以朂焉兹舉也綱紀振作
使士不懈則有都察院右副
都御史秦〔鉞〕之昔任撫綏甄
陶長育使材有成則有巡撫
===
右副都御史胡〔岳〕之昔總方
嶽平定保釐使人樂學則有
右副都御史王〔浚〕之提督軍
務風勵褒嘉使吏知重則有
督木工部右侍郎兼右僉都
御史潘〔鑑〕及刑部郎中馮〔岳〕
工部員外郎陳〔垣〕户部主事
punctuated:
賀於聖敎也已。否則直藝焉耳，豈所望於今日哉？〔偉〕不敏，敢因成事，遂以朂焉。
兹舉也，綱紀振作，使士不懈，則有都察院右副都御史秦〔鉞〕之昔任；撫綏甄陶，長育使材有成，則有巡撫右副都御史胡〔岳〕之昔總方嶽；平定保釐，使人樂學，則有右副都御史王〔浚〕之提督軍務；風勵褒嘉，使吏知重，則有督木工部右侍郎兼右僉都御史潘〔鑑〕及刑部郎中馮〔岳〕、工部員外郎陳〔垣〕、户部主事
translation_en:
…do no discredit to the Sage’s teaching [?]. Otherwise, it would merely be a matter of literary skill. Could that be what is hoped for today? I, Wei 偉, though lacking in ability, venture to take the completion of this undertaking as an occasion to offer this encouragement.
In this examination, the strengthening of discipline and order, which kept the scholars from slackening, owed much to the former service of Qin Yue 秦鉞, Right Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate. The nurturing and molding of talent, bringing it to maturity, owed much to Hu Yue 胡岳, Provincial Governor and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, during his former administration of the province. Pacification and the maintenance of peace, enabling people to pursue learning gladly, owed much to Wang Jun 王浚, Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, in his supervision of military affairs. Encouragement, commendation, and praise, which made officials recognize the importance of this undertaking, owed much to Pan Jian 潘鑑, Right Vice Minister of Works and concurrently Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief, supervising timber procurement; Feng Yue 馮岳, Director in the Ministry of Justice; Chen Yuan 陳垣, Vice Director in the Ministry of Works; and the Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue …

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
尹〔字〕行人龍〔遂〕先後以使事
登〔至〕而御史兼有其勞綜理防
衛小大咸飭則有右叅政潘
〔潢〕尹〔嗣忠〕副使侯〔緘〕管〔懷理〕
嚴〔時泰〕左叅議今遷副使戴
〔鱀〕雲南副使毛〔紹元〕右叅議
丘〔茂中〕僉事林〔應標〕朱〔孔陽〕
===
周〔相〕方〔遠宜〕今遷叅議趙〔葉〕
都指揮李〔時〕張〔鯨〕而御史總
其凡云
福建建寧府儒學教授伍〔偉〕
謹序
punctuated:
尹〔字〕、行人龍〔遂〕先後以使事登〔至〕，而御史兼有其勞。綜理防衛，小大咸飭，則有右叅政潘〔潢〕、尹〔嗣忠〕，副使侯〔緘〕、管〔懷理〕、嚴〔時泰〕，左叅議今遷副使戴〔鱀〕，雲南副使毛〔紹元〕，右叅議丘〔茂中〕，僉事林〔應標〕、朱〔孔陽〕、周〔相〕、方〔遠宜〕，今遷叅議趙〔葉〕，都指揮李〔時〕、張〔鯨〕，而御史總其凡云。
福建建寧府儒學教授伍〔偉〕謹序。
translation_en:
…Yin Zi [?] and Messenger Long Sui arrived successively on official missions [?], and the Censor also shared in their labors. Those who coordinated defense and security, ensuring that matters great and small were all put in order, were Right Administration Vice Commissioners Pan Huang and Yin Sizhong; Surveillance Vice Commissioners Hou Jian, Guan Huaili, and Yan Shitai; Dai Ji, formerly Left Administration Assistant Commissioner and now promoted to Surveillance Vice Commissioner; Mao Shaoyuan, Surveillance Vice Commissioner of Yunnan; Right Administration Assistant Commissioner Qiu Maozhong; Surveillance Assistant Commissioners Lin Yingbiao, Zhu Kongyang, Zhou Xiang, and Fang Yuanyi; Zhao Ye, now promoted to Administration Assistant Commissioner; and Regional Military Commissioners Li Shi and Zhang Jing. The Censor oversaw their work as a whole.
This preface is respectfully composed by Wu Wei, Professor of the Confucian School of Jianning Prefecture, Fujian.

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:

巡按江西監察御史陳　褎〔邦進福建寧德縣人　癸未進士〕

江西等處承宣布政使司左布政使李崧祥〔時望直隷貴池縣人　甲戌進士〕
江西等處承宣布政使司左參政陳　卿〔汝忠四川富順縣人　乙丑進士〕

punctuated:
嘉靖十六年江西鄉試

監臨官
巡按江西監察御史陳　褎〔邦進，福建寧德縣人，癸未進士〕。

提調官
江西等處承宣布政使司左布政使李崧祥〔時望，直隷貴池縣人，甲戌進士〕。
江西等處承宣布政使司左參政陳　卿〔汝忠，四川富順縣人，乙丑進士〕。

江西等處提刑按察司按察使劉士奇〔邦正，廣東順德縣人，丁丑進士〕。
江西等處提刑按察司副使陸　堂〔肯堂，直隷常熟縣人，癸未進士〕。

福建建寧府儒學教授伍　偁〔良臣，湖廣漢陽縣人，壬午貢士〕。

同考試官
直隷鳳陽府定遠縣儒學教諭林應鳳〔鳴岡，福建莆田縣人，辛卯貢士〕。
應天府溧陽縣儒學教諭孫　憲〔孔章，浙江奉化縣人，戊子貢士〕。
湖廣德安府孝感縣儒學教諭葉　潤〔子雨，廣西桂林□□□□□，江□陽縣人，乙酉貢士〕。
福建建寧府崇安縣儒學教諭胡希定〔宗正，廣西桂林衛人，壬午貢士〕。
直隷池州府貴池縣儒學教諭徐　轂〔良用，浙江山陰縣人，戊子貢士〕。
translation_en:
Jiangxi Provincial Examination, the sixteenth year of Jiajing (1537)

Supervising Official
Chen You [?] 陳褎, Investigating Censor assigned to inspect Jiangxi. His courtesy name was Bangjin; he was from Ningde County, Fujian, and became a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) in the guiwei year.

Proctors
Li Songxiang, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of the Jiangxi Provincial Administration Commission. His courtesy name was Shiwang; he was from Guichi County in the directly administered metropolitan region, and became a metropolitan graduate in the jiaxu year.
Chen Qing, Left Administration Vice Commissioner of the Jiangxi Provincial Administration Commission. His courtesy name was Ruzhong; he was from Fushun County, Sichuan, and became a metropolitan graduate in the yichou year.

Examination Monitoring Officials
Liu Shiqi, Surveillance Commissioner of the Jiangxi Provincial Surveillance Commission. His courtesy name was Bangzheng; he was from Shunde County, Guangdong, and became a metropolitan graduate in the dingchou year.
Lu Tang, Surveillance Vice Commissioner of the Jiangxi Provincial Surveillance Commission. His courtesy name was Kentang; he was from Changshu County in the directly administered metropolitan region, and became a metropolitan graduate in the guiwei year.

Examiners
Wu Cheng, Professor in the Confucian School of Jianning Prefecture, Fujian. His courtesy name was Liangchen; he was from Hanyang County, Huguang, and became a tribute student (gongshi) in the renwu year.
Ye Tianrong, Instructor in the Confucian School of Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang. His courtesy name was Liangqing; he was from Wuyuan County in the directly administered metropolitan region, and became a tribute student in the wuzi year.

Associate Examiners
Lin Yingfeng, Instructor in the Confucian School of Dingyuan County, Fengyang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. His courtesy name was Minggang; he was from Putian County, Fujian, and became a tribute student in the xinmao year.
Sun Xian, Instructor in the Confucian School of Liyang County, Yingtian Prefecture. His courtesy name was Kongzhang; he was from Fenghua County, Zhejiang, and became a tribute student in the wuzi year.
Ye Run, Instructor in the Confucian School of Xiaogan County, De’an Prefecture, Huguang. His courtesy name was Ziyu. His place of origin is partly illegible: Guilin, Guangxi, followed by five illegible characters, then “Jiang □ yang County” [?]. He became a tribute student in the yiyou year.
Hu Xiding, Instructor in the Confucian School of Chong’an County, Jianning Prefecture, Fujian. His courtesy name was Zongzheng; he was from Guilin Guard, Guangxi, and became a tribute student in the renwu year.
Xu Gu, Instructor in the Confucian School of Guichi County, Chizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. His courtesy name was Liangyong; he was from Shanyin County, Zhejiang, and became a tribute student in the wuzi year.

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
河南河南府永寧縣儒學教諭王　臣〔賢甫福建同安縣人辛卯貢士〕
山東兖州府滋陽縣儒學教諭唐　魯〔□□□□□□□□□□□□□□〕
湖廣黄州府蘄水縣儒學教諭李　仁〔□□□□□□□□□□□□□〕
湖廣長沙府益陽縣儒學教諭李時暘〔元和廣西桂林□□□□□□人乙酉貢士〕

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
嘗獨立鯉趨而過庭曰學詩乎對曰未也
不學詩無以言鯉退而學詩他日又獨
立鯉趨而過庭曰學禮乎對曰未也不
學禮無以立鯉退而學禮
知斯三者則知所以脩身知所以脩身則
知所以治人知所以治人則知所以治
天下國家矣
孟施舍之守氣又不如曾子之守約也
===
易
君子行此四德者故曰乾元亨利貞
益動而巽日進无疆
知變化之道者其知神之所爲乎
師者衆也衆必有所比故受之以比比者
比也比必有所畜故受之以小畜物畜
然後有禮故受之以履
書
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

嘗獨立，鯉趨而過庭，曰：「學詩乎？」對曰：「未也。」「不學詩，無以言。」鯉退而學詩。他日，又獨立，鯉趨而過庭，曰：「學禮乎？」對曰：「未也。」「不學禮，無以立。」鯉退而學禮。

知斯三者，則知所以脩身；知所以脩身，則知所以治人；知所以治人，則知所以治天下國家矣。

孟施舍之守氣，又不如曾子之守約也。

易

君子行此四德者，故曰：「乾，元亨利貞。」

益，動而巽，日進无疆。

知變化之道者，其知神之所爲乎！

師者，衆也。衆必有所比，故受之以比。比者，比也。比必有所畜，故受之以小畜。物畜然後有禮，故受之以履。

書
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

Once, when he [Confucius] was standing alone, Li hurried across the courtyard. He asked, “Have you studied the Odes?” Li replied, “Not yet.” “Unless you study the Odes, you will have no means of expressing yourself.” Li withdrew and studied the Odes. On another day, he was again standing alone, and Li hurried across the courtyard. He asked, “Have you studied ritual?” Li replied, “Not yet.” “Unless you study ritual, you will have no means of establishing yourself.” Li withdrew and studied ritual.

Knowing these three things, one knows how to cultivate oneself; knowing how to cultivate oneself, one knows how to govern others; knowing how to govern others, one knows how to govern the world, the states, and the families.

Meng Shishe’s maintenance of his vital energy was nevertheless inferior to Master Zeng’s holding fast to the essential.

Book of Changes

The gentleman practices these four virtues. Hence it is said: “Qian: primal inception, successful passage, benefit, and steadfast correctness.”

Increase (Yi): movement joined with yielding; daily advance without limit.

One who knows the way of change and transformation surely knows what the numinous powers do!

The Army (Shi) means a multitude. A multitude must have something to which it adheres; thus Holding Together (Bi) follows it. Holding Together means joining together. Where there is joining together, there must be some accumulation; thus the Lesser Accumulation (Xiao Xu) follows it. Only after things have accumulated is there ritual; thus Treading (Lü) follows it.

Book of Documents

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
安民則惠黎民懷之
導沇水東流爲濟入于河溢爲滎東出于
陶丘北又東至于菏又東北會于汶又
北東入于海
其爾克紹乃辟于先王永綏民
凡人未見聖若不克見旣見聖亦不克由
聖爾其戒哉爾惟風下民惟草
詩
樹之榛栗椅桐梓漆爰伐琴瑟
===
似續妣祖築室百堵西南其戶爰居爰處
爰笑爰語
王命召虎來旬來宣文武受命召公維翰
無曰予小子召公是似肇敏戎公用錫
爾祉
維女荊楚居國南鄉昔有成湯自彼氐羌
莫敢不來享莫敢不來王曰商是常
春秋
秋荊伐鄭公會齊人宋人救鄭〔莊公二十〕
punctuated:
安民則惠，黎民懷之。
導沇水，東流爲濟，入于河，溢爲滎，東出于陶丘北，又東至于菏，又東北會于汶，又北，東入于海。
其爾克紹乃辟于先王，永綏民。
凡人未見聖，若不克見；旣見聖，亦不克由聖。爾其戒哉！爾惟風，下民惟草。
詩
樹之榛栗、椅桐、梓漆，爰伐琴瑟。
似續妣祖，築室百堵，西南其戶，爰居爰處，爰笑爰語。
王命召虎，來旬來宣。文武受命，召公維翰。無曰予小子，召公是似。肇敏戎公，用錫爾祉。
維女荊楚，居國南鄉。昔有成湯，自彼氐羌，莫敢不來享，莫敢不來王，曰商是常。
春秋
秋，荊伐鄭，公會齊人、宋人救鄭。〔莊公二十〕
translation_en:
Bring peace to the people and act benevolently, and the common people will cherish you.
He traced the Yan River, which flows east as the Ji, enters the Yellow River, and spills out to form the Xing marsh. It emerges eastward north of Taoqiu, continues east to He, then northeast to join the Wen, then north, and enters the sea to the east.
May you enable your sovereign to carry on the legacy of the former kings and bring lasting peace to the people.
People, before seeing a sage, seem afraid that they will never be able to see him; once they have seen him, they still cannot follow him. Take warning! You are the wind; the people below are the grass.

Book of Odes
Plant hazels and chestnuts, yi trees and paulownias, catalpas and lacquer trees, to be felled for making qin and se zithers.
Continuing the legacy of foremothers and forefathers, he built a dwelling with a hundred stretches of wall, its doors facing west and south. Here they dwell and abide; here they laugh and converse.
The king commanded Shao Hu: “Come to inspect; come to proclaim. When Wen and Wu received the Mandate, the Duke of Shao was their pillar. Do not say, ‘I am but a young man’; emulate the Duke of Shao. Begin diligently upon your great service, and thereby receive blessings.”
You, Jing-Chu, dwell in the southern region of the realm. In former times, under Cheng Tang, even those Di and Qiang dared not fail to come with offerings, dared not fail to come and acknowledge him as king, saying, ‘Shang is the enduring sovereign.’

Spring and Autumn Annals
In autumn, Jing attacked Zheng. The duke joined men of Qi and Song to relieve Zheng. 〔Duke Zhuang, year twenty…〕

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
有八年　楚人伐鄭公子遂會晉人宋
人衛人許人救鄭〔文公九年〕
十有二月癸丑公會諸侯盟于薄釋宋公
〔僖公二十有一年〕
冬楚人陳侯蔡侯鄭伯許男圍宋〔僖公二
十有七年〕　六月公會宋公陳侯衛侯
鄭伯許男曹伯晉趙盾癸酉同盟于新
城〔文公十有四年〕　九月晉侯宋公衛
侯鄭伯曹伯會于扈〔宣公九年〕　夏叔
孫豹會晉趙武楚屈建蔡公孫歸生衛
石惡陳孔奐鄭良霄許人曹人于宋〔襄
公二十有七年〕
===
夏六月乙卯晉荀林父帥師及楚子戰于
邲晉師敗績〔宣公十有二年〕　吳伐我
〔哀公八年〕
禮記
君子齊戒處必掩身無躁止聲色毋或進
薄滋味毋致和節耆欲定心氣百官靜
punctuated:
有八年。楚人伐鄭，公子遂會晉人、宋人、衛人、許人救鄭〔文公九年〕。
十有二月癸丑，公會諸侯盟于薄，釋宋公〔僖公二十有一年〕。
冬，楚人、陳侯、蔡侯、鄭伯、許男圍宋〔僖公二十有七年〕。六月，公會宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯、晉趙盾，癸酉，同盟于新城〔文公十有四年〕。九月，晉侯、宋公、衛侯、鄭伯、曹伯會于扈〔宣公九年〕。夏，叔孫豹會晉趙武、楚屈建、蔡公孫歸生、衛石惡、陳孔奐、鄭良霄、許人、曹人于宋〔襄公二十有七年〕。
夏六月乙卯，晉荀林父帥師及楚子戰于邲，晉師敗績〔宣公十有二年〕。吳伐我〔哀公八年〕。
禮記
君子齊戒，處必掩身，無躁；止聲色，毋或進；薄滋味，毋致和；節耆欲，定心氣，百官靜
translation_en:
…the twenty-eighth year. Men of Chu attacked Zheng. Prince Sui joined men of Jin, Song, Wei, and Xu in relieving Zheng. 〔Ninth year of Duke Wen〕
In the twelfth month, on guichou, the duke met the feudal lords and made a covenant at Bo. They released the Duke of Song. 〔Twenty-first year of Duke Xi〕
In winter, men of Chu, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Cai, the Earl of Zheng, and the Baron of Xu besieged Song. 〔Twenty-seventh year of Duke Xi〕 In the sixth month, the duke met the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, the Earl of Cao, and Zhao Dun of Jin; on guiyou, they jointly entered into a covenant at Xincheng. 〔Fourteenth year of Duke Wen〕 In the ninth month, the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, and the Earl of Cao met at Hu. 〔Ninth year of Duke Xuan〕 In summer, Shusun Bao met Zhao Wu of Jin, Qu Jian of Chu, Gongsun Guisheng of Cai, Shi E of Wei, Kong Huan of Chen, Liang Xiao of Zheng, and men of Xu and Cao at Song. 〔Twenty-seventh year of Duke Xiang〕
In summer, in the sixth month, on yimao, Xun Linfu of Jin led an army into battle against the Viscount of Chu at Bi. The Jin army suffered a crushing defeat. 〔Twelfth year of Duke Xuan〕 Wu attacked our state. 〔Eighth year of Duke Ai〕
Record of Rites (Liji)
When a gentleman observes ritual purification and abstinence, he must keep his person secluded in his dwelling and avoid agitation. He puts a stop to music and sensual attractions, allowing none to be presented; he reduces rich flavors, seeking no harmonious blending of tastes; he restrains his appetites and desires, settles his mind and vital energies, and stills all his bodily faculties…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
□無刑以定晏陰之所成
天垂象聖人則之郊所以明天道也
合父子之親明長幼之序以敬四海之内
天子如此則禮行矣
與仁同功其仁未可知也與仁同過然後
其仁可知也
第貳塲
論
聖人貴未然之防
===
詔誥表〔內科 一道〕
擬漢勸農桑禁采黃金珠玉詔〔景帝後三年〕
擬唐以長孫無忌爲司徒房玄齡爲司空
誥〔貞觀十六年〕
擬禮部尚書陶凱等進宴饗九奏樂章表〔洪武四年〕
判語〔五條〕
磨勘卷宗
punctuated:
□無刑，以定晏陰之所成。
天垂象，聖人則之。郊所以明天道也。
合父子之親，明長幼之序，以敬四海之内。天子如此，則禮行矣。
與仁同功，其仁未可知也；與仁同過，然後其仁可知也。
第貳塲
論
聖人貴未然之防。
詔誥表〔內科 一道〕
擬漢勸農桑禁采黃金珠玉詔〔景帝後三年〕。
擬唐以長孫無忌爲司徒、房玄齡爲司空誥〔貞觀十六年〕。
擬禮部尚書陶凱等進宴饗九奏樂章表〔洪武四年〕。
判語〔五條〕
磨勘卷宗。
translation_en:
…[illegible] impose no punishments, so as to secure what the tranquil yin has brought to completion.

Heaven displays its signs, and the sage takes them as his model. The suburban sacrifice serves to make manifest the Way of Heaven.

Unite fathers and sons in affection, clarify the order of senior and junior, and thereby show respect to all within the Four Seas. When the Son of Heaven acts thus, ritual propriety prevails.

When someone's achievements accord with benevolence, his benevolence cannot yet be known; only when his faults likewise accord with benevolence can his benevolence be known.

Second Session

Discourse
The sage prizes taking precautions before trouble arises.

Edicts, Proclamations, and Memorials 〔One question from these categories [?]〕
Compose an edict in the manner of the Han dynasty encouraging agriculture and sericulture and prohibiting the extraction of gold, pearls, and jade. 〔Third year of Emperor Jing's final reign period〕

Compose a proclamation in the manner of the Tang dynasty appointing Zhangsun Wuji Minister of Education and Fang Xuanling Minister of Works. 〔Sixteenth year of Zhenguan〕

Compose a memorial in the voice of Tao Kai, Minister of Rites, and others presenting the texts for the nine musical performances at court banquets. 〔Fourth year of Hongwu〕

Legal Judgments 〔Five items〕
Scrutiny of dossiers.

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
功臣田土
乘輿服御物
孳生馬疋
盜賊捕限
第叄場
策五道
問書曰有典有則貽厥子孫詩曰貽厥孫
謀以燕翼子是帝王所以計久遠者在
教其子若孫而已洪惟我
===
太祖高皇帝深覽斯義建大本堂延四方名儒
教
皇太子及
諸王又著
祖訓錄
儲君昭鑑錄以
賜至
太宗文皇帝命吏部翰林諸臣舉老成正大儒
者傳
punctuated:
功臣田土。
乘輿服御物。
孳生馬疋。
盜賊捕限。

第叄場
策五道

問：書曰：「有典有則，貽厥子孫。」詩曰：「貽厥孫謀，以燕翼子。」是帝王所以計久遠者，在教其子若孫而已。洪惟我太祖高皇帝深覽斯義，建大本堂，延四方名儒，教皇太子及諸王，又著《祖訓錄》《儲君昭鑑錄》以賜。至太宗文皇帝，命吏部、翰林諸臣舉老成正大儒者傳
translation_en:
Lands of meritorious officials.
Articles for the emperor’s personal use and wear.
Horse breeding.
Time limits for apprehending bandits and thieves.

Third Session
Five Policy Questions

Question: The Book of Documents says: “There are established institutions and rules, bequeathed to their descendants.” The Book of Odes says: “Bequeath plans to your descendants, thereby bringing peace to and aiding your children.” Thus, the means by which emperors and kings plan for the distant future lie simply in educating their sons and grandsons. We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao understood this principle profoundly. He established the Dabentang, the Hall of the Great Foundation, and invited renowned Confucian scholars from every region to instruct the imperial heir apparent and the princes. He also compiled the Record of Ancestral Instructions and the Record of Illuminating Examples for the Heir Apparent to bestow upon them. In the reign of Emperor Taizong Wen, he commanded the officials of the Ministry of Personnel and the Hanlin Academy to recommend mature, experienced, upright Confucian scholars to tutor [?] …

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
皇太孫輯
文華寶鑑
聖學心法賜
皇太子其爲教詳矣顧於
東宮不設府僚以廷臣兼領其職何歟抑有
所祖述歟古之教太子必遠庖厨所以
長恩明有仁也而我
太祖高皇帝乃諭輔臣教
皇太子以兵事
===
太宗文皇帝北伐復俾
皇太孫侍行何歟抑有所取法歟昔漢臣賈
誼言太子之善在於早諭教與選左右
三代所以長久以有此具也然三代之
政具於書周之法尤莫詳於周禮顧於
教太子者無聞焉何歟漢唐宋東宮官
屬漸多亦多製述以示訓戒其治效反
不古若又何歟豈所謂善在太子師傅
之教固不足恃歟抑帝王所謂典則燕
punctuated: 皇太孫，輯《文華寶鑑》《聖學心法》賜皇太子，其爲教詳矣。顧於東宮不設府僚，以廷臣兼領其職，何歟？抑有所祖述歟？古之教太子，必遠庖厨，所以長恩明有仁也。而我太祖高皇帝乃諭輔臣教皇太子以兵事，太宗文皇帝北伐，復俾皇太孫侍行，何歟？抑有所取法歟？昔漢臣賈誼言：「太子之善，在於早諭教與選左右。」三代所以長久，以有此具也。然三代之政具於《書》，周之法尤莫詳於《周禮》，顧於教太子者無聞焉，何歟？漢唐宋東宮官屬漸多，亦多製述以示訓戒，其治效反不古若，又何歟？豈所謂善在太子師傅之教，固不足恃歟？抑帝王所謂典則燕
translation_en:
…the imperial grandson, and compiled the Precious Mirror of Literary Splendor (Wenhua baojian) and the Essential Principles of Sagely Learning (Shengxue xinfa) to bestow upon the crown prince. These provisions for instruction were indeed thorough. Yet why were no separate staff appointed to the Eastern Palace, with court officials instead concurrently assuming its duties? Was there some precedent being followed?

In antiquity, when educating a crown prince, he was always kept away from the kitchens, so as to nurture kindness and manifest benevolence [?]. Yet our Emperor Taizu Gao instructed his assisting ministers to teach the crown prince military affairs; and when Emperor Taizong Wen campaigned in the north, he had the imperial grandson accompany him. Why was this? Was there some model being emulated?

Jia Yi, a minister of the Han, once said: “The crown prince’s goodness depends upon instructing him early and selecting those who attend him.” The Three Dynasties endured because they possessed these provisions. Yet the government of the Three Dynasties is fully set forth in the Book of Documents, and nowhere are the institutions of the Zhou detailed more fully than in the Rites of Zhou. Why, then, do we hear nothing there concerning the education of the crown prince?

Under the Han, Tang, and Song, the officials attached to the Eastern Palace gradually increased in number, and many works were also composed to convey instruction and admonition. Why, nevertheless, did the results of their government fall short of antiquity? Could it be that the claim that the crown prince’s goodness depends upon the instruction of his teachers and tutors is, after all, insufficient to rely upon? Or did what emperors called establishing enduring norms and securing repose for …

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
翼者别有任也兹我
皇上天錫祚亂本支日蕃敎之之術蓋所欲聞
者諸士子咸懷忠愛之心將何以仰助
焉幸明告我
問仁統四端兼萬善故君子之學莫先焉
然道統之傳肇自堯舜乃獨言人心道
心而不及仁者何歟孔門之問答於仁
蓋數數矣乃猶謂子罕言仁者何歟子
思之學本諸孔子者也其書曰脩身以
道脩道以仁仁與道果二歟孟子之學
又得之子思者也其言曰仁者人也合
而言之道也仁與道果一歟嗣是諸儒
之說或以公言或以愛言或以覺言三
者果孰爲近歟若夫統同合一之論將
安所歸歟今世以公言仁者未之聞矣
專主夫愛則曰天地萬物爲一體夫固
有所受也然其弊不惟使人含胡昏緩
無警切之□□□□□認物爲己而論於
punctuated:
翼者，别有任也？兹我皇上，天錫祚亂，本支日蕃，敎之之術，蓋所欲聞者。諸士子咸懷忠愛之心，將何以仰助焉？幸明告我。

問：仁統四端，兼萬善，故君子之學莫先焉。然道統之傳肇自堯舜，乃獨言人心、道心，而不及仁者，何歟？孔門之問答於仁，蓋數數矣，乃猶謂「子罕言仁」者，何歟？子思之學，本諸孔子者也，其書曰：「脩身以道，脩道以仁。」仁與道果二歟？孟子之學，又得之子思者也，其言曰：「仁者，人也，合而言之，道也。」仁與道果一歟？嗣是諸儒之說，或以公言，或以愛言，或以覺言，三者果孰爲近歟？若夫統同合一之論，將安所歸歟？今世以公言仁者，未之聞矣。專主夫愛，則曰：「天地萬物爲一體。」夫固有所受也，然其弊不惟使人含胡昏緩，無警切之□□□□□認物爲己，而論於
translation_en:
…provision for descendants involves some other responsibility? Now our Emperor has received Heaven’s blessings and good order [?], and the main and collateral branches of the imperial lineage grow daily more numerous. Methods for educating them are surely what he wishes to hear about. All you candidates cherish loyalty and devotion: how will you assist him in this? Please explain it clearly to me.

Question: Benevolence encompasses the four beginnings of moral virtue and embraces every good; hence nothing takes precedence over it in the gentleman’s learning. Yet the transmission of the Way began with Yao and Shun, who spoke only of the human mind and the mind of the Way, without mentioning benevolence. Why was this? Questions and answers about benevolence were frequent in the school of Confucius, yet it is still said, “The Master seldom spoke of benevolence.” Why? Zisi’s learning was rooted in Confucius. His book says, “Cultivate the self through the Way; cultivate the Way through benevolence.” Are benevolence and the Way really two things? Mengzi’s learning, in turn, derived from Zisi. He said, “Benevolence is being human; bringing them together and speaking of them as one, this is the Way.” Are benevolence and the Way really one? Among the explanations of subsequent Confucian scholars, some speak in terms of impartiality, some in terms of love, and some in terms of awareness. Which of these three comes closest? And where should we place the argument that comprehensively unites them into one? In our own age, I have heard of no one explaining benevolence in terms of impartiality. Those who concentrate exclusively on love say, “Heaven, earth, and the myriad things form one body.” This certainly has a basis in inherited teaching. Yet its harmful effects do not merely make people vague, befuddled, and lax, lacking alertness and earnestness [five illegible characters] [?], taking things to be the self, and discoursing in terms of …

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
兼愛之失專主夫覺則曰心有知覺之
謂仁夫亦有所受也然其弊不惟使人
張皇躁迫無沉潜之味且或至認物爲
理而昧夫精一之宗是其可無慎歟諸
士子相與究言之明似是之非趨聖傳
之正是主司所深望也
問大江以西土瘠民貧風氣爲弱自滕王
分封以來雄文傑閣膾炙人口往往遂
爲宗室之所托居世傳李氏出自唐裔
===
代有顯人今亦無以考其世矣迨夫宋
室南遷諸趙散處大率亦於玆土爲盛
而其間名公哲人多由科目以進其立
身行事之畧時或載諸史志可考也以
今言之孝則有都監酒庫祖孫之相承
忠則有安吉南海後先之並著政事則
有心存豈弟而民稱趙母者有講學行
禮而士風翕然者文學則有延禮大儒
而潜心理學者有兩請漕舉而卓有詩
punctuated:
兼愛之失。專主夫覺，則曰：「心有知覺之謂仁。」夫亦有所受也，然其弊，不惟使人張皇躁迫，無沉潜之味，且或至認物爲理，而昧夫精一之宗，是其可無慎歟？諸士子相與究言之，明似是之非，趨聖傳之正，是主司所深望也。
問：大江以西，土瘠民貧，風氣爲弱。自滕王分封以來，雄文傑閣，膾炙人口，往往遂爲宗室之所托居。世傳李氏出自唐裔，代有顯人，今亦無以考其世矣。迨夫宋室南遷，諸趙散處，大率亦於玆土爲盛，而其間名公哲人，多由科目以進。其立身行事之畧，時或載諸史志，可考也。以今言之，孝則有都監、酒庫祖孫之相承；忠則有安吉、南海後先之並著；政事則有心存豈弟，而民稱趙母者，有講學行禮，而士風翕然者；文學則有延禮大儒，而潜心理學者，有兩請漕舉，而卓有詩
translation_en:
…the error of indiscriminate love. Those who place exclusive emphasis on awareness say, “The mind’s capacity for knowing and perceiving is what is meant by humaneness.” This, too, has an inherited basis. Yet its harmful consequences not only make people agitated and impetuous, without any savor of quiet reflection; they may even lead them to mistake things for principle and lose sight of the essential teaching of refinement and single-mindedness. Can one fail to exercise caution here? You candidates should investigate and discuss this together, discerning the errors in what appears correct and turning toward the true teaching transmitted by the sages. This is the earnest hope of those presiding over the examination.
Question: West of the great river, the soil is poor, the people impoverished, and the prevailing spirit weak. Since the Prince of Teng received his fief, magnificent writing and an outstanding pavilion have been celebrated on everyone’s lips, and this region has frequently become a place of residence for members of the imperial clan. Tradition holds that the Li families descend from the Tang imperial house and have produced distinguished men in every generation, but their genealogies can no longer be verified. When the Song court moved south and members of the Zhao clan dispersed to settle in various places, they were particularly numerous in this region. Among them, many eminent and wise men advanced through the examinations. Accounts of their conduct and deeds are occasionally recorded in histories and local gazetteers and can be examined. To enumerate them now: in filial devotion, there were the military supervisor and the wine-depot official [?], grandfather and grandson, who carried on the same tradition; in loyalty, there were those associated with Anji and Nanhai, whose distinction shone alike, one earlier and one later. In government, there was one who cherished kindness and was called “Mother Zhao” by the people, and another who taught learning and practiced ritual, bringing the scholars into harmonious accord. In literary learning, there was one who invited and honored great Confucian scholars and devoted himself to the learning of principle, and another who twice sought recommendation through the Transport Commission and possessed outstanding poetic…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
兼愛之失專主夫覺則曰心有知覺之
謂仁夫亦有所受也然其弊不惟使人
張皇躁迫無沉潛之味且或至認物爲
理而眛夫精一之宗是其可無愼歟諸
士子相與究言之明似是之非趨聖傳
之正是主司所深望也
問大江以西士齊民貧風氣爲弱自滕王
分封以來雄文傑閣膾炙人口往往遂
爲宗室之所托居世傳李氏出自唐裔
===
代有顯人今亦無以考其世矣迨夫宋
室南遷諸趙散處大率亦於茲土爲盛
而其間名公哲人多由科目以進其立
身行事之畧時或載諸史志可考也以
今言之孝則有都監酒庫祖孫之相承
忠則有安吉南海後先之並著政事則
有心存豈弟而民稱趙母者有講學行
禮而士風翕然者文學則有延禮大儒
而潛心理學者有兩請漕舉而卓有詩
punctuated:
兼愛之失。專主夫覺，則曰心有知覺之謂仁，夫亦有所受也。然其弊，不惟使人張皇躁迫，無沉潛之味，且或至認物爲理，而眛夫精一之宗，是其可無愼歟？諸士子相與究言之，明似是之非，趨聖傳之正，是主司所深望也。

問：大江以西，士齊民貧，風氣爲弱。自滕王分封以來，雄文傑閣，膾炙人口，往往遂爲宗室之所托居。世傳李氏出自唐裔，代有顯人，今亦無以考其世矣。迨夫宋室南遷，諸趙散處，大率亦於茲土爲盛。而其間名公哲人，多由科目以進，其立身行事之畧，時或載諸史志可考也。以今言之，孝則有都監、酒庫祖孫之相承；忠則有安吉、南海後先之並著；政事則有心存豈弟而民稱趙母者，有講學行禮而士風翕然者；文學則有延禮大儒而潛心理學者，有兩請漕舉而卓有詩
translation_en:
…the error of indiscriminate love. Those who focus exclusively on awareness say that the mind’s capacity for knowing and perceiving is what is called humaneness; this, too, has an inherited basis. Yet its pernicious effects not only make people agitated and impetuous, depriving them of the savor of quiet immersion, but may even lead them to mistake things for principle and obscure the essential teaching of refinement and single-mindedness. Can one fail to exercise caution here? You candidates should investigate and discuss this together, distinguish errors that appear correct, and turn toward the true teaching transmitted by the sages. This is the earnest hope of those presiding over the examination.

Question: West of the Great River, the scholars are alike [?], the common people poor, and the prevailing temper weak. Since the Prince of Teng was granted his fief, magnificent writing and a splendid pavilion have been celebrated on everyone’s lips, and this region has often become a place where members of imperial clans have made their homes. Tradition holds that the Li families descend from the Tang imperial house and produced eminent men in successive generations, but today their lineages can no longer be verified. When the Song court moved south, members of the Zhao clan dispersed, and their numbers were generally especially great in this region. Among them, many distinguished and wise men advanced through the examinations. Accounts of their personal conduct and deeds are sometimes recorded in histories and gazetteers and can be consulted.

To speak of examples now: in filial piety, there were the Military Supervisor and the Wine Depot official [?], grandfather and grandson who carried on the same tradition; in loyalty, there were those of Anji and Nanhai, equally renowned in earlier and later times. In government, there was one who cherished kindness and amiability and whom the people called ‘Mother Zhao,’ and another whose teaching and observance of ritual brought the scholars into harmonious accord. In literary learning, there was one who respectfully welcomed great Confucian scholars and devoted himself to the learning of principle, and another who twice sought nomination through the Transport Commission examination [?] and was outstanding in poetry…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
名者行誼則有棄著庶能之稱而大儒
器之者有蚤聞忠義之訓而所立卓然
者清脩則有退居錦水二十年不磨勘
者有身爲帝胄而甘守布衣之操者俱
可得而言之歟至若身居宰輔文武忠
孝此固古今之所尊仰又不獨一鄉之
望而已而亦可獨舉而許之歟我
祖宗封建法周親愛如舜唐宋不足言矣而其
爵封玆土者枝流蕃衍與
===
國同休不識於有宋諸賢之中亦或可取以
爲東平樂善之勸否也諸士子留心經
濟久矣玆非若輩所當尚論時邪
問五穀三幣之行世非不貴且便也惟以
其便也而輕用之則其勢不得不趨於
錢鈔矣且幣以利用宜矣彼錢者何爲
乎錢猶金之類可矣彼鈔者何爲乎歷
代之錢輕重不一而孰爲便而可行歟
鈔固
punctuated:
名者。行誼則有棄著庶能之稱而大儒器之者，有蚤聞忠義之訓而所立卓然者。清脩則有退居錦水二十年不磨勘者，有身爲帝胄而甘守布衣之操者。俱可得而言之歟？至若身居宰輔，文武忠孝，此固古今之所尊仰，又不獨一鄉之望而已，而亦可獨舉而許之歟？我祖宗封建法周，親愛如舜，唐宋不足言矣。而其爵封玆土者，枝流蕃衍，與國同休，不識於有宋諸賢之中，亦或可取以爲東平樂善之勸否也？諸士子留心經濟久矣，玆非若輩所當尚論時邪？

問：五穀三幣之行世，非不貴且便也。惟以其便也而輕用之，則其勢不得不趨於錢鈔矣。且幣以利用宜矣，彼錢者何爲乎？錢猶金之類可矣，彼鈔者何爲乎？歷代之錢輕重不一，而孰爲便而可行歟？鈔固
translation_en:
…renowned for poetry. As for conduct and integrity, there were those reputed to possess many abilities [the wording 棄著庶能 is doubtful] whom great Confucian scholars esteemed, and those who received instruction in loyalty and righteousness early in life and distinguished themselves by their achievements. As for purity of conduct and self-cultivation, there were those who retired to Jinshui and went twenty years without an assessment for promotion, and those who, though descendants of emperors, willingly maintained the principles of an untitled commoner. Can all these be identified and discussed? As for those who held office as chief councillors, accomplished in civil and military affairs, loyal and filial: they have surely been revered in every age, and were more than merely the pride of a single locality. Yet can they alone be singled out for approval? Our imperial ancestors modeled their enfeoffments on the Zhou and showed affection for their kinsmen as Shun did; the Tang and Song do not merit comparison. Those enfeoffed in this land have multiplied in their branches and lineages, sharing in the dynasty’s blessings. Might some examples among the worthy men of the Song be chosen to encourage them to emulate the Prince of Dongping’s delight in goodness? You examination candidates have long devoted your attention to statecraft. Is this not the occasion for you to discuss the worthies of the past?

Question: The five grains and the three metallic currencies, as they circulate in the world, are certainly valuable and convenient. Yet if their convenience leads to their indiscriminate use, circumstances must inevitably tend toward coin and paper money. Now, it is fitting that metallic currency should facilitate use; but what purpose, then, do coins serve? Coins may be acceptable as still belonging to the category of metals; but what purpose does paper money serve? Coins have varied in weight through successive dynasties: which were convenient and practicable? Paper money admittedly…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
時制也然亦有敝好不同而何能使之不墜
歟或謂錢宜行於通都而不行於僻地
鈔宜行於草昧而不行於承平則今日
所爲論功議辟者無乃失實歟常聞先
王制錢義精而博後世之鈔則鈔而已
亦有可言者歟方今
大工告興國用爲絀急計則爲輸粟遠謀則有
發礦秪爲銀幣計耳而其間所得不補
其所亡者亦有之不知是二物者古昔
===
所以通變宜民之方而積於無用之地
顧猶以匱乏爲言何歟夫錢穀皆吾分
內而世務由於經術無曰明明求財利
者庶人之事也而忽諸
問救荒弭盜之策在爲政者均所當講而
江西尤急何者地狹人稠耕稼不足自
給一有水旱之災即其荒易見也深山
重湖姦慝藉以藏匿一有萑符之警即
其勢難靖也古之爲荒備者有平糴法
punctuated:
時制也，然亦有敝好不同，而何能使之不墜歟？或謂錢宜行於通都，而不行於僻地；鈔宜行於草昧，而不行於承平。則今日所爲論功議辟者，無乃失實歟？常聞先王制錢，義精而博；後世之鈔，則鈔而已，亦有可言者歟？方今大工告興，國用爲絀，急計則爲輸粟，遠謀則有發礦，秪爲銀幣計耳。而其間所得不補其所亡者，亦有之。不知是二物者，古昔所以通變宜民之方，而積於無用之地，顧猶以匱乏爲言，何歟？夫錢穀皆吾分內，而世務由於經術，無曰明明求財利者，庶人之事也，而忽諸。

問：救荒弭盜之策，在爲政者均所當講，而江西尤急。何者？地狹人稠，耕稼不足自給，一有水旱之災，即其荒易見也。深山重湖，姦慝藉以藏匿，一有萑符之警，即其勢難靖也。古之爲荒備者，有平糴法。
translation_en:
…were an institution devised for the needs of their time. Yet they too differ in their defects and merits: how can they be kept from falling into disuse? Some say that coins should circulate in great cities but not in remote places, and that paper currency should circulate in unsettled times but not in times of peace. If so, do present-day discussions of their merits and faults [?] not depart from reality? We have often heard that the principles underlying the former kings’ creation of coinage were subtle and comprehensive. As for the paper currency of later ages, is it merely paper currency, or is there something further to be said about it?

Now that major construction works have been initiated and state finances are straitened, the immediate expedient is to procure deliveries of grain, while the longer-term plan is to open mines. These measures concern only the acquisition of silver currency. Yet in some cases the gains do not make up for the losses. We do not understand: these two forms of currency were the means by which people in antiquity adapted to changing circumstances and benefited the populace; yet they now accumulate in places where they serve no purpose, while scarcity is still pleaded. Why is this? Money and grain both fall within our responsibilities, and the management of worldly affairs derives from learning in the Classics. Do not dismiss these matters by saying that openly seeking financial gain [?] is the business of commoners.

Question: Measures for relieving famine and suppressing banditry are equally matters that those who govern should study, but they are especially urgent in Jiangxi. Why is this? The land is limited and the population dense; cultivation does not provide enough for self-sufficiency. Whenever flood or drought strikes, famine readily manifests itself. Deep mountains and extensive lakes provide hiding places for evildoers; whenever an alarm of banditry arises [?], the situation is difficult to pacify. Among the measures used in antiquity to prepare against famine was the system of purchasing grain at equitable prices…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
有常平法有義倉社倉法其在君子蓋
不無異議矣今將曷從爲益備者有沈
命法有檛鼓法有義营懸賞法其行之
當時亦不能皆效矣今將安出或有爲
本末源流之論而推言禹湯受災不困
之因似平糴諸法可盡廢也其信然歟
有爲舍本禁末之說而力沮熙寧盜賊
重法之請似沈命諸法可盡弛也抑確
論歟夫君子不恃患之未至恃吾有以
===
待之苟莫爲之所豈徒主司之憂亦二
三子生於其鄉者之羞也願詳言之
punctuated: 有常平法，有義倉、社倉法，其在君子，蓋不無異議矣。今將曷從？爲益備者，有沈命法，有檛鼓法，有義营懸賞法，其行之當時，亦不能皆效矣。今將安出？或有爲本末源流之論，而推言禹湯受災不困之因，似平糴諸法可盡廢也，其信然歟？有爲舍本禁末之說，而力沮熙寧盜賊重法之請，似沈命諸法可盡弛也，抑確論歟？夫君子不恃患之未至，恃吾有以待之。苟莫爲之所，豈徒主司之憂，亦二三子生於其鄉者之羞也。願詳言之。
translation_en:
…there are the ever-normal granary system and the systems of charitable and community granaries. Among gentlemen, these have certainly not been free from disagreement. Which should we now follow? As for measures against banditry [?], there are the Shenming law imposing death for failure to report or apprehend bandits, the system of beating drums to raise the alarm, and measures involving volunteer militia camps [?] and rewards. Even when first implemented, these did not all prove effective. What course should we now adopt?

Some discuss roots and branches, sources and streams, and explain further why Yu and Tang suffered disasters without being reduced to distress. This would seem to imply that the equitable grain-purchasing system and all the other measures could be abolished. Is that really so? Others argue that suppressing consequences neglects the root causes, and vigorously oppose proposals for the severe laws against banditry of the Xining era. This would seem to imply that the Shenming law and all the other measures could be relaxed. But is this a sound judgment?

The gentleman relies not on trouble having yet to arrive, but on possessing the means to meet it. If no provision is made, this is surely not merely a concern for the officials in charge; it is also a disgrace to you candidates, who were born in this province. Please explain in detail.

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
乎宜無不厚之恩聖人實無陰厚之教吾試舉
家庭所嘗聞者以告子焉是故退朝以燕退燕
以閒夫子蓋嘗獨立矣家有嚴君其可無禮鯉
之過庭而必恭敬以趨之也斯時也堂上惟父
堂下惟子欲有所厚此其可以厚矣夫子則問
以學詩乎而鯉以未也對之夫子則曰詩以聲
志而所由以言者不學則事理昧而心氣乖其
何以言鯉承夫子之教退而學詩本二南以求
其端也參列國以盡其變也正於雅以大其規
===
和於頌以要其止也必使涵泳從容而自得性
情之正言其寡尤乎然此特一事耳未足以盡
觀夫子也他日又嘗獨立矣雖見之狎夫敢不
貌鯉之過庭亦必齋栗以趨之也斯時也童蒙
匪求英才未待欲有所厚此又可以厚矣夫子
則問以學禮乎而鯉復以未也對之夫子則曰
禮以治躬而所由以立者不學則品節踈而德
性蕩其何以立鯉服夫子之訓退而學禮忠信
以立其本也義理以考其文也求之實以體□
punctuated: 乎，宜無不厚之恩，聖人實無陰厚之教。吾試舉家庭所嘗聞者，以告子焉。是故退朝以燕，退燕以閒，夫子蓋嘗獨立矣。家有嚴君，其可無禮？鯉之過庭，而必恭敬以趨之也。斯時也，堂上惟父，堂下惟子，欲有所厚，此其可以厚矣。夫子則問以「學詩乎？」而鯉以「未也」對之。夫子則曰：「詩以聲志，而所由以言者。不學，則事理昧而心氣乖，其何以言？」鯉承夫子之教，退而學詩。本二南以求其端也，參列國以盡其變也，正於雅以大其規，和於頌以要其止也。必使涵泳從容，而自得性情之正，言其寡尤乎？然此特一事耳，未足以盡觀夫子也。他日，又嘗獨立矣。雖見之狎，夫敢不貌？鯉之過庭，亦必齋栗以趨之也。斯時也，童蒙匪求，英才未待，欲有所厚，此又可以厚矣。夫子則問以「學禮乎？」而鯉復以「未也」對之。夫子則曰：「禮以治躬，而所由以立者。不學，則品節踈而德性蕩，其何以立？」鯉服夫子之訓，退而學禮。忠信以立其本也，義理以考其文也，求之實以體□
translation_en:
…As a father, he should indeed bestow every kindness; yet as a sage, he truly imparts no teaching that privately favors his son. Let me recount for you what I have heard within our household. After withdrawing from court, the Master would rest at home; after resting, he would enjoy some leisure. On one such occasion, he was standing alone. With a stern father presiding over the household, how could I neglect propriety? Whenever I, Li 鯉, crossed the courtyard, I would hasten forward reverently and respectfully. At that moment, there was only the father above in the hall and only the son below. Had he wished to show special favor, this would have been an opportunity. But the Master asked, “Have you studied the Odes?” I replied, “Not yet.” The Master said, “The Odes give voice to one’s aspirations and provide the means of speaking. Without studying them, one remains ignorant of the principles of affairs, and one’s mind and vital energies fall out of harmony. How, then, could one speak?”

Receiving the Master’s teaching, I withdrew and studied the Odes. I took the two ‘South’ sections as my foundation to seek their beginnings, compared the Airs of the various states to comprehend the full range of their variations, found correctness in the Elegantiae to enlarge my scope, and sought harmony in the Hymns to grasp their ultimate aim. I had to immerse myself in them at ease until I personally attained correctness of disposition and feeling. Would my speech then not incur few faults? Yet this was only one incident, insufficient for a complete understanding of the Master.

On another day, he was again standing alone. Though I saw him in familiar circumstances, how could I dare to be disrespectful? As I crossed the courtyard, I again hastened forward with solemnity and awe. At that moment, he was not seeking out untutored pupils, nor awaiting outstanding talents. Had he wished to show special favor, this too would have been an opportunity. But the Master asked, “Have you studied ritual?” Again I replied, “Not yet.” The Master said, “Ritual regulates one’s conduct and provides the means of establishing oneself. Without studying it, one’s observance of proper distinctions becomes lax and one’s moral nature unrestrained. How, then, could one establish oneself?”

Accepting the Master’s instruction, I withdrew and studied ritual. I established its foundation through conscientiousness and trustworthiness, examined its forms through righteousness and principle, and sought it in actual practice in order to embody [illegible]…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
常協諸義以盡其變也必使閫成交錯而自無
易慢之入立其可與乎是則家庭所嘗聞者如
此然皆學者之所共聞也又何異焉夫子嘗曰
天有四時春秋冬夏風雨霜露無非敎也地載
神氣神氣風霆風霆流形庶物露生無非敎也
則夫子之敎一天地也豈以父子而有所擇但
其敎之之序則又視其所至何如耳是故顏之
四勿曾之一貫反爲夫子之所獨厚而鯉則未
有聞也故陳亢無疑於聖人惟當求其獨厚
===
知斯三者則知所以脩身知所以脩身則
知所以治人知所以治人則知所以治
天下國家矣
張希舉

經而言最是
同考試官教諭唐 批〔脩身治人中以有君有〕
臣爲政貫說得中庸之旨
同考試官教諭徐 批〔是題包含一章之旨𢾼〕
punctuated:
常，協諸義以盡其變也，必使閫成交錯，而自無易慢之入，立其可與乎？是則家庭所嘗聞者如此，然皆學者之所共聞也，又何異焉？夫子嘗曰：「天有四時，春秋冬夏，風雨霜露，無非敎也。地載神氣，神氣風霆，風霆流形，庶物露生，無非敎也。」則夫子之敎，一天地也，豈以父子而有所擇？但其敎之之序，則又視其所至何如耳。是故顏之四勿、曾之一貫，反爲夫子之所獨厚，而鯉則未有聞也。故陳亢無疑於聖人，惟當求其獨厚。

知斯三者，則知所以脩身；知所以脩身，則知所以治人；知所以治人，則知所以治天下國家矣。

…constancy, bringing it into accord with righteousness to encompass all its variations. One must ensure that its inner formation is interwoven [?], so that carelessness and disrespect find no entrance. Could one then stand firm? Such, then, were the teachings heard within the household. Yet these were all teachings commonly heard by students: what difference was there? The Master once said: “Heaven has its four seasons—spring, autumn, winter, and summer; wind, rain, frost, and dew are all instruction. Earth bears spiritual forces; these forces become wind and thunder; wind and thunder circulate and take form, and the myriad things emerge into life: all are instruction.” The Master’s teaching thus accords with Heaven and Earth. How could he show preference because of the relationship between father and son? The sequence of his instruction, however, depended upon the stage each learner had reached. Thus Yan’s four prohibitions and Zeng’s single unifying thread were, instead, instances of the Master’s special generosity, while Li had not heard these teachings. Chen Kang therefore need have no doubts about the sage; he should only seek that special generosity.

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
□人之稱對巳也天下國家盡人也旣知所
以治人則積小高大而一變有至道之機由邇
可遠而四國有洽德之美自天下而言則遠人
也諸侯也吾皆有以曲成之而不遺自國家而
言則庶民也百工也臣也親也吾皆有以順施
之而各當矣不知所以治天下國家乎夫至於
治天下國家則文武之政行矣而其本則自脩
身始其機易決而其化至神君何憚而不爲耶
抑夫子作春秋以尊周爲本而此告哀公則勸
===
以治天下國家若王魯者何耶葢春秋立君臣
之義以定萬世之經故其辭嚴而告哀公則徵
視天命人心之去留向背以徇一時之權故其
辭婉要之平王東遷王迹已熄而天下漸不可
爲矣孔子之告哀公亦孟子勸齊梁之意也吾
於是又知孔孟之心則同
孟施舍之守氣又不如曾子之守約也
鄒懋卿
同考試官教諭李 批〔守約處能盡說孟舍曾子〕
punctuated:
□人之稱，對巳也。天下國家，盡人也。旣知所以治人，則積小高大，而一變有至道之機；由邇可遠，而四國有洽德之美。自天下而言，則遠人也，諸侯也，吾皆有以曲成之而不遺；自國家而言，則庶民也，百工也，臣也，親也，吾皆有以順施之而各當矣。不知所以治天下國家乎？夫至於治天下國家，則文武之政行矣，而其本則自脩身始。其機易決，而其化至神，君何憚而不爲耶？抑夫子作《春秋》，以尊周爲本，而此告哀公，則勸以治天下國家，若王魯者，何耶？葢《春秋》立君臣之義，以定萬世之經，故其辭嚴；而告哀公，則徵視天命人心之去留向背，以徇一時之權，故其辭婉。要之，平王東遷，王迹已熄，而天下漸不可爲矣。孔子之告哀公，亦孟子勸齊梁之意也。吾於是又知孔孟之心則同。

孟施舍之守氣，又不如曾子之守約也。

鄒懋卿

同考試官教諭李批〔守約處，能盡說孟舍曾子〕
translation_en:
…[illegible] the designation “others” is relative to oneself. All under Heaven, the state, and the family consist entirely of people. Once one knows how to govern people, one can accumulate the small to attain the lofty and great: a single transformation offers the possibility of reaching the Way. From what is near one can reach what is distant, bringing the beauty of pervasive virtue to the states in all four quarters. Speaking of all under Heaven, there are people from afar and the feudal lords: I have the means to bring each to fulfillment according to their circumstances, overlooking none. Speaking of the state and family, there are the common people, the various artisans, ministers, and relatives: I have the means to deal fittingly with them all, giving each their due. Would this not be knowing how to govern all under Heaven, the state, and the family?

When one succeeds in governing all under Heaven, the state, and the family, the government of Kings Wen and Wu is put into practice; yet its foundation begins with cultivating oneself. The decisive step is readily taken, while its transforming influence is supremely wondrous. What should make the ruler hesitate to act? Yet the Master composed the Spring and Autumn Annals with honoring Zhou as his fundamental purpose. Here, however, in addressing Duke Ai, he urges him to govern all under Heaven, the state, and the family, as though he would make Lu king. Why is this? The Spring and Autumn Annals establishes the proper relationship between ruler and minister to fix an enduring norm for ten thousand generations; hence its language is stern. In addressing Duke Ai, however, he examines [?] whether Heaven’s mandate and the people’s allegiance remain or depart, turn toward a ruler or turn away, and accommodates the exigencies of the moment; hence his language is gentle. In essence, after King Ping moved the capital east, the vestiges of true kingship had already vanished, and affairs throughout the realm were gradually becoming beyond remedy. Confucius’s advice to Duke Ai had the same intent as Mencius’s exhortations to the rulers of Qi and Liang. From this I know further that Confucius and Mencius shared the same purpose.

“Meng Shishe’s holding fast to his vital energy was, in turn, inferior to Zengzi’s holding fast to the essentials.”

Zou Maoqing.

之心殆邃於理學者
同考試官教諭王　批〔以守氣守約合比而作愈出愈深非淺學所及〕
同考試官教諭孫　批〔氣充才贍沛然不窮可式〕
考試官教諭葉　批〔是亦學而知要者矣〕
考試官教授伍　批〔講守約處甚精詳〕
大賢斷前人之勇主於理者大於氣也夫君子
靜定之學一理以爲之本也然則曾子義理之
勇豈孟舍血氣之可及哉孟子因論不動心之
===
有道而歸於曾子若謂語其槩則隨所執皆足
以不動心而要其極則非執之當者不足以語
不動心之至也是故勝不懼不勝亦不懼此孟
舍之所守以不動心者矣縮則往不縮則不往
此曾子之所守以不動心者矣然觀舍之把持
於進會之餘而卓然三軍之不畏者直守彼之
氣耳未必其理之果縮而可恃以無畏也若夫
會之量度於縮不縮之間而毅然萬人之亦往
者則守吾之理也理縮則氣可壯又焉計乎衆
punctuated:
之心，殆邃於理學者。
同考試官教諭王　批〔以守氣守約合比而作，愈出愈深，非淺學所及。〕
同考試官教諭孫　批〔氣充才贍，沛然不窮，可式。〕
考試官教諭葉　批〔是亦學而知要者矣。〕
考試官教授伍　批〔講守約處甚精詳。〕
大賢斷前人之勇，主於理者大於氣也。夫君子靜定之學，一理以爲之本也。然則曾子義理之勇，豈孟舍血氣之可及哉？孟子因論不動心之有道而歸於曾子，若謂語其槩，則隨所執皆足以不動心；而要其極，則非執之當者，不足以語不動心之至也。是故勝不懼，不勝亦不懼，此孟舍之所守以不動心者矣；縮則往，不縮則不往，此曾子之所守以不動心者矣。然觀舍之把持於進會之餘，而卓然三軍之不畏者，直守彼之氣耳，未必其理之果縮，而可恃以無畏也。若夫會之量度於縮不縮之間，而毅然萬人之亦往者，則守吾之理也。理縮則氣可壯，又焉計乎衆
translation_en:
…their minds; he is probably deeply versed in the learning of principle.

Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: 〔The essay develops a comparison between maintaining one's vital force and holding to the essentials. Its exposition grows ever deeper, beyond the reach of superficial learning.〕

Associate Examiner Sun, Instructor, comments: 〔Its energy is full and its talent abundant, flowing inexhaustibly. It can serve as a model.〕

Examiner Ye, Instructor, comments: 〔Here, too, is someone who has studied and understands what is essential.〕

Examiner Wu, Professor, comments: 〔The discussion of holding to the essentials is exceptionally precise and detailed.〕

The great worthy, judging the courage of his predecessors, held that courage governed by principle surpasses courage grounded in vital force. The gentleman's cultivation of stillness and stability takes principle alone as its foundation. How, then, could Meng She's courage of blood and vital force equal Zengzi's courage of moral principle? In discussing the way to keep the mind unmoved, Mengzi ultimately turned to Zengzi. It is as though he were saying that, broadly speaking, whatever each man holds to may suffice to keep his mind unmoved; but, considered in its ultimate perfection, only someone who holds to what is right can be said to have attained the highest degree of an unmoved mind.

Thus, to fear neither victory nor defeat was what Meng She held to in keeping his mind unmoved. To advance when upright, and not advance when not upright, was what Zengzi held to in keeping his mind unmoved. Yet when we observe She's self-command in advancing and withdrawing [?], standing firm without fear of the armies, he was merely maintaining his vital force. His principle was not necessarily truly upright, such that he could rely on it to be fearless. As for Zengzi [?], who weighed whether he was upright or not, and resolutely advanced even against ten thousand men, he held to the principle within himself. When principle is upright, vital force can be strong; why, then, reckon with the multitude…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
寡之不敵哉故以舍比黝吾固以爲舍之守約
矣若以曾比舍吾又以爲曾之守約焉何也蓋
氣雖不可以不守然無理以主之則氣易窮惟
以理而御乎氣則氣之行也無往不利故自舍
言之曰能無懼也然所處不當自爾震蘇即使
隱忍以制終索然而不寧也以曾言之若不量
力也然內省不疚夫何憂懼即使不幸而敗亦
脫然無所悔也是舍之不動者猶有時而動也
而曾之不動者則無時而動也然則孟舍雖似
===
曾子又豈得於曾子班乎特以比於黝爲彼善
於此矣孟子之不動心其原蓋出於此故知言
所以明理養氣所以聚理其當大任而不動心
誠自以爲守約不殊於曾子也彼告子者雖曰
外義强制以幸不動心之名而究其類不免施
舍之守氣耳皆不足以語聖賢之道也嗚呼舍
之不得爲曾子固也告子學於孟子而不免焉
可惜也已
punctuated: 寡之不敵哉？故以舍比黝，吾固以爲舍之守約矣；若以曾比舍，吾又以爲曾之守約焉。何也？蓋氣雖不可以不守，然無理以主之，則氣易窮；惟以理而御乎氣，則氣之行也，無往不利。故自舍言之，曰能無懼也，然所處不當，自爾震蘇，即使隱忍以制，終索然而不寧也。以曾言之，若不量力也，然內省不疚，夫何憂懼？即使不幸而敗，亦脫然無所悔也。是舍之不動者，猶有時而動也；而曾之不動者，則無時而動也。然則孟舍雖似曾子，又豈得於曾子班乎？特以比於黝，爲彼善於此矣。孟子之不動心，其原蓋出於此。故知言所以明理，養氣所以聚理；其當大任而不動心，誠自以爲守約不殊於曾子也。彼告子者，雖曰外義强制，以幸不動心之名，而究其類，不免施舍之守氣耳，皆不足以語聖賢之道也。嗚呼！舍之不得爲曾子固也，告子學於孟子而不免焉，可惜也已！
translation_en:
…why, then, reckon with being outmatched in numbers? Thus, comparing Meng Shishe with Beigong You, I certainly consider Shishe’s hold on what is essential to be firmer. Yet comparing Zengzi with Shishe, I consider Zengzi’s hold on the essential firmer still. Why? Although one cannot neglect to maintain one’s vital energy, without moral principle to govern it, that energy is easily exhausted. Only when principle directs vital energy can its exercise succeed wherever it goes. Thus, speaking of Shishe, one may say that he could be fearless; yet when his position was improper, he would naturally become agitated [?]. Even if he restrained himself through forbearance, he would ultimately remain dispirited and uneasy. Speaking of Zengzi, he might seem not to assess his own strength; yet if self-examination revealed nothing to reproach himself for, what anxiety or fear could he have? Even if he unfortunately suffered defeat, he would remain unburdened and without regret. Thus Shishe’s unmoved mind could still at times be moved, whereas Zengzi’s unmoved mind could never be moved. Although Meng Shishe resembled Zengzi, how could he rank alongside him? It is only in comparison with Beigong You that he may be called better than the other.

The source of Mencius’s unmoved mind lay here. Thus, understanding words serves to illuminate principle, and nourishing vital energy serves to accumulate principle. In remaining unmoved when undertaking great responsibilities, he truly considered his hold on the essential no different from Zengzi’s. As for Gaozi, although he treated righteousness as external and forcibly restrained himself, hoping thereby to gain the reputation of having an unmoved mind, examination of his approach shows that it amounted to no more than Shishe’s maintenance of vital energy. Neither approach suffices for discussing the Way of the sages and worthies. Alas! That Shishe could not equal Zengzi is understandable; but that Gaozi studied under Mencius and still failed to escape this limitation is truly regrettable!

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
益動而巽日進无疆
能鳴臣
同考試官教諭李　批〔益卦題士子下筆最易成文然細味之率蔓語耳理趣圓融若此篇者主司寧不爲之〕
刮目邪
同考試官教諭王　批〔理既精到詞復渾融求益之士也〕
同考試官教諭孫　批〔動巽相濟是一事作者多支離故錄此以式〕
===
考試官教諭葉　批〔動巽二字體認真切若子者可與幾矣〕
考試官教授伍　批〔以遷善改過立說尤取是結更有味〕
易傳本益之卦德具爲學之大益焉蓋益長裕
而不設者也動巽兼資以爲學而學斯日進矣
其益也不亦大乎易傳廣益之義如此今夫學
問之道固所以求益於得而夫人之學每病其
不善於求故怠於有爲者或失則止非動也撓
punctuated:
「益，動而巽，日進无疆。」
能鳴臣
同考試官教諭李批〔益卦題，士子下筆最易成文，然細味之，率蔓語耳。理趣圓融若此篇者，主司寧不爲之〕刮目邪？
同考試官教諭王批〔理既精到，詞復渾融，求益之士也。〕
同考試官教諭孫批〔動巽相濟是一事，作者多支離，故錄此以式。〕
考試官教諭葉批〔動巽二字，體認真切，若子者可與幾矣。〕
考試官教授伍批〔以遷善改過立說，尤取是結，更有味。〕
易傳本益之卦德，具爲學之大益焉。蓋益，長裕而不設者也。動巽兼資以爲學，而學斯日進矣。其益也，不亦大乎？易傳廣益之義如此。今夫學問之道，固所以求益於得，而夫人之學，每病其不善於求。故怠於有爲者，或失則止，非動也；撓
translation_en:
“Increase: active and yielding, daily advancing without limit.”
Neng Mingchen

Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “On a topic concerning the hexagram Increase, candidates can readily produce an essay as soon as they take up the brush. Yet, when examined closely, their writing is mostly rambling verbiage. When an essay’s reasoning is as rounded and integrated as this one’s, how could the presiding examiners fail to regard its author with fresh eyes?”

Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: “The reasoning is penetrating and precise, and the language thoroughly integrated. Here is a scholar who seeks improvement.”

Associate Examiner Sun, Instructor, comments: “Activity and yielding mutually supporting one another constitute a single process. Writers often treat them in a fragmented manner; thus we have selected this essay as a model.”

Examiner Ye, Instructor, comments: “His understanding of the two words ‘active’ and ‘yielding’ is genuine and exact. Someone like this candidate may be said to have nearly attained the Way.”

Examiner Wu, Professor, comments: “He grounds his argument in turning toward goodness and correcting faults. I especially commend the conclusion, which has still greater depth of meaning.”

The Commentary on the Changes draws upon the virtues of the hexagram Increase to set forth fully the great benefit of learning. Increase means growth and abundance without limit [?]. Drawing on both activity and yielding in pursuing learning, one’s learning advances daily. Is this not a great increase? Such is how the Commentary on the Changes expands the meaning of Increase. Now, the way of learning and inquiry is indeed the means of seeking to increase what one has attained. Yet people’s learning constantly suffers from their inability to seek properly. Thus those who are indolent in taking action may stop when they encounter a setback: this is not activity. Those who waver …

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
即而施者或失則易非巽也是卦下體震也而
其德爲動上體巽也而其德爲巽則是自强不
息志不安於小成循序有常學惟欲其自得見
善則遷其行果矣而必寬裕以居之所謂勿忘
勿助者也有過則改自治勇矣而必優游以養
之所謂遜志時敏者也夫然學其不日進哉蓋
學之不進與進而不繼以无其機也自强不息
則上達之機存焉矣亦以无其漸也循序有常
則深造之漸存焉矣將見善之遷者由勉以至
===
於安積小高大而天德位焉王道行焉其爲學
也與日而俱進者也夫豈有彊乎過之改者由
寡以至於无厭脩乃來而盛德成焉大業出焉
其爲進也與日而俱邁者也又奚有彊乎學至
於是信乎其益之大矣吁此動而巽所以爲益
也雖然動巽以進學宜矣乃若艮則止之義也
大畜於艮亦以日新其德言之何歟蓋動巽君
子進脩之功也艮止聖人主静立極之事也然
主静非可以空寂求之則動巽者固其資耳學
punctuated: 即而施者，或失則易，非巽也。是卦下體震也，而其德爲動；上體巽也，而其德爲巽。則是自强不息，志不安於小成；循序有常，學惟欲其自得。見善則遷，其行果矣，而必寬裕以居之，所謂勿忘勿助者也；有過則改，自治勇矣，而必優游以養之，所謂遜志時敏者也。夫然，學其不日進哉？蓋學之不進，與進而不繼，以无其機也；自强不息，則上達之機存焉矣。亦以无其漸也；循序有常，則深造之漸存焉矣。將見善之遷者，由勉以至於安，積小高大，而天德位焉，王道行焉。其爲學也，與日而俱進者也，夫豈有彊乎？過之改者，由寡以至於无，厭脩乃來，而盛德成焉，大業出焉。其爲進也，與日而俱邁者也，又奚有彊乎？學至於是，信乎其益之大矣！吁！此動而巽所以爲益也。雖然，動巽以進學宜矣，乃若艮，則止之義也；大畜於艮，亦以日新其德言之，何歟？蓋動巽，君子進脩之功也；艮止，聖人主静立極之事也。然主静非可以空寂求之，則動巽者固其資耳。學
translation_en:
…those who proceed immediately to act [?], but change course upon encountering a setback, lack yielding compliance. In this hexagram, the lower trigram is Zhen, whose virtue is movement; the upper trigram is Xun, whose virtue is yielding compliance. Thus one strengthens oneself without cease, one's ambition never content with a minor achievement; one follows a regular sequence, seeking in learning only to attain understanding for oneself. On seeing goodness, one turns toward it, acting decisively, yet must dwell in it with ease and ample patience. This is what is meant by “neither forgetting nor forcing growth.” On having faults, one corrects them, courageously governing oneself, yet must nurture oneself with unhurried ease. This is what is meant by “making one's will humble and continually applying oneself diligently.” With these qualities, how could learning fail to advance daily?

Learning fails to advance, or advances without continuing, because it lacks an impetus. Through unceasing self-strengthening, the impetus toward higher understanding is preserved. Failure also comes from lacking gradual stages. Through following a regular sequence, the stages leading to profound attainment are preserved. We shall then see those who turn toward goodness proceed from effort to ease, accumulating small gains to attain greatness and height, until heavenly virtue is established and the kingly Way is put into practice. Their learning advances with each passing day: how could it have any limit [?]? Those who correct their faults proceed from having few to having none; cultivation then comes to fruition [?], abundant virtue is perfected, and great undertakings emerge. Their progress moves forward with each passing day: how, again, could it have any limit [?]? When learning reaches this point, great indeed is its increase!

Ah! This is why movement joined with yielding compliance constitutes Increase. Yet, although movement and yielding compliance fittingly serve to advance learning, Gen means stopping. Why, then, does the discussion of Gen in Great Taming (Daxu) likewise speak of daily renewing one's virtue? Movement and yielding compliance are the work through which the gentleman advances his self-cultivation; Gen and stopping are the means by which the sage makes stillness central and establishes the ultimate standard. Yet making stillness central cannot be sought through emptiness and quiescence, so movement and yielding compliance are assuredly its resources. Students…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
者慎無以異觀之
知變化之道者其知神之所爲乎
邵奎明
同考試官教諭李　批〔變化神非二也知變化則〕
知神矣此作得之
同考試官教諭王　批〔理无滲漏語有斟酌遂〕
於易者也
同考試官教諭孫　批〔此是聖人歎數法之妙雖〕
不重在两知字然善作者下語自別録之
考試官教諭葉　批〔說理文字最難下筆何子〕
獨易衆人之所難耶健羡健羡
===
考試官教授伍　批〔體認精切〕
大傳即易之數法而深歎其妙焉甚矣數法之
變化皆神之所爲也知變化則知神矣宜聖人
有以發其妙而嘆之與且其意以爲易有數焉
有法焉皆變化之道也但人率以河圖爲虛文
蓍卦爲陳迹而知變化之道者鮮矣誠能於天
地大衍之數而凡奇偶生成之屈伸往來者皆
punctuated:
者慎無以異觀之。

「知變化之道者，其知神之所爲乎！」
邵奎明

同考試官教諭李　批〔變化、神非二也，知變化則〕知神矣，此作得之。

同考試官教諭王　批〔理无滲漏，語有斟酌，遂〕於易者也。

同考試官教諭孫　批〔此是聖人歎數法之妙，雖〕不重在两知字，然善作者下語自別，録之。

考試官教諭葉　批〔說理文字最難下筆，何子〕獨易衆人之所難耶？健羡，健羡！

考試官教授伍　批〔體認精切。〕

大傳即易之數法而深歎其妙焉。甚矣，數法之變化皆神之所爲也！知變化則知神矣，宜聖人有以發其妙而嘆之與！且其意以爲易有數焉，有法焉，皆變化之道也。但人率以河圖爲虛文，蓍卦爲陳迹，而知變化之道者鮮矣。誠能於天地大衍之數，而凡奇偶生成之屈伸往來者皆
translation_en:
…those who study should take care not to regard them as different.

“Those who know the way of change and transformation—surely they know what the numinous does!”
Shao Kuiming

Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “Change and transformation and the numinous are not two separate things. Knowing change and transformation, one knows the numinous. This composition grasps that.”

Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: “The reasoning leaves no gaps, and the wording is carefully weighed. This is someone accomplished in the Changes [?].”

Associate Examiner Sun, Instructor, comments: “Here the sage marvels at the subtlety of the numbers and procedures. Although the emphasis does not lie on the two occurrences of ‘know,’ a skilled writer is distinctive in his choice of words. Include it.”

Examiner Ye, Instructor, comments: “Writing that expounds principles is the hardest to undertake. Why do you alone find easy what everyone else finds difficult? How I envy you, how I envy you!”

Examiner Wu, Professor, comments: “Precise and penetrating comprehension.”

The Great Commentary takes up the numbers and procedures of the Book of Changes and marvels deeply at their subtlety. How profound it is that the changes and transformations of these numbers and procedures are all the workings of the numinous! To know change and transformation is to know the numinous. Surely it is fitting that the sage should disclose their subtlety and marvel at it! His meaning is that the Changes has numbers and has procedures, all constituting the way of change and transformation. Yet people generally regard the River Chart as an empty pattern and the milfoil stalks and hexagrams as relics of the past; few know the way of change and transformation. If one could truly, in the numbers of Heaven and Earth and of the Great Expansion, comprehend all the contraction and extension, coming and going, of the odd and even numbers and the numbers of generation and completion…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
□之進退離合者皆有以潛會其用不徒觀數
之文而已因數考變而得意以忘言謂圖具天
地之數可也謂吾心卽圖之精亦可也蓋有得
於形器之外者矣不徒究卦之迹而已假象明
理而極深以研幾謂法洩天地之秘可也謂吾
心卽法之靈亦可也蓋有契於言意之表者矣
若然則知數之有變化也孰主張是要皆莫之
爲而自爲者人之心思固有所不逮焉法之有
===
變化也孰綱維是要皆莫之致而自致者人之
智力則亦无所容焉故人徒知夫數法之原天
地開之也而不知天地者能開其端而不能必
其成至於曲成之妙天地亦不得而專也又徒
知夫數法之行聖人制之也而不知聖人者能
成其能而不能强其合至於會合之妙聖人亦
不得而與也噫其殆天下之至神者乎是故知
變化之道者則知神之所爲矣竊嘗疑之□□
不可知之謂也今而曰知神之爲何哉□□
punctuated: □之進退離合者，皆有以潛會其用，不徒觀數之文而已。因數考變，而得意以忘言，謂圖具天地之數可也，謂吾心卽圖之精亦可也，蓋有得於形器之外者矣。不徒究卦之迹而已，假象明理，而極深以研幾，謂法洩天地之秘可也，謂吾心卽法之靈亦可也，蓋有契於言意之表者矣。若然，則知數之有變化也，孰主張是？要皆莫之爲而自爲者，人之心思固有所不逮焉。法之有變化也，孰綱維是？要皆莫之致而自致者，人之智力則亦无所容焉。故人徒知夫數法之原，天地開之也，而不知天地者能開其端，而不能必其成；至於曲成之妙，天地亦不得而專也。又徒知夫數法之行，聖人制之也，而不知聖人者能成其能，而不能强其合；至於會合之妙，聖人亦不得而與也。噫，其殆天下之至神者乎！是故知變化之道者，則知神之所爲矣。竊嘗疑之：□□，不可知之謂也。今而曰知神之爲，何哉？□□
translation_en:
…their advance and retreat, separation and union [?]: in all these one can inwardly comprehend their operation, rather than merely observe the outward patterns of the numbers. By examining change through numbers, one grasps the meaning and forgets the words. One may say that the Diagram contains the numbers of Heaven and Earth; one may also say that one’s own mind is the very essence of the Diagram. This is to have grasped something beyond material forms. Nor does one merely investigate the traces of the hexagrams. By using images to illuminate principles and plumbing the depths to investigate the incipient signs of change, one may say that the methods disclose the secrets of Heaven and Earth; one may also say that one’s own mind is the very numinous efficacy of the methods. This is to have attained an accord beyond words and meanings.

If so, when we recognize that numbers undergo change and transformation, what presides over this? Ultimately, all this occurs of itself, without anything making it occur; human thought certainly has limits beyond which it cannot reach. When the methods undergo change and transformation, what orders and sustains this? Ultimately, all this comes about of itself, without anything bringing it about; human intelligence and effort likewise have no place to intervene. Thus people know only that Heaven and Earth initiated the numbers and methods, but do not know that Heaven and Earth can initiate them without being able to ensure their completion. As for the wondrous working that brings each thing to fulfillment in its particular circumstances, even Heaven and Earth cannot claim sole mastery over it. Again, people know only that the sages established the practice of the numbers and methods, but do not know that the sages can bring their capacities to fruition without being able to force their correspondence. As for the wondrous working of their convergence and correspondence, even the sages cannot intervene in it.

Ah! Is this not perhaps the utmost numinous power in all the world? Thus those who understand the Way of change and transformation understand what the numinous accomplishes. I have ventured to question this: [two illegible characters] signifies that which cannot be known. Why, then, speak now of knowing what the numinous accomplishes? [Two illegible characters]…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
君德故爲治者患民不安耳誠能容保無疆合
羣生而長養之使各迪于吉康教思無窮舉一
世而甄陶之使各正其性命安民如是則是仁
足以長人德之出于身者無不漸被何異於乾
之以美利利天下乎愛足以濟衆澤之加于民
者無不淪洽何異於坤之以厚德載物乎是則
所謂惠矣夫惠固無心之感也然君以民爲心
則民必以君爲心自愛戴而歸往仁特君之自
盡耳然愼厥麗乃勸則民亦惟刑用勸自仰慕
===
而悅服若于政者遂所欲而懷其恩樂樂利利
蓋有沒世不能忘者矣化于訓者全所性而懷
其德尊尊親親蓋有固結不可解者矣是則安
民而至於民懷則仁之功用著矣況幷其官人
而兼盡之其可以易而爲乎抑孔子之贊舜曰
無爲而治者其舜也與則治又若易易焉者何
耶蓋君天也天運於上而四時行百物生易簡
而已矣人君任相相舉賢才天下之民不勞而
治者法天而已矣故孟子曰舜以不得禹皋陶

translation_en:
…the ruler’s virtue. Thus those who govern need only be concerned that the people are not at peace. If the ruler can embrace and protect without limit, gathering all living beings and nurturing them so that each advances toward well-being; if his concern for instruction is inexhaustible, molding an entire generation so that each fulfills its proper nature and destiny—then, by bringing peace to the people in this way, his benevolence suffices to lead others, and the virtue issuing from his person spreads everywhere. How does this differ from Qian, Heaven, benefiting all under Heaven with its excellent bounty? His love suffices to succor the multitude, and the blessings he bestows upon the people penetrate everywhere. How does this differ from Kun, Earth, bearing all things through its ample virtue? This is what is called beneficence.

Beneficence indeed moves others without deliberate intent. Yet when the ruler takes the people’s concerns as his own, the people will surely take the ruler’s concerns as theirs, naturally loving and supporting him and turning to him in allegiance. Benevolence is simply the ruler’s fulfillment of his own moral responsibilities. Yet if he carefully chooses what he cleaves to, people are encouraged toward goodness; the people likewise follow his example and are encouraged, naturally admiring him and submitting gladly. Those who comply with his government attain what they desire and cherish his kindness, delighting in what brings them delight and benefiting from what benefits them; indeed, some cannot forget him for the rest of their lives. Those transformed by his instruction fully realize their nature and cherish his virtue, honoring those worthy of honor and loving those close to them; indeed, their attachment becomes so firm that it cannot be dissolved. When bringing peace to the people thus leads to their affectionate attachment, the efficacy of benevolence becomes manifest.

How much more demanding it is to fulfill this together with the task of appointing people to office! Can this be accomplished easily? Yet Confucius praised Shun, saying, “Was it not Shun who governed through nonaction?” Why, then, does governing again appear so very easy? The ruler is Heaven. Heaven revolves above, the four seasons proceed, and the myriad things are born: it is simply ease and simplicity. The ruler appoints chief councilors, and the chief councilors recommend worthy and talented men. That the people throughout the realm are governed without toil is simply a matter of modeling oneself on Heaven. Thus Mengzi said, “Shun regarded not obtaining Yu and Gao Yao …

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
聞而輕於所見方其未見聖也則好德動於秉
彝之良而曰聖人吾不得而見矣慨慕之甚切
若弗克見焉及其既見聖也則私心奪於物欲
之蔽而曰聖人亦若是而已矣怠忽之隨生亦
弗克由焉是則人之情大抵然也爾之東郊必
戒之哉夫爾於周公則既嘗見之矣周公目擊
殷民之亂其操心甚危而慮患甚深也汝繼其
後必以周公之心爲心期於共濟而不必其法
自我立周公深惟東郊之治其爲謨甚訏而爲
===
猷甚遠也汝居其位必以周公之事爲事期於
相成而不必其功自己出所以然者何哉蓋爾
之於民以鼓舞爲德譬之在天其惟風也民之
於爾以順從爲德譬之在地其惟草也風行則
草偃而自有感應之孚上立則下從而自有神
化之妙故爾能由周公之訓以風乎民則民亦
以懷周公者而從乎爾其於化殷也又何難哉
雖然周公治殷以謹毖爲務成王欲君陳由訓
乃有取於寬和何邪蓋道有定體政無定用故
punctuated:

translation_en:
…what they hear, while making light of what they see. Before they have seen a sage, their love of virtue stirs from the goodness of their innate moral nature, and they say, “A sage—I have not been able to see one!” Their longing and admiration are so earnest that they seem afraid they will never be able to see him. Once they have seen a sage, however, their selfish minds are overcome by the obscuring influence of material desires, and they say, “A sage is merely like this, after all.” Indifference and neglect arise accordingly, and they cannot follow him either. Such, by and large, are human feelings. When you go to the eastern suburbs, you must guard against this!
You have already seen the Duke of Zhou. The Duke of Zhou witnessed the disorder among the people of Yin; he was deeply apprehensive in his heart and gave profound thought to possible troubles. In succeeding him, you must take the Duke of Zhou’s concerns as your own, striving to bring the undertaking to completion together, without insisting that its methods originate with you. The Duke of Zhou pondered deeply the governance of the eastern suburbs; his plans were expansive and his designs far-reaching. In occupying his position, you must take the Duke of Zhou’s work as your own, striving to complete his achievement, without insisting that the credit come from you.
Why is this so? Your virtue in relation to the people lies in inspiring and stirring them: to draw an analogy from the heavens, you are the wind. The people’s virtue in relation to you lies in following obediently: to draw an analogy from the earth, they are the grass. When the wind blows, the grass bends; influence and response naturally accord with one another. When those above establish an example, those below follow; therein naturally lies the subtle efficacy of wondrous transformation. Thus, if you can follow the Duke of Zhou’s instructions and thereby influence the people, they will follow you with the same affection they cherish for the Duke of Zhou. What difficulty, then, could there be in transforming the people of Yin?
Nevertheless, in governing Yin, the Duke of Zhou made caution and vigilance his chief concern. Why, when King Cheng wished Jun Chen to follow those instructions, did he instead favor leniency and harmony? The Way has a constant essential form, but government has no fixed manner of application; therefore…

…one must adapt to changing circumstances so that the people do not grow weary, transforming them with spiritual efficacy so that they find what suits them. Only then will government through luminous virtue be renewed daily, and its fragrant influence reach ever more fully to the spirits. If one professes to follow the Duke of Zhou’s instructions yet remains bound to the outward traces of his initial caution, this is no way to follow the Duke of Zhou’s underlying intent. This, too, is something those who discuss following his instructions should understand.

Book of Odes

“Continuing the work of ancestral mothers and forefathers, he built a dwelling with a hundred stretches of wall, its doors facing west and south. Here they dwell, here they abide; here they laugh, here they converse.”

Zhang Xiju

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
如此意謂天子以四海爲家而聖人以繼述爲
孝昔周中葉王靈嘗不振矣王居嘗不守矣維
王勵修攘之功樹中興之業知夫宅中圖大妣
祖之經營以垂裕者甚備也而不敢使耿光之
遏佚又念夫居重馭輕妣祖之締造以貽後者
甚艱也而必期於大烈之對揚勞非所憚也身
任夫堂構之責而若或臨之凡謀爲於今者固
將以似其事焉費非所惜也志專於茨塈之圖
而若或見之凡興作於今者罔非以續其緒焉
===
是故乃召司空乃召司徒則絡勾陳以繚垣而
翼然百堵之在望矣考諸中星揆諸日景則闢
閶闔以啓扉而翚然西南之錯見矣於是居且
處焉所謂當宁而朝當依而覲者此也所謂路
寢聽政小寢釋服者此也而其景象不有以新
天下之耳目乎於是笑且語焉以睦九族以親
諸侯以樂嘉賓者此也以圖大事以陳衆謨以
協群慮者此也而其氣勢不有以繫天下之心
志乎故曰匪棘其欲遹追來孝信宣王之能中
punctuated:
如此。意謂天子以四海爲家，而聖人以繼述爲孝。昔周中葉，王靈嘗不振矣，王居嘗不守矣。維王勵修攘之功，樹中興之業，知夫宅中圖大，妣祖之經營以垂裕者甚備也，而不敢使耿光之遏佚；又念夫居重馭輕，妣祖之締造以貽後者甚艱也，而必期於大烈之對揚。勞非所憚也，身任夫堂構之責，而若或臨之，凡謀爲於今者，固將以似其事焉。費非所惜也，志專於茨塈之圖，而若或見之，凡興作於今者，罔非以續其緒焉。
是故乃召司空，乃召司徒，則絡勾陳以繚垣，而翼然百堵之在望矣。考諸中星，揆諸日景，則闢閶闔以啓扉，而翚然西南之錯見矣。於是居且處焉，所謂當宁而朝、當依而覲者，此也；所謂路寢聽政、小寢釋服者，此也。而其景象不有以新天下之耳目乎？於是笑且語焉，以睦九族、以親諸侯、以樂嘉賓者，此也；以圖大事、以陳衆謨、以協群慮者，此也。而其氣勢不有以繫天下之心志乎？故曰：「匪棘其欲，遹追來孝。」信宣王之能中
translation_en:
…in this way. The meaning is that the Son of Heaven takes all within the Four Seas as his home, while the sage regards carrying on and completing his predecessors’ work as filial piety. In the middle period of the Zhou, royal majesty had fallen into decline, and the royal residence had ceased to be secure. The king exerted himself to restore order within and repel threats from without, establishing the achievement of dynastic resurgence. He understood how thoroughly his ancestral mothers and fathers had planned to occupy the center and pursue great undertakings, bequeathing abundant resources to their descendants; he dared not allow their brilliant glory to be obscured or lost. He also reflected on how arduous their founding work had been, establishing a commanding center from which to govern the lesser dependencies and leaving it to posterity; he was determined to acknowledge and exalt their great achievements. He did not shrink from toil. Personally assuming responsibility for building upon his predecessors’ foundations, he acted as though they stood over him: everything he planned and undertook in the present was intended to carry on their work. Nor did he begrudge expense. Devoting himself to plans for thatching and plastering, he acted as though they watched him: every building project undertaken in the present continued the work they had begun.
Thus he summoned the Minister of Works and the Minister of Education. Encircling the palace precincts with enclosing walls, he brought a hundred stately stretches of wall into view. Observing the stars at their meridian transit and measuring the sun’s shadow, he laid out the palace gates and opened their doors; buildings to the west and south appeared in an interlacing array, their roofs like pheasants spreading their wings. Here he dwelt and took his repose. This was where, as the ritual texts say, he stood in the space before the main hall to hold court and before the ceremonial screen to receive the feudal lords. This was where he heard affairs of government in the principal chamber and removed his ceremonial robes in the lesser chamber. Did this spectacle not offer something new to the eyes and ears of all under Heaven? Here he laughed and conversed. This was where he brought harmony to the nine degrees of kinship, cultivated affection with the feudal lords, and entertained honored guests; here he planned great affairs, heard the many counsels presented, and brought diverse deliberations into agreement. Did its imposing grandeur not bind to him the hearts and aspirations of all under Heaven? Thus the poem says: “He was not hastening to gratify his desires, but pursuing the filial devotion handed down to him.” Truly, King Xuan was able to bring about a dynastic…

興也雖然此特以侈一時之盛耳乃如其本則
不在是側身脩行不有雲漢之憂乎早朝晏罷
不有夜如何之問乎是故斯干宮室有宣王之
治則爲孝無宣王之治終亦後世千門萬戶之
爲也論興作者宜辯諸此
維女荆楚居國南鄉昔有成湯自彼氐羌
莫敢不來享莫敢不來王曰商是常

興也。雖然，此特以侈一時之盛耳。乃如其本，則不在是。側身脩行，不有《雲漢》之憂乎？早朝晏罷，不有「夜如何」之問乎？是故《斯干》宮室，有宣王之治則爲孝，無宣王之治，終亦後世千門萬戶之爲也。論興作者，宜辯諸此。

translation_en:
…restore the dynasty. Even so, this merely served to display the splendor of a single age. Its foundation lay elsewhere. Did he not humble himself and cultivate his conduct, with the anxiety expressed in “The Milky Way” (Yunhan)? Did he not attend court early and retire late, asking, “How goes the night?” Thus, the palace buildings celebrated in “The River Banks” (Sigan), when accompanied by government like King Xuan’s, constituted filial devotion. Without government like his, they would ultimately amount only to the construction of a thousand gates and ten thousand doors in later ages. Those who discuss building projects should distinguish them on this basis.
You, Jing-Chu, dwell in the southern region of the realm. Formerly there was Cheng Tang: even from among those Di and Qiang, none dared fail to come with offerings; none dared fail to come to acknowledge his kingship. They said, “For Shang, this is the constant rule.”
Zhou Ji.
