title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
責楚人也有以哉此祀高宗之樂歌叙其既克
楚而告之之言曰天立君也所以爲華夷之主
也故天下之政必出於一而不可以今昔言天
下之人必歸於一而不可以遠近論嗟女荊楚
阻洞庭彭蠡以爲雄自以爲居則遠矣然依五
服九州以立國實在乎毫之南焉封疆伊邇聲
敎所加風土不殊正朔必及昔則我商之臣僕
也而今何如哉不聞我商之盛時乎由盤庚而
上則有成湯爲之君中間太甲太戊之統承無
===
論巳自荊楚而西亦有氐羌爲之國近而帝顧
昆吾之率服無論巳是故時必以享賓服之制
也而彼則不敢以數而不恭凡所以脩庭實而
將問者靡或遠也終必以王荒服之制也而彼
則不敢以遠而遂廢凡所以執玉帛而稱臣者
無敢懈也則曰玆享也非自今作也自受命以
來未之有改也且吾聞先王之訓不享者有征
討之備而又奚後焉亦曰玆王也非自玆始也
自立國以來未之有變也且吾聞先王之制不
punctuated: 責楚人也，有以哉！此祀高宗之樂歌，叙其既克楚而告之之言曰：「天立君也，所以爲華夷之主也。故天下之政必出於一，而不可以今昔言；天下之人必歸於一，而不可以遠近論。嗟女荊楚，阻洞庭、彭蠡以爲雄，自以爲居則遠矣。然依五服九州以立國，實在乎毫之南焉。封疆伊邇，聲敎所加；風土不殊，正朔必及。昔則我商之臣僕也，而今何如哉？不聞我商之盛時乎？由盤庚而上，則有成湯爲之君，中間太甲、太戊之統承無論巳；自荊楚而西，亦有氐羌爲之國，近而帝顧、昆吾之率服無論巳。是故時必以享，賓服之制也，而彼則不敢以數而不恭，凡所以脩庭實而將問者，靡或遠也；終必以王，荒服之制也，而彼則不敢以遠而遂廢，凡所以執玉帛而稱臣者，無敢懈也。則曰：『玆享也，非自今作也，自受命以來，未之有改也。且吾聞先王之訓，不享者有征討之備，而又奚後焉？』亦曰：『玆王也，非自玆始也，自立國以來，未之有變也。且吾聞先王之制，不
translation_en:
…there were indeed grounds for rebuking the people of Chu! This sacrificial hymn to Gaozong recounts the words with which he admonished Chu after conquering it:

“Heaven establishes a ruler to be lord over both the Chinese and the non-Chinese peoples. Thus government throughout the realm must issue from a single source, without distinction between past and present; the people throughout the realm must give allegiance to a single ruler, without distinction between near and far. Ah, you people of Jingchu! Relying on the barriers of Dongting and Pengli, you deem yourselves mighty and suppose that your dwelling place is remote. Yet your state was established within the five service zones and the Nine Provinces, and lies in fact south of Hao [?, probably Bo]. Your borders are close by, within reach of our civilizing influence; your lands and customs are not different, and our calendar must extend to you. Formerly you were servants of our Shang: how do matters stand today?

“Have you not heard of the flourishing days of our Shang? Looking back beyond Pan Geng, there was Cheng Tang as its ruler, to say nothing of the intervening succession of Tai Jia and Tai Wu. West of Jingchu there were also the states of the Di and Qiang, to say nothing of the submission of the nearer Digu [?] and Kunwu. Hence they were required to present offerings at the prescribed times: this was the regulation for the guest service zone. They dared not become disrespectful because these duties were frequent; none considered the journey too distant to prepare the gifts displayed in the royal courtyard and convey their greetings. They were required to pay homage to the king once in each generation: this was the regulation for the remote service zone. They dared not abandon this duty because of the distance; none dared be negligent in bearing jade and silk and acknowledging themselves as subjects.

“Thus they said: ‘These offerings are no new institution of today. Since the reception of Heaven’s mandate, they have never been altered. Moreover, we have heard the former kings’ instruction: against those who fail to present offerings, preparations are made for punitive expeditions. Why, then, should we lag behind?’ They also said: ‘This homage to the king did not begin only now. Since the founding of our state, it has never changed. title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
王者有文告之辭而又爲後焉是則服於遠而
不服於近服於先王而不服於今日謂之當震
可乎序戍而凌不至我以是陳兵而來也亦求
以纘湯緒而已豈欲勤兵於遠哉吁不觀之兵
則爲不武不聲之罪則爲無名而高宗之師衆
有之吾以是而知其中興之有自矣雖然窮兵
遠討老師費財皆兵家之所忌也而鬼方之伐
深入其阻三年而後克之不幾於犯厥忌乎而
終以克者何也孟子嘗言之矣由湯至於武丁
===
賢聖之君六七作盖人之戴商也維舊而楚之
叛之也獨先此高宗所以不得已而興師也故
雖深入而不爲窮三年而不爲老卒亦未嘗不
直且壯也否則其不爲秦皇漢武之師也者幾
希
春秋
秋荆伐鄭公會齊人宋人救鄭〔莊公二十〕
有八年楚人伐鄭公子遂會晉人宋人
衛人許人救鄭〔文公九年〕
punctuated:
王者有文告之辭，而又爲後焉。是則服於遠而不服於近，服於先王而不服於今日，謂之當震可乎？序戍而凌不至，我以是陳兵而來也，亦求以纘湯緒而已，豈欲勤兵於遠哉？吁！不觀之兵，則爲不武；不聲之罪，則爲無名。而高宗之師衆有之，吾以是而知其中興之有自矣。雖然，窮兵遠討，老師費財，皆兵家之所忌也。而鬼方之伐，深入其阻，三年而後克之，不幾於犯厥忌乎？而終以克者，何也？孟子嘗言之矣：「由湯至於武丁，賢聖之君六七作。」盖人之戴商也維舊，而楚之叛之也獨先，此高宗所以不得已而興師也。故雖深入而不爲窮，三年而不爲老，卒亦未嘗不直且壯也。否則，其不爲秦皇漢武之師也者幾希。

春秋

秋，荆伐鄭，公會齊人、宋人救鄭。〔莊公二十〕有八年。
楚人伐鄭，公子遂會晉人、宋人、衛人、許人救鄭。〔文公九年〕
translation_en:
…for those who fail to attend the royal court, there are formal proclamations of admonition; yet why do they still lag behind? This is to submit to the distant but not to the near, to submit to the former kings but not to the present ruler. Can they be called duly overawed [?]? “The ordered garrisons” and “presumptuously failing to appear” [?]—it is on this account that I have arrayed my troops and come. I seek only to continue Tang’s legacy; how could I wish to toil with armies in distant lands? Ah! Failing to display military force would be unmartial; failing to proclaim their crimes would leave the campaign without a legitimate cause. Gaozong’s army possessed both, and from this I know that his restoration of the dynasty had its foundations.

Even so, exhausting military strength in distant campaigns, wearying armies, and wasting resources are all things military strategists warn against. Yet in the expedition against Guifang, the army penetrated deep into its difficult terrain and conquered it only after three years. Did this not verge on violating those warnings? Why, then, did it ultimately prevail? Mencius once said: “From Tang to Wuding, six or seven worthy and sagely rulers arose.” The people’s allegiance to Shang was longstanding, while Chu alone took the lead in rebelling against it. This was why Gaozong had no choice but to raise an army. Thus, although it penetrated deeply, it did not exhaust its strength; although the campaign lasted three years, it did not become worn out. In the end, its cause remained just and its strength vigorous. Otherwise, there would have been scarcely anything to distinguish it from the armies of the First Emperor of Qin and Emperor Wu of Han.

Spring and Autumn Annals

In autumn, Jing attacked Zheng. The duke joined men of Qi and Song to rescue Zheng. (Twenty-eighth year of Duke Zhuang; the date is split in the transcription.)

Men of Chu attacked Zheng. Prince Sui joined men of Jin, Song, Wei, and Xu to rescue Zheng. (Ninth year of Duke Wen.)

When outside forces first ravaged a state divided in its allegiance, the hegemonic lord acted diligently to relieve its distress. When outside forces subsequently ravaged that state, the minister responsible for relief [?] acted negligently in relieving its distress. Such diligence and negligence in the conduct of hegemonic affairs bear upon the rise and decline of the non-Chinese peoples and the Chinese states. There is good reason why the Spring and Autumn Annals gives particular attention to recording the attacks on Zheng by Jing-Chu and the relief of Zheng by Qi and Jin!

In the closing years of our Duke Zhuang’s reign, the beneficent influence of the royal house was already exhausted, and Chu’s power was gradually growing stronger. Although Duke Huan of Qi had begun to exercise hegemony and aspired to lead the regional lords, Chu did not yet fear him. Chu then brought its might to bear, prompted by Ziyuan’s shame at a woman’s seeking vengeance [?], and sent troops to attack Zheng. Why did it do this? It merely relied on its strength to intimidate the Central States. Was this not an army that brutalized the weak?

Duke Huan had constantly been concerned about this. He immediately joined with the two states of Lu and Song to relieve Zheng. Although the commanders were of low rank and the forces small, and he did not go in person, he could not rest at ease once intelligence of the attack first reached him. The call to righteous action swiftly spread, and the troops did not shrink from a rapid march. In the end, Chu’s army, fearing their might, fled by night, and the people of Zheng were thus spared flight to Tongqiu. Ah! Huan…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
用也仁者物無不愛雖可以徵其爲用之
廣而直謂之仁則是不究夫體用之辯惻
隱之心仁也是非之心智也仁者心有知
覺雖可以見其包智之用而直謂之仁則
是不審夫仁智之殊獨尹焞所謂公者庶
幾近之然公所以體仁不可以言仁善乎
程子之言曰仁者必愛指愛爲仁則不可
不仁者無所知覺指知覺爲仁則不可又
曰公只是仁之理不可將公便喚做仁蓋
===
有以斷乎此矣愚故曰學有正傳而失焉
者說之者之好爲異也朱子集諸儒之大
成闡四德之名義其於仁曰心之德愛之
理蓋孔子所未發也然仁者天地生物之
心而人得之以爲心方其未發四德具焉
曰仁義禮智而仁無不統及其已發四端
著焉曰惻隱羞惡辭遜是非而惻隱之心
無不通則其指以爲心之德而義禮智不
得竝焉宜矣仁以言乎其理渾然在中而
punctuated:
用也。仁者物無不愛，雖可以徵其爲用之廣，而直謂之仁，則是不究夫體用之辯。惻隱之心，仁也；是非之心，智也。仁者心有知覺，雖可以見其包智之用，而直謂之仁，則是不審夫仁智之殊。獨尹焞所謂公者，庶幾近之。然公所以體仁，不可以言仁。善乎程子之言曰：「仁者必愛，指愛爲仁則不可；不仁者無所知覺，指知覺爲仁則不可。」又曰：「公只是仁之理，不可將公便喚做仁。」蓋有以斷乎此矣。
愚故曰：「學有正傳，而失焉者，說之者之好爲異也。」朱子集諸儒之大成，闡四德之名義，其於仁曰：「心之德，愛之理。」蓋孔子所未發也。然仁者，天地生物之心，而人得之以爲心。方其未發，四德具焉，曰仁義禮智，而仁無不統；及其已發，四端著焉，曰惻隱、羞惡、辭遜、是非，而惻隱之心無不通。則其指以爲心之德，而義禮智不得竝焉，宜矣。仁以言乎其理，渾然在中而
translation_en:
…is its functioning. The benevolent person loves all things without exception. Although this can demonstrate the breadth of benevolence’s functioning, to identify it directly as benevolence is to fail to investigate the distinction between substance and function. The heart of compassion is benevolence; the heart that distinguishes right from wrong is wisdom. The benevolent person’s heart possesses awareness. Although this shows that benevolence’s functioning encompasses wisdom, to identify awareness directly as benevolence is to fail to examine the difference between benevolence and wisdom. Only what Yin Tun calls impartiality comes close. Yet impartiality is the means by which one embodies benevolence; it cannot itself be called benevolence. How well Master Cheng put it: “The benevolent person necessarily loves, but one cannot identify love as benevolence. A person without benevolence lacks awareness, but one cannot identify awareness as benevolence.” He also said: “Impartiality is only the principle of benevolence; one cannot simply call impartiality benevolence.” These statements surely provide grounds for settling the matter.
Thus I, in my humble opinion, say: “Learning has an orthodox transmission; departures from it arise from interpreters’ fondness for novel views.” Master Zhu brought together the achievements of the Confucian scholars and elucidated the names and meanings of the four virtues. Of benevolence he said: “The virtue of the heart and the principle of love.” This was something Confucius had not made explicit. Benevolence is the heart through which Heaven and Earth give life to things, and human beings receive it as their own heart. Before it is aroused, the four virtues are fully present—benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom—and benevolence encompasses them all. Once it is aroused, the four beginnings become manifest—compassion, shame and aversion, deference and yielding, and the discernment of right and wrong—and the heart of compassion pervades them all. It is therefore fitting that he identifies benevolence as the virtue of the heart, with which righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom cannot stand on an equal footing. Benevolence, considered in terms of its principle, exists within as an undivided whole, and…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
所謂愛者出焉而不窮愛以言乎其事充
然各足而所謂仁者資之而無盡則其指
以爲愛之理對夫義之宜禮之敬智之知
而言之宜矣是不可見朱子精義之極而
道之定論在是乎夫何學之者之不知求
以爲朱子之言未然也而思以易之於是
復取昔人之論仁者或進而托於程子一
體之説以爲仁之惻怛慈愛必如是乃可
以名也或近而守夫謝氏知覺之説以爲
===
仁之周流貫徹必如是乃可以名也殊不
知愛之在人其理雖一而其分則殊專主
夫愛則於所謂分之殊者有未明而將淪
於兼愛之失心之在人其覺雖同而理慾
則異專主夫覺則於所謂理與慾者有不
察而將昧夫精一之宗善乎朱子之言曰
泛言同體者使人含胡昏緩而無警切之
功其弊或至認物爲己者有之專言知覺
者使人張皇躁迫而無沉潛之味其弊或
punctuated: 所謂愛者出焉而不窮。愛以言乎其事，充然各足，而所謂仁者資之而無盡，則其指以爲愛之理，對夫義之宜、禮之敬、智之知而言之，宜矣。是不可見朱子精義之極，而道之定論在是乎？夫何學之者之不知求，以爲朱子之言未然也，而思以易之？於是復取昔人之論仁者，或進而托於程子一體之説，以爲仁之惻怛慈愛，必如是乃可以名也；或近而守夫謝氏知覺之説，以爲仁之周流貫徹，必如是乃可以名也。殊不知愛之在人，其理雖一，而其分則殊。專主夫愛，則於所謂分之殊者有未明，而將淪於兼愛之失。心之在人，其覺雖同，而理慾則異。專主夫覺，則於所謂理與慾者有不察，而將昧夫精一之宗。善乎朱子之言曰：「泛言同體者，使人含胡昏緩，而無警切之功，其弊或至認物爲己者有之；專言知覺者，使人張皇躁迫，而無沉潛之味，其弊或
translation_en:
…what is called love issues from it without exhaustion. When love is considered in terms of its actual manifestations, each is abundantly sufficient, and what is called benevolence supplies it without end. Thus it is fitting to designate benevolence as the principle of love, speaking of it alongside the appropriateness of righteousness, the reverence of ritual propriety, and the discernment of wisdom. Does this not show the utmost refinement of Master Zhu’s exposition of meaning, and that here lies the definitive account of the Way? Why, then, do those who study fail to seek understanding, deem Master Zhu’s words incorrect, and think to replace them? They consequently return to earlier discussions of benevolence. Some advance a claim based on Master Cheng’s teaching of forming one body, holding that only in this way can benevolence’s compassion and loving kindness be properly named. Others take their stand on Master Xie’s teaching of awareness, holding that only in this way can benevolence’s all-pervading operation be properly named.

They utterly fail to understand that although love in human beings has a single principle, its particular obligations differ. If one makes love alone the governing consideration, one fails to understand these differences in obligation and will sink into the error of indiscriminate love. Although the mind’s awareness is common to all human beings, principle and desire are distinct. If one makes awareness alone the governing consideration, one fails to discriminate between principle and desire and will obscure the essential teaching of refinement and single-mindedness.

How well Master Zhu put it: “Those who speak vaguely of forming one body make people muddled, benighted, and lax, without the effort of vigilant self-examination; the resulting error may even lead some to take external things as their own selves. Those who speak exclusively of awareness make people agitated, restless, and impetuous, without any appreciation of deep, quiet reflection; the resulting error may…”

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
至認欲爲理者有之蓋已預憂乎此矣愚
故曰道有定論而晦焉者學之者之不知
求也然則執事爲今之計將若之何請戒
於衆曰爾欲求仁有孔子之正傳在焉愼
毋侮聖人守之可也爾欲言仁有朱子之
定論存焉愼毋小朱子信之可也如是而
日申飭之士固當畋其趨矣由是而又申
飭之則士眞積之久將自有以識夫仁體
而所謂定論者不至於晦體驗之深將自
不能已於求仁而所謂正傳者不至於亡
交養而互發執事之憂庶幾其免夫狂瞽
之言未知是否惟進教之幸甚
===
第三問
同考試官教諭胡　批〔教答詳明吾學之識　可槩見矣〕
葉龍
同考試官教諭葉　批〔宗主之良論十足策備矣　景行先哲而愼厥藩屏者乎錄之〕
punctuated:
至認欲爲理者有之。」蓋已預憂乎此矣。愚故曰：「道有定論，而晦焉者，學之者之不知求也。」然則執事爲今之計，將若之何？請戒於衆曰：「爾欲求仁，有孔子之正傳在焉，愼毋侮聖人，守之可也；爾欲言仁，有朱子之定論存焉，愼毋小朱子，信之可也。」如是而日申飭之，士固當畋其趨矣。由是而又申飭之，則士眞積之久，將自有以識夫仁體，而所謂定論者不至於晦；體驗之深，將自不能已於求仁，而所謂正傳者不至於亡。交養而互發，執事之憂，庶幾其免夫！狂瞽之言，未知是否，惟進教之，幸甚。

第三問

同考試官教諭胡，批〔教答詳明，吾學之識，可槩見矣。〕

葉龍

同考試官教諭葉，批〔宗主之良論，十足策備矣。景行先哲而愼厥藩屏者乎？錄之。〕
translation_en:
…there are some who even come to mistake desire for principle.” He had evidently already foreseen this danger. Thus I venture to say: “There is a settled account of the Way; when it becomes obscured, this is because those who study it do not know how to seek it.” What, then, should you do under present circumstances? I ask that you admonish the assembled scholars as follows: “If you wish to seek humaneness, the orthodox transmission of Confucius is there for you. Take care not to slight the Sage; hold fast to it. If you wish to discuss humaneness, Master Zhu’s settled account remains available. Take care not to belittle Master Zhu; trust it.” If you reiterate these admonitions daily, the scholars should surely rectify their course [?]. If you then continue to admonish them, their prolonged accumulation of genuine effort will naturally enable them to recognize the substance of humaneness, and the settled account will not become obscured. As their personal understanding deepens, they will naturally be unable to cease seeking humaneness, and the orthodox transmission will not be lost. These will nourish and illuminate one another, and perhaps you may thereby be spared your concern! Whether these rash and unenlightened words are right, I do not know. I would be most grateful for your further instruction.

Third Question

Associate Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: 〔The answer [?] is detailed and clear; one can gain a general sense of the writer’s understanding of our learning.〕

Ye Long

Associate Examiner Ye, Instructor, comments: 〔An excellent discussion of what should serve as the guiding authority [?]; the policy essay is fully developed. Does he not emulate the former worthies and give careful attention to the realm’s protective bulwarks? Accept it.〕

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭葉　批〔該博之學精確之見無踰〕
〔子者宜置前列〕
考試官教授伍　批〔考事尚賢可以風矣〕
論封建於三代之下師其意而已矣求人
才於封建之外取其志而已矣封建其起
於理乎緣於情乎成於勢乎理與賢者共
而不及惡德情先乎九族而後萬邦勢則
宜於古而尼於今吾見封建之難復也雖
然後世之封建已與古意異矣後世之封
===
建之科目又與封建之意異矣封建之科
目之不究其用又與科目之意異矣勢不
同而理同吾求同理而已遑恤乎其他是
故不車服而榮不爵賞而勸隨其所遭而
吾無與焉豈不誠志士哉南宋之諸趙是
已於戲彼皆江右之產而科目之良也孰
事舉以爲問豈欲求才於封建之外而論
治於三代之上乎愚獨以爲非封建意也
是故知勢者則不必襲古以爲瀆知情者
punctuated:
考試官教諭葉，批〔該博之學，精確之見，無踰〕〔子者，宜置前列。〕
考試官教授伍，批〔考事尚賢，可以風矣。〕
論封建於三代之下，師其意而已矣；求人材於封建之外，取其志而已矣。封建，其起於理乎？緣於情乎？成於勢乎？理與賢者共，而不及惡德；情先乎九族，而後萬邦；勢則宜於古，而尼於今。吾見封建之難復也。雖然，後世之封建已與古意異矣；後世之封建之科目，又與封建之意異矣；封建之科目之不究其用，又與科目之意異矣。勢不同而理同，吾求同理而已，遑恤乎其他？是故不車服而榮，不爵賞而勸，隨其所遭，而吾無與焉，豈不誠志士哉？南宋之諸趙是已。於戲！彼皆江右之產，而科目之良也。孰事舉以爲問，豈欲求才於封建之外，而論治於三代之上乎？愚獨以爲非封建意也。是故知勢者，則不必襲古以爲瀆；知情者
translation_en:
Examiner Ye, Instructor, comments: 〔For breadth of learning and precision of insight, none surpass〕〔you. You should be placed among the foremost.〕
Examiner Wu, Professor, comments: 〔He examines historical affairs and honors the worthy; this can serve as an example.〕
To discuss enfeoffment in the ages after the Three Dynasties is simply to take its intent as a guide; to seek talented men outside the system of enfeoffment is simply to value their aspirations. Did enfeoffment originate in principle, arise from human affections, or take shape through circumstances? In principle, rule was shared with the worthy, excluding those of evil character. In affection, the nine degrees of kinship came first, followed by the myriad states. As for circumstances, these favored it in antiquity but obstruct it today. I see how difficult it would be to restore enfeoffment. Nevertheless, enfeoffment in later ages already differed from its ancient intent. The examination system associated with enfeoffment in later ages [?] differed in turn from the intent of enfeoffment; and the failure to realize the practical purpose of this examination system under enfeoffment [?] differed yet again from the intent of the examinations themselves. Circumstances differ, but principle remains the same. I seek only that common principle: what leisure have I to concern myself with anything else?
Thus, men who feel honored without ceremonial carriages and robes, and are encouraged without ranks and rewards, accept whatever circumstances they encounter without seeking to intervene on their own behalf. Are they not truly men of high resolve? Such were the various members of the Zhao clan under the Southern Song. Ah! They were all natives of Jiangyou and outstanding men of the examination system. In raising these matters as a question [?], do you wish to seek talent outside enfeoffment and discuss government before the Three Dynasties? In my humble view alone, this is not the intent of enfeoffment. Thus, those who understand circumstances need not imitate antiquity to the point of debasing it; those who understand human affections …

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
則不必易今以爲治知理者則不必違天
以病民合是三者神而明之無封建無郡
縣而同歸於治無世官無科目而同歸於
才亦何庸心其間必爲此而不爲彼哉且
秦取天下而郡縣之而守令不以賢聞漢
更郡國而分置之而諸侯王數至僭叛人
才之不係於封建與否也明矣唐猶漢也
而隴西未嘗無賢士宋猶唐也而南渡未
嘗無善人人才之不係於世官與否也亦
===
明矣姑以江右論之昌邑肇封於漢世遠
而莫究元嬰胙土于唐枝散而日微可考
者其惟南宋之宗室乎時則有若善應之
刺血和藥崇憲之表明父心事雖不同而
同爲孝良淳之死守孤城時倚之以身殉
主地雖不同而同爲忠人稱趙母則有彥
端力變士風則有與清其政事何如也師
晦菴而究心理學則有汝靚請漕舉而苦
志詩賦則有希晉其文學何如也至若必
punctuated:
則不必易今以爲治；知理者，則不必違天以病民。合是三者，神而明之，無封建，無郡縣，而同歸於治；無世官，無科目，而同歸於才。亦何庸心其間，必爲此而不爲彼哉？且秦取天下而郡縣之，而守令不以賢聞；漢更郡國而分置之，而諸侯王數至僭叛。人才之不係於封建與否也，明矣。唐猶漢也，而隴西未嘗無賢士；宋猶唐也，而南渡未嘗無善人。人才之不係於世官與否也，亦明矣。
姑以江右論之：昌邑肇封於漢，世遠而莫究；元嬰胙土于唐，枝散而日微。可考者，其惟南宋之宗室乎？時則有若善應之刺血和藥，崇憲之表明父心，事雖不同，而同爲孝；良淳之死守孤城，時倚之以身殉主，地雖不同，而同爲忠。人稱趙母，則有彥端；力變士風，則有與清。其政事何如也？師晦菴而究心理學，則有汝靚；請漕舉而苦志詩賦，則有希晉。其文學何如也？至若必
translation_en:
…then one need not change present institutions to achieve good government; those who understand principle need not defy Heaven and cause suffering to the people. Bring these three considerations together and comprehend their subtleties: whether through enfeoffment or through commanderies and counties, both can lead to good government; whether through hereditary office or through examinations, both can yield talented men. Why, then, trouble oneself over the distinction, insisting on adopting one and rejecting the other? Qin conquered the realm and organized it into commanderies and counties, yet its governors and magistrates were not renowned for worthiness. Han reorganized commanderies and kingdoms and established them separately, yet its feudatory kings repeatedly resorted to usurpation and rebellion. Clearly, the emergence of talented men does not depend upon whether enfeoffment is practiced. Tang was like Han, yet Longxi never lacked worthy scholars; Song was like Tang, yet after the court crossed south it never lacked good men. It is likewise clear that the emergence of talented men does not depend upon whether offices are hereditary.
Let us discuss Jiangyou alone. The Prince of Changyi first received his fief under Han, but that age is too remote for thorough investigation. Yuanying received territory under Tang, but his descendants dispersed and gradually declined. Are not the Southern Song imperial clansmen the only ones whose deeds can be examined? Among them were Zhao Shanying, who drew his own blood to mix with medicine, and Zhao Chongxian, who made his father's intentions clear. Their deeds differed, but both were filial. Zhao Liangchun defended an isolated city to the death, while Zhao Shiyi gave his life for his lord. Their circumstances differed, but both were loyal. There was Zhao Yanduan, whom people called “Mother Zhao,” and Zhao Yuqing, who worked vigorously to transform the ethos of scholars. What does this tell us of their achievements in government? There was Zhao Rujing, who took Hui'an as his teacher and devoted himself to the study of principle, and Zhao Xijin, who sought examination nomination through the Transport Commission and applied himself strenuously to poetry and rhapsodies. What does this tell us of their literary learning? As for Bi…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
願早聞忠義之訓善堅勵志廉能之節可
以語行誼矣不黜退居錦水而以樂善名
汝偵甘守布衣而以固窮著可以語清脩
矣之數人者或起於科目或老于山林而
其立身行事之節有如此而吾所尊仰之
者則惟丞相汝愚而已好善忘勢有仕優
則學之風正色立朝有國爾忘家之節其
期待也則以司馬光富弼韓琦范仲淹爲
已任其淵源也則以朱熹張栻呂祖謙王
===
十朋汪應辰爲師友忠結人主而有文武
威風之稱行孚于朝而有忠孝大節之薦
是蓋不徒誓志於功名而實任道之器也
豈直一鄉之望而已哉使寧宗而竟其用
則其施爲氣象將必有可觀者而中興之
功易與也夫以韓侂冑爲之搆讒京鏜爲
之傅議李沐爲之疏詆正謂市虎三人能
保其不爲來之行乎雖然吾惜其辭相之
不力也宗室不爲宰執高宗之訓也而爲
punctuated: 願早聞忠義之訓，善堅勵志廉能之節，可以語行誼矣。不黜退居錦水而以樂善名，汝偵甘守布衣而以固窮著，可以語清脩矣。之數人者，或起於科目，或老于山林，而其立身行事之節有如此。而吾所尊仰之者，則惟丞相汝愚而已。好善忘勢，有仕優則學之風；正色立朝，有國爾忘家之節。其期待也，則以司馬光、富弼、韓琦、范仲淹爲已任；其淵源也，則以朱熹、張栻、呂祖謙、王十朋、汪應辰爲師友。忠結人主，而有文武威風之稱；行孚于朝，而有忠孝大節之薦。是蓋不徒誓志於功名，而實任道之器也。豈直一鄉之望而已哉！使寧宗而竟其用，則其施爲氣象將必有可觀者，而中興之功易與也夫！以韓侂冑爲之搆讒，京鏜爲之傅議，李沐爲之疏詆，正謂市虎三人，能保其不爲來之行乎？雖然，吾惜其辭相之不力也。宗室不爲宰執，高宗之訓也，而爲
translation_en: …[Bi]yuan received instruction in loyalty and righteousness early in life, while Shanjian set his resolve on integrity and competence: these men merit discussion for their virtuous conduct. Buchu retired to Jinshui and became known for delighting in goodness; Ruzhen willingly remained a commoner and became renowned for holding firm in poverty: these men merit discussion for their purity of character. These several men either rose through the examinations or grew old in rural retirement, yet such were the principles by which they established themselves and conducted their affairs. The one whom I most revere, however, is Chief Councilor Ruyu alone. Loving goodness and disregarding his own power, he exemplified the principle that an official with energy to spare should study. Maintaining a stern countenance at court, he displayed the integrity of one who forgets his family in devotion to the state. In his aspirations, he took it upon himself to emulate Sima Guang, Fu Bi, Han Qi, and Fan Zhongyan; in his intellectual lineage, he had Zhu Xi, Zhang Shi, Lü Zuqian, Wang Shipeng, and Wang Yingchen as teachers and friends. His loyalty bound him to his sovereign, earning him praise for his commanding presence in both civil and military affairs; his conduct inspired trust at court, earning him recommendations for his outstanding loyalty and filial devotion. Surely he was not merely someone resolved to achieve merit and fame, but a man truly capable of bearing responsibility for the Way. How could he have been merely the pride of a single locality! Had Ningzong employed him to the full, his accomplishments and the character of his administration would surely have been worthy of admiration, and the achievement of dynastic restoration would have been readily attainable! But Han Tuozhou fabricated slanders against him, Jing Tang lent support to the accusations, and Li Mu submitted memorials vilifying him. This was precisely the proverbial case of three men reporting a tiger in the marketplace: could anyone guarantee that he would not be driven away [?]? Nevertheless, I regret that he did not strive harder to decline the chief councillorship. That members of the imperial clan should not serve as chief councilors or executive officials was Gaozong’s injunction; yet …

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
眛此乎然趙氏者又豈特一時之盛而已
哉使宋室而世其官則其夾輔忠貞又將
有可觀者而世臣之功可收也夫以崇憲
爲之子必愿爲之孫良淳爲之曾孫可謂
四世名德而獨無有知之者乎雖然吾惜
其逢時之不偶也人衆則能勝天往事之
監也而又何論乎方是時也晦菴十里命
駕註騷以洩不平蓋不待良淳之身而已
決矣君子以是知忠賢之進退而百年之
===
氣運係之一門之盛衰而終宋之命脉係
之彼小人者所自爲謀則巧矣而其流至
于禍人家國而不悟亦獨何哉蓋嘗即宋
事而論之宋之立國也始於公天下而成
於私其身故其初也兄弟之太恩而其後
也子姓之不保其仁也篤於養士而其澆
世畧於懿親羣臣任子九族不免乎編氓
罷政乞祠諸宗顧以之應舉倣之以先王
親睦之風誠無以塈其後求諸大易通變
punctuated:
眛此乎？然趙氏者，又豈特一時之盛而已哉？使宋室而世其官，則其夾輔忠貞又將有可觀者，而世臣之功可收也。夫以崇憲爲之子，必愿爲之孫，良淳爲之曾孫，可謂四世名德，而獨無有知之者乎？雖然，吾惜其逢時之不偶也。人衆則能勝天，往事之監也，而又何論乎？方是時也，晦菴十里命駕，註騷以洩不平，蓋不待良淳之身而已決矣。君子以是知忠賢之進退，而百年之氣運係之；一門之盛衰，而終宋之命脉係之。彼小人者，所自爲謀則巧矣，而其流至于禍人家國而不悟，亦獨何哉？

蓋嘗即宋事而論之：宋之立國也，始於公天下而成於私其身，故其初也兄弟之太恩，而其後也子姓之不保。其仁也篤於養士，而其澆世畧於懿親。羣臣任子，九族不免乎編氓；罷政乞祠，諸宗顧以之應舉。倣之以先王親睦之風，誠無以塈其後。求諸大易通變
translation_en:
…be blind to this? Yet was the Zhao family's distinction confined to a single age? Had the Song house allowed its offices to pass down through this family, their loyal and steadfast assistance to the throne would again have been worthy of admiration, and the dynasty could have reaped the benefits of service across generations. With Chongxian as his son, Biyuan as his grandson, and Liangchun as his great-grandson, this was indeed a family renowned for virtue through four generations. Was there really no one who recognized this? Nevertheless, I lament that the times they encountered were so adverse. When people are numerous enough, they can overcome Heaven: past events provide this warning. What more is there to say? At that time, Hui'an ordered his carriage for a journey of ten li and annotated the Encountering Sorrow to vent his indignation. The outcome had surely already been decided, without waiting until Liangchun's own lifetime. From this, the gentleman understands that a century's fortunes depended upon the advancement or dismissal of loyal and worthy men, and that the lifeblood of the Song, down to its end, depended upon the flourishing or decline of a single family. Those petty men were clever enough in plotting for themselves; yet the consequences brought disaster upon others' families and the state, and they remained unaware. Why was this so?

I have considered this in light of Song history. The founding of the Song began with treating the realm as a public trust, but was completed through private concern for oneself. Thus, at its beginning there was excessive favor between brothers, while afterward their descendants could not be protected. Its benevolence was generous in nurturing scholars, but in its declining age it neglected close imperial kin. Officials secured appointments for their sons through privilege, while the imperial clan's nine degrees of kinship could not escape being registered as commoners. Men who left governmental office requested temple sinecures, yet members of the imperial clan instead used these to enter the examinations [?]. Measured against the former kings' practice of maintaining affection and harmony among kin, this truly provided no means of bringing repose to their descendants. If one looks to the Great Book of Changes for the way of adapting to change…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
之道彼固以爲得之矣然而豪傑之才固
無恃乎門第神明之胄終弗類乎寒微卒
能以其忠孝之姿而赴功名之會入而爲
良相出而爲賢牧生而爲善士死而爲忠
臣炳炳乎起而爲中原文獻之傳此豈爵
祿名寵之所能勸而封建科目之所能限
者哉愚以是知有志之士無所待而猶興
者雖以宋之宗室猶能自飭其身自淑其
政以爲國家之重則凡爲今日之
===
藩國者
祖宗之富貴若此
朝廷之親愛若此又將何以爲報哉然非欲
其舉成法而棄之讀書業科舉効儒生輩
爲也亦曰
祖訓者
皇祖之家灋也守之以不越則自有餘貴矣境
內者
夫子之子民也居之以不擾則自有餘富矣故
punctuated: 之道，彼固以爲得之矣。然而豪傑之才，固無恃乎門第；神明之胄，終弗類乎寒微。卒能以其忠孝之姿，而赴功名之會，入而爲良相，出而爲賢牧，生而爲善士，死而爲忠臣，炳炳乎起而爲中原文獻之傳。此豈爵祿名寵之所能勸，而封建科目之所能限者哉？愚以是知有志之士，無所待而猶興者。雖以宋之宗室，猶能自飭其身，自淑其政，以爲國家之重，則凡爲今日之藩國者，祖宗之富貴若此，朝廷之親愛若此，又將何以爲報哉？然非欲其舉成法而棄之，讀書業科舉，効儒生輩爲也。亦曰：祖訓者，皇祖之家灋也，守之以不越，則自有餘貴矣；境內者，夫子之子民也，居之以不擾，則自有餘富矣。故
translation_en:
…the Way: they certainly believed they had grasped it. Yet outstanding talent assuredly does not depend upon family standing, and the descendants of divinely enlightened rulers are, after all, unlike those of humble origins. In the end, through their loyalty and filial devotion, they could seize opportunities for achievement and renown: serving at court as worthy chief councillors, serving in the provinces as able governors, living as good men, and dying as loyal ministers. They rose resplendently to carry forward the cultural heritage of the Central Plain. Could such men be spurred on merely by rank, emoluments, fame, and favour, or be confined by the institutions of enfeoffment and examination selection?

From this I understand that men of resolve rise to action even without awaiting external encouragement. Even members of the Song imperial clan could discipline their conduct and improve their administration, becoming pillars of the state. Then how should all those who hold princely domains today repay the wealth and honour bestowed by their ancestors and the affection shown them by the court? Yet I do not mean that they should cast aside established laws, study books, make the examinations their occupation, and imitate the practices of Confucian scholars. I mean only this: the Ancestral Instructions are the imperial ancestor’s household laws. Observe them without transgression, and honour will naturally be yours in abundance. Those within your territory are the people under the Master’s paternal care [?]. Dwell among them without disturbing them, and wealth will naturally be yours in abundance. Therefore…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
曰居上不驕高而不危所以長守貴也制
節謹度滿而不溢所以長守富也此謂無
所事事而有利於國與民夫無所事事之
利與有所事事而未必利者其勞逸難易
奚啻十百千萬莫之禁而弗爲豈不大有
負於時乎於戲此義行則不惟爵封茲土
者之知所以勸而凡天下之爲王國者靡
不竭忠夾輔以綿我
國家無疆之休矣故曰師其意也以此
===
第四問　　　江鯤
同考試官教諭李　批　〔五策條答無遺而皆有天下之慮此篇抜其尤者〕
同考試官教諭林　批　〔談錢幣有通變之術可謂識時務者〕
考試官教諭葉　批　〔考古而不遺酌今而不泥有用之才也〕
考試官教授伍　批　〔知今言國用其有禆□〕
punctuated:
曰：「居上不驕，高而不危，所以長守貴也；制節謹度，滿而不溢，所以長守富也。」此謂無所事事而有利於國與民。夫無所事事之利，與有所事事而未必利者，其勞逸難易，奚啻十百千萬！莫之禁而弗爲，豈不大有負於時乎？於戲！此義行，則不惟爵封茲土者之知所以勸，而凡天下之爲王國者，靡不竭忠夾輔，以綿我國家無疆之休矣。故曰師其意也，以此。

第四問，江鯤。
同考試官教諭李批：〔五策條答無遺而皆有天下之慮此篇抜其尤者〕
同考試官教諭林批：〔談錢幣有通變之術可謂識時務者〕
考試官教諭葉批：〔考古而不遺酌今而不泥有用之才也〕
考試官教授伍批：〔知今言國用其有禆□〕
translation_en:
…it is said: “To occupy a superior position without arrogance, to stand high without peril: this is how one preserves noble rank for long. To restrain expenditure and carefully observe limits, to be full without overflowing: this is how one preserves wealth for long.” This is what is meant by undertaking no particular business yet benefiting the state and the people. As for the benefit of undertaking no particular business, compared with undertaking business that may not prove beneficial, the difference in toil and ease, difficulty and simplicity, is surely more than tenfold, a hundredfold, a thousandfold, or ten thousandfold! If nothing forbids this course, yet one fails to follow it, does one not gravely fail the needs of the times? Alas! If this principle is put into practice, not only will those enfeoffed in this territory know what should spur them on, but all who hold princely domains throughout the realm will exert their utmost loyalty in support of the throne, perpetuating the boundless blessings of our dynasty. This is why I say that one should take its underlying intention as one’s model.

Fourth Policy Question. Jiang Kun 江鯤.

Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “His five policy essays answer every point without omission, and all show concern for the realm. This essay has been selected as the most outstanding.”

Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: “In discussing currency, he offers methods for adapting to changing circumstances. He may be called someone who understands the needs of the times.”

Examiner Ye, Instructor, comments: “He investigates antiquity without omissions and weighs present circumstances without rigidity. He is a man of practical ability.”

Examiner Wu, Professor, comments: “He understands the present and discusses state expenditure; his contribution should prove beneficial [?].”

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
人君欲制用以足國則不可不通變以裕
民蓋天之立君本以治民而君之足國亦
惟以利民耳以利民爲心則用之詘也不
可不善其道以處之遷之弊也不可不通
其變以宜之民宜則百姓足君孰與不足
君足則百度舉天下又焉有不治哉愚讀
明問及此作而嘆曰是欲修政非爲理財
也欲裕民非爲足國也敢不掇拾以對粤
昔民之有生易於困也天必生財以資之
===
財之爲用易於乏也君必立法以理之是
故稻黍稷麥菽之五穀珠玉金刀布之三
幣非財之生於天者乎錢以濟穀幣之不
通鈔以補錢幣之不足非法之立於君者
乎蓋五穀可以取用而不可以致遠三幣
可以致遠而不可以常得則其勢不得不
趨於錢鈔矣夫三品之金銅爲下以之鑄
錢爲最宜是物也在陶唐氏謂之泉商人
謂之布齊人莒人謂之刀周人槩謂之帛
punctuated: 人君欲制用以足國，則不可不通變以裕民。蓋天之立君，本以治民，而君之足國，亦惟以利民耳。以利民爲心，則用之詘也，不可不善其道以處之；遷之弊也，不可不通其變以宜之。民宜則百姓足，君孰與不足？君足則百度舉，天下又焉有不治哉？愚讀明問及此，作而嘆曰：「是欲修政，非爲理財也；欲裕民，非爲足國也。」敢不掇拾以對？粤昔民之有生，易於困也，天必生財以資之；財之爲用，易於乏也，君必立法以理之。是故稻黍稷麥菽之五穀，珠玉金刀布之三幣，非財之生於天者乎？錢以濟穀幣之不通，鈔以補錢幣之不足，非法之立於君者乎？蓋五穀可以取用，而不可以致遠；三幣可以致遠，而不可以常得，則其勢不得不趨於錢鈔矣。夫三品之金，銅爲下，以之鑄錢爲最宜。是物也，在陶唐氏謂之泉，商人謂之布，齊人莒人謂之刀，周人槩謂之帛。
translation_en:
If a ruler wishes to regulate expenditure so as to provide adequately for the state, he must adapt to changing circumstances so as to enrich the people. Heaven established rulers fundamentally to govern the people, and a ruler’s provision for the state likewise serves only to benefit the people. With their benefit at heart, when resources fall short of expenditure, he must find sound means of addressing the shortage; when changes produce abuses [?], he must adapt his measures to make them appropriate. When conditions suit the people, the common people have enough; and when they have enough, how could the ruler alone lack enough? When the ruler has enough, all the affairs of government can be carried out. How, then, could the realm fail to be well governed? Upon reaching this point in your illuminating question, I rose and exclaimed: “This seeks to improve government, rather than merely manage wealth; to enrich the people, rather than merely provide for the state.” How could I fail to gather what observations I can in reply?

From earliest times, people have been readily beset by hardship in sustaining their lives, so Heaven necessarily produces wealth to support them. Wealth is readily exhausted through use, so rulers necessarily establish regulations to administer it. Thus, are not the five grains—rice, glutinous millet, millet, wheat, and beans—and the three kinds of currency, comprising pearls, jade, metals, and knife and spade money, wealth produced by Heaven? Coins facilitate exchange where grain and other currencies do not circulate, while paper money supplements an insufficient supply of coins: are these not arrangements established by rulers? The five grains can be put to use, but cannot be conveyed over long distances; the three kinds of currency can be conveyed over long distances, but cannot always be obtained. Circumstances therefore inevitably lead to the use of coins and paper money.

Of the three grades of metal, copper ranks lowest, yet it is best suited to casting coins. This thing was called quan, “spring,” under the Taotang ruler; the people of Shang called it bu, “cloth” or “spade money”; the people of Qi and Ju called it dao, “knife”; and the people of Zhou called it, in general, bo, “silk” [?]…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
至景王鑄錢則謂之寶貨而錢始有文矣
後是或爲八銖四銖或爲開元通寶或爲
皇宋通寶及其弊也則有榆莢鵝眼二銖
四分而失之太輕又有赤仄半兩直百當
千而失之太重求其得中者其惟漢之五
銖唐之開元乎然孰若我
朝通寶爲最善夫百物之質楮爲輕以之制
鈔爲尤便是物也在漢謂之皮幣在唐謂
之飛錢在宋謂之便錢至蜀張守蜀則謂
===
之交子而始用楮矣後是或爲錢引或爲
交鈔或爲兌會或爲會子及其行也有一
界印一千百萬一界印三千萬萬而多寡
之不同有至元一貫準中統五貫有至大
一貫準至元五貫而貴賤之不同求其適
均者其惟宋之天聖元之中統乎然孰若
我
朝寶鈔爲最良夫錢之制旣善則通之天下
而可行而行聞于天下而無弊也鈔之制既良
punctuated: 至景王鑄錢，則謂之寶貨，而錢始有文矣。後是，或爲八銖、四銖，或爲開元通寶，或爲皇宋通寶。及其弊也，則有榆莢、鵝眼、二銖、四分，而失之太輕；又有赤仄、半兩、直百、當千，而失之太重。求其得中者，其惟漢之五銖、唐之開元乎？然孰若我朝通寶爲最善？夫百物之質，楮爲輕，以之制鈔爲尤便。是物也，在漢謂之皮幣，在唐謂之飛錢，在宋謂之便錢，至蜀張守蜀，則謂之交子，而始用楮矣。後是，或爲錢引，或爲交鈔，或爲兌會，或爲會子。及其行也，有一界印一千百萬，一界印三千萬萬，而多寡之不同；有至元一貫準中統五貫，有至大一貫準至元五貫，而貴賤之不同。求其適均者，其惟宋之天聖、元之中統乎？然孰若我朝寶鈔爲最良？夫錢之制旣善，則通之天下而可行，而行聞于天下而無弊也。鈔之制既良，
translation_en:
… When King Jing cast coins, they were called “precious currency,” and coins began to bear inscriptions. Thereafter there were eight-zhu and four-zhu coins, Kaiyuan tongbao, and Huang Song tongbao. When abuses arose, there were “elm-pod,” “goose-eye,” two-zhu, and four-fen coins, which erred in being too light; there were also “red-rim,” half-liang, “worth a hundred,” and “worth a thousand” coins, which erred in being too heavy. If we seek those that struck the proper balance, were they not the Han five-zhu and the Tang Kaiyuan coins? Yet how could any compare with our dynasty’s tongbao coins, the best of all?

Among the materials of the myriad things, paper is light, making it especially convenient for producing notes. This form of currency was called “leather currency” under the Han, “flying cash” under the Tang, and “convenient cash” under the Song. When Zhang governed Shu [?], it was called jiaozi, and paper first came into use. Thereafter there were qianyin, jiaochao, duihui, and huizi notes. In their issuance, one issue might comprise eleven million [?], another three hundred billion [?], so their quantities differed. One string in Zhiyuan notes was equivalent to five strings in Zhongtong notes, while one string in Zhida notes was equivalent to five strings in Zhiyuan notes, so their values differed. If we seek those that achieved a proper balance, were they not the notes of the Song Tiansheng and Yuan Zhongtong eras? Yet how could any compare with our dynasty’s precious notes, the finest of all?

Since the system of coinage is sound, the coins can circulate and be accepted throughout the realm, and their circulation is known throughout the realm [?] without abuses. Since the system of paper notes is sound, …

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
則推之後世而皆準而何分於草昧承平
然而猶有不能盡如立灋之始而多積於
無用者此無他不能通其變於未窮焉耳
且錢之稱爲泉布以其流通而無滯也鈔
而稱爲楮幣以其輕便均爲寶也今世之
用者惟銀幣是資自官府之催科以至民
間之貿易率惟是之售至於錢之用獨居
常小費而已錢安得不滯鈔之用特論功
議辟而已鈔安得可行錢鈔既輕則銀幣
===
益重銀重則用之者日不足而取之者盡
錙銖于是乎有輸粟之計有發礦之謀是
亦不得已而爲是權宜以紓
宵旰之憂以濟用度之急耳然輸粟若可也
而名器懼其或濫發礦若可也而採取未
免殃民二者誠非足國裕民之要道其惟
於錢鈔之用救其弊而使之不匱通其變
而使之宜民可矣何者錢不患其滯也立
灋以疏之則通鈔不患其輕也立灋以反
punctuated: 則推之後世而皆準，而何分於草昧承平？然而猶有不能盡如立灋之始，而多積於無用者，此無他，不能通其變於未窮焉耳。且錢之稱爲泉布，以其流通而無滯也；鈔而稱爲楮幣，以其輕便，均爲寶也。今世之用者，惟銀幣是資，自官府之催科，以至民間之貿易，率惟是之售。至於錢之用，獨居常小費而已，錢安得不滯？鈔之用，特論功議辟而已，鈔安得可行？錢鈔既輕，則銀幣益重；銀重，則用之者日不足，而取之者盡錙銖。于是乎有輸粟之計，有發礦之謀，是亦不得已而爲是權宜，以紓宵旰之憂，以濟用度之急耳。然輸粟若可也，而名器懼其或濫；發礦若可也，而採取未免殃民。二者誠非足國裕民之要道，其惟於錢鈔之用，救其弊而使之不匱，通其變而使之宜民可矣。何者？錢不患其滯也，立灋以疏之則通；鈔不患其輕也，立灋以反
translation_en:
…then it can be extended to later generations and serve as a standard for them all. What distinction need there be between an age of founding turmoil and one of settled peace? Yet currency still fails to function entirely as it did when the regulations were first established, and much accumulates unused. This is for no other reason than that adjustments have not been made before its functioning reaches an impasse. Coins are called quanbu because they circulate without obstruction; notes are called paper currency because they are light and convenient. Both are treasures. In present-day transactions, however, silver alone is relied upon. From the authorities’ collection of taxes to trade among the people, transactions are generally settled in silver alone. Coins are used only for small everyday expenses: how could their circulation fail to stagnate? Notes are used only in assessing rewards for merit and determining penalties: how could they circulate? Once coins and notes are depreciated, silver becomes still more valuable. As silver becomes more valuable, those who use it find it increasingly insufficient, while those who exact it demand every last fraction of an ounce.

Hence the proposals to accept grain contributions and to open mines. These, too, are merely expedients adopted out of necessity to relieve the anxieties that keep the emperor occupied before dawn and late into the night, and to meet urgent expenditure. Yet although accepting grain contributions may seem feasible, there is a danger of indiscriminately bestowing ranks and honors; although opening mines may seem feasible, extraction inevitably brings suffering upon the people. Neither is truly an essential means of enriching the state and bringing prosperity to the people. What is needed is simply to remedy the defects in the use of coins and notes so that their supply does not fail, and to adapt their operation to changing circumstances so that they serve the people’s needs. Why is this? There is no need to fear stagnation in the circulation of coins: establish regulations to clear the obstructions, and they will circulate. There is no need to fear the depreciation of notes: establish regulations to reverse…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
之則重蓋錢之鑄本以濟幣之窮鈔之制
又以濟錢之乏玆欲錢鈔之行必別其大
小之分權其子母之勢於錢則分古今以
今之一而當古之二濫惡者不得雜於其
間於鈔則分新舊以舊之二而當新之一
折壞者不得預以爲算二者又皆以銀爲
準銀一分而準錢十文鈔十張而準銀一
分由是立爲一定之則凡有行使大約以
三分爲率雖銀之多也不得專用銀銀二
===
而錢居其一雖錢之多也不得專用錢錢
二而鈔居其一上而科派徵收下而輸納
懋遷率守是遵而罔俾踰易至於鈔重則
出錢以易鈔錢重則出鈔以易錢又必嚴
銅楮之禁絶僞造之奸謹關市之令杜越
境之私將見出於官者有以資於民入於
民者可以用之官錢鈔尚何有不行哉或
謂銀銅竝行未免爲擾則古有之矣周禮
內府掌邦之大用外府掌邦之小用準此
punctuated: 之則重。蓋錢之鑄，本以濟幣之窮；鈔之制，又以濟錢之乏。玆欲錢鈔之行，必別其大小之分，權其子母之勢。於錢則分古今，以今之一而當古之二，濫惡者不得雜於其間；於鈔則分新舊，以舊之二而當新之一，折壞者不得預以爲算。二者又皆以銀爲準：銀一分而準錢十文，鈔十張而準銀一分。由是立爲一定之則，凡有行使，大約以三分爲率。雖銀之多也，不得專用銀，銀二而錢居其一；雖錢之多也，不得專用錢，錢二而鈔居其一。上而科派徵收，下而輸納懋遷，率守是遵，而罔俾踰易。至於鈔重，則出錢以易鈔；錢重，則出鈔以易錢。又必嚴銅楮之禁，絶僞造之奸；謹關市之令，杜越境之私。將見出於官者有以資於民，入於民者可以用之官，錢鈔尚何有不行哉？或謂銀銅竝行，未免爲擾，則古有之矣。《周禮》內府掌邦之大用，外府掌邦之小用。準此
translation_en: …and the notes will regain their value. Coins were originally cast to remedy a shortage of currency, and paper notes were instituted to remedy a shortage of coins. To secure the circulation of coins and notes now, we must distinguish their greater and lesser denominations and weigh the relationship between the principal and subsidiary currencies. For coins, distinguish old from current issues, counting one current coin as equivalent to two old ones; inferior coins must not be allowed among them. For notes, distinguish new from old, counting two old notes as equivalent to one new one; torn or damaged notes must not be included in the reckoning. Both should also be measured against silver: one fen of silver should equal ten cash, and ten paper notes should equal one fen of silver. Establish these as fixed standards. In all transactions, the general rule should be to reckon in three parts. Even where silver is plentiful, silver alone must not be used: two parts should be silver and one part coins. Even where coins are plentiful, coins alone must not be used: two parts should be coins and one part notes. Above, in official assessments and collections, and below, in payments and trade, everyone must observe these rules, without being allowed to depart from or alter them. When notes rise in value, release coins to exchange for notes; when coins rise in value, release notes to exchange for coins. Moreover, restrictions on copper and paper must be strictly enforced to eliminate counterfeiting, and regulations at customs barriers and markets must be carefully upheld to prevent illicit transfers across borders. We shall then see currency issued by the authorities serving the people’s needs, and currency received by the people usable in payments to the authorities. How could coins and notes still fail to circulate? Some may say that the concurrent circulation of silver and copper inevitably causes disruption. Yet there was a precedent for this in antiquity. In the Rites of Zhou, the Inner Treasury administered the state’s major expenditures, and the Outer Treasury administered its minor expenditures. Taking this as a standard…

translation_en: …then it is weighty [?]. The minting of copper cash was originally intended to remedy a shortage of currency, and the creation of paper notes likewise to remedy a shortage of cash. Now, to make cash and notes circulate, we must distinguish their greater and lesser denominations and balance their relative values as “mother” and “child.” Cash should be distinguished as ancient or modern, with one modern coin equivalent to two ancient coins; inferior coins must not be mixed among them. Notes should be distinguished as new or old, with two old notes equivalent to one new note; torn or damaged notes must not be included in the reckoning. Both should furthermore be measured against silver: one fen of silver should equal ten cash, and ten notes should equal one fen of silver. These should be established as fixed rules, with transactions generally apportioned into three shares. Even where silver is plentiful, silver alone must not be used: two shares should be silver and one cash. Even where cash is plentiful, cash alone must not be used: two shares should be cash and one paper notes. Above, in official assessments and collections, and below, in payments and commerce, all should observe this rule, without allowing departures or alterations. When notes rise in value, cash should be issued in exchange for notes; when cash rises in value, notes should be issued in exchange for cash. Prohibitions concerning copper cash and paper notes must also be strictly enforced to eliminate counterfeiting, and regulations at customs barriers and markets carefully upheld to prevent smuggling across the borders. We shall then see currency issued by the authorities providing resources for the people, and currency received by the people usable in payments to the authorities. How could cash and notes still fail to circulate? Some may say that the joint circulation of silver and copper inevitably causes disruption; yet there is ancient precedent for it. The Rites of Zhou states that the Inner Treasury managed the state's major expenditures and the Outer Treasury its minor expenditures. On this basis…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
以銀爲大用錢爲小用又何不可乎又謂
銅楮錯用日見其勞則古又有之矣單穆
公曰民患輕則爲母權子而行民患重則
爲子權母而行準此以錢爲母以鈔爲子
又何不可乎行之旣利習之而安則錢鈔
與銀幣相兼相濟相補相浅不出二三年
之間國可使富而民亦有餘大則
朝廷之祭祀征伐營繕錫予隨用皆充小則
閭閻之衣食用度致遠輕齎隨在各足所
===
謂制用裕民誠莫有要於此矣雖然此特
語其末耳又有其本在焉傳曰官之失職
寵賂章也抑孰知古人之制用其意固已
嚴乎夫錢之名曰流于泉以言清也清斯
惠流矣曰利于刀以言决也决斯利辯矣
曰布于布以言德也德斯令布矣曰束于
帛以言約也潔也約斯不濫潔斯不瀆矣
凡以爲用錢者言也鈔之名其制取諸券
義取諸交易上之交下而補助行焉否則
punctuated:
以銀爲大用，錢爲小用，又何不可乎？又謂銅楮錯用，日見其勞，則古又有之矣。單穆公曰：「民患輕，則爲母權子而行；民患重，則爲子權母而行。」準此，以錢爲母，以鈔爲子，又何不可乎？行之旣利，習之而安，則錢鈔與銀幣相兼相濟，相補相浅。不出二三年之間，國可使富，而民亦有餘。大則朝廷之祭祀、征伐、營繕、錫予，隨用皆充；小則閭閻之衣食用度、致遠輕齎，隨在各足。所謂制用裕民，誠莫有要於此矣。

雖然，此特語其末耳，又有其本在焉。傳曰：「官之失職，寵賂章也。」抑孰知古人之制用，其意固已嚴乎？夫錢之名，曰流于泉，以言清也，清斯惠流矣；曰利于刀，以言决也，决斯利辯矣；曰布于布，以言德也，德斯令布矣；曰束于帛，以言約也、潔也，約斯不濫，潔斯不瀆矣。凡以爲用錢者言也。鈔之名，其制取諸券，義取諸交易。上之交下，而補助行焉，否則
translation_en:
…to use silver for major expenditures and copper cash for minor ones—why should this not be permissible? Others say that using copper cash and paper money together makes the burden of handling them greater every day. Yet this, too, has ancient precedent. Duke Mu of Shan said: “When the people suffer from currency being too light, make the mother balance the child and circulate them; when the people suffer from currency being too heavy, make the child balance the mother and circulate them.” Following this principle, why should we not make copper cash the mother and paper money the child? Once their use proves beneficial and familiarity makes people comfortable with them, copper cash, paper money, and silver currency will work together, support one another, and supplement one another [?]. Within no more than two or three years, the state can be made wealthy and the people, too, will have a surplus. On the larger scale, the court’s sacrifices, military expeditions, construction and repairs, and grants and gifts will all be amply supplied as needs arise. On the smaller scale, households will have enough everywhere for clothing, food, and daily expenses, and for conveying value over long distances with light loads. As for what is called regulating expenditure and enriching the people, truly nothing is more essential than this.

Nevertheless, this speaks only of the secondary aspects; there is also a fundamental principle. The Commentary says: “Officials’ failure in their duties arises from the prevalence of favoritism and bribery.” Yet who recognizes how exacting the ancients’ intentions already were in regulating expenditure? Consider the names of money. It is said to flow like a spring, expressing purity: with purity, beneficence flows. It is said to be sharp like a knife, expressing decisiveness: with decisiveness, benefits are clearly distinguished [?]. It is said to spread like cloth, expressing virtue: with virtue, commands are disseminated. It is said to be bound like silk, expressing restraint and integrity: with restraint there is no excess, and with integrity there is no corruption. All these sayings are addressed to those who use money. As for paper money, its form derives from certificates, and its meaning derives from exchange. Through those above engaging with those below, assistance is provided; otherwise …

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
廢天下之交上而貢賦輸焉否則畔矣凡
以為用鈔者言也若私與公交遠臣與近
臣交正魯褒之所謂神者是謂不泉不刀
不布不帛固已失其制用之本而又益之
以非道之交其不傷財而害民也者幾希
此後世之財所以日見其告匱而理財又
難於昔之人無惑也故曰其本則在
朝廷而不在有司
第五問
===
江一川
考試官教諭葉批經畫備荒弭盜之畧咸
中時宜中一結尤有餘味有用之才也
考試官教授伍批敷答詳整是有見者
善為政者不恃無荒而恃吾有備荒之術
不恃無盜而恃吾有弭盜之方蓋有備無
患為政之大經也荒與盜之無固不足恃
而吾備荒之術弭盜之方豈可不豫為之
所乎誠能於豊登有餘之日恒為荒歉不

以爲用鈔者言也若私與公交遠臣與近
臣交正與邪之所謂神者是謂不泉不刀
不布不帛固已失其制用之本而又益之
以非道之交其不傷財而害民也者幾希
此後世之財所以日見其告匱而理財又
難於昔之人無惑也故曰其本則在
朝廷而不在有司
第五問
===
江一川
考試官教諭葉　批〔經書備荒弭盜之畧咸中時宜而一結尤有餘味有用之才也〕
考試官教授伍　批〔敷答詳整言之有見者〕
善爲政者不恃無荒而恃吾有備荒之術
不恃無盜而恃吾有弭盜之方蓋有備無
患爲政之大經也荒與盜之無固不足恃
而吾備荒之術弭盜之方豈可不豫爲之
所乎誠能於豐登有餘之日恒爲荒歉不
punctuated:
廢。天下之交上，而貢賦輸焉，否則畔矣。凡以為用鈔者言也。若私與公交，遠臣與近臣交，正魯褒之所謂神者，是謂不泉不刀、不布不帛，固已失其制用之本，而又益之以非道之交，其不傷財而害民也者幾希。此後世之財所以日見其告匱，而理財又難於昔之人，無惑也。故曰：其本則在朝廷，而不在有司。

第五問

江一川

考試官教諭葉批：經畫備荒弭盜之畧，咸中時宜，中一結尤有餘味，有用之才也。

考試官教授伍批：敷答詳整，是有見者。

善為政者，不恃無荒，而恃吾有備荒之術；不恃無盜，而恃吾有弭盜之方。蓋有備無患，為政之大經也。荒與盜之無，固不足恃，而吾備荒之術、弭盜之方，豈可不豫為之所乎？誠能於豊登有餘之日，恒為荒歉不
translation_en:
…ceases. When all under Heaven deal with those above, tribute and taxes are remitted; otherwise, there is rebellion. All this concerns those who use paper currency. But when private interests deal with public authorities, and officials distant from the ruler deal with his intimates, this is precisely what Lu Bao called a “god.” Such money is neither a flowing spring nor a knife, neither cloth nor silk: the fundamental purpose of its regulation and use has already been lost, and dealings contrary to the Way compound the harm. Rare indeed would it be for this not to damage resources and harm the people. This explains why resources in later ages are increasingly reported exhausted, and why managing them is harder than it was for people of old. There is nothing puzzling about this. Thus I say: the root of the matter lies with the imperial court, not with the responsible officials.

Fifth Question

Jiang Yichuan

Comment by Examiner Ye, an Instructor: “His plans for preparing against famine and suppressing banditry all suit the needs of the times. The concluding passage in the middle is especially rich in implications. Here is a man of useful talent.”

Comment by Examiner Wu, a Professor: “His answer is detailed and orderly. This is someone with insight.”

Those skilled in governing do not rely on the absence of famine, but on having methods of preparing against it; they do not rely on the absence of bandits, but on having means of suppressing them. To be prepared and thus free from calamity is a cardinal principle of government. We certainly cannot rely on the absence of famine and banditry; how, then, can we fail to make advance provision for our methods of preparing against famine and our means of suppressing banditry? If, in days of abundant harvests and surplus, we can constantly remain concerned about famine, poor harvests, and insufficiency…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
給之憂及太平無事之時每懷反側擾攘之
慮則荒與盜皆有其備斯善爲政矣請復
明問饑饉薦臻國家代有蓋天時之不常
地利人事之不及也顧吾所以備之何如
耳觀諸成周荒政十二以及遺人廩人所
掌則所以慮災防患也至矣盜賊竊發古
今皆然蓋其困於饑寒而弄兵山海以爲
假息之計也亦顧吾所以弭之何如耳觀
諸成周聯比什伍以爲追逐胥伺之備則
===
所以思患預防也深矣此三代之民所以
遇災無患承平無事也先王往矣成濾具
在乃若江西則目前之近固難卒以周濾
行之而亦不可不爲之深思遠慮也是故
地狹矣而猶有曠土民稠矣而類多游民
是無惟乎蓄積寡而荒易見也執事固嘗
慮及此矣而今者南贛之水泛濫瀰漫又
得無爲地方之患乎民財窮矣而賦歛愈
繁民力竭矣而征役不息是無惟乎姦宄
punctuated: 給之憂，及太平無事之時，每懷反側擾攘之慮，則荒與盜皆有其備，斯善爲政矣。請復明問：饑饉薦臻，國家代有，蓋天時之不常，地利人事之不及也，顧吾所以備之何如耳。觀諸成周荒政十二，以及遺人、廩人所掌，則所以慮災防患也至矣。盜賊竊發，古今皆然，蓋其困於饑寒，而弄兵山海，以爲假息之計也，亦顧吾所以弭之何如耳。觀諸成周聯比什伍，以爲追逐胥伺之備，則所以思患預防也深矣。此三代之民所以遇災無患，承平無事也。先王往矣，成濾具在。乃若江西，則目前之近，固難卒以周濾行之，而亦不可不爲之深思遠慮也。是故地狹矣，而猶有曠土；民稠矣，而類多游民。是無惟乎蓄積寡，而荒易見也。執事固嘗慮及此矣，而今者南贛之水，泛濫瀰漫，又得無爲地方之患乎？民財窮矣，而賦歛愈繁；民力竭矣，而征役不息。是無惟乎姦宄
translation_en: …concern over shortages; and if, in times of peace and tranquility, one always keeps in mind the danger of unrest and disorder, then preparations will be in place against both famine and banditry. This is good government. Allow me to reply to your discerning question. Famines have repeatedly afflicted the realm in every age, owing to irregularities in the seasons and inadequacies in the resources of the land and in human efforts. What matters is how we prepare for them. Consider the twelve famine measures of the Zhou, together with the responsibilities of the grain-distribution and granary officials: their provisions for anticipating calamity and guarding against suffering were most thorough. Bandits have risen unexpectedly in ancient and modern times alike. Driven by hunger and cold, they take up arms in the mountains and by the sea as a means of eking out a precarious existence. Here too, what matters is how we suppress them. Consider how the Zhou linked households in groups of ten and five to provide for pursuit and mutual surveillance: their foresight in anticipating trouble and preventing it was profound. This is why the people of the Three Dynasties suffered no distress when calamities struck and enjoyed tranquility in times of peace. The former kings are gone, but their established provisions [?] remain fully available. As for Jiangxi and its immediate circumstances, it would certainly be difficult to put the Zhou provisions [?] into practice all at once; nevertheless, we must give the matter deep thought and consider its long-term implications. Thus, although land is limited, some still lies unused; although the population is dense, many people lack settled occupations. Is it any wonder [?] that reserves are scant and famine readily appears? You, honored examiners, have surely considered this already. Yet now the waters of Nan-Gan are overflowing and spreading far and wide: can they fail to threaten the region? The people's wealth is exhausted, yet taxes and exactions grow ever more burdensome; their strength is spent, yet levies and labor services never cease. Is it any wonder [?] that malefactors…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
生而盜易作也執事亦嘗加之意矣如向
者姚源之賊出沒剽掠又得無爲今日之
防乎蓋嘗求之古人如中饑則發中熟之
所斂大饑則發大熟之所斂此平糴之濫
李悝嘗行於魏矣穀賤則增價而糴穀貴
則減價而糶此常平之濫耿壽昌嘗行於
漢矣至若隋之開皇則有長孫平之爲義
倉取之於民不厚而置之當社爲近宋之
孝宗則有朱熹之爲社倉始則請官米以
===
加息而給則止息米以加耗凡此皆備荒
之術也然地有遠近戶有多寡人有老幼
強弱自不能以皆同以今論之平糴慮有
拘泥之失常平恐失斂散之宜義倉委之
社司或非人以長吏奸惟社倉則官無所
費民有所利誠鄉閭無窮之計也使郡邑
皆倣而行而又斟酌以適中焉庶備荒其
有濟乎在漢武帝則作沈命之濫盜起不
發發而捕弗滿品主者皆死在魏李崇則
punctuated:
生而盜易作也。執事亦嘗加之意矣。如向者姚源之賊出沒剽掠，又得無爲今日之防乎？蓋嘗求之古人，如中饑則發中熟之所斂，大饑則發大熟之所斂，此平糴之濫，李悝嘗行於魏矣。穀賤則增價而糴，穀貴則減價而糶，此常平之濫，耿壽昌嘗行於漢矣。至若隋之開皇，則有長孫平之爲義倉，取之於民不厚，而置之當社爲近；宋之孝宗，則有朱熹之爲社倉，始則請官米以加息，而給則止息米以加耗。凡此皆備荒之術也。然地有遠近，戶有多寡，人有老幼強弱，自不能以皆同。以今論之，平糴慮有拘泥之失，常平恐失斂散之宜，義倉委之社司，或非人以長吏奸。惟社倉則官無所費，民有所利，誠鄉閭無窮之計也。使郡邑皆倣而行，而又斟酌以適中焉，庶備荒其有濟乎？
在漢武帝則作沈命之濫，盜起不發，發而捕弗滿品，主者皆死。在魏李崇則
translation_en:
…evildoers arise and banditry readily breaks out. You, sir, have also given this your attention. Consider the bandits of Yaoyuan, who recently appeared and disappeared, plundering and pillaging: must they not also be guarded against today? I have sought precedents among the ancients. In a moderate famine, they released what had been collected from a moderate harvest; in a severe famine, they released what had been collected from an abundant harvest. This was the equitable grain-purchasing system [?], which Li Kui implemented in Wei. When grain was cheap, they raised the price and purchased it; when grain was dear, they lowered the price and sold it. This was the ever-normal granary system [?], which Geng Shouchang implemented under the Han. During the Kaihuang reign of the Sui, Zhangsun Ping established charitable granaries: contributions exacted from the people were light, and the granaries were conveniently situated within their respective communities. Under Emperor Xiaozong of the Song, Zhu Xi established community granaries. Initially, he requested government rice to lend at interest; once supplies were sufficient, interest was discontinued, with only an allowance for wastage added [?]. These were all methods of preparing against famine. Yet places differ in distance, households in number, and people in age and strength; naturally, they cannot all be treated alike. Judged by present circumstances, equitable grain purchasing risks excessive rigidity; the ever-normal granaries may fail to collect and distribute grain appropriately; and charitable granaries, entrusted to community administrators, may fall into unsuitable hands and foster official malfeasance. Only community granaries entail no expense for the authorities while benefiting the people: they truly offer a lasting provision for local communities. If every prefecture and county followed this example, adapting it judiciously to achieve a proper balance, might this not make famine preparations effective?
Under Emperor Wu of the Han, the Shenming statute [?] was instituted: if banditry arose and was not reported, or if it was reported but arrests fell short of the prescribed quota, the responsible officials were all put to death. Under the Wei, Li Chong …

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
置樓鼓之防盜發而擊擊則四村皆集救
之而聲布百里義營之瀼行之者寔儆也
一户爲盜累其一村一户被盜累其一將
懸賞之瀼爲之者崔安潛也告捕一盜賞
錢伍百同侶捕之賞同平人此皆弭盜之
方也然地有險易勢有强弱情有向背順
逆亦不能以相一自今觀之况命誠禁之
太嚴樓鼓止用之有警懸賞所費官錢亦
可暫而不可久惟義營則村村自相保盜無
===
所脫實獨清一境之效也使郡邑皆行而
瀼而又變通以宜民庶弭盜其或得乎雖
然此特藿時之宜而非探本之論求其本
于備荒則荀卿所謂田野縣鄙者財之本
垣窌倉廩者財之末百姓時和事業得敘
者貨之源等賦府庫者貨之流而欲人君
養其和節其流開其源則上下俱富乃國
計之極故禹十年水湯七年旱而民無菜
色者以此故也知此則平糴諸瀼又似
punctuated:
置樓鼓之防，盜發而擊，擊則四村皆集救之，而聲布百里。義營之瀼，行之者寔儆也。一户爲盜，累其一村；一户被盜，累其一將。懸賞之瀼，爲之者崔安潛也。告捕一盜，賞錢伍百；同侶捕之，賞同平人。此皆弭盜之方也。然地有險易，勢有强弱，情有向背順逆，亦不能以相一。自今觀之，况命誠禁之太嚴，樓鼓止用之有警，懸賞所費官錢亦可暫而不可久。惟義營則村村自相保，盜無所脫，實獨清一境之效也。使郡邑皆行而瀼，而又變通以宜民，庶弭盜其或得乎？

雖然，此特藿時之宜，而非探本之論。求其本于備荒，則荀卿所謂「田野縣鄙者，財之本；垣窌倉廩者，財之末；百姓時和，事業得敘者，貨之源；等賦府庫者，貨之流」，而欲人君養其和，節其流，開其源，則上下俱富，乃國計之極。故禹十年水，湯七年旱，而民無菜色者，以此故也。知此，則平糴諸瀼又似
translation_en:
…established a defense system of watchtowers and drums. When bandits appeared, the drums were beaten; at their sound, the four surrounding villages all assembled to give aid, and the sound carried a hundred li. The system [?] of community defense companies was put into practice by Shi Jing 寔儆 [?]. If one household engaged in banditry, its entire village was held accountable; if one household was robbed, the commander responsible for it was held accountable. The system [?] of offering rewards was instituted by Cui Anqian 崔安潛. Whoever reported and apprehended one bandit received five hundred cash; an accomplice who apprehended him received the same reward as an ordinary person. These were all methods for suppressing banditry. Yet terrain varies in difficulty, forces in strength, and popular sentiment in allegiance and opposition, obedience and defiance; these too cannot be treated uniformly. Viewed from the present, the shenming law [?] was indeed excessively harsh in its prohibitions; watchtowers and drums were useful only when an alarm arose; and the expenditure of public funds on rewards could be sustained temporarily but not indefinitely. Only the community defense companies enabled every village to protect itself, leaving bandits nowhere to escape: this alone effectively cleared an entire territory of banditry. If prefectures and counties all implemented this system [?], adapting it flexibly to suit the people, might suppression of banditry perhaps be achieved?

Even so, these are merely expedients suited to the time [?], rather than an argument that probes the root. To seek the root of famine preparedness, we have what Master Xun called: “Fields and outlying settlements are the foundation of wealth; enclosed storage pits and granaries are its branches. When the common people live in seasonal harmony and their occupations proceed in due order, this is the source of goods; graded taxation and government treasuries are their flow.” He therefore wished the ruler to nurture that harmony, regulate the flow, and open up the source. Then those above and below would all be prosperous—the highest achievement of state finance. This is why, despite ten years of flooding under Yu and seven years of drought under Tang, the people showed no signs of starvation. Once this is understood, the various systems [?], such as purchasing grain at equitable prices, again seem…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
必行矣求其本於弭盜則范祖禹所謂因
衣食之源立教化之官先之以節儉示之
以純朴而欲人君不舍其本而專禁其末
必如唐太宗之使民衣食有餘不必如宋
熙寧別立盜賊重法焉則邪僻不作乃邦
成之至故路不拾遺外戶不閉而商旅野
宿者坐是焉耳知此則淳命諸法又似不
必用矣雖然猶末也三年耕必有一年之
食九年耕必有三年之食此王制之儲畜
===
之灋不使其非國也荀子之不欲雖賞之
不竊子欲善而民善此聖人主教化之意
不欲以徒灋也而蘇轍亦曰古之聖人上
盜以義使天下皆知父子君臣而誰與爲
亂朱熹又曰爲政者當順五行脩五事以
安百姓又荀范之所不及也持此而往雖
措之天下可也豈獨江西然哉昔人有云
勢不同而理同又云有治人而無治灋歟
事以爲何如
punctuated:
必行矣。求其本於弭盜，則范祖禹所謂因衣食之源，立教化之官，先之以節儉，示之以純朴，而欲人君不舍其本而專禁其末，必如唐太宗之使民衣食有餘，不必如宋熙寧別立盜賊重法焉，則邪僻不作，乃邦成之至。故路不拾遺，外戶不閉，而商旅野宿者，坐是焉耳。知此，則淳命諸法又似不必用矣。
雖然，猶末也。三年耕，必有一年之食；九年耕，必有三年之食。此《王制》之儲畜之灋，不使其非國也。荀子之不欲，雖賞之不竊；子欲善而民善。此聖人主教化之意，不欲以徒灋也。而蘇轍亦曰：「古之聖人上盜以義，使天下皆知父子君臣，而誰與爲亂？」朱熹又曰：「爲政者當順五行，脩五事，以安百姓。」又荀、范之所不及也。持此而往，雖措之天下可也，豈獨江西然哉！昔人有云：「勢不同而理同。」又云：「有治人而無治灋。」歟事以爲何如？
translation_en:
…must indeed be put into practice. To seek the root of suppressing banditry, there is what Fan Zuyu said: build upon the sources of clothing and food, establish officials responsible for moral instruction, lead the people through frugality, and show them simplicity and honesty. The ruler should not abandon the root and concentrate exclusively on prohibiting its outward manifestations. He must follow Emperor Taizong of the Tang in ensuring that the people have clothing and food to spare; he need not follow the example of the Song’s Xining reign period in separately establishing severe laws against bandits. Then depravity will not arise: this is the highest achievement of government. Thus, people did not pick up things lost on the road, outer doors were left unbarred, and traveling merchants slept in the open countryside—all for this reason alone. Understanding this, the various laws termed “chunming” [?] would again seem unnecessary.
Even so, these are still secondary matters. Three years of cultivation must provide one year’s food in reserve; nine years of cultivation must provide three years’ food in reserve. These are the rules for storing provisions in Royal Regulations, which prevent a state from ceasing to be a state [?]. “If you yourself had no desire for wealth, even if you rewarded people for stealing, they would not steal” [the opening of this quotation is garbled]; “If you desire goodness, the people will be good.” This expresses the sage’s intention to give priority to moral instruction, rather than rely on laws alone. Su Zhe likewise said: “The sages of antiquity checked theft through righteousness [?], making everyone under Heaven understand the relationships between father and son, ruler and minister. Who, then, would join in creating disorder?” Zhu Xi also said: “Those who govern should accord with the Five Phases and cultivate the Five Activities, thereby bringing peace to the common people.” This, too, goes beyond what Xun and Fan addressed. Proceeding on these principles, one could apply them throughout the realm. How could they hold true only for Jiangxi? Someone of old said: “Circumstances differ, but the principle is the same.” It was also said: “There are people who bring about good government, but no laws that bring about good government by themselves.” What do you think of this [?]?

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試錄後序
凡試事成有司爲錄以
獻錄成序之皆
制也而序以爲戒也禮也序其後
申戒之也士之始進也猶女
子之嫁也禮女子之嫁也父
醮而戒之母送之階而又戒
===
之蓋慎其始也江西之試至
是爲錄凡幾序凡幾其主司
之得士與否其士之貞不貞
皆可觀已於其始也敢弗慎
與雖然彼爲是者徒以文焉
耳文果足恃耶我
國家體道爲治文出于一壹而
punctuated:
江西鄉試錄後序

凡試事成，有司爲錄以獻。錄成，序之，皆制也。而序以爲戒也，禮也。序其後，申戒之也。士之始進也，猶女子之嫁也。禮，女子之嫁也，父醮而戒之，母送之階而又戒之，蓋慎其始也。

江西之試，至是爲錄凡幾，序凡幾？其主司之得士與否，其士之貞不貞，皆可觀已。於其始也，敢弗慎與？雖然，彼爲是者，徒以文焉耳。文果足恃耶？我國家體道爲治，文出于一壹而
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination

Whenever an examination has been completed, the responsible officials compile a record for presentation to the throne. When the record is complete, a preface is written: all this is prescribed by regulation. Using the preface to offer admonition accords with ritual propriety. Appending a postface reiterates that admonition. A scholar’s first advancement is like a woman’s marriage. According to ritual, when a woman marries, her father offers her a ceremonial cup of wine and admonishes her; her mother accompanies her to the steps and admonishes her again. This is to exercise care at the beginning.

By now, how many records of the Jiangxi examinations have been compiled, and how many prefaces written? Whether the presiding examiners have obtained worthy scholars, and whether those scholars have remained upright, can all be discerned. At the beginning, dare we fail to exercise care? Nevertheless, those who undertake this rely solely on literary composition. Can literary composition truly be relied upon? Our dynasty embodies the Way in its governance; literary expression proceeds from a single unity, and…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
又曰似司馬遷似陸贄韓愈
也今試求之非似之間而其
所見者則一矣脩之言曰三
代之上政出于一而禮樂達
於天下是也知一則知文矣
於是則有本論濮議知一則
知士矣於是則有蘇軾曾鞏
===
固脩之所自得於文者是不
寧鄉士之濙而天下公言之
矣雖然昔脩起五季排佛老
爲功矣而今得無進之以爲
博乎脩變鉤棘黜啇軋稱復
古矣而今得無目之以爲才
乎彼其主司士之相遭也有
punctuated: 又曰似司馬遷，似陸贄、韓愈也。今試求之非似之間，而其所見者則一矣。脩之言曰：「三代之上，政出于一，而禮樂達於天下。」是也。知一則知文矣，於是則有《本論》、《濮議》；知一則知士矣，於是則有蘇軾、曾鞏。固脩之所自得於文者，是不寧鄉士之濙，而天下公言之矣。雖然，昔脩起五季，排佛老爲功矣，而今得無進之以爲博乎？脩變鉤棘，黜啇軋，稱復古矣，而今得無目之以爲才乎？彼其主司、士之相遭也，有
translation_en:
…and also say that it resembles Sima Qian, or Lu Zhi and Han Yu. Now, if we seek it in those respects in which it does not resemble them, what we discern is unity. As [Ouyang] Xiu said: “In the Three Dynasties and earlier, government issued from a single source, and rites and music reached throughout the realm.” This is precisely the point. Understanding unity, one understands writing; hence his Fundamental Discourse and Deliberations on the Prince of Pu. Understanding unity, one understands scholars; hence Su Shi and Zeng Gong. Certainly, what Xiu himself attained in writing was proclaimed publicly throughout the realm, not merely among local scholars [?; the transcription here is unclear].

Nevertheless, in the past Xiu emerged in the wake of the Five Dynasties, and his rejection of Buddhism and Daoism was counted an achievement. Yet today, might people not promote these teachings as broad learning? Xiu reformed the hooked and thorny style of writing and rejected “shang ya” [?], and this was acclaimed as a return to antiquity. Yet today, might people not regard such writing as talent? In the encounters between those presiding over examinations and the scholars, there are…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
不爲今弊也者幾希夫豈以
脩爲不美哉不變則不奇不奇不
利則不變固世之恒者比其
後也而習成焉習也而厭生
焉習而厭厭而奇吾不知文
所止矣是故文也者變而未
始變者也至奇而易簡者也
===
此脩之謂一或者其有遺志
於斯我
祖宗朝用少師楊士奇言特取脩
之文顯行之士奇之文固脩
之瀶也而後之作者漸以異
須者禮官之論又以正文體
請禮官之請又士奇之意也
punctuated:
不爲今弊也者幾希。夫豈以脩爲不美哉？不變則不奇，不奇不利則不變，固世之恒者。比其後也，而習成焉；習也，而厭生焉。習而厭，厭而奇，吾不知文所止矣。是故文也者，變而未始變者也，至奇而易簡者也。
此脩之謂一。或者其有遺志於斯。我祖宗朝，用少師楊士奇言，特取脩之文，顯行之。士奇之文，固脩之瀶也，而後之作者漸以異。須者，禮官之論，又以正文體請。禮官之請，又士奇之意也。
translation_en:
…very few have not become abuses in our own day. Does this mean that Xiu’s writing was not excellent? Without change there is no novelty; without novelty or advantage, there is no change: this is indeed the constant way of the world. In time, familiarity develops; with familiarity, weariness arises. Familiarity brings weariness, and weariness prompts novelty. I do not know where writing will end. Thus writing changes yet has never fundamentally changed; it reaches the utmost novelty yet remains easy and simple.
This is what Xiu called oneness [?]. Perhaps he left an intention concerning this for posterity. During the reigns of our imperial ancestors, following the advice of Junior Preceptor Yang Shiqi, the court specially selected Xiu’s writings and prominently circulated them. Shiqi’s writing was itself modeled on Xiu’s [?], but later writers gradually departed from it. Recently [?], the ritual officials, in their deliberations, again requested that literary style be rectified. Their request likewise expressed Shiqi’s intention.

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
太祖
太宗能繼其盛歟執事發策秋闈首以
皇上本支日蕃預求教
皇太子及
諸王之術以獻甚盛心也愚何能知之然而
太祖
太宗佑啓之功
皇上光裕之德則在臣子不可以無言也敢因
明問揄揚其萬一且古帝王教子孫之瀍
===
何始乎自舜命夔教胄子而其瀍以肇禹
有典則貽子孫而其瀍漸詳周人貽孫謀
燕翼子而其瀍彌備其見於記則文王世
子之篇有曰學世子及學士必時春夏學
干戈秋冬學羽籥有曰三王教世子必以
禮樂有曰立太傅少傅以養之太傅審父
子君臣之道以示之少傅奉世子以觀太
傅之德行而審喻之太傅在前少傅在後
入則有保出則有師是以教喻而德成而
punctuated:
太祖、太宗能繼其盛歟？執事發策秋闈，首以皇上本支日蕃，預求教皇太子及諸王之術以獻，甚盛心也。愚何能知之？然而太祖、太宗佑啓之功，皇上光裕之德，則在臣子不可以無言也。敢因明問，揄揚其萬一。
且古帝王教子孫之瀍，何始乎？自舜命夔教胄子，而其瀍以肇；禹有典則貽子孫，而其瀍漸詳；周人貽孫謀、燕翼子，而其瀍彌備。其見於記，則《文王世子》之篇有曰：「學世子及學士，必時。春夏學干戈，秋冬學羽籥。」有曰：「三王教世子，必以禮樂。」有曰：「立太傅、少傅以養之。太傅審父子君臣之道以示之；少傅奉世子以觀太傅之德行，而審喻之。太傅在前，少傅在後；入則有保，出則有師。是以教喻而德成。」而
translation_en:
…Could Taizu and Taizong carry on that flourishing legacy? In setting the policy questions for the autumn Provincial Examination, you, honored examiners, began with the daily increase of His Majesty’s principal and collateral lines, seeking in advance methods for educating the Imperial Heir Apparent and the princes, to submit to the throne. This is a most noble intention. How could someone as ignorant as I understand these matters? Yet, as a subject, I cannot remain silent about Taizu and Taizong’s achievements in protecting and establishing the dynasty, or His Majesty’s virtue in gloriously enriching their legacy. I venture, in response to your discerning question, to extol one ten-thousandth of these accomplishments.
Now, where did the methods [?] by which ancient emperors and kings educated their descendants begin? When Shun commanded Kui to teach the sons of the nobility, these methods [?] originated. Yu had standards and rules to bequeath to his descendants, and these methods [?] gradually became more detailed. The people of Zhou bequeathed plans to their grandsons and provided security and support for their sons, and these methods [?] became still more complete. As for their appearance in the Record of Rites, the chapter “King Wen as Heir Apparent” states: “In teaching the heir apparent and the students, one must observe the seasons. In spring and summer they learn the shield-and-halberd dances; in autumn and winter they learn the feather-and-flute dances.” It also states: “The Three Kings invariably taught their heirs apparent through rites and music.” It also states: “A Grand Preceptor and a Junior Preceptor are appointed to nurture him. The Grand Preceptor carefully examines the Way governing father and son, ruler and subject, and demonstrates it to him. The Junior Preceptor accompanies the heir apparent to observe the Grand Preceptor’s virtuous conduct and carefully explains it to him. The Grand Preceptor is before him and the Junior Preceptor behind him. Within, he has a guardian; outside, he has a teacher. Through such instruction and guidance, his virtue is perfected.” And…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
曰世子齒於學樂正司業父師司成今皆
可稽也其見於史則賈誼治安之策有曰
太子始生固舉以禮使士負之有司齋肅
端冕見之南郊有曰成王幼在襁褓之中
召公爲太保周公爲太傅太公爲太師有
曰選天下之端士孝悌博聞有道術者以
衛翼之有曰太子既冠成人免於保傅之
嚴則有記過之史徹膳之宰進善之旌誹
謗之木敢諫之鼓瞽史誦詩工誦箴諫大
===
夫進謀士傳民語今皆可稽也而執事有
疑於書及周禮之未載愚則以爲此無足
疑也蓋胄子之教既載於舜典而虞夏商
周師保疑丞四輔三公不必備惟其人則
其教初未嘗廢三公三孤既載於周官而
三公無官不隸六卿則其事固無由見於
周禮耳執事又謂帝王典則燕翼別有所
在而深慨夫漢唐宋治效之衰愚則以
此執事之卓識而實愚之所謂本也
punctuated:
曰：「世子齒於學，樂正司業，父師司成。」今皆可稽也。其見於史，則賈誼治安之策有曰：「太子始生，固舉以禮，使士負之，有司齋肅，端冕見之南郊。」有曰：「成王幼在襁褓之中，召公爲太保，周公爲太傅，太公爲太師。」有曰：「選天下之端士，孝悌博聞有道術者，以衛翼之。」有曰：「太子既冠成人，免於保傅之嚴，則有記過之史、徹膳之宰、進善之旌、誹謗之木、敢諫之鼓，瞽史誦詩，工誦箴諫，大夫進謀，士傳民語。」今皆可稽也。
而執事有疑於《書》及《周禮》之未載，愚則以爲此無足疑也。蓋胄子之教既載於《舜典》，而虞夏商周，師保疑丞，四輔三公，不必備，惟其人，則其教初未嘗廢。三公三孤既載於《周官》，而三公無官，不隸六卿，則其事固無由見於《周禮》耳。
執事又謂帝王典則燕翼別有所在，而深慨夫漢唐宋治效之衰，愚則以此執事之卓識，而實愚之所謂本也。
translation_en:
…it says: “At school, the heir apparent takes his place according to age. The Director of Music oversees his studies, and the paternal tutor oversees their completion.” All these statements can be verified today. As for what appears in historical writings, Jia Yi’s policy essay on securing peace states: “When the heir apparent is first born, he is duly lifted up according to ritual, and an officer is made to carry him. The responsible officials purify themselves and adopt a reverent bearing; wearing ceremonial robes and caps, they present him at the southern suburban altar.” It also states: “When King Cheng was an infant still in swaddling clothes, the Duke of Shao served as Grand Guardian, the Duke of Zhou as Grand Preceptor, and the Grand Duke as Grand Mentor.” It also states: “Upright men from throughout the realm, filial and respectful toward their elder brothers, widely learned and versed in the Way and its methods, were selected to protect and assist him.” It also states: “Once the heir apparent had undergone capping and reached adulthood, and was released from the strict supervision of guardians and preceptors, there were scribes to record his faults, stewards to withdraw his meals, banners for presenting good counsel, wooden posts for criticism, and drums for bold remonstrance. Blind musicians and scribes recited poems; musicians recited admonitions and remonstrances; grand masters offered plans; and officers conveyed the people’s words.” All these statements can be verified today.
Yet you, sir, express doubt because these matters are not recorded in the Book of Documents or the Rites of Zhou. In my humble view, there is no cause for doubt here. The education of the sons of the nobility is already recorded in the “Canon of Shun.” Under Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou, there were mentors, guardians, counselors, and assistants—the Four Aides—and the Three Dukes. These posts did not all have to be filled: what mattered was finding the right men. Thus, this education was never abandoned. The Three Dukes and the Three Solitary Dignitaries are already recorded in “The Offices of Zhou” in the Book of Documents. But the Three Dukes had no departmental offices and were not subordinate to the Six Ministers; there was therefore no occasion for their duties to appear in the Rites of Zhou.
You further say that the standards established by emperors and kings, and their provision for the welfare of their descendants, lie elsewhere, and you deeply lament the decline in effective government under the Han, Tang, and Song. I humbly regard this as your penetrating insight [?], and it is indeed what I mean by the foundation.

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
蓋帝王之爲典則于其身不于其言其貽
謀燕翼于其道不于其儀而漢唐宋諸君
乃闊略於身心之間而徒致飾於言語事
爲之末故雖六傅之設賓客等官之設崇
文崇賢桂坊諸館局之設名位日繁帝範
之作戒子篇之作元良述承華要畧之作
後先相望而善在太子卒不免如楚士壹
所云耳洪惟我
太祖高皇帝道冠百王見高千古即位之初既
===
建大本堂取古今圖書充其中延四方名
儒教
皇太子及
諸王矣又著
祖訓錄
儲君昭鑑錄以賜而其爲書或紬繹六年始
克成編或采經傳格言以示訓戒天下之
至文也
太宗文皇帝入正大統益篤前烈嗣位之後既
punctuated:
蓋帝王之爲典則，于其身，不于其言；其貽謀燕翼，于其道，不于其儀。而漢唐宋諸君乃闊略於身心之間，而徒致飾於言語事爲之末。故雖六傅之設、賓客等官之設、崇文崇賢桂坊諸館局之設，名位日繁；帝範之作、戒子篇之作、元良述承華要畧之作，後先相望，而善在太子，卒不免如楚士壹所云耳。
洪惟我太祖高皇帝，道冠百王，見高千古。即位之初，既建大本堂，取古今圖書充其中，延四方名儒教皇太子及諸王矣。又著《祖訓錄》《儲君昭鑑錄》以賜，而其爲書，或紬繹六年始克成編，或采經傳格言以示訓戒，天下之至文也。
太宗文皇帝入正大統，益篤前烈。嗣位之後，既
translation_en:
For emperors and kings establish exemplary standards through their own persons, not through their words; they bequeath plans for the security of their descendants through their Way, not through their ceremonies. Yet the rulers of the Han, Tang, and Song were neglectful in cultivating their persons and minds, merely embellishing the superficial details of speech and action. Thus, although they established the six preceptorial offices, officials such as the Advisers to the Heir Apparent, and institutions such as the Chongwen and Chongxian Academies and the Guifang office, with titles and ranks multiplying daily; and although works such as Models for Emperors (Difan), Admonitions to a Son (Jiezi pian), An Account of the Heir Apparent (Yuanliang shu), and Essentials for the Heir Apparent (Chenghua yaolüe) appeared one after another, goodness in the crown prince ultimately could not escape the predicament described in the passage about “one scholar of Chu” [?].
We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao surpassed all kings in the Way, and that his insight exceeded that of all preceding ages. At the beginning of his reign, he established the Hall of the Great Foundation (Dabentang), filled it with books ancient and modern, and invited renowned Confucian scholars from all quarters to instruct the imperial crown prince and the princes. He also composed and bestowed upon them the Record of Ancestral Instructions (Zuxun lu) and the Record of Clear Mirrors for the Heir Apparent (Chujun zhaojian lu). Of these works, one required six years of searching examination before it could be completed; another gathered exemplary sayings from the classics and their commentaries to provide instruction and admonition. These were writings of the highest excellence in all the realm.
Emperor Taizong Wen assumed the rightful imperial succession and further strengthened the illustrious achievements of his predecessor. After succeeding to the throne, he had already…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
命翰林諸臣舉老成正大儒者得禮部侍
郎儀智以傳
皇太孫矣又輯
文華寶鑑
聖學心濼賜
皇太子而其爲書或克廣
昭鑒之義而重戒夫秦皇晉元之失或推極
帝王之學而深懲夫秦漢以下之非聖者
之謨訓也至若
太祖於
東宮不設府僚以廷臣兼領其職非有忽於
敎諭德成之任也觀其示詹同等以良匠
拙工之喻示李善長等以恐生嫌疑之說
則其爲慮至深而不獨祖述於周召保傅
之制如執事所云矣
太祖屬輔臣敎
皇太子以兵事
太宗以
punctuated:
命翰林諸臣舉老成正大儒者，得禮部侍郎儀智以傳皇太孫矣。又輯《文華寶鑑》《聖學心濼》賜皇太子，而其爲書，或克廣《昭鑒》之義而重戒夫秦皇、晉元之失，或推極帝王之學而深懲夫秦漢以下之非，聖者之謨訓也。
至若太祖於東宮不設府僚，以廷臣兼領其職，非有忽於敎諭德成之任也。觀其示詹同等以良匠拙工之喻，示李善長等以恐生嫌疑之說，則其爲慮至深，而不獨祖述於周召保傅之制，如執事所云矣。
太祖屬輔臣敎皇太子以兵事，太宗以
translation_en:
…ordered the Hanlin officials to recommend a mature, upright, and principled Confucian scholar, and obtained Yi Zhi, Vice Minister of Rites, to tutor the imperial grandson. He also compiled the Precious Mirror of Literary Brilliance (Wenhua baojian) and the Heart’s Joy in Sagely Learning (Shengxue xinluo [?]) and bestowed them upon the crown prince. Of these works, one expanded the meaning of the Luminous Mirror, emphatically warning against the errors of the First Emperor of Qin and Emperor Yuan of Jin; the other explored sovereign learning to its fullest extent, sternly condemning the wrongs committed from the Qin and Han onward. These were the counsels and instructions of a sage.
As for Taizu’s decision not to appoint a separate staff for the Eastern Palace, but to have court officials concurrently undertake its duties, this did not mean that he neglected the responsibility of instructing the heir and bringing his virtue to maturity. Consider how he presented Zhan Tong and others with the analogy of the skilled craftsman and the clumsy workman, and explained to Li Shanchang and others his fear that suspicion might arise. His deliberations were thus profoundly considered; he was not merely following the system under which the Dukes of Zhou and Shao served as guardians and tutors, as you have stated.
Taizu charged his assisting ministers with teaching the crown prince military affairs; Taizong took…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
皇太孫從征北虜非有昧於長恩明仁之道
也觀其諭李善長等以居安慮危不忘武
備諭楊榮以俾知用兵之瀝及知將士勞
苦則其爲謀至遠而不獨有取於春夏干
戈之學如執事所云矣然此愚以爲特其
瀝也乃如其本則
太祖
太宗之德猶之天地日月雖非繪畫之工所能
形容摹擬而愚也莊誦
===
聖訓亦間獲窺其精蘊之所存矣蓋
太祖嘗謂侍郎曾魯曰朕求古帝王之治莫盛
於堯舜觀其授受其要在允執厥中謂學士
宋濂曰人心虛靈乘氣機出入操而存之爲
難又曰朕之爲君上畏天地下畏兆民兢兢
業業不敢自逸又曰人君能清心寡慾勤於
政事不作無益害有益使民安田里足衣食
熙熙皞皞而不自知此卽神僊也功業垂太
一簡册瞀名流於後世此卽長生不死也謂
punctuated:
皇太孫從征北虜，非有昧於長恩明仁之道也。觀其諭李善長等以居安慮危、不忘武備，諭楊榮以俾知用兵之瀝及知將士勞苦，則其爲謀至遠，而不獨有取於春夏干戈之學，如執事所云矣。然此愚以爲特其瀝也，乃如其本，則太祖、太宗之德猶之天地日月，雖非繪畫之工所能形容摹擬，而愚也莊誦聖訓，亦間獲窺其精蘊之所存矣。
蓋太祖嘗謂侍郎曾魯曰：「朕求古帝王之治，莫盛於堯舜。觀其授受，其要在允執厥中。」謂學士宋濂曰：「人心虛靈，乘氣機出入，操而存之爲難。」又曰：「朕之爲君，上畏天地，下畏兆民，兢兢業業，不敢自逸。」又曰：「人君能清心寡慾，勤於政事，不作無益害有益，使民安田里、足衣食，熙熙皞皞而不自知，此卽神僊也。功業垂太一簡册，瞀名流於後世，此卽長生不死也。」謂
translation_en:
…the imperial grandson accompany him on campaign against the northern barbarians; this did not mean that he was ignorant of the way of nurturing kindness and manifesting benevolence. Consider his admonition to Li Shanzhang and the others to anticipate danger while dwelling in security and never neglect military preparedness, and his explanation to Yang Rong that the purpose was to let the grandson learn the particulars [?] of warfare and understand the hardships of officers and soldiers. His planning was exceedingly far-sighted; it was not merely that he valued the spring and summer instruction in shields and spears, as you have stated. Yet I, in my humble view, regard these as merely its outward traces [?]. As for the foundation, the virtue of Taizu and Taizong was like Heaven and Earth, the sun and moon. Although no painter’s skill could depict or reproduce it, through reverently reciting their sacred instructions I have occasionally gained a glimpse of their profound essence.
