Taizu once said to Vice Minister Zeng Lu: “When I examine the government of the ancient emperors and kings, none surpasses that of Yao and Shun. Looking at their transmission and reception of sovereignty, its essential principle lay in sincerely holding fast to the Mean.” He said to Academician Song Lian: “The human mind is empty and numinous; it comes and goes with the workings of vital energy. To hold it fast and preserve it is difficult.” He also said: “As ruler, above I stand in awe of Heaven and Earth; below I stand in awe of the myriad people. Cautious and diligent, I dare not indulge in ease.” He also said: “If a ruler can purify his mind and reduce his desires, attend diligently to government, and refrain from undertaking useless things that harm useful ones, enabling the people to dwell securely among their fields and villages, with sufficient clothing and food, contented and carefree without being conscious of it—this is to be a divine immortal. To have one’s achievements recorded in the historical annals [?] and one’s reputation transmitted to later generations [?]—this is longevity without death.” He said to…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
臣詹同曰聲色乃伐性之斧斤易以溺人一
有溺焉則禍敗隨之嗚呼玆數言也帝王正
心脩身之學漢唐宋所未有也
太宗嘗諭學士解縉等曰人君一有好樂泥而
不返則慾必勝理朕每退朝默坐未嘗不思
管束此心爲切要諭廵視監察御史曰朕居
深宮一飲一食未嘗不念及軍民斥獻道經
者曰朕所用治天下者五經耳道經何用諭
皇太子曰堯舜相傳惟曰允執厥中帝王之
道貴乎知要郤永春侯王寧飯僧奉佛之請
曰天子以四海爲家能思天位者親之所傳
大業者親之所建天下生民親之所保而敬
以奉天勤以守業仁以臨民使萬物得所四
夷咸賓光昭祖宗傳之子孫可以爲孝何必
事佛乃爲孝乎嗚呼玆數言也帝王正心脩
身之學漢唐宋所未有也
聖子神孫得諸觀感其興起善端成就令德信
當有潛移默化而不自知者百七十年
punctuated:
臣詹同曰：「聲色乃伐性之斧斤，易以溺人，一有溺焉，則禍敗隨之。」嗚呼！玆數言也，帝王正心脩身之學，漢唐宋所未有也。
太宗嘗諭學士解縉等曰：「人君一有好樂，泥而不返，則慾必勝理。朕每退朝默坐，未嘗不思管束此心爲切要。」諭廵視監察御史曰：「朕居深宮，一飲一食，未嘗不念及軍民。」斥獻道經者曰：「朕所用治天下者，五經耳，道經何用？」諭皇太子曰：「堯舜相傳，惟曰允執厥中。帝王之道，貴乎知要。」郤永春侯王寧飯僧奉佛之請，曰：「天子以四海爲家，能思天位者親之所傳，大業者親之所建，天下生民親之所保，而敬以奉天，勤以守業，仁以臨民，使萬物得所，四夷咸賓，光昭祖宗，傳之子孫，可以爲孝，何必事佛乃爲孝乎？」嗚呼！玆數言也，帝王正心脩身之學，漢唐宋所未有也。
聖子神孫得諸觀感，其興起善端，成就令德，信當有潛移默化而不自知者。百七十年
translation_en:
…to his minister Zhan Tong: “Sensual pleasures are axes that hew away at one’s moral nature and readily engulf a person. Once one succumbs to them, disaster and ruin follow.” Ah! These few sayings express a learning of rectifying the mind and cultivating the self for emperors and kings such as the Han, Tang, and Song never possessed.
Taizong once instructed the Academicians Xie Jin and others: “Once a ruler becomes mired in something he delights in and fails to turn back, desire will inevitably overcome principle. Whenever I retire from court and sit silently, I invariably reflect that keeping this mind under control is of the utmost importance.” He instructed the investigating censors on inspection duty: “Living deep within the palace, I never take a drink or a meal without thinking of the soldiers and the people.” Rebuking someone who presented Daoist scriptures, he said: “What I use to govern the realm is simply the Five Classics. What use have I for Daoist scriptures?” He instructed the imperial heir apparent: “What Yao and Shun transmitted to each other was simply this: ‘Sincerely hold fast to the Mean.’ In the Way of emperors and kings, what matters is knowing the essentials.” Rejecting the request of Wang Ning, Marquis of Yongchun, to feed monks and worship the Buddha, he said: “The Son of Heaven takes all within the Four Seas as his family. If he can reflect that his heavenly throne was transmitted by his parents, that his great undertaking was established by his parents, and that the people of the realm were protected by his parents; if he then serves Heaven with reverence, preserves that undertaking with diligence, and governs the people with benevolence, enabling all things to find their proper place and the peoples of the four quarters all to submit; and if he brings glory to his ancestors and transmits his inheritance to his descendants—this may count as filial piety. Why must one serve the Buddha to be filial?” Ah! These few sayings express a learning of rectifying the mind and cultivating the self for emperors and kings such as the Han, Tang, and Song never possessed.
Their sagely sons and divine grandsons acquired this through observing their example and being moved by it. In awakening the beginnings of goodness and bringing excellent virtue to fruition, they surely underwent a gradual, imperceptible transformation without themselves being aware of it. For one hundred and seventy years…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
聖相承天下乂安和氣旁達豈偶然之故哉
乃今
皇上
仁孝聰明得之天縱凡古今所謂曠典旣次
第舉之而恭黙思道至誠無息緝熙敬止
聖學日新是卽
太祖
太宗之爲德也
天章睿藻出自性成凡古今所謂大製作旣兼
===
有之而
敬一一箴獨遡心學之源星變一
勑曲盡時幾之義是卽
太祖
太宗之爲文也然則今日欽
皇太子及
諸王之術亦奚必求之遠哉
皇上建極綏猷本已立矣乃其濬則
太祖
punctuated: 聖相承，天下乂安，和氣旁達，豈偶然之故哉？乃今皇上仁孝聰明，得之天縱，凡古今所謂曠典，旣次第舉之，而恭黙思道，至誠無息，緝熙敬止，聖學日新，是卽太祖、太宗之爲德也。天章睿藻，出自性成，凡古今所謂大製作，旣兼有之，而《敬一》一箴，獨遡心學之源；星變一勑，曲盡時幾之義，是卽太祖、太宗之爲文也。然則今日欽皇太子及諸王之術，亦奚必求之遠哉？皇上建極綏猷，本已立矣，乃其濬則太祖
translation_en:
…sage sovereigns have succeeded one another; all under Heaven is peaceful and well governed, and harmonious influences spread everywhere. Could this have happened by chance? Now His Majesty possesses Heaven-endowed benevolence, filial piety, intelligence, and discernment. He has undertaken, in succession, all those exceptional observances spoken of in ancient and modern times. Yet he remains reverent and silent in contemplation of the Way, unceasing in utmost sincerity, continually illuminating his virtue and abiding in reverence. His sagely learning is renewed daily. These are the very virtues of Taizu and Taizong.

His imperial compositions and discerning literary expressions arise from his innate nature. He already possesses the full range of what ancient and modern times have called great literary productions. Yet his single admonition, Reverent Single-mindedness (Jingyi), uniquely traces learning of the mind to its source; and his edict concerning celestial anomalies fully elucidates the significance of the incipient tendencies of the times. This is the very literary achievement of Taizu and Taizong.

Why, then, must one seek far afield today for a method of showing reverence toward [?] the Crown Prince and the other princes? His Majesty has established the supreme standard and secured the guiding principles of government: the foundation is already laid. As for tracing it to its source [?], Taizu…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
太宗成憲具存守而循之雖萬世可也愚也遭
逢
聖明涵濡大化覩
元良之有賴而益以知
宗社靈長之休計屏翰之有眷而益以知磐石
奠安之慶蓋有不勝其欣忭者執事倘與
其進尚當爲
聖天子頌之謹對
第二問
能鳴臣
===
同考試官教諭李　批　朱子論仁深得孔門遺意而好異者或持其說以亂之是作考據折衷確有定見於
可與言仁矣
同考試官教諭王　批　說學者在仁處論辨而意
足必有得於仁者
同考試官教諭孫　批　考據詳而議論正可式
考試官教諭葉　批　論仁折衷於朱子深爲有見
考試官教授伍　批　□□□□□□□
punctuated:
太宗成憲具存，守而循之，雖萬世可也。愚也遭逢聖明，涵濡大化，覩元良之有賴，而益以知宗社靈長之休；計屏翰之有眷，而益以知磐石奠安之慶。蓋有不勝其欣忭者。執事倘與其進，尚當爲聖天子頌之。謹對。
第二問
能鳴臣
同考試官教諭李批：朱子論仁，深得孔門遺意，而好異者或持其說以亂之。是作考據折衷，確有定見，於可與言仁矣。
同考試官教諭王批：說學者在仁處論辨而意足，必有得於仁者。
同考試官教諭孫批：考據詳而議論正，可式。
考試官教諭葉批：論仁折衷於朱子，深爲有見。
考試官教授伍批：□□□□□□□
translation_en:
…Taizong’s established institutions remain fully intact. By preserving and following them, one could carry on even for ten thousand generations. I, in my ignorance, have had the fortune to live under a sagely and enlightened ruler and to be steeped in his great transforming influence. Seeing that the heir apparent has support, I understand all the more the blessing of enduring longevity for the ancestral temples and altars of state. Reflecting on the care bestowed upon the princes who serve as protective bulwarks, I understand all the more the felicity of a foundation as secure as a great rock. My joy is indeed beyond measure. If you, honored examiners, should approve my advancement, I shall further extol this on behalf of the sagely Son of Heaven. Respectfully submitted in reply.
Second Question
Neng Mingchen 能鳴臣 [?]
Associate Examiner, Instructor Li, comments: “Master Zhu’s discussion of benevolence profoundly captures the meaning transmitted from the school of Confucius. Yet those fond of novelty sometimes advance their own theories to throw it into confusion. This composition examines the evidence and weighs the interpretations, displaying a firm and settled judgment. Its author may indeed be engaged in discussion of benevolence [?].”
Associate Examiner, Instructor Wang, comments: “In discussing learning, the author argues the points concerning benevolence and fully develops his meaning [?]. He must have attained some understanding of benevolence.”
Associate Examiner, Instructor Sun, comments: “The examination of evidence is thorough and the argument sound. It may serve as a model.”
Examiner, Instructor Ye, comments: “The discussion of benevolence takes Master Zhu as its standard of judgment and displays considerable insight.”
Examiner, Professor Wu, comments: “[Seven illegible characters.]”

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
學有正傳而失焉者說之者之好爲異也
道有定論而晦焉者學之者之不知求也
道莫大於仁君子之學莫先於求仁然是
學也在聖人有正傳矣苟說之者無秉之
以好異之心則於學當有所得而益見其
傳之不容廢是仁也在大儒有定論矣苟
學之者能持之以必求之志則於道當有
所契而益見其論之不可易夫惟不然也
是故傳而或失焉論而或晦焉其始也非
有意於病道與學而卒不免爲之病嗚呼
是豈非君子之大戒哉執事於此思救正
之以詢承學愚也於求仁之學嘗得之孔
子論仁之言嘗得之朱子矣請執以復焉
何如蓋昔堯舜之爲治莫非仁也然其見
諸授受者不過曰人心惟危道心惟微惟
精惟一允執厥中而已於仁未始及也是
豈有所遺而然哉道心即仁人心即慾惟
從事精一之間則仁在是矣孔門之爲教
punctuated:
學有正傳，而失焉者，說之者之好爲異也；道有定論，而晦焉者，學之者之不知求也。道莫大於仁，君子之學莫先於求仁。然是學也，在聖人有正傳矣。苟說之者無秉之以好異之心，則於學當有所得，而益見其傳之不容廢。是仁也，在大儒有定論矣。苟學之者能持之以必求之志，則於道當有所契，而益見其論之不可易。夫惟不然也，是故傳而或失焉，論而或晦焉。其始也，非有意於病道與學，而卒不免爲之病。嗚呼！是豈非君子之大戒哉？執事於此思救正之，以詢承學。愚也，於求仁之學嘗得之孔子，論仁之言嘗得之朱子矣。請執以復焉，何如？
蓋昔堯舜之爲治，莫非仁也。然其見諸授受者，不過曰：「人心惟危，道心惟微，惟精惟一，允執厥中。」而已。於仁未始及也。是豈有所遺而然哉？道心即仁，人心即慾。惟從事精一之間，則仁在是矣。孔門之爲教
translation_en:
Learning has an orthodox transmission; when it is lost, this is because its interpreters delight in novelty. The Way has settled explanations; when it is obscured, this is because its students do not know how to seek it. Nothing in the Way is greater than benevolence, and nothing in the gentleman’s learning takes precedence over seeking benevolence. This learning has an orthodox transmission from the sages. If its interpreters do not approach it with a fondness for novelty, they should gain something through learning and see ever more clearly that its transmission cannot be abandoned. Benevolence has received settled explanations from the great Confucian scholars. If students can hold to it with a resolve to seek it out, they should attain some accord with the Way and see ever more clearly that these explanations cannot be altered. Yet precisely because they fail to do so, the transmission is sometimes lost and the explanations sometimes obscured. At the outset, they have no intention of harming the Way and learning, but in the end they cannot avoid doing them harm. Alas! Is this not a grave warning for the gentleman? Wishing to remedy and correct this, you gentlemen have questioned those who pursue learning. As for my humble self, I have gained an understanding of the learning that seeks benevolence from Kongzi, and of the words that explain benevolence from Zhuzi. Allow me to draw upon these in reply—may I?
In antiquity, the governance of Yao and Shun was entirely an expression of benevolence. Yet what appeared in the instructions handed down from one to the other was no more than this: “The human mind is precarious; the mind of the Way is subtle. Be discerning, be single-minded, and faithfully hold to the mean.” Benevolence itself was never mentioned. Could this have been because something was omitted? The mind of the Way is benevolence; the human mind is desire. Simply devote yourself to discernment and singleness of mind, and benevolence is to be found therein. As for the teaching in the school of Kongzi…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
莫非仁也然其見諸問荅者不過曰克己
復禮主敬行恕先難後獲言之能訒而已
於仁殆罕言也夫豈有所隱而然哉仁固
難言在於心會惟從事數者之中則仁可
求矣至若子思得傳於夫子而著於中庸
者曰脩身以道脩道以仁夫身以道脩道
以仁脩則仁與道固非兩物而脩道之責
實存乎人也孟子得傳於子思而著於七
篇者曰仁者人也合而言之道也夫人而
具此仁則爲人人而體此仁則爲道是道
與仁誠非二致而體仁之功乃繫於人也
是不可見聖人立教之意而學之正傳在
是乎夫何說之者之好爲異以爲聖人之
言未盡也而思以足之於是競求所以釋
夫仁者蓋自漢世以恩愛爲仁至唐韓愈
主之之過遂以博愛名之今原道所言是
也又至謝良佐矯之之過遂以知覺名之
今桃仁杏仁之喻是也殊不知仁體也愛
punctuated: 莫非仁也。然其見諸問荅者，不過曰克己復禮、主敬行恕、先難後獲、言之能訒而已，於仁殆罕言也。夫豈有所隱而然哉？仁固難言，在於心會，惟從事數者之中，則仁可求矣。至若子思得傳於夫子而著於中庸者曰：「脩身以道，脩道以仁。」夫身以道脩，道以仁脩，則仁與道固非兩物，而脩道之責實存乎人也。孟子得傳於子思而著於七篇者曰：「仁者人也，合而言之，道也。」夫人而具此仁，則爲人；人而體此仁，則爲道。是道與仁誠非二致，而體仁之功乃繫於人也。是不可見聖人立教之意，而學之正傳在是乎？夫何說之者之好爲異，以爲聖人之言未盡也，而思以足之？於是競求所以釋夫仁者。蓋自漢世以恩愛爲仁，至唐韓愈主之之過，遂以博愛名之，今原道所言是也。又至謝良佐矯之之過，遂以知覺名之，今桃仁杏仁之喻是也。殊不知仁體也，愛
translation_en:
…was entirely concerned with benevolence. Yet what appeared in his questions and answers amounted merely to overcoming oneself and returning to ritual propriety, maintaining reverence and practicing reciprocity, putting the difficult task first and its rewards afterward, and being hesitant in speech. He scarcely spoke directly of benevolence. Could this have been because he concealed something? Benevolence is indeed difficult to express in words; it must be apprehended in the heart. Only by applying oneself to these several practices can benevolence be sought.

Zisi received the transmission from the Master and recorded in the Doctrine of the Mean: “Cultivate oneself through the Way, and cultivate the Way through benevolence.” If the self is cultivated through the Way, and the Way through benevolence, then benevolence and the Way are certainly not two separate things; the responsibility for cultivating the Way truly rests with the individual. Mengzi received the transmission from Zisi and recorded in his seven books: “Benevolence is being human. Taken together, they constitute the Way.” A person who possesses this benevolence is human; a person who embodies this benevolence realizes the Way. Thus the Way and benevolence truly do not differ in their ultimate import, and the work of embodying benevolence depends upon the individual. Can we not see here the sages’ intention in establishing their teaching, and that the orthodox transmission of learning lies in this?

Why, then, are those who expound it so fond of differing, believing that the sages’ words are incomplete and wishing to supplement them? They consequently compete to find explanations of benevolence. From Han times, kindness and affection were taken to be benevolence. In the Tang, Han Yu carried his endorsement of this view too far and named it “universal love”; this is what is said in his Inquiry into the Way. Later, Xie Liangzuo went too far in correcting this view and named it “awareness”; this is the point of the analogy of peach and apricot kernels. They utterly failed to understand that benevolence is the substance, while love …

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
用也仁者物無不愛雖可以徵其爲用之
廣而直謂之仁則是不究夫體用之辯惻
隱之心仁也是非之心智也仁者心有知
覺雖可以見其包智之用而直謂之仁則
是不審夫仁智之殊獨尹焞所謂公者庶
幾近之然公所以體仁不可以言仁善乎
程子之言曰仁者必愛指愛爲仁則不可
不仁者無所知覺指知覺爲仁則不可又
曰公只是仁之理不可將公便喚做仁蓋
===
有以斷乎此矣愚故曰學有正傳而失焉
者說之者之好爲異也朱子集諸儒之大
成闡四德之名義其於仁曰心之德愛之
理蓋孔子所未發也然仁者天地生物之
心而人得之以爲心方其未發四德具焉
曰仁義禮智而仁無不統及其已發四端
著焉曰惻隱羞惡辭遜是非而惻隱之心
無不通則其指以爲心之德而義禮智不
得竝焉宜矣仁以言乎其理渾然在中而
punctuated:
用也。仁者物無不愛，雖可以徵其爲用之廣，而直謂之仁，則是不究夫體用之辯。惻隱之心，仁也；是非之心，智也。仁者心有知覺，雖可以見其包智之用，而直謂之仁，則是不審夫仁智之殊。獨尹焞所謂公者，庶幾近之。然公所以體仁，不可以言仁。善乎程子之言曰：「仁者必愛，指愛爲仁則不可；不仁者無所知覺，指知覺爲仁則不可。」又曰：「公只是仁之理，不可將公便喚做仁。」蓋有以斷乎此矣。愚故曰：「學有正傳，而失焉者，說之者之好爲異也。」
朱子集諸儒之大成，闡四德之名義，其於仁曰：「心之德，愛之理。」蓋孔子所未發也。然仁者天地生物之心，而人得之以爲心。方其未發，四德具焉，曰仁義禮智，而仁無不統；及其已發，四端著焉，曰惻隱、羞惡、辭遜、是非，而惻隱之心無不通。則其指以爲心之德，而義禮智不得竝焉，宜矣。仁以言乎其理，渾然在中而
translation_en:
…is its function. The benevolent person loves all things without exception. Although this can attest to the breadth of benevolence’s functioning, to identify love directly as benevolence is to fail to investigate the distinction between substance and function. The heart of compassion is benevolence; the heart that distinguishes right from wrong is wisdom. The benevolent person’s heart possesses awareness. Although this shows that benevolence encompasses the functioning of wisdom, to identify awareness directly as benevolence is to fail to discern the difference between benevolence and wisdom. Only what Yin Tun called impartiality comes close. Yet impartiality is the means of embodying benevolence; it cannot be called benevolence itself. How apt are Master Cheng’s words: “The benevolent person necessarily loves, but one cannot identify love as benevolence. Those without benevolence lack awareness, but one cannot identify awareness as benevolence.” He also said: “Impartiality is simply the principle of benevolence; one cannot take impartiality and simply call it benevolence.” These words surely settle the matter. Thus I humbly say: “Learning has an orthodox transmission; its loss results from interpreters’ fondness for making their explanations different.”
Master Zhu brought the achievements of the various Confucian scholars to their fullest expression and elucidated the names and meanings of the four virtues. Of benevolence he said: “The virtue of the heart and the principle of love.” This was something Confucius had not explicitly expounded. Yet benevolence is the heart through which Heaven and Earth engender things, and human beings receive it as their own heart. Before it is aroused, the four virtues are fully present—benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom—and benevolence encompasses them all. Once it is aroused, the four beginnings become manifest—compassion, shame and aversion, deference and yielding, and the discernment of right and wrong—and the heart of compassion pervades them all. It is therefore fitting that he identified benevolence as the virtue of the heart, with righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom unable to stand alongside it as equals. As for benevolence considered in terms of its principle, it resides within as an undivided whole, and…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
所謂愛者出焉而不窮愛以言乎其事充
然各足而所謂仁者資之而無盡則其指
以爲愛之理對夫義之宜禮之敬智之知
而言之宜矣是不可見朱子精義之極而
道之定論在是乎夫何學之者之不知求
以爲朱子之言未然也而思以易之於是
復取昔人之論仁者或進而托於程子一
體之說以爲仁之惻怛慈愛必如是乃可
以名也或近而守夫謝氏知覺之說以爲
===
仁之周流貫徹必如是乃可以名也殊不
知愛之在人其理雖一而其分則殊專主
夫愛則於所謂分之殊者有未明而將淪
於兼愛之失心之在人其覺雖同而理慾
則異專主夫覺則於所謂理與慾者有不
察而將昧夫精一之宗善乎朱子之言曰
泛言同體者使人含胡昏緩而無警切之
功其弊或至認物爲已者有之專言知覺
者使人張皇躁迫而無沉潛之味其弊或
punctuated: 所謂愛者出焉而不窮。愛以言乎其事，充然各足，而所謂仁者資之而無盡，則其指以爲愛之理，對夫義之宜、禮之敬、智之知而言之，宜矣。是不可見朱子精義之極，而道之定論在是乎？夫何學之者之不知求，以爲朱子之言未然也，而思以易之？於是復取昔人之論仁者，或進而托於程子一體之說，以爲仁之惻怛慈愛必如是乃可以名也；或近而守夫謝氏知覺之說，以爲仁之周流貫徹必如是乃可以名也。殊不知愛之在人，其理雖一，而其分則殊；專主夫愛，則於所謂分之殊者有未明，而將淪於兼愛之失。心之在人，其覺雖同，而理慾則異；專主夫覺，則於所謂理與慾者有不察，而將昧夫精一之宗。善乎朱子之言曰：「泛言同體者，使人含胡昏緩而無警切之功，其弊或至認物爲已者有之；專言知覺者，使人張皇躁迫而無沉潛之味，其弊或
translation_en:
…what is called love issues from it inexhaustibly. Speaking of love in terms of its concrete workings, it is abundantly sufficient in each instance, while what is called humaneness supplies it without end. Thus it is fitting to identify humaneness as the principle of love, speaking of it alongside the appropriateness of righteousness, the reverence of ritual propriety, and the discernment of wisdom. Does this not show the utmost refinement of Zhu Xi’s understanding of moral principles, and that here lies the definitive account of the Way? Why, then, do students fail to seek understanding, consider Zhu Xi’s words incorrect, and think of replacing them? They consequently return to earlier discussions of humaneness. Some go further and appeal to Master Cheng’s doctrine of forming one body, believing that only in these terms can the compassion and loving care of humaneness be named. Others take the nearer approach of adhering to Master Xie’s doctrine of awareness, believing that only in these terms can the all-pervading operation of humaneness be named.

They fail utterly to understand that, although the principle of love in human beings is one, its allotted obligations differ. If one concentrates exclusively on love, one fails to understand these differences and will lapse into the error of indiscriminate love. Although the capacity for awareness in the human mind is shared by all, moral principle and desire are distinct. If one concentrates exclusively on awareness, one fails to distinguish principle from desire and will lose sight of the essential teaching of refinement and single-mindedness.

How well Zhu Xi expressed it: “Those who speak vaguely of forming one body make people muddled, benighted, and slack, without the benefit of vigilant self-examination. In some cases, this error even leads them to take external things as the self [?]. Those who speak exclusively of awareness make people agitated and impatient, without a taste for deep, sustained contemplation. This error may…”

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
至認欲爲理者有之蓋已預憂乎此矣愚
故曰道有定論而晦焉者學之者之不知
求也然則執事爲今之計將若之何請戒
於衆曰爾欲求仁有孔子之正傳在焉愼
毋侮聖人守之可也爾欲言仁有朱子之
定論存焉愼毋小朱子信之可也如是而
日申飭之士固當盼其趨矣由是而又申
飭之則士眞積之久將自有以識夫仁體
而所謂定論者不至於晦體驗之深將自
===
不能已於求仁而所謂正傳者不至於亡
交養而互發執事之憂庶幾其免夫狂瞽
之言未知是否惟進敎之幸甚
第三問
同考試官敎諭胡　批〔敎爲詳明吾子之學之識　〕
葉龍
可槩見矣
同考試官敎諭葉　批〔宗主之良論千是策者亦　景行先哲而愼厥藩屛者平錄之〕
punctuated:
至認欲爲理者有之。」蓋已預憂乎此矣。愚故曰：「道有定論，而晦焉者，學之者之不知求也。」然則執事爲今之計，將若之何？請戒於衆曰：「爾欲求仁，有孔子之正傳在焉，愼毋侮聖人，守之可也；爾欲言仁，有朱子之定論存焉，愼毋小朱子，信之可也。」如是而日申飭之，士固當盼其趨矣。由是而又申飭之，則士眞積之久，將自有以識夫仁體，而所謂定論者不至於晦；體驗之深，將自不能已於求仁，而所謂正傳者不至於亡。交養而互發，執事之憂，庶幾其免夫！狂瞽之言，未知是否，惟進敎之，幸甚！

第三問

同考試官敎諭胡，批〔敎爲詳明，吾子之學之識。〕
葉龍
可槩見矣。
同考試官敎諭葉，批〔宗主之良，論千是策者亦，景行先哲而愼厥藩屛者平，錄之。〕
translation_en:
…some even come to mistake desire for principle.” He had evidently already foreseen this danger. Thus I venture to say: “There is a settled account of the Way; if it becomes obscured, it is because those who study it do not know how to seek it.” What, then, should you do under present circumstances? I ask that you admonish the assembled scholars: “If you wish to seek humaneness, the orthodox transmission of Confucius is there for you. Take care not to slight the sage; hold fast to it. If you wish to speak of humaneness, Master Zhu’s settled account remains available. Take care not to belittle Master Zhu; put your trust in it.” If you repeat these admonitions daily, one may surely expect scholars to turn toward it [?]. If you continue to admonish them, then, through prolonged accumulation of genuine effort, they will come of themselves to recognize the essential nature of humaneness, and the settled account will not become obscured. Through profound personal examination and experience, they will become unable to cease seeking humaneness, and the orthodox transmission will not be lost. These will nourish and illuminate one another, and you may thereby be relieved of your concern! These are rash and unenlightened words; I do not know whether they are correct. I would be most grateful for your further instruction.

Third Question

Comment by Associate Examiner Hu, School Instructor: “The exposition is detailed and clear [?]; your learning and discernment…”

Ye Long

“…can be seen in broad outline.” [This appears to complete Hu’s comment, interrupted in the transcription by the name.]

Comment by Associate Examiner Ye, School Instructor: “The excellence of the authority taken as one’s guide [?] … the writer of this policy essay also … admires and follows the former worthies and carefully guards their protective boundaries [?]. Accept it.” [The transcribed comment is garbled.]

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭葉　批〔該博之學精確之見無踰〕
〔子者宜置前列〕
考試官教授伍　批〔考事尚賢可以風矣〕
論封建於三代之下師其意而已矣求人
才於封建之外取其志而已矣封建其起
於理乎緣於情乎成於勢乎理所賢者共
而不及惡德情先乎九族而後萬邦勢則
宜於古而尼於今吾見封建之難復也雖
然後世之封建已與古意異矣後世之封
===
建之科目又與封建之意異矣封建之科
目之不究其用又與科目之意異矣勢不
同而理同吾求同理而已遑恤乎其他是
故不車服而榮不爵賞而勸隨其所遭而
吾無與焉豈不誠志士哉南宋之諸趙是
已於戲彼皆江右之產而科目之良也孰
事舉以為問豈欲求才於封建之外而論
治於三代之上乎愚獨以為非封建意也
是故知勢者則不必襲古以為濾知情者
punctuated:
考試官教諭葉，批〔該博之學，精確之見，無踰〕〔子者，宜置前列。〕
考試官教授伍，批〔考事尚賢，可以風矣。〕
論封建於三代之下，師其意而已矣；求人 才於封建之外，取其志而已矣。封建，其起於理乎？緣於情乎？成於勢乎？理所賢者共，而不及惡德；情先乎九族，而後萬邦；勢則宜於古，而尼於今。吾見封建之難復也。雖然，後世之封建，已與古意異矣；後世之封建之科目，又與封建之意異矣；封建之科目之不究其用，又與科目之意異矣。勢不同而理同，吾求同理而已，遑恤乎其他？是故不車服而榮，不爵賞而勸，隨其所遭，而吾無與焉。豈不誠志士哉？南宋之諸趙是已。於戲！彼皆江右之產，而科目之良也。孰事舉以為問，豈欲求才於封建之外，而論治於三代之上乎？愚獨以為非封建意也。是故知勢者，則不必襲古以為濾；知情者
translation_en:
Examiner Ye, Instructor, comments: 〔“In breadth of learning and precision of judgment, none surpass〕〔you. You should be placed among the foremost.”〕
Examiner Wu, Professor, comments: 〔“Examining past affairs and esteeming the worthy: this can serve as an example to others.”〕
To discuss enfeoffment in the ages after the Three Dynasties is simply to emulate its intent; to seek talented men outside enfeoffment is simply to value their aspirations. Did enfeoffment arise from principle, originate in human attachments, or take shape through circumstances? In principle, those deemed worthy share in it, while men of evil character are excluded. In human attachments, the nine degrees of kinship come first, and the myriad states afterward. As for circumstances, they favored it in antiquity but obstruct it today. I see how difficult it would be to restore enfeoffment. Nevertheless, the enfeoffment of later ages already differed from the ancient intent. The examination categories associated with later enfeoffment [?] differed in turn from the intent of enfeoffment; and the failure of these examination categories to fulfill their function differed again from the intent of the examinations. Circumstances differ, but principle is the same. I seek only that common principle; what leisure have I to concern myself with anything else?
Thus there are men who feel honored without ceremonial carriages and robes, and encouraged without ranks and rewards. Whatever circumstances they encounter, they remain personally unconcerned. Are they not truly men of high aspirations? Such were the various Zhaos of the Southern Song. Ah! They were all natives of Jiangyou and outstanding men selected through the examinations. These affairs have been raised as a question [?]: is the intention to seek talent outside enfeoffment and discuss government reaching back beyond the Three Dynasties? In my humble view, this alone is not the intent of enfeoffment.
Thus those who understand circumstances need not imitate antiquity as their guiding consideration [?]; those who understand human attachments…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
則不必易今以爲治知理者則不必達天
以病民合是三者神而明之無封建無郡
縣而同歸於治無世官無科目而同歸於
才亦何庸心其間必爲此而不爲彼哉且
秦取天下而郡縣之而守令不以賢聞漢
更郡國而分置之而諸侯王數至僭叛人
才之不係於封建與否也明矣唐猶漢也
而隴西未嘗無賢士宋猶唐也而南渡未
嘗無善人人才之不係於世官與否也亦
明矣姑以江右論之昌邑肇封於漢世遠
而莫究元嬰胙土于唐枝散而日微可考
者其惟南宋之宗室乎時則有若善應之
刺血和藥崇憲之表明父心事雖不同而
同爲孝良淳之死守孤城時倚之以身殉
主地雖不同而同爲忠人稱趙母則有彥
端力變士風則有與清其政事何如也師
晦菴而究心理學則有汝靚請漕舉而苦
志詩賦則有希晉其文學何如也至若必
punctuated:
則不必易今以爲治；知理者，則不必達天以病民。合是三者，神而明之，無封建，無郡縣，而同歸於治；無世官，無科目，而同歸於才。亦何庸心其間，必爲此而不爲彼哉？且秦取天下而郡縣之，而守令不以賢聞；漢更郡國而分置之，而諸侯王數至僭叛。人才之不係於封建與否也，明矣。唐猶漢也，而隴西未嘗無賢士；宋猶唐也，而南渡未嘗無善人。人才之不係於世官與否也，亦明矣。

姑以江右論之：昌邑肇封於漢，世遠而莫究；元嬰胙土于唐，枝散而日微。可考者，其惟南宋之宗室乎？時則有若善應之刺血和藥，崇憲之表明父心，事雖不同，而同爲孝；良淳之死守孤城，時倚之以身殉主，地雖不同，而同爲忠。人稱趙母，則有彥端；力變士風，則有與清。其政事何如也？師晦菴而究心理學，則有汝靚；請漕舉而苦志詩賦，則有希晉。其文學何如也？至若必
translation_en:
…then one need not alter present institutions to achieve good government; those who understand principle need not “reach Heaven” [?] and thereby afflict the people. Combine these three kinds of understanding and apply them with inspired discernment: whether enfeoffment or prefectures and counties, both can lead to good government; whether hereditary office or examination recruitment, both can yield talent. Why trouble oneself over the distinction, insisting upon this and rejecting that? Qin seized the realm and organized it into prefectures and counties, yet its prefects and magistrates were not renowned for worthiness. Han reconfigured the prefectures and kingdoms, establishing them separately, yet its feudatory kings repeatedly resorted to usurpation and rebellion. Clearly, the presence of talented men does not depend on whether enfeoffment exists. Tang was like Han, yet Longxi never lacked worthy scholars; Song was like Tang, yet after the southward transfer of the court it never lacked good men. Clearly, too, the presence of talented men does not depend on whether offices are hereditary.

Let us consider Jiangyou alone. The Prince of Changyi was first enfeoffed there under Han, but that age is too distant for thorough investigation. Yuanying received a territorial grant under Tang, but his descendants dispersed and dwindled day by day. Those whose deeds can be examined are perhaps chiefly members of the Southern Song imperial clan. Among them were Zhao Shanying, who drew his own blood to mix with medicine, and Zhao Chongxian, who made his father’s intentions manifest: their deeds differed, but both exemplified filial devotion. Zhao Liangchun died defending an isolated city, and Zhao Shiyi sacrificed his life for his lord: their circumstances differed, but both exemplified loyalty. There was Zhao Yanduan, whom people called “Mother Zhao,” and Zhao Yuqing, who vigorously reformed the conduct of scholars. How admirable were their achievements in government! There was Zhao Rujing, who studied under Hui’an and devoted himself to the learning of principle, and Zhao Xijin, who sought recommendation through the Transport Commission’s examination and diligently applied himself to poetry and rhapsodies. How admirable were their literary accomplishments! As for Bi…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
願早聞忠義之訓善堅勵志廉能之節可
以語行誼矣不黜退居錦水而以樂善名
汝偵其守布衣而以固窮著可以語清脩
矣之數人者或起於科目或老于山林而
其立身行事之節有如此而吾所尊仰之
者則惟丞相汝愚而已好善忘勢有仕優
則學之風正色立朝有國爾忘家之節其
期待也則以司馬光富弼韓琦范仲淹爲
已任其淵源也則以朱熹張栻吕祖謙王
===
十朋汪應辰爲師友忠結人主而有文武
威風之稱行乎于朝而有忠孝大節之薦
是蓋不徒誓志於功名而實任道之器也
豈直一鄉之望而已哉使寧宗而竟其用
則其施爲氣象將必有可觀者而中興之
功易與也夫以韓侂胄爲之搆讒京鏜爲
之傅議李沐爲之疏詆正謂市虎三人能
保其不爲永之行乎雖然吾惜其辭相之
不力也宗室不爲宰執高宗之訓也而汝
punctuated: 願早聞忠義之訓，善堅勵志廉能之節，可以語行誼矣。不黜退居錦水而以樂善名，汝偵其守布衣而以固窮著，可以語清脩矣。之數人者，或起於科目，或老于山林，而其立身行事之節有如此。而吾所尊仰之者，則惟丞相汝愚而已。好善忘勢，有仕優則學之風；正色立朝，有國爾忘家之節。其期待也，則以司馬光、富弼、韓琦、范仲淹爲已任；其淵源也，則以朱熹、張栻、吕祖謙、王十朋、汪應辰爲師友。忠結人主，而有文武威風之稱；行乎于朝，而有忠孝大節之薦。是蓋不徒誓志於功名，而實任道之器也。豈直一鄉之望而已哉！使寧宗而竟其用，則其施爲氣象將必有可觀者，而中興之功易與也。夫以韓侂胄爲之搆讒，京鏜爲之傅議，李沐爲之疏詆，正謂市虎三人，能保其不爲永之行乎？雖然，吾惜其辭相之不力也。宗室不爲宰執，高宗之訓也，而汝
translation_en:
…Biyuan early received instruction in loyalty and righteousness, while Shanjian set his resolve upon integrity and competence: their conduct merits discussion. Buchu retired to Jinshui and became known for delighting in good deeds; Ruzhen remained a commoner and gained renown for steadfastness in poverty. Their purity of conduct merits discussion. These men either rose through the examinations or grew old in retirement among the mountains and forests, yet such was the integrity with which they conducted their lives and affairs.

The one whom I revere, however, is Chief Councilor Ruyu alone. He loved goodness and disregarded his power and standing, exemplifying the principle that one who has strength to spare after official service should study. He stood solemnly at court, displaying the integrity of one who forgets his family in devotion to the state. In his aspirations, he took it upon himself to emulate Sima Guang, Fu Bi, Han Qi, and Fan Zhongyan; in the sources of his learning, he had Zhu Xi, Zhang Shi, Lü Zuqian, Wang Shipeng, and Wang Yingchen as teachers and friends. His loyalty bound him to his sovereign, and he was praised for his commanding presence in both civil and military affairs. His conduct at court [?] won him recommendations for his outstanding loyalty and filial devotion. He was thus not merely committed to achievement and reputation, but truly a man capable of bearing responsibility for the Way. How could he have been merely the pride of a single locality?

Had Ningzong employed him to the fullest, his accomplishments and bearing would surely have been impressive, and the achievement of dynastic restoration would have been readily attainable. But Han Tuozhou fabricated slanders against him, Jing Tang lent support to the accusations, and Li Mu submitted memorials vilifying him. This was precisely the case of three men reporting a tiger in the marketplace: could anyone guarantee that he would escape the journey to Yongzhou [?]? Nevertheless, I regret that he did not decline the chief councilorship more firmly. That members of the imperial clan should not serve as chief councilors or executive officials was Gaozong’s injunction; yet Ru…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
昧此乎然趙氏者又豈特一時之盛而已
哉使宋室而世其官則其夾輔忠貞又將
有可觀者而世臣之功可收也夫以崇憲
爲之子必愿爲之孫良淳爲之曾孫可謂
四世名德而獨無有知之者乎雖然吾惜
其逢時之不偶也人衆則能勝天往事之
監也而又何論乎方是時也晦菴千里命
駕詿騷以洩不平蓋不待良淳之身而已
決矣君子以是知忠賢之進退而百年之
===
氣運係之一門之盛衰而終宋之命脉係
之彼小人者所自爲謀則巧矣而其流至
于禍人家國而不悟亦獨何哉蓋嘗即宋
事而論之宋之立國也始於公天下而成
於私其身故其初也兄弟之太恩而其後
也子姓之不保其仁也優於養士而其濫
世畧於懿親羣臣任子九族不免乎編氓
罷政乞祠諸宗顧以之應舉儌之以先王
親睦之風誠無以望其後求諸大易通變
punctuated:
昧此乎？然趙氏者，又豈特一時之盛而已哉？使宋室而世其官，則其夾輔忠貞又將有可觀者，而世臣之功可收也。夫以崇憲爲之子，必愿爲之孫，良淳爲之曾孫，可謂四世名德，而獨無有知之者乎？雖然，吾惜其逢時之不偶也。人衆則能勝天，往事之監也，而又何論乎？方是時也，晦菴千里命駕，詿騷以洩不平，蓋不待良淳之身而已決矣。君子以是知忠賢之進退，而百年之氣運係之；一門之盛衰，而終宋之命脉係之。彼小人者，所自爲謀則巧矣，而其流至于禍人家國而不悟，亦獨何哉？

蓋嘗即宋事而論之：宋之立國也，始於公天下，而成於私其身。故其初也，兄弟之太恩；而其後也，子姓之不保。其仁也，優於養士，而其濫世畧於懿親。羣臣任子，九族不免乎編氓；罷政乞祠，諸宗顧以之應舉。儌之以先王親睦之風，誠無以望其後；求諸大易通變
translation_en:
…be unaware of this? Yet was the flourishing of this Zhao family confined to a single age? Had the Song ruling house allowed its offices to pass from generation to generation, the family’s loyal and steadfast support would again have been worthy of admiration, and the benefits of service by hereditary ministers could have been secured. With Chongxian as his son, Biyuan as his grandson, and Liangchun as his great-grandson, theirs could indeed be called four generations renowned for virtue. Could there really have been no one who recognized this? Nevertheless, I lament that they encountered such unfavorable times. When men are numerous, they can overcome Heaven: past events offer this warning. What more is there to say? At that time, Hui’an ordered his carriage prepared for a journey of a thousand li and expressed his indignation in a lament [?]. The outcome had already been decided, without waiting for Liangchun’s own lifetime. From this the gentleman understands that the fortunes of a hundred years depended on whether loyal and worthy men advanced or withdrew, and that the lifeblood of the Song, down to its end, depended on the flourishing or decline of a single family. Those petty men were clever enough in plotting for themselves; yet the consequences brought disaster upon others’ families and the state, and still they failed to understand. Why was this so?

I have considered the matter in light of Song history. The establishment of the Song began with treating the realm as a public trust, but was completed through concern for private interests. Thus, at the beginning there was extraordinary kindness between brothers, while afterward their descendants could not be protected. Its benevolence was generous in nurturing scholars, yet in its disordered later age [?] it neglected close imperial kin. Officials could secure appointments for their sons through hereditary privilege, while members of the imperial lineage, within the nine degrees of kinship, could not escape being registered as commoners. Officials retired from government and requested temple sinecures, yet members of the imperial clan used these to present themselves for the examinations [?]. If measured against the ancient kings’ practice of maintaining affection and harmony among kin [?], there was truly no prospect of matching their example. If one seeks in the great Book of Changes the principle of adapting to change…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
之道彼固以爲得之矣然而豪傑之才固
無恃乎門第神明之冑終弗類乎寒微卒
能以其忠孝之姿而赴功名之會入而爲
良相出而爲賢牧生而爲善士死而爲忠
臣炳炳乎起而爲中原文獻之傳此豈爵
祿名寵之所能勸而封建科目之所能限
者哉愚以是知有志之士無所待而猶興
者雖以宋之宗室猶能自飭其身自淑其
政以爲國家之重則凡爲今日之
===
藩國者
祖宗之富貴若此
朝廷之親愛若此又將何以爲報哉然非欲
其舉成法而棄之讀書業科舉効儒生輩
爲也亦曰
祖訓者
皇祖之家灋也守之以不越則自有餘貴矣境
內者
天子之子民也居之以不擾則自有餘富矣故
punctuated:
之道，彼固以爲得之矣。然而豪傑之才，固無恃乎門第；神明之冑，終弗類乎寒微。卒能以其忠孝之姿，而赴功名之會，入而爲良相，出而爲賢牧，生而爲善士，死而爲忠臣，炳炳乎起而爲中原文獻之傳。此豈爵祿名寵之所能勸，而封建科目之所能限者哉？愚以是知有志之士，無所待而猶興者。雖以宋之宗室，猶能自飭其身，自淑其政，以爲國家之重，則凡爲今日之藩國者，祖宗之富貴若此，朝廷之親愛若此，又將何以爲報哉？
然非欲其舉成法而棄之，讀書業科舉，効儒生輩爲也。亦曰：祖訓者，皇祖之家灋也，守之以不越，則自有餘貴矣；境內者，天子之子民也，居之以不擾，則自有餘富矣。故
translation_en:
…the Way, they certainly believed they had grasped it. Yet outstanding talent assuredly does not depend upon family standing, and the descendants of divine sovereigns are, after all, unlike those of humble origins. Ultimately, their qualities of loyalty and filial devotion enabled them to seize opportunities for achievement and distinction: serving at court, they became worthy chief councilors; serving in the provinces, worthy governors; in life, good men; and in death, loyal ministers. They rose in brilliance to carry on the cultural heritage of the Central Plains. Could such men be spurred on merely by rank, emoluments, reputation, and favor, or confined by the institutions of enfeoffment and examination categories? From this I humbly understand that men of aspiration rise even without awaiting external encouragement. Even members of the Song imperial clan could discipline their own conduct and improve their administration, becoming pillars of the state. How, then, will all those who hold princely domains today repay the wealth and honor bestowed by their ancestors and the affection shown them by the court?
Yet this does not mean wishing them to discard established statutes wholesale, study books, and pursue the examinations in imitation of Confucian students. It means only this: the Ancestral Instructions are the imperial founding ancestor’s household laws. By observing them without transgression, they will naturally have honor in abundance. Those within their domains are the Son of Heaven’s subjects, whom he cherishes as his children. By dwelling among them without disturbing them, they will naturally have wealth in abundance. Therefore…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
曰居上不驕高而不危所以長守貴也制
節謹度滿而不溢所以長守富也是謂無
所事事而有利於國與民夫無所事事之
利與有所事事而未必利者其勞逸難易
奚啻十百千萬莫之禁而弗爲豈不大有
負於時乎於戲此義行則不惟爵封兹土
者之知所以勸而凡天下之爲王國者靡
不竭忠夾輔以綿我
國家無疆之休矣故曰師其意也以此
===
第四問　江鯤
同考試官教諭李　批〔五策條答無遺而此尤有天下之慮此篇拔其尤者〕
同考試官教諭林　批〔談錢幣有通變之術可謂識時務者〕
考試官教諭葉　批〔考古而不遺酌今而不泥有用之才也〕
考試官教授伍　批〔知今言國用具有□□〕
punctuated:
曰：「居上不驕，高而不危，所以長守貴也；制節謹度，滿而不溢，所以長守富也。」是謂無所事事而有利於國與民。夫無所事事之利，與有所事事而未必利者，其勞逸難易，奚啻十百千萬！莫之禁而弗爲，豈不大有負於時乎？於戲！此義行，則不惟爵封兹土者之知所以勸，而凡天下之爲王國者，靡不竭忠夾輔，以綿我國家無疆之休矣。故曰師其意也，以此。

第四問，江鯤。
同考試官教諭李，批〔五策條答無遺，而此尤有天下之慮，此篇拔其尤者。〕
同考試官教諭林，批〔談錢幣有通變之術，可謂識時務者。〕
考試官教諭葉，批〔考古而不遺，酌今而不泥，有用之才也。〕
考試官教授伍，批〔知今言國用，具有□□。〕
translation_en:
…it says: “Occupying a superior position without arrogance, one stands high without peril: this is how one preserves noble rank for long. Exercising restraint and carefully observing limits, one is full without overflowing: this is how one preserves wealth for long.” This is what is meant by benefiting the state and the people without undertaking any activity. Between the benefits of undertaking no activity and undertaking activities that may not prove beneficial, the difference in toil and ease, difficulty and simplicity, is surely more than tenfold, a hundredfold, a thousandfold, or ten thousandfold! If nothing prohibits this course, yet one fails to follow it, does one not gravely fail the age? Ah! If this principle is put into practice, not only will those enfeoffed with noble rank in this territory know what should spur them to exertion; all who hold princely domains throughout the realm will exhaust their loyalty in supporting the throne, thereby perpetuating the boundless blessings of our state. This is why I said that one should emulate its intent.

Fourth Question. Jiang Kun 江鯤.
Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “His five policy essays answer every point without omission, and this one especially displays concern for the whole realm. This essay has been selected as the most outstanding.”
Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: “His discussion of coinage offers methods for adapting to changing circumstances. He may be called someone who understands the needs of the times.”
Examiner Ye, Instructor, comments: “He investigates antiquity without omissions and weighs present circumstances without rigidity. He is a man of talent suited to practical service.”
Examiner Wu, Professor, comments: “He understands the present and discusses state expenditure, fully possessing [two illegible characters: □□][?].”

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
人君欲制用以足國則不可不通變以裕
民蓋天之立君本以治民而君之足國亦
惟以利民耳以利民爲心則用之詘也不
可不善其道以處之遷之弊也不可不通
其變以宜之民宜則百姓足君孰與不足
君足則百度舉天下又焉有不治哉愚讀
明問及此作而嘆曰是欲修政非爲理財
也欲裕民非爲足國也敢不掇拾以對粤
昔民之有生易於困也天必生財以資之
===
財之爲用易於乏也君必立法以理之是
故稻黍稷麥菽之五穀珠玉金刀布之三
幣非財之生於天者乎錢以濟穀幣之不
通鈔以補錢幣之不足非法之立於君者
乎蓋五穀可以取用而不可以致遠三幣
可以致遠而不可以常得則其勢不得不
趨於錢鈔矣夫三品之金銅爲下以之鑄
錢爲最宜是物也在陶唐氏謂之泉商人
謂之布齊人莒人謂之刀周人槩謂之帛
punctuated: 人君欲制用以足國，則不可不通變以裕民。蓋天之立君，本以治民，而君之足國，亦惟以利民耳。以利民爲心，則用之詘也，不可不善其道以處之；遷之弊也，不可不通其變以宜之。民宜則百姓足，君孰與不足？君足則百度舉，天下又焉有不治哉？愚讀明問及此，作而嘆曰：「是欲修政，非爲理財也；欲裕民，非爲足國也。」敢不掇拾以對？粤昔民之有生，易於困也，天必生財以資之；財之爲用，易於乏也，君必立法以理之。是故稻、黍、稷、麥、菽之五穀，珠玉、金、刀布之三幣，非財之生於天者乎？錢以濟穀幣之不通，鈔以補錢幣之不足，非法之立於君者乎？蓋五穀可以取用，而不可以致遠；三幣可以致遠，而不可以常得，則其勢不得不趨於錢鈔矣。夫三品之金，銅爲下，以之鑄錢爲最宜。是物也，在陶唐氏謂之泉，商人謂之布，齊人、莒人謂之刀，周人槩謂之帛，
translation_en:
If a ruler wishes to regulate expenditure so that the state has sufficient resources, he must adapt to changing circumstances so as to enrich the people. Heaven established rulers fundamentally to govern the people, and a ruler’s provision for the state likewise serves only to benefit them. With the people’s benefit at heart, when resources for expenditure fall short, he must devise sound means of addressing the shortage; when abuses arise in currency [?], he must make appropriate adaptations. When the people’s circumstances are favorable, the common people have enough; and when they have enough, how could the ruler alone lack sufficient resources? When the ruler has enough, all affairs of government can be carried out. How, then, could the realm fail to be well governed? Reading this far in your illuminating question, I rose and exclaimed: “This seeks to improve government, rather than merely manage finances; to enrich the people, rather than merely provide for the state.” How could I fail to gather what I know and offer a reply?

From ancient times, people have readily fallen into hardship in sustaining their lives, so Heaven necessarily produces wealth to support them. Wealth is readily exhausted through use, so rulers must establish regulations to manage it. Thus the five grains—rice, glutinous millet, millet, wheat, and beans—and the three forms of currency—pearls and jade, gold, and knife and spade money—are these not wealth produced by Heaven? Coin serves to overcome impediments to the circulation of grain and currency, while paper money supplements an insufficient supply of coin: are these not arrangements established by rulers? The five grains can be put to use, but cannot readily be conveyed over long distances; the three forms of currency can be conveyed over long distances, but cannot always be obtained. Circumstances therefore inevitably lead to the use of coin and paper money. Of the three grades of metal, copper ranks lowest, yet it is best suited to casting coins. This thing, under the Taotang ruler, was called quan, “spring”; the people of Shang called it bu, “cloth” or “spade money”; the people of Qi and Ju called it dao, “knife”; and the people of Zhou called it, in general, bo, “silk” [?] …

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
至景王鑄錢則謂之寳貨而錢始有文矣
後是或爲八銖四銖或爲開元通寳或爲
皇宋通寳及其弊也則有榆莢鵝眼二銖
四分而失之太輕又有赤仄半兩直百當
千而失之太重求其得中者其惟漢之五
銖唐之開元乎然孰若我
朝通寳爲最善夫百物之質楮爲輕以之制
鈔爲尤便是物也在漢謂之皮幣在唐謂
之飛錢在宋謂之便錢至蜀□守□謂
===
之交子而始用楮矣後是或爲錢引或爲
交鈔或爲兊會或爲會子及其衍也有一
界印一千百萬一界印三千萬萬而多寡
之不同有至元一貫準中統五貫有至大
一貫準至元五貫而貴賤之不同求其適
均者其惟宋之天聖元之中統乎然孰若
我
朝寳鈔爲最良夫錢之制既善則通之天下
而可行而行間□大都鈔之制既良
punctuated:
至景王鑄錢，則謂之寳貨，而錢始有文矣。後是，或爲八銖、四銖，或爲開元通寳，或爲皇宋通寳。及其弊也，則有榆莢、鵝眼、二銖、四分，而失之太輕；又有赤仄、半兩、直百、當千，而失之太重。求其得中者，其惟漢之五銖、唐之開元乎？然孰若我朝通寳爲最善？

夫百物之質，楮爲輕，以之制鈔爲尤便。是物也，在漢謂之皮幣，在唐謂之飛錢，在宋謂之便錢，至蜀□守□謂之交子，而始用楮矣。後是，或爲錢引，或爲交鈔，或爲兊會，或爲會子。及其衍也，有一界印一千百萬，一界印三千萬萬，而多寡之不同；有至元一貫準中統五貫，有至大一貫準至元五貫，而貴賤之不同。求其適均者，其惟宋之天聖、元之中統乎？然孰若我朝寳鈔爲最良？

夫錢之制既善，則通之天下而可行，而行間□大都。鈔之制既良
translation_en:
…By the time King Jing cast coins, they were called “precious currency,” and coins first bore inscriptions. Thereafter there were eight-zhu and four-zhu coins, Kaiyuan tongbao (“Circulating Treasure of the Kaiyuan Era”), and Huang Song tongbao (“Circulating Treasure of the Imperial Song”). When abuses arose, there were “elm-seed” and “goose-eye” coins, two-zhu coins, and four-fen coins, which erred by being too light; there were also “red-rim” and half-liang coins, coins worth a hundred, and coins worth a thousand, which erred by being too heavy. If we seek those that struck the proper balance, were they not the Han five-zhu coins and the Tang Kaiyuan coins? Yet how could any compare with the supreme excellence of our dynasty’s circulating treasure?

Of the materials used for all manner of things, paper is light, making it especially convenient for producing currency notes. This currency was called “hide currency” under the Han, “flying cash” under the Tang, and “convenient cash” under the Song. When it came to the [?] prefect [?] in Shu, it was called jiaozi (“exchange notes”), and paper first came into use. Thereafter there were qianyin (“cash certificates”), jiaochao (“exchange notes”), duihui (“exchange certificates”), and huizi (“notes”). As their issuance expanded, one issue might comprise eleven million, another three hundred billion [?], so that quantities differed. One string in Zhiyuan notes was equivalent to five strings in Zhongtong notes, while one string in Zhida notes was equivalent to five strings in Zhiyuan notes, so that values differed. If we seek those that achieved a suitable balance, were they not the notes of the Song Tiansheng era and the Yuan Zhongtong era? Yet how could any compare with the supreme excellence of our dynasty’s precious notes?

Since the system of coinage is sound, coins can circulate and be used throughout the realm; the following words concerning their circulation and the great capital are unclear [?]. Since the system of paper currency is sound…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
則推之後世而皆準而何分於草昧承平
然而猶有不能盡如立灋之始而多積於
無用者此無他不能通其變於未窮焉耳
且錢之稱爲泉布以其流通而無滯也鈔
而稱爲楮幣以其輕便均爲寶也今世之
用者惟銀幣是資自官府之催科以至民
間之貿易率惟是之害至於錢之用獨居
常小費而已錢安得不滯鈔之用特論功
議辟而已鈔安得可行錢鈔既輕則銀幣
===
益重銀重則用之者日不足而取之者盡
錙銖于是乎有輸粟之計有發礦之謀是
亦不得已而爲是權宜以紓
宵旰之憂以濟用度之急耳然輸粟若可也
而名器懼其或濫發礦若可也而採取未
免殃民二者誠非足國裕民之要道其惟
於錢鈔之用救其弊而使之不匱通其變
而使之宜民可矣何者錢不患其滯也立
灋以疏之則通鈔不患其輕也立灋以反
punctuated: 則推之後世而皆準，而何分於草昧承平？然而猶有不能盡如立灋之始，而多積於無用者，此無他，不能通其變於未窮焉耳。且錢之稱爲泉布，以其流通而無滯也；鈔而稱爲楮幣，以其輕便，均爲寶也。今世之用者，惟銀幣是資，自官府之催科，以至民間之貿易，率惟是之害。至於錢之用，獨居常小費而已，錢安得不滯？鈔之用，特論功議辟而已，鈔安得可行？錢鈔既輕，則銀幣益重；銀重，則用之者日不足，而取之者盡錙銖。于是乎有輸粟之計，有發礦之謀，是亦不得已而爲是權宜，以紓宵旰之憂，以濟用度之急耳。然輸粟若可也，而名器懼其或濫；發礦若可也，而採取未免殃民。二者誠非足國裕民之要道。其惟於錢鈔之用，救其弊而使之不匱，通其變而使之宜民，可矣。何者？錢不患其滯也，立灋以疏之則通；鈔不患其輕也，立灋以反
translation_en:
…then it can be extended to later ages and serve as a standard throughout. What distinction need there be between the unsettled beginnings of a dynasty and an age of peace? Yet its operation still cannot fully match that at the inception of the regulations, and much currency accumulates unused. There is no other reason for this than the failure to adapt it to changing circumstances before its possibilities are exhausted. Coins are called quanbu, “flowing currency,” because they circulate without obstruction; notes are called chubi, “paper currency,” because they are light and convenient. Both are treasures. Nowadays, however, people rely solely on silver as currency. From the authorities’ collection of taxes to trade among the people, all are generally harmed by this [?]. Coins are used only for small everyday expenses: how could their circulation fail to stagnate? Notes are used only in assessing rewards for merit and deliberating on punishments. How could they circulate? Once coins and notes lose value, silver becomes still more valuable. As silver grows dearer, those who use it find it increasingly insufficient, while those who exact it demand every last fraction of an ounce.

Hence the proposals for grain contributions and the plans to open mines. These, too, are merely expedients adopted under compulsion, to ease the worries that keep the emperor awake before dawn and occupied until late, and to meet urgent expenditure. Yet even if grain contributions seem acceptable, there is a fear that official titles and honors may be bestowed indiscriminately; even if opening mines seems acceptable, extraction will inevitably bring suffering upon the people. Neither is truly an essential means of enriching the state and bringing prosperity to the people. It would suffice to remedy the defects in the use of coins and notes so that their supply does not fail, and to adapt them to changing circumstances so that they benefit the people. Why is this? There need be no anxiety about the stagnation of coins: establish regulations to clear the obstructions, and they will circulate. There need be no anxiety about the low value of notes: establish regulations to reverse…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
之則重蓋錢之鑄本以濟幣之窮鈔之制
又以濟錢之乏玆欲錢鈔之行必别其大
小之分權其子母之勢於錢則分古今以
今之一而當古之二濫惡者不得雜於其
間於鈔則分新舊以舊之二而當新之一
折壞者不得預以爲算二者又皆以銀爲
準銀一分而準錢十文鈔十張而準銀一
分由是立爲一定之則凡有行使大約以
三分爲率雖銀之多也不得專用銀銀二
===
而錢居其一雖錢之多也不得專用錢錢
二而鈔居其一上而科派徵收下而輸納
懋遷率守是灋而罔俾踰易至於鈔重則
出錢以易鈔錢重則出鈔以易錢又必嚴
銅楮之禁絶僞造之奸謹關市之令杜越
境之私將見出於官者有以資於民入於
民者可以用之官錢鈔尚何有不行哉或
謂銀銅竝行未免爲幣則古有之矣周禮
內府掌邦之大用外府掌邦之小用準此
punctuated:
之則重。蓋錢之鑄，本以濟幣之窮；鈔之制，又以濟錢之乏。玆欲錢鈔之行，必别其大小之分，權其子母之勢。於錢則分古今，以今之一而當古之二，濫惡者不得雜於其間；於鈔則分新舊，以舊之二而當新之一，折壞者不得預以爲算。二者又皆以銀爲準：銀一分而準錢十文，鈔十張而準銀一分。由是立爲一定之則，凡有行使，大約以三分爲率。雖銀之多也，不得專用銀，銀二而錢居其一；雖錢之多也，不得專用錢，錢二而鈔居其一。上而科派徵收，下而輸納懋遷，率守是灋，而罔俾踰易。至於鈔重，則出錢以易鈔；錢重，則出鈔以易錢。又必嚴銅楮之禁，絶僞造之奸；謹關市之令，杜越境之私。將見出於官者有以資於民，入於民者可以用之官，錢鈔尚何有不行哉？

或謂銀銅竝行，未免爲幣，則古有之矣。《周禮》，內府掌邦之大用，外府掌邦之小用。準此
translation_en:
…it will then regain its value. Casting coins was originally intended to remedy a shortage of currency; instituting paper notes was in turn intended to remedy a shortage of coins. To ensure that coins and notes circulate now, we must distinguish their larger and smaller denominations and weigh their relative values. Coins should be distinguished as ancient or modern, with one modern coin counting as two ancient coins; inferior coins must not be allowed among them. Notes should be distinguished as new or old, with two old notes counting as one new note; torn or damaged notes must not be included in the reckoning. Both should also be valued against silver: one fen of silver should equal ten cash, and ten notes should equal one fen of silver. These ratios should establish a fixed standard. All payments should generally follow a rule of three parts. Even where silver is plentiful, silver alone must not be used: two parts should be silver and one part coins. Even where coins are plentiful, coins alone must not be used: two parts should be coins and one part notes. From official assessments and collections above to remittances and commercial exchanges below, all should observe this rule, without allowing departures or alterations. When notes rise in value, coins should be issued in exchange for notes; when coins rise in value, notes should be issued in exchange for coins. Restrictions on copper and paper currency must also be strictly enforced to eliminate counterfeiting, and regulations at customs barriers and markets carefully upheld to prevent illicit movements across the borders. We shall then see that what the authorities issue supplies the people’s needs, and what comes into the people’s hands can be used in payments to the authorities. How could coins and notes then fail to circulate?

Some may say that circulating silver and copper together will inevitably entail abuses [?]. Yet there was precedent for this in antiquity. In the Rites of Zhou, the Inner Treasury administered the state’s major expenditures, and the Outer Treasury its minor expenditures. Taking this as the standard…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
之則重蓋錢之鑄本以濟幣之窮鈔之制
又以濟錢之乏玆欲錢鈔之行必別其大
小之分雜其子母之勢於錢則分古今以
今之一而當古之二濫惡者不得雜於其
間於鈔則分新舊以舊之二而當新之一
折壞者不得預以爲算二者又皆以銀爲
準銀一分而準錢十文鈔十張而準銀一
分由是立爲一定之則凡有行使大約以
三分爲率雖銀之多也不得專用銀銀二
===
而錢居其一雖錢之多也不得專用錢錢
二而鈔居其一上而科派徵收下而輸納
懋遷率守是灋而罔俾踰易至於鈔重則
出錢以易鈔錢重則出鈔以易錢又必嚴
銅楮之禁絶僞造之奸謹關市之令杜越
境之私將見出於官者有以資於民入於
民者可以用之官錢鈔尚何有不行哉或
謂銀銅竝行未免爲擾則古有之矣周禮
內府掌邦之大用外府掌邦之小用準此
punctuated: 之則重。蓋錢之鑄，本以濟幣之窮；鈔之制，又以濟錢之乏。玆欲錢鈔之行，必別其大小之分，雜其子母之勢。於錢則分古今，以今之一而當古之二，濫惡者不得雜於其間；於鈔則分新舊，以舊之二而當新之一，折壞者不得預以爲算。二者又皆以銀爲準，銀一分而準錢十文，鈔十張而準銀一分。由是立爲一定之則，凡有行使，大約以三分爲率。雖銀之多也，不得專用銀，銀二而錢居其一；雖錢之多也，不得專用錢，錢二而鈔居其一。上而科派徵收，下而輸納懋遷，率守是灋，而罔俾踰易。至於鈔重，則出錢以易鈔；錢重，則出鈔以易錢。又必嚴銅楮之禁，絶僞造之奸；謹關市之令，杜越境之私。將見出於官者有以資於民，入於民者可以用之官，錢鈔尚何有不行哉？或謂銀銅竝行，未免爲擾，則古有之矣。《周禮》內府掌邦之大用，外府掌邦之小用。準此
translation_en: …it then becomes dear [?]. Casting copper cash was originally intended to remedy a shortage of currency; issuing paper notes was likewise intended to remedy a shortage of cash. To secure the circulation of cash and notes now, we must distinguish their greater and lesser denominations and combine their relative roles as “mother” and “child.” For cash, distinguish ancient from present-day coins: one present-day coin should equal two ancient coins, and inferior coins must not be mixed among them. For notes, distinguish new from old: two old notes should equal one new note, and torn or damaged notes must not be counted. Both should moreover be valued against silver: one fen of silver should equal ten cash, and ten paper notes should equal one fen of silver. Establish these as fixed rules. All payments should generally follow a ratio expressed in three parts. Even where silver is abundant, silver alone must not be used: two parts should be silver and one part cash. Even where cash is abundant, cash alone must not be used: two parts should be cash and one part notes. From the authorities’ assessment and collection of levies to the people’s payment of taxes and exchange of goods, all should observe these rules, without being allowed to evade or alter them. When notes become dear, issue cash in exchange for notes; when cash becomes dear, issue notes in exchange for cash. Furthermore, strictly enforce the prohibitions governing copper coin and paper currency, putting an end to counterfeiting; carefully enforce the regulations at customs barriers and markets, preventing cross-border smuggling. We shall then see currency issued by the authorities serving the people’s needs, and currency received by the people usable in payments to the authorities. How could cash and notes still fail to circulate? Some may say that circulating silver and copper together inevitably causes disruption; yet there was precedent for this in antiquity. In the Rites of Zhou, the Inner Treasury managed the state’s major expenditures, and the Outer Treasury its minor expenditures. Following this precedent…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
以銀爲大用錢爲小用又何不可乎又謂
銅楮錯用日見其勞則古又有之矣單穆
公曰民患輕則爲母權子而行民患重則
爲子權母而行凖此以錢爲母以鈔爲子
又何不可乎行之旣利習之而安則錢鈔
與銀幣相兼相濟相補相洩不出二三年
之間國可使富而民亦有餘大則
朝廷之祭祀征伐營繕錫予隨用皆充小則
閭閻之衣食用度致遠輕齎隨在各足所
===
謂制用裕民誠莫有要於此矣雖然此特
語其末耳又有其本在焉傳曰官之失職
寵賂章也抑孰知古人之制用其意固已
嚴乎夫錢之名曰流于泉以言清也清斯
惠流矣曰利于刀以言夬也夬斯利辯矣
曰布于布以言德也德斯令布矣曰束于
帛以言約也潔也約斯不濫潔斯不瀆矣
凡以爲用錢者言也鈔之名其制取諸券
義取諸交易上之交下而補助行焉否則
punctuated:
以銀爲大用，錢爲小用，又何不可乎？又謂銅楮錯用，日見其勞，則古又有之矣。單穆公曰：「民患輕，則爲母權子而行；民患重，則爲子權母而行。」凖此，以錢爲母，以鈔爲子，又何不可乎？行之旣利，習之而安，則錢鈔與銀幣相兼相濟，相補相洩，不出二三年之間，國可使富，而民亦有餘。大則朝廷之祭祀、征伐、營繕、錫予，隨用皆充；小則閭閻之衣食用度、致遠輕齎，隨在各足。所謂制用裕民，誠莫有要於此矣。
雖然，此特語其末耳，又有其本在焉。傳曰：「官之失職，寵賂章也。」抑孰知古人之制用，其意固已嚴乎？夫錢之名，曰流于泉，以言清也，清斯惠流矣；曰利于刀，以言夬也，夬斯利辯矣；曰布于布，以言德也，德斯令布矣；曰束于帛，以言約也、潔也，約斯不濫，潔斯不瀆矣。凡以爲用錢者言也。鈔之名，其制取諸券，義取諸交易。上之交下，而補助行焉，否則
translation_en:
…using silver for major expenditures and copper cash for minor ones—why should this not be permissible? It is also said that using copper cash and paper money together brings daily trouble; yet this too has ancient precedent. Duke Mu of Shan said: “When the people suffer from currency being too light, make the mother balance the child and circulate them; when the people suffer from currency being too heavy, make the child balance the mother and circulate them.” Following this precedent, why should we not make copper cash the mother and paper money the child? Once the practice proves beneficial and familiarity makes people comfortable with it, copper cash, paper money, and silver currency will work together and support one another, making up deficiencies and relieving excesses. Within no more than two or three years, the state can be made wealthy and the people will also have a surplus. At the higher level, the court’s sacrifices, military campaigns, construction and repairs, and grants and rewards will all be amply funded as needs arise. At the lower level, ordinary households will have enough wherever they are for clothing, food, and daily expenses, and for carrying funds over long distances with light loads. For what is called regulating expenditure and enriching the people, truly nothing is more essential than this.
Nevertheless, this speaks only of the branches; there is also a root. The Commentary says: “Officials neglect their duties when favoritism and bribery are manifest.” Yet who recognizes how stringent the ancients’ intentions already were in regulating expenditure? As for the names of money: its flowing is expressed through “spring” (quan), signifying purity; with purity, beneficence flows. Its sharpness is expressed through “knife” (dao), signifying decisiveness; with decisiveness, benefits are distinguished. Its spreading is expressed through “cloth” (bu), signifying virtue; with virtue, commands spread. Its binding is expressed through “silk” (bo), signifying restraint and integrity; with restraint there is no excess, and with integrity there is no corruption. All these sayings address those who use money. As for paper money, its form derives from certificates and its meaning from exchange. When those above engage with those below, aid and assistance are provided; otherwise…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
睒矣下之交上而貢賦輸焉否則畔矣凡
以爲用鈔者言也若私與公交遠臣與近
臣交正與邪之所謂神者是謂不泉不刀
不布不帛固已失其制用之本而又益之
以非道之交其不傷財而害民也者幾希
此後世之財所以日見其告匱而理財又
難於昔之人無惑也故曰其本則在
朝廷而不在有司
第五問
===
考試官教諭葉　批〔經世備荒弭盜之畧咸中時宜而一結尤有餘味有用之才也〕
考試官教授伍　批〔敷答詳懇藎有見者〕
善爲政者不恃無荒而恃吾有備荒之術
不恃無盜而恃吾有弭盜之方蓋有備無
患爲政之大經也荒與盜之無固不足恃
而吾備荒之術弭盜之方豈可不豫爲之
所乎誠能於豐登有餘之日恒爲荒歉不
banxin: 鄉試錄　卷一　江一川
punctuated:
睒矣。下之交上而貢賦輸焉，否則畔矣。凡以爲用鈔者言也。若私與公交，遠臣與近臣交，正與邪之所謂神者，是謂不泉、不刀、不布、不帛，固已失其制用之本，而又益之以非道之交，其不傷財而害民也者幾希。此後世之財所以日見其告匱，而理財又難於昔之人，無惑也。故曰：其本則在朝廷，而不在有司。
第五問
考試官教諭葉批〔經世備荒弭盜之畧，咸中時宜，而一結尤有餘味，有用之才也。〕
考試官教授伍批〔敷答詳懇，藎有見者。〕
善爲政者，不恃無荒，而恃吾有備荒之術；不恃無盜，而恃吾有弭盜之方。蓋有備無患，爲政之大經也。荒與盜之無，固不足恃，而吾備荒之術、弭盜之方，豈可不豫爲之所乎？誠能於豐登有餘之日，恒爲荒歉不
translation_en:
…there is flickering [?]. In dealings of those below with those above, tribute and taxes are remitted; otherwise, there is rebellion. All this concerns those who use paper currency. But when private interests enter into dealings with public authority, and distant officials with officials close to the throne—the so-called mysterious power operating between the upright and the wicked [?]—this amounts to abandoning the meanings of spring, knife, cloth, and silk. The fundamental intent governing the institution and use of currency has already been lost; when improper dealings are added to this, scarcely any can avoid damaging wealth and harming the people. It is therefore no wonder that in later ages financial resources become increasingly depleted, and managing them is harder than it was for people of earlier times. Thus I say: the root lies with the imperial court, not with the responsible officials.
Fifth Question
Examiner Ye, Instructor, comments: 〔The strategies for ordering the world, preparing for famine, and suppressing banditry all suit the needs of the times. The conclusion is especially rich in implications. Here is a man of practical talent.〕
Examiner Wu, Professor, comments: 〔The response is detailed and earnest, displaying sincere insight.〕
Those skilled in governing do not rely on the absence of famine, but on having methods for preparing for it; they do not rely on the absence of bandits, but on having means to suppress them. Preparedness prevents calamity: this is a cardinal principle of government. We certainly cannot count on the absence of famine and banditry. How, then, could we fail to make advance provision for our methods of famine preparedness and bandit suppression? If, in days of abundant harvests and surplus, we can constantly remain concerned about famine, poor harvests, and insufficiency…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
給之憂於太平無事之時每懷反側擾攘之
慮則荒與盜皆有其備斯善爲政矣請復
明問饑饉薦臻國家代有蓋天時之不常
地利人事之不及也顧吾所以備之何如
耳觀諸成周荒政十二以及遺人廩人所
掌則所以慮災防患也至矣盜賊竊發古
今皆然蓋其困於饑寒而弄兵山海以爲
假息之計也亦顧吾所以弭之何如耳觀
諸成周聯比什伍以爲追逐胥伺之備則
===
所以思患預防也深矣此三代之民所以
遇災無患承平無事也先王往矣成濾具
在乃若江西則目前之近固難卒以周濾
行之而亦不可不爲之深思遠慮也是故
地狹矣而猶有曠土民稠矣而類多游民
是無惟乎蓄積寡而荒易見也執事固嘗
慮及此矣而今者南贛之水泛濫瀰漫又
得無爲地方之患乎民財窮矣而賦歛愈
繁民力竭矣而征役不息是無惟乎姦宄
punctuated: 給之憂，於太平無事之時，每懷反側擾攘之慮，則荒與盜皆有其備，斯善爲政矣。請復明問。饑饉薦臻，國家代有，蓋天時之不常、地利人事之不及也，顧吾所以備之何如耳。觀諸成周荒政十二，以及遺人、廩人所掌，則所以慮災防患也至矣。盜賊竊發，古今皆然，蓋其困於饑寒，而弄兵山海，以爲假息之計也，亦顧吾所以弭之何如耳。觀諸成周聯比什伍，以爲追逐胥伺之備，則所以思患預防也深矣。此三代之民所以遇災無患、承平無事也。先王往矣，成濾具在。乃若江西，則目前之近，固難卒以周濾行之，而亦不可不爲之深思遠慮也。是故地狹矣，而猶有曠土；民稠矣，而類多游民。是無惟乎蓄積寡而荒易見也？執事固嘗慮及此矣，而今者南贛之水泛濫瀰漫，又得無爲地方之患乎？民財窮矣，而賦歛愈繁；民力竭矣，而征役不息。是無惟乎姦宄
translation_en:
…concern over insufficient supplies, and in times of peace and tranquility always keep in mind the danger of unrest and disorder: then preparations will have been made against both famine and banditry. This is skillful government. Allow me to respond to your illuminating question.

Famines have struck repeatedly under every dynasty. They arise from irregularities in the seasons and deficiencies in the resources of the land and in human efforts. What matters is how we prepare for them. Consider the twelve famine-relief measures of the Zhou, together with the responsibilities of the Provisioners (yiren) and Granary Directors (linren): their provisions for anticipating disaster and averting harm were comprehensive indeed. Bandit outbreaks have likewise occurred in ancient and modern times alike. Driven by hunger and cold, people take up arms in the mountains and along the seas as a means of eking out their lives. Here too, what matters is how we suppress them. Consider how the Zhou linked households into groups of ten and five, providing for pursuit and mutual surveillance: their foresight in anticipating trouble and preventing it was profound indeed. This was why the people of the Three Dynasties could encounter disasters without suffering calamity and live undisturbed in times of peace.

The former kings are gone, but their established plans [?] remain fully available. As for Jiangxi, given the immediate circumstances, it would certainly be difficult to put the Zhou plans [?] into practice all at once; nevertheless, we must give the matter deep thought and consider the distant future. Thus, although land is scarce, uncultivated land remains; although the population is dense, many people lack settled occupations. Is it any wonder [?] that reserves are scant and famine readily appears? You, sir, have surely considered this before. Yet now the waters of Nan-Gan are overflowing and spreading far and wide: can they fail to pose a threat to the region? The people's wealth is exhausted, yet tax exactions grow ever more numerous; their strength is spent, yet levies and labor service never cease. Is it any wonder [?] that evildoers…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
生而盜易作也執事亦嘗加之意矣如向
者姚源之賊出沒剽掠又得無爲今日之
防乎蓋嘗求之古人如中饑則發中熟之
所斂大饑則發大熟之所斂此平糴之濫
李悝嘗行於魏矣穀賤則增價而糴穀貴
則減價而糶此常平之濫耿壽昌嘗行於
漢矣至若隋之開皇則有長孫平之爲義
倉取之於民不厚而置之當社爲近宋之
孝宗則有朱熹之爲社倉始則請官米以
===
加息而給則止息米以加耗凡此皆備荒
之術也然地有遠近戶有多寡人有老幼
强弱自不能以皆同以今論之平糴慮有
拘泥之失常平恐失斂散之宜義倉委之
社司或非人以長吏奸惟社倉則官無所
費民有所利誠鄉閭無窮之計也使郡邑
皆倣而行之而又斟酌以適中焉庶備荒其
有濟乎在漢武帝則作沈命之濫盜起不
發發而捕弗滿品主者皆死在魏李崇則
punctuated:
生而盜易作也。執事亦嘗加之意矣。如向者姚源之賊出沒剽掠，又得無爲今日之防乎？蓋嘗求之古人，如中饑則發中熟之所斂，大饑則發大熟之所斂，此平糴之濫，李悝嘗行於魏矣。穀賤則增價而糴，穀貴則減價而糶，此常平之濫，耿壽昌嘗行於漢矣。至若隋之開皇，則有長孫平之爲義倉，取之於民不厚，而置之當社爲近；宋之孝宗，則有朱熹之爲社倉，始則請官米以加息，而給則止息米以加耗。凡此皆備荒之術也。然地有遠近，戶有多寡，人有老幼强弱，自不能以皆同。以今論之，平糴慮有拘泥之失，常平恐失斂散之宜，義倉委之社司，或非人以長吏奸；惟社倉則官無所費，民有所利，誠鄉閭無窮之計也。使郡邑皆倣而行之，而又斟酌以適中焉，庶備荒其有濟乎？

在漢武帝則作沈命之濫，盜起不發，發而捕弗滿品，主者皆死。在魏李崇則
translation_en:
…arise, and banditry readily breaks out. You, sir, have also given this your attention. As for the bandits of Yaoyuan, who recently appeared and disappeared, pillaging and plundering, must we not guard against such a threat today?

I have sought precedents among the ancients. In a moderate famine, they released what had been collected from a moderately good harvest; in a great famine, they released what had been collected from a bountiful harvest. This was the system [?] of equitable grain purchasing, which Li Kui once implemented in Wei. When grain was cheap, they raised the purchase price; when grain was dear, they lowered the selling price. This was the ever-normal granary system [?], which Geng Shouchang once implemented under the Han. During the Kaihuang reign of the Sui, Zhangsun Ping established charitable granaries: contributions exacted from the people were light, and the granaries were conveniently situated within their respective communities. Under Emperor Xiaozong of the Song, Zhu Xi established community granaries. Initially, he requested government grain to lend at interest; subsequently, in distributing loans, he discontinued interest in grain and added only an allowance for wastage [?]. All these were methods of preparing for famine.

Yet places differ in their remoteness, households in their numbers, and people in age and strength; naturally, they cannot all be treated alike. Judged by present circumstances, equitable grain purchasing risks excessive rigidity; the ever-normal system may fail to collect and distribute grain appropriately; and charitable granaries, entrusted to community administrators, may fall into unsuitable hands and foster official malfeasance [?]. Community granaries alone entail no expense to the government while benefiting the people. They truly offer a lasting provision for local communities. If prefectures and counties all followed this example, adapting it judiciously to achieve a proper balance, might it not make preparations against famine effective?

Under Emperor Wu of the Han, the Shenming statute [?] was instituted: if banditry arose and was not reported, or was reported but the prescribed quota of arrests was not met, the responsible officials were all put to death. Under the Wei, Li Chong…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
置樓鼓之防盜發而擊擊則四村皆集救
之而聲布百里義營之瀵行之者實徵也
一户爲盜累其一村一户被盜累其一將
懸賞之瀵爲之者崔安潛也告捕一盜賞
錢伍百同侣捕之賞同平人此皆弭盜之
方也然地有險易勢有强弱情有向背順
逆亦不能以相一自今觀之况命誡禁之
太嚴樓鼓止用之有警懸賞所費官錢亦
可暫而不可久惟義營則村村自相保盜無
===
所脫實獨清一境之效也使郡邑皆行而
瀵而又變通以宜民庶弭盜其或得乎雖
然此特藋時之宜而非探本之論求其本
于備荒則荀卿所謂田野縣鄙者財之本
垣窌倉廩者財之末百姓時和事業得叙
者貨之源等賦府庫者貨之流而欲人君
養其和節其流開其源則上下俱富乃國
計之極故禹十年水湯七年旱而民無菜
色者以此故也知此則平糴諸瀵又似
punctuated:
置樓鼓之防，盜發而擊，擊則四村皆集救之，而聲布百里。義營之瀵，行之者實徵也。一户爲盜，累其一村；一户被盜，累其一將。懸賞之瀵，爲之者崔安潛也。告捕一盜，賞錢伍百；同侣捕之，賞同平人。此皆弭盜之方也。然地有險易，勢有强弱，情有向背順逆，亦不能以相一。自今觀之，况命誡禁之太嚴，樓鼓止用之有警，懸賞所費官錢亦可暫而不可久。惟義營則村村自相保，盜無所脫，實獨清一境之效也。使郡邑皆行而瀵，而又變通以宜民，庶弭盜其或得乎？

雖然，此特藋時之宜，而非探本之論。求其本于備荒，則荀卿所謂田野縣鄙者財之本，垣窌倉廩者財之末，百姓時和、事業得叙者貨之源，等賦府庫者貨之流。而欲人君養其和，節其流，開其源，則上下俱富，乃國計之極。故禹十年水，湯七年旱，而民無菜色者，以此故也。知此，則平糴諸瀵又似
translation_en:
…established a defense system of towers and drums: when bandits appeared, the drums were struck; at their sound, the four surrounding villages would all assemble to give assistance, and the sound carried for a hundred li. The community militia method [?] was implemented by Shi Zheng [?]. If one household engaged in banditry, its entire village was held accountable; if one household suffered a bandit attack, its commanding officer was held accountable. The method of offering rewards [?] was instituted by Cui Anqian. Reporting and capturing one bandit earned a reward of five hundred cash; an accomplice who captured him received the same reward as an ordinary person. These were all ways of suppressing banditry. Yet terrain differs in difficulty, strength varies, and popular sentiment ranges from allegiance to opposition, obedience to defiance; these circumstances cannot all be treated alike. Viewed from the present, the prohibitions and penalties of the Shenming law [?] were excessively severe; towers and drums were useful only when an alarm arose; and the expenditure of government funds on rewards could be sustained temporarily, but not indefinitely. Only the community militia system, under which every village protected itself and bandits had no escape, was uniquely effective in pacifying an entire jurisdiction. If prefectures and counties all adopted and emulated it [?], adapting it to suit the people, might some success in suppressing banditry be achieved?

Nevertheless, these are merely measures suited to the circumstances of the moment [?], rather than an argument that probes the fundamentals. To seek the fundamentals of famine preparedness, consider what Master Xun said: fields and outlying districts are the root of wealth; enclosed stores, underground storage pits, and granaries are its branches. The common people living in seasonal harmony and their occupations proceeding in proper order constitute the source of material resources; graded levies and government treasuries constitute their flow. He therefore wished the ruler to nurture that harmony, regulate the flow, and open up the source. Then those above and those below would both be prosperous: the highest achievement of state economic management. This is why, despite ten years of flooding under Yu and seven years of drought under Tang, the people bore no signs of hunger. Understanding this, the various methods [?] of purchasing grain at equitable prices would again seem…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
必行矣求其本於弭盜則范祖禹所謂因
衣食之源立教化之官先之以節儉示之
以純朴而欲人君不舍其本而專禁其末
必如唐太宗之使民衣食有餘不必如宋
熙寧別立盜賊重法焉則邪僻不作乃邦
成之至故路不拾遺外戶不閉而商旅野
宿者坐是焉耳知此則淮命諸法又似不
必用矣雖然猶未也三年耕必有一年之
食九年耕必有三年之食此王制之儲畜
===
之灋不使其非國也荀子之不欲雖賞之
不竊子欲善而民善此聖人主教化之意
不欲以徒灋也而蘇轍亦曰古之聖人上
盜以義使天下皆知父子君臣而誰與爲
亂朱熹又曰爲政者當順五行脩五事以
安百姓又荀范之所不及也持此而往雖
措之天下可也豈獨江西然哉昔人有云
勢不同而理同又云有治人而無治灋歟
事以爲何如
punctuated:
必行矣。求其本於弭盜，則范祖禹所謂因衣食之源，立教化之官，先之以節儉，示之以純朴，而欲人君不舍其本而專禁其末，必如唐太宗之使民衣食有餘，不必如宋熙寧別立盜賊重法焉，則邪僻不作，乃邦成之至。故路不拾遺，外戶不閉，而商旅野宿者，坐是焉耳。知此，則淮命諸法又似不必用矣。
雖然，猶未也。三年耕必有一年之食，九年耕必有三年之食，此《王制》之儲畜之灋，不使其非國也。荀子之不欲，雖賞之不竊；子欲善而民善，此聖人主教化之意，不欲以徒灋也。而蘇轍亦曰：「古之聖人上盜以義，使天下皆知父子君臣，而誰與爲亂？」朱熹又曰：「爲政者當順五行，脩五事，以安百姓。」又荀、范之所不及也。持此而往，雖措之天下可也，豈獨江西然哉？昔人有云：「勢不同而理同。」又云：「有治人而無治灋。」歟事以爲何如？
translation_en:
…must be implemented. If we seek the root of suppressing banditry, there is what Fan Zuyu advocated: build upon the sources of clothing and food, establish officials responsible for moral instruction, lead the people through frugality, and show them simplicity and sincerity. A ruler should not abandon the root and concentrate solely on prohibiting its outward manifestations. He must follow Emperor Taizong of the Tang in ensuring that the people have clothing and food to spare; he need not follow the Song practice during the Xining era of separately instituting harsh laws against banditry. Then wicked and deviant conduct will not arise: this is the highest achievement of government. Thus, that people did not pick up lost property on the roads, left their outer doors unbarred, and allowed traveling merchants to sleep in the open was simply the result of this. Once this is understood, the various laws called “Huaiming” [?] would seem unnecessary.
Yet even this is not enough. Three years of cultivation must yield provisions sufficient for one year, and nine years of cultivation must yield provisions sufficient for three years. This is the rule for accumulating reserves in “Royal Regulations,” so that the realm does not cease to be a state [?]. The passage attributed here to Xunzi [?], “If you yourself had no desires, they would not steal even if rewarded for doing so,” and “If you desire goodness, the people will be good,” expresses the sage’s intention to give priority to moral instruction, rather than rely on laws alone. Su Zhe also said: “The sages of antiquity checked banditry through righteousness [?], enabling everyone under Heaven to understand the relationships between father and son and between ruler and minister. Who, then, would join in rebellion?” Zhu Xi further said: “Those who govern should accord with the Five Phases and cultivate the Five Activities, thereby bringing peace to the common people.” This goes beyond what Xun and Fan addressed. Proceeding on this basis, one could apply it throughout the realm; how could it hold true for Jiangxi alone? Someone of old said, “Circumstances differ, but the principle is the same.” Another saying runs, “There are men who bring good government, but no laws that bring good government of themselves.” What is your judgment on this [?]?

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試錄後序
凡試事成有司爲錄以
獻錄成序之皆
制也而序以爲戒也禮也序其後
申戒之也士之始進也猶女
子之嫁也禮女子之嫁也父
醮而戒之母送之階而又戒
===
之蓋慎其始也江西之試至
是爲錄凡幾序凡幾其主司
之得士與否其士之貞不貞
皆可觀已於其始也敢弗慎
與雖然彼爲是者徒以文焉
耳文果足恃耶我
國家體道爲治文出于一垂百
punctuated:
江西鄉試錄後序

凡試事成，有司爲錄以獻。錄成，序之，皆制也。而序以爲戒也，禮也。序其後，申戒之也。士之始進也，猶女子之嫁也。禮，女子之嫁也，父醮而戒之，母送之階而又戒之，蓋慎其始也。

江西之試至是，爲錄凡幾，序凡幾？其主司之得士與否，其士之貞不貞，皆可觀已。於其始也，敢弗慎與？雖然，彼爲是者，徒以文焉耳。文果足恃耶？我國家體道爲治，文出于一，垂百
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination

Whenever an examination has been completed, the responsible officials compile a record for presentation to the throne. Once the record is complete, a preface is written: these are all prescribed procedures. To use the preface to offer admonition accords with ritual propriety. To append a postface is to reiterate that admonition. A scholar’s first entry into official life resembles a woman’s marriage. According to ritual, when a woman marries, her father offers her a ceremonial cup of wine and admonishes her; her mother escorts her to the steps and admonishes her again. This is to exercise care at the beginning.

By now, how many records of the Jiangxi examination have been compiled, and how many prefaces written? Whether those presiding have secured worthy scholars, and whether those scholars remain steadfast, can all be observed by now. At the beginning, dare we fail to exercise care? Nevertheless, those who undertake this rely solely on literary compositions. Can literary compositions truly be relied upon? Our dynasty embodies the Way in its governance; its literary expression issues from the One and is transmitted to a hundred [?]…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
又曰似司馬遷似陸贄韓愈
也今試求之非似之間而其
所見者則一矣脩之言曰三
代之上政出于一而禮樂達
於天下是也知一則知文矣
於是則有本論濮議知一則
知士矣於是則有蘇軾曾鞏
===
固脩之所自得於文者是不
寧鄉士之瀆而天下公言之
矣雖然昔脩起五季排佛老
爲功矣而今得無進之以爲
博乎脩變鉤棘黜葸軋稱復
古矣而今得無目之以爲才
乎彼其主司士之相遭也有
punctuated:
又曰：「似司馬遷，似陸贄、韓愈也。」今試求之非似之間，而其所見者則一矣。脩之言曰：「三代之上，政出于一，而禮樂達於天下。」是也。知一則知文矣，於是則有《本論》、《濮議》；知一則知士矣，於是則有蘇軾、曾鞏。固脩之所自得於文者，是不寧鄉士之瀆，而天下公言之矣。

雖然，昔脩起五季，排佛老爲功矣，而今得無進之以爲博乎？脩變鉤棘，黜葸軋，稱復古矣，而今得無目之以爲才乎？彼其主司、士之相遭也，有
translation_en:
…It is also said: “He resembles Sima Qian; he resembles Lu Zhi and Han Yu.” Now, if we seek amid these resemblances and differences, what we discern is unity. As Xiu [Ouyang Xiu] said: “In the Three Dynasties and earlier, government issued from a single source, and rites and music reached throughout the realm.” This is precisely the point. To understand unity is to understand writing: hence his On Fundamentals and Deliberations on the Prince of Pu. To understand unity is to understand men of talent: hence Su Shi and Zeng Gong. Certainly, this was what Xiu had grasped for himself in writing. It was not merely the presumptuous talk of local scholars [?]; the whole realm spoke of it with one voice.

Nevertheless, when Xiu arose in the wake of the Five Dynasties, he made it his achievement to oppose Buddhism and Daoism. Yet today, might these teachings not be promoted as evidence of broad learning? Xiu reformed the thorny, contorted style of writing and rejected its timid, constricted manner [?], winning praise for restoring antiquity. Yet today, might those very qualities not be regarded as talent? In the encounters between examination officials and candidates, there are…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
不爲今弊也者幾希夫豈以
脩爲不美哉不變則不奇不
利則不變固世之恒者比其
後也而習成焉習也而厭生
焉習而厭厭而奇吾不知文
所止矣是故文也者變而未
始變者也至奇而易簡者也
===
此脩之謂一或者其有遺志
於斯我
祖宗朝用少師楊士奇言特取脩
之文顯行之士奇之文固脩
之瀶也而後之作者漸以異
須者禮官之論又以正文體
請禮官之請又士奇之意也
punctuated:
不爲今弊也者幾希，夫豈以脩爲不美哉？不變則不奇，不利則不變，固世之恒者。比其後也，而習成焉；習也，而厭生焉。習而厭，厭而奇，吾不知文所止矣。是故文也者，變而未始變者也，至奇而易簡者也。此脩之謂一，或者其有遺志於斯。
我祖宗朝用少師楊士奇言，特取脩之文顯行之。士奇之文固脩之瀶也，而後之作者漸以異。須者，禮官之論又以正文體請。禮官之請，又士奇之意也。
translation_en:
…there are very few that have not become abuses today. But does this mean that Xiu is not admirable? Without change there is no novelty; without advantage there is no change. This has always been the way of the world. In time, habit takes hold; once habit takes hold, weariness arises. Familiarity breeds weariness, and weariness breeds the pursuit of novelty: I do not know where writing will end. Thus writing changes yet has never fundamentally changed; it is supremely novel yet easy and simple. This is what Xiu meant by unity [?]; perhaps he left an aspiration in this regard for others to fulfill.
During the reigns of our imperial ancestors, the court adopted the recommendation of Yang Shiqi, Junior Preceptor, and specially selected Xiu’s writings for prominent circulation. Shiqi’s own writing indeed followed Xiu’s example [?], but subsequent writers gradually diverged. The officials responsible for rites then [?] submitted a proposal requesting that literary style be rectified. Their request likewise expressed Shiqi’s intention.

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試錄序
嘉靖丁酉秋制當鄉試先期
巡按江西監察御史陳〔褎謀〕
於藩臬之長聘〔儁〕及教諭葉
〔天榮〕爲考試官林〔應鳳〕孫〔憲〕
葉〔潤〕胡〔希定〕徐〔轂〕王〔臣〕唐〔魯〕
李〔仁〕李〔時暘〕鄧〔體靜〕以所專
===
經爲同考試官比至則御史
旣已貞度集思愼簡諸執事
曁提調左布政使李〔崧祥〕左
叅政陳〔鄉〕監試按察使劉〔士
奇〕副使陸〔堂〕各矢心以俟乃
合提學副使徐〔階〕所選士三
千七百人三試之〔儁〕獲縱觀
punctuated:
江西鄉試錄序

嘉靖丁酉秋，制當鄉試。先期，巡按江西監察御史陳〔褎謀〕於藩臬之長，聘〔儁〕及教諭葉〔天榮〕爲考試官，林〔應鳳〕、孫〔憲〕、葉〔潤〕、胡〔希定〕、徐〔轂〕、王〔臣〕、唐〔魯〕、李〔仁〕、李〔時暘〕、鄧〔體靜〕以所專經爲同考試官。比至，則御史旣已貞度集思，愼簡諸執事，曁提調左布政使李〔崧祥〕、左叅政陳〔鄉〕、監試按察使劉〔士奇〕、副使陸〔堂〕，各矢心以俟。乃合提學副使徐〔階〕所選士三千七百人，三試之。〔儁〕獲縱觀
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination

In the autumn of the dingyou year of Jiajing [1537], the Provincial Examination was due to be held according to imperial regulation. In advance, Chen Bao [?], the Regional Inspector serving as Investigating Censor for Jiangxi, consulted the heads of the provincial administration and surveillance commissions and invited Jun and Ye Tianrong, an Instructor, to serve as Examiners. Lin Yingfeng, Sun Xian, Ye Run, Hu Xiding, Xu Gu, Wang Chen, Tang Lu, Li Ren, Li Shiyang, and Deng Tijing were appointed Associate Examiners according to the Classics in which they specialized.

By the time we arrived, the Censor had already carefully deliberated, gathered counsel, and selected the examination staff with care. Together with the Proctors, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Li Songxiang and Left Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner Chen Xiang, and the examination supervisors, Surveillance Commissioner Liu Shiqi and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Lu Tang, they had each pledged their wholehearted commitment and stood ready. They then assembled the 3,700 candidates selected by Xu Jie, the Surveillance Vice Commissioner in charge of education, and examined them in three sessions. I, Jun, was able to survey comprehensively …

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
其文麗而則辯而不誇深而
不鑿謹拜手言曰於戲此盛
世之文也
聖天子以身立教功效固然哉維
昔帝王觀文成化于時人士
之文渾渾噩噩舉足以徵德
樹業無俟議矣秦漢而降世
===
無主張斯文之君本喪質窮
於是恠誕不經之書雕鏤絺
繪之技雜然並出獨一二賢
人君子相與私正救之若八
代之衰得韓愈氏以興五季
之餘習得歐陽脩氏以振孔
孟仁義之旨得周敦頤氏程
punctuated: 其文麗而則，辯而不誇，深而不鑿，謹拜手言曰：「於戲！此盛世之文也。聖天子以身立教，功效固然哉！維昔帝王觀文成化，于時人士之文渾渾噩噩，舉足以徵德樹業，無俟議矣。秦漢而降，世無主張斯文之君，本喪質窮，於是恠誕不經之書、雕鏤絺繪之技，雜然並出。獨一二賢人君子相與私正救之，若八代之衰，得韓愈氏以興；五季之餘習，得歐陽脩氏以振；孔孟仁義之旨，得周敦頤氏、程
translation_en: …their compositions were elegant yet conformed to proper standards, eloquent without exaggeration, profound without strained interpretation. Respectfully bowing with hands clasped, I said: “Ah! These are the writings of a flourishing age. The sagely Son of Heaven establishes moral teaching through his own example: surely these are its fruits! In antiquity, emperors and kings observed cultural patterns and thereby brought about moral transformation. The writings of the scholars of that time were whole and uncontrived, all sufficient to attest to virtue and establish worthy achievements; no further discussion was needed. From the Qin and Han onward, the world lacked rulers who upheld this cultural tradition. Its roots were lost and its substance exhausted. Thus books of bizarre tales contrary to the classics and techniques of elaborate literary ornamentation emerged together in profusion. Only one or two worthy gentlemen joined in private efforts to rectify and rescue it. Thus, after the decline of eight dynasties, Han Yu arose to revive it; amid the lingering habits of the Five Dynasties, Ouyang Xiu arose to reinvigorate it; the purport of Confucius’s and Mencius’s teachings on benevolence and righteousness found its exponents in Zhou Dunyi and Cheng…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
顓頊氏以發其微朱熹氏陸
九淵氏往復辯難以究其藴
雖功在斯文炳然不誣而復
古之盛卒不見於天下何也
其勢誠弗尊弗從也洪惟我
太祖高皇帝以
上聖之德續道統之傳表章六經
罷斥百氏學者旣曉然識其
===
所宗肆今
皇上敬一之學得之性成言發爲
經聲出爲律薄海内外人誦
習之蓋天之文也乃者病文
體之謬又特
詔有司正之所謂道兼
punctuated: 顓頊氏以發其微，朱熹氏、陸九淵氏往復辯難，以究其藴。雖功在斯文，炳然不誣，而復古之盛卒不見於天下，何也？其勢誠弗尊弗從也。洪惟我太祖高皇帝，以上聖之德，續道統之傳，表章六經，罷斥百氏，學者旣曉然識其所宗。肆今皇上，敬一之學得之性成，言發爲經，聲出爲律，薄海内外，人誦習之，蓋天之文也。乃者病文體之謬，又特詔有司正之，所謂道兼
translation_en:
…Zhuanxu [?] brought their subtleties to light, while Zhu Xi and Lu Jiuyuan debated back and forth to plumb their depths. Although their contributions to this cultural tradition were manifest and undeniable, the flourishing restoration of antiquity was ultimately never seen throughout the realm. Why? Their position lacked the authority to command reverence and obedience.

We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao, through the virtue of a supreme sage, continued the transmission of the succession of the Way, exalted the Six Classics, and rejected the hundred schools. Scholars thus clearly understood what they should take as their guiding authority. Now His Majesty possesses by his innate nature the learning of reverent concentration on the One. His utterances become canonical standards; his voice establishes the pitch-pipes. Throughout the lands within and beyond the seas, people recite and study them: these are indeed Heaven’s own writings.
