title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
自楚人服鄭於圍方將返轅之日也而晉復禦
楚以救鄭楚莊其肯避敵乎於是因伍參之激
以兵進接而戰于邲地焉當時爲晉將者林父
也而主兵之道則失之矣蓋自楚言之少西之
討既成伐義之名皇門之攻又得退師之善果
何釁之可乘哉是以隨會進養晦之言知莊陳
否臧之戒林父非不知也雖先縠欲以中軍佐
濟夫豈不可按軍法而行辟乎何乃畏失屬而
亡師思分惡以同罪知難冒進以喪晉師是豈
===
辛兵專制之道哉其視欒書止八軍之欲戰荀
偃沮二將之班師而卒不爲所撓者有愧矣故
獨書林父以主此戰蓋專其責也而爲將之道
見焉及自吳人責魯於會方將棄疾之時也而
魯乃背吳以伐邾夫差其肯甘心乎於是因夷
鴻之請以兵來伐而至于國都焉當時爲魯相
者季孫也而謀國之道則失之矣蓋自吳言之
東陽之克本無必取之心泗上之遷已有將歸
之勢果何釁之難救哉是以微虎奮背攻之勇
punctuated:
自楚人服鄭於圍，方將返轅之日也，而晉復禦楚以救鄭，楚莊其肯避敵乎？於是因伍參之激，以兵進接，而戰于邲地焉。當時爲晉將者林父也，而主兵之道則失之矣。蓋自楚言之，少西之討既成伐義之名，皇門之攻又得退師之善，果何釁之可乘哉？是以隨會進養晦之言，知莊陳否臧之戒，林父非不知也。雖先縠欲以中軍佐濟，夫豈不可按軍法而行辟乎？何乃畏失屬而亡師，思分惡以同罪，知難冒進，以喪晉師？是豈辛兵專制之道哉？其視欒書止八軍之欲戰、荀偃沮二將之班師而卒不爲所撓者，有愧矣。故獨書林父以主此戰，蓋專其責也，而爲將之道見焉。

及自吳人責魯於會，方將棄疾之時也，而魯乃背吳以伐邾，夫差其肯甘心乎？於是因夷鴻之請，以兵來伐，而至于國都焉。當時爲魯相者季孫也，而謀國之道則失之矣。蓋自吳言之，東陽之克本無必取之心，泗上之遷已有將歸之勢，果何釁之難救哉？是以微虎奮背攻之勇，
translation_en:
When the men of Chu had compelled Zheng to submit through a siege and were about to turn their chariots homeward, Jin again opposed Chu to rescue Zheng. Would King Zhuang of Chu willingly avoid the enemy? Thus, spurred on by Wu Can, he advanced his troops to engage them, and they fought at Bi. Linfu was then Jin’s commander, but he failed in the proper conduct of military command. From Chu’s perspective, its punitive expedition against Shaoxi had already earned it a reputation for righteous warfare, and its attack on Huangmen had also won it credit for withdrawing its army. What vulnerability was there to exploit? Accordingly, Sui Hui urged that they nurture their strength and keep a low profile, while Zhi Zhuang warned of the adverse and favorable circumstances. Linfu was not unaware of these considerations. Even though Xian Hu, as assistant commander of the central army, wished to cross the river, could he not have been punished under military law? Why, fearing the loss of a subordinate, did Linfu instead lose his army? Why did he seek to share wrongdoing and bear guilt together, recklessly advancing despite knowing the difficulties, and thereby destroy Jin’s army? Was this the proper way to command troops [?] and exercise sole authority? Compared with Luan Shu, who restrained the eight armies [?] when they wished to fight, and Xun Yan, who thwarted two commanders’ attempt to withdraw their troops—neither ultimately allowing himself to be swayed—Linfu had cause for shame. Thus the Spring and Autumn Annals names Linfu alone as directing this battle, assigning responsibility exclusively to him. In this way, the proper conduct of a commander is revealed.

Then, when the men of Wu had called Lu to account at a meeting and were about to abandon the sick [?], Lu turned against Wu and attacked Zhu. Would Fuchai willingly accept this? Accordingly, acting on Yihong’s request [?], he brought troops to attack and reached the capital. Jisun was then Lu’s chief minister, but he failed in the proper conduct of planning for the state. From Wu’s perspective, when it captured Dongyang, it had originally had no fixed intention of taking possession; when it moved to the banks of the Si River, it already showed signs of preparing to return home. What breach was there that could not readily be repaired? Thus Wei Hu summoned the courage to attack from the rear…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
縈伯戲少待之謀李孫非不知也雖叔子偶以
𦨦師戰敗夫豈不可收餘燼而借一乎何乃欲
姑息於目前遂受盟於城下臨難苟免以辱魯
國是豈謀國自强之道哉其視華元退楚人之
急園國佐郤晉師之進逼而終不爲所屈者有
愧多矣故不言四鄙及與吳盟蓋諱其恥也而爲
相之道見焉雖然將相之道有本焉仁義而已
矣明於仁義則必先格君心以興周道故以之
治人則爲德政以之戡亂則爲德威而臨敵應
變折衝禦侮皆不足言矣世衰道微莫知此義
陷溺既深愈趨愈下遂使楚遂夫差相繼爭伯
而中國不復得爲中國矣悲夫
===
禮記
君子齊戒處必掩身毋躁止聲色毋或進
薄滋味毋致和節耆欲定心氣百官靜
事無刑以定晏陰之所成
江一川
考試官教諭蔡　批　陰之微陽爲之爲陰陽之
punctuated:
縈伯戲少待之謀，李孫非不知也。雖叔子偶以𦨦師戰敗，夫豈不可收餘燼而借一乎？何乃欲姑息於目前，遂受盟於城下，臨難苟免，以辱魯國？是豈謀國自强之道哉？其視華元退楚人之急園、國佐郤晉師之進逼而終不爲所屈者，有愧多矣。故不言四鄙及與吳盟，蓋諱其恥也，而爲相之道見焉。雖然，將相之道有本焉，仁義而已矣。明於仁義，則必先格君心以興周道，故以之治人則爲德政，以之戡亂則爲德威，而臨敵應變、折衝禦侮皆不足言矣。世衰道微，莫知此義，陷溺既深，愈趨愈下，遂使楚遂、夫差相繼爭伯，而中國不復得爲中國矣。悲夫！

禮記
君子齊戒，處必掩身，毋躁；止聲色，毋或進；薄滋味，毋致和；節耆欲，定心氣；百官靜，事無刑，以定晏陰之所成。
江一川

translation_en:
…Ying Bo’s proposal to wait a little [?] was not unknown to Li Sun [?]. Although Shuzi happened to suffer defeat with a detachment [?], could he not have gathered the surviving forces and made one more attempt [?]? Why seek immediate accommodation and consequently accept a covenant beneath the city walls, escaping danger at any cost and bringing disgrace upon the state of Lu? Was this the way to plan for the state and strengthen it? Compared with Hua Yuan, who relieved the urgent siege by the men of Chu [?], and Guo Zuo, who repelled the advancing army of Jin, neither ultimately yielding to the enemy, he had much to be ashamed of. Thus the text does not mention the four border regions or the covenant with Wu: it conceals this disgrace. Here the proper way of serving as a minister becomes apparent.
Nevertheless, the way of generals and ministers has a foundation: benevolence and righteousness alone. Those who understand benevolence and righteousness must first rectify their ruler’s heart so as to revive the Way of Zhou. Applied to governing the people, these become virtuous government; applied to suppressing disorder, they become virtuous might. Facing enemies, responding to changing circumstances, repelling attacks, and resisting aggression are then scarcely worth mentioning. As the age declined and the Way grew faint, no one understood this principle. Deeply sunk in error, they descended ever further, allowing Chu Sui [?] and Fuchai successively to contend for hegemony, until the Central States could no longer be the Central States. Alas!

Book of Rites
“When the noble man purifies himself and fasts, he must remain secluded in his dwelling and avoid agitation. He must put a stop to music and sensual pleasures, allowing none to be presented; eat plain food, without richly blended flavors; restrain his appetites and desires; and steady his mind and vital energy. The hundred officials must remain quiet, and affairs must involve no punishments, so as to secure what yin has brought to completion in repose.”
Jiang Yichuan

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□可及
考試官教授匡　批
定是篇之所成處以身與刑
分配發明扶陽抑陰之意始盡庭試詰陰之疑矣
君子無所不謹者惟以俟天之定而已夫陰陽
交競而災疾乘之矣君子於未定之前烏得忽
而不謹哉今夫身以立政固不可不使强固君
子則齋戒以致精明掩蔽以防身體匪直無躁
也而於耳目之聲色皆止之而不進匪直薄和
也而於諸事之愛欲皆節之而不淫凡於心氣
===
經靜定之功不使搖精以勞形也刑以輔治固
不可不致欽恤君子則以王者任德不任刑居
上以寬不以猛故百官府皆靜事不行雖有奸
慝亦措刑不用凡以刑罰亦陰事之屬不欲助
陰以抑陽也所以然者何哉誠以陽主動陰居
靜乃造化之常而陽主生陰主殺有淑慝之分
故凡人身之疾天下之災皆陰之侵陽爲之也
此仲夏之月天地相遇而不無彼此之爭陰陽
相摩而或致乖異之應故定心氣者所以□□
punctuated:
□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□可及。
考試官教授匡批：「定，是篇之所成處，以身與刑分配發明，扶陽抑陰之意始盡，庭試詰陰之疑矣。」
君子無所不謹者，惟以俟天之定而已。夫陰陽交競，而災疾乘之矣。君子於未定之前，烏得忽而不謹哉？今夫身以立政，固不可不使强固。君子則齋戒以致精明，掩蔽以防身體，匪直無躁也，而於耳目之聲色，皆止之而不進；匪直薄和也，而於諸事之愛欲，皆節之而不淫。凡於心氣，經靜定之功，不使搖精以勞形也。刑以輔治，固不可不致欽恤。君子則以王者任德不任刑，居上以寬不以猛，故百官府皆靜事不行，雖有奸慝，亦措刑不用。凡以刑罰亦陰事之屬，不欲助陰以抑陽也。所以然者何哉？誠以陽主動，陰居靜，乃造化之常；而陽主生，陰主殺，有淑慝之分。故凡人身之疾、天下之災，皆陰之侵陽爲之也。此仲夏之月，天地相遇，而不無彼此之爭；陰陽相摩，而或致乖異之應。故定心氣者，所以□□
translation_en:
…[Twenty-four illegible characters] can attain [?].
Examiner Kuang, Instructor, comments: “‘Settling’ is where this essay achieves its purpose. By explaining it separately in relation to the person and to punishments, the essay fully brings out the intention of supporting yang and restraining yin, addressing the doubt about yin raised in the court examination [?].”
The gentleman is careful in all things simply so that he may await Heaven’s settling into order. When yin and yang contend, calamities and illnesses take advantage of their contention. Before order has been settled, how could the gentleman be negligent and fail to exercise care? Now, since the person is the basis for establishing government, one must certainly make it strong and sound. The gentleman therefore purifies himself through fasting and abstinence to achieve spiritual clarity, and keeps himself secluded to protect his body. He does not merely avoid agitation: he excludes all sounds and sights that might reach his ears and eyes, allowing none to enter. He does not merely reduce rich, blended flavors: he moderates his desires concerning all affairs, allowing no excess. In everything concerning his mind and vital energy, he applies the discipline of stillness and composure, preventing disturbance of his vital essence from exhausting his body.
Since punishments assist in governing, one must certainly exercise reverent care and compassion in their use. The gentleman holds that a true king relies on virtue rather than punishment, and, in occupying a superior position, employs leniency rather than severity. Thus all government offices suspend their business and undertake no action; even when there is wickedness, punishments are set aside and left unused. This is because punishments, too, belong to the category of yin affairs, and he does not wish to strengthen yin so as to suppress yang.
Why is this so? It is because yang governs movement and yin abides in stillness: this is the constant pattern of creation and transformation. Yet yang governs life and yin governs killing, so there is a distinction between the beneficial and the harmful. Thus all illnesses of the human body and calamities throughout the realm arise from yin encroaching upon yang. In this midsummer month, Heaven and Earth encounter each other, and some contention between them is inevitable; yin and yang press against each other and may produce anomalous responses. Hence settling the mind and vital energy is the means by which [two illegible characters]…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
陽也陽道常饒而微陰不敢與爭及其久也
陽□而陰進矣循序而往無所爭競豈爲吾身
之災乎靜刑罰省所以抑彼之陰使陰道常乏
而不能與盛陽爭及其既也陰成而陽往矣順
序而行無所乖逆豈爲天下之災乎是則君子
不惟致和於一身而又致和於天下其順時行
令也何如哉抑考坤之初六曰履霜堅氷至姤
之初六曰羸豕孚蹢躅蓋皆於其□□而欲早
爲之備也夫天地以生物爲心豈陽直善而陰
===
直惡哉但其大分則如此耳故聖人作易於一
陽初生常慮其微於一陰初生常慮其盛蓋純
陽不害純陰亦不害惟其交際之時陰與陽競
斯害矣是故月令於夏之午冬之子各致其愼
重之意焉亦所以爲訓也讀禮君子不可不知
合父子之親明長幼之序以敬四海之内
天子如此則禮行矣
劉昭文
考試官教諭葉　批　禮行庭抑言五□□□□
punctuated:
陽也。陽道常饒，而微陰不敢與爭。及其久也，陽□而陰進矣，循序而往，無所爭競，豈爲吾身之災乎？靜刑罰省，所以抑彼之陰，使陰道常乏，而不能與盛陽爭。及其既也，陰成而陽往矣，順序而行，無所乖逆，豈爲天下之災乎？是則君子不惟致和於一身，而又致和於天下，其順時行令也何如哉！抑考《坤》之初六曰：「履霜，堅氷至。」《姤》之初六曰：「羸豕孚蹢躅。」蓋皆於其□□而欲早爲之備也。夫天地以生物爲心，豈陽直善而陰直惡哉？但其大分則如此耳。故聖人作《易》，於一陽初生，常慮其微；於一陰初生，常慮其盛。蓋純陽不害，純陰亦不害；惟其交際之時，陰與陽競，斯害矣。是故《月令》於夏之午、冬之子，各致其愼重之意焉，亦所以爲訓也。讀《禮》君子不可不知。

合父子之親，明長幼之序，以敬四海之内。天子如此，則禮行矣。

劉昭文

考試官教諭葉，批：禮行庭抑言五□□□□
translation_en:
…yang. The way of yang remains abundant, and the faint yin does not dare contend with it. In time, yang [illegible] and yin advances. Proceeding in due sequence without contention, how could this bring calamity upon one’s own person? Keeping still and reducing punishments [?] serves to restrain that yin, keeping its way deficient so that it cannot contend with flourishing yang. When this process is complete, yin matures and yang withdraws. Moving in proper sequence without discord or opposition, how could this bring calamity upon the realm? Thus the gentleman brings harmony not only to his own person but also to all under Heaven. How well he follows the seasons in carrying out their ordinances!

Consider also the first, yin line of Kun, the Receptive: “Tread on frost, and solid ice will come”; and the first, yin line of Gou, Encounter: “The lean pig is sure to leap and stamp.” Both seek to make preparations early, when [two characters illegible]. Now, Heaven and Earth take the generation of living things as their purpose. Could yang be simply good and yin simply evil? It is only in their broad distinction that they are so. Thus, when the sages composed the Changes, they were always concerned about the weakness of the single yang line at its first emergence, and about the strength of the single yin line at its first emergence. Pure yang does no harm, nor does pure yin. It is only at their meeting, when yin contends with yang, that harm arises. Accordingly, the Monthly Ordinances expresses particular caution at summer’s wu and winter’s zi—the summer and winter solstices. This too serves as instruction. Gentlemen who read the Rites must understand it.

“Unite fathers and sons in affection, clarify the order between elder and younger, and thereby bring respect throughout the Four Seas. When the Son of Heaven acts thus, ritual propriety prevails.”

Liu Zhaowen.

Examiner Ye, Instructor, comments: “Ritual propriety prevails … [the remaining transcription, 庭抑言五□□□□, is unclear] …”

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
見大禮之本
考試官教授伍　批　能道出天子行禮之家
王者立愛敬而推於天下此禮之所以行也夫
天下之禮皆本於王者之一身也愛敬立而德
教加焉禮烏有不行哉記樂者意謂禮樂不與
則王道不成而樂之所至必禮之至者爲之先
也非王者其孰能之是故不可解於心者父子
之親而或有不合者以人而間天也王者則以
孰不爲子而我則子之大者乃於親有不合焉
===
何以立愛於是合其父子之親則所以尊養之
者無不至矣不可紊於人者長幼之序而或有
不明者以欲而滅理也王者則以孰不爲幼而
我則幼之大者乃於序有不明焉何以立敬於
是明其長幼之序則所以惇叙之者無不周旁
夫親合則家齊而四海之家其父同也民彝洪
亂不有弗祗服厥父者乎由是親以及親而於
以孝使各率其天性之良而無傷厥考是四海
之父吾皆得而敬之也序明則族睦而四海之
punctuated:
見大禮之本。
考試官教授伍，批：「能道出天子行禮之家。」
王者立愛敬而推於天下，此禮之所以行也。夫天下之禮，皆本於王者之一身也。愛敬立而德教加焉，禮烏有不行哉？記樂者意謂禮樂不與，則王道不成，而樂之所至，必禮之至者爲之先也。非王者，其孰能之？是故不可解於心者，父子之親；而或有不合者，以人而間天也。王者則以孰不爲子，而我則子之大者，乃於親有不合焉，何以立愛？於是合其父子之親，則所以尊養之者無不至矣。不可紊於人者，長幼之序；而或有不明者，以欲而滅理也。王者則以孰不爲幼，而我則幼之大者，乃於序有不明焉，何以立敬？於是明其長幼之序，則所以惇叙之者無不周旁。夫親合則家齊，而四海之家，其父同也。民彝洪亂，不有弗祗服厥父者乎？由是親以及親，而於以孝，使各率其天性之良，而無傷厥考，是四海之父，吾皆得而敬之也。序明則族睦，而四海之
translation_en:
…reveals the foundation of the great rites.
Examiner Wu, an Instructor, comments: “It succeeds in expressing the household in which the Son of Heaven practices ritual [?].”
The ruler establishes love and reverence and extends them throughout the realm: this is how ritual comes to be practiced. All the rites of the realm have their foundation in the ruler’s own person. Once love and reverence are established and moral instruction is applied, how could ritual fail to prevail? The author of the Record of Music means that unless ritual and music flourish together, the kingly Way cannot be perfected; wherever music reaches, ritual must first have reached. Who but the ruler could accomplish this?
Thus, the affection between father and son must never be loosened in the heart. Where their relationship nevertheless lacks harmony, human interference has come between them and Heaven. The ruler therefore reflects: “Who is not a son? Yet I am the foremost among sons. If I should fail to maintain harmony in this affection, how could I establish love?” Accordingly, he brings harmony to the affection between father and son, leaving nothing wanting in the honor and support he gives his father.
The order between elder and younger must never be confused in human relations. Where it is nevertheless unclear, desire has extinguished principle. The ruler therefore reflects: “Who is not a junior? Yet I am the foremost among juniors. If I should fail to make this order clear, how could I establish reverence?” Accordingly, he clarifies the order between elder and younger, leaving nothing incomplete in his efforts to strengthen and properly arrange these relationships [?].
When familial affection is harmonious, the household is well regulated; and fathers in households throughout the realm share the same standing. When the constant norms of human relations fall into great disorder, are there not those who fail reverently to serve their fathers? Hence, extending affection for one’s own parent to the parents of others and instructing them in filial devotion [?], one enables each person to follow the goodness of his innate nature and not cause his father hurt. In this way, I can show reverence to all fathers throughout the realm. When the order between elder and younger is clear, the lineage is harmonious; and throughout the realm…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
族其長同也人紀廢壞不有弗克念天顯者乎
由是長以及長而敎以順使各展其固心之友
而貴於用命是四海之長吾皆得而敬之也夫
禮之所以不行於天下者誠以上無皇極之君
也今天子如此但見天叙有典父子其一也合
親以敬四海之父則典自我立而用行於天下
自是而推之五典將無不惇矣天秩有禮長幼
其一也明序以敬四海之長則禮自我立而用
行於天下自是而推之五禮將無不庸矣謂之
曰禮行信乎其禮之行達之四海而不悖歟嘗
讀書至堯典曰克明峻德以親九族平章百姓
協和萬邦伊尹之訓大甲則曰立愛惟親立敬
惟長始於家邦終於四海此可見唐虞三代之
治無非脩禮以達義也其至和薰蒸而大樂達
厥有由已後世禮樂不明治皆茍且故程子曰
先王以道治天下後世只是以法把持而已然
則神而明之豈不存乎其人哉
第貳塲
punctuated:
族，其長同也。人紀廢壞，不有弗克念天顯者乎？由是長以及長，而敎以順，使各展其固心之友，而貴於用命，是四海之長吾皆得而敬之也。夫禮之所以不行於天下者，誠以上無皇極之君也。今天子如此，但見天叙有典，父子其一也；合親以敬四海之父，則典自我立，而用行於天下，自是而推之，五典將無不惇矣。天秩有禮，長幼其一也；明序以敬四海之長，則禮自我立，而用行於天下，自是而推之，五禮將無不庸矣。謂之曰禮行，信乎其禮之行，達之四海而不悖歟！嘗讀書至堯典，曰：「克明峻德，以親九族，平章百姓，協和萬邦。」伊尹之訓大甲，則曰：「立愛惟親，立敬惟長，始於家邦，終於四海。」此可見唐虞三代之治，無非脩禮以達義也。其至和薰蒸，而大樂達，厥有由已。後世禮樂不明，治皆茍且。故程子曰：「先王以道治天下，後世只是以法把持而已。」然則神而明之，豈不存乎其人哉？

第貳塲
translation_en:
…clans throughout the realm have elders whose standing is the same. When human relationships fall into ruin, are there not those who fail to heed Heaven’s manifest order? Thus, one extends regard for one’s own elders to the elders of others and teaches obedience, enabling everyone to express the fraternal affection inherent in the heart [?] and to value compliance with commands. In this way I can show respect to all the elders within the Four Seas.

The reason ritual fails to prevail throughout the world is surely that there is no ruler above who embodies the supreme standard. With the Son of Heaven acting thus, we see that Heaven’s ordering of relationships has its norms, of which the relationship between father and son is one. By uniting kin and thereby respecting all fathers within the Four Seas, I establish these norms and put them into practice throughout the world. Extending this further, all five norms of human relationships will be earnestly observed. Heaven’s ordering of ranks has its rites, of which the relationship between elder and younger is one. By clarifying precedence and thereby respecting all elders within the Four Seas, I establish these rites and put them into practice throughout the world. Extending this further, all five categories of rites will be employed. This is called the prevalence of ritual. Truly, its practice reaches throughout the Four Seas without contradiction!

I once read in the Book of Documents, in the Canon of Yao: “He made manifest his lofty virtue and thereby brought affection to the nine degrees of kinship; he distinguished and ordered the hundred clans and harmonized the myriad states.” In Yi Yin’s instruction to Tai Jia, he says: “Establish love through one’s kin; establish respect through one’s elders. Begin with the family and state, and extend to the Four Seas.” From this we can see that the government of Tang and Yu and of the Three Dynasties consisted entirely in cultivating ritual to give full expression to righteousness. There was indeed a reason why their consummate harmony suffused all things and their great music spread everywhere. In later ages, ritual and music were no longer understood, and government became wholly makeshift. Thus Master Cheng said: “The former kings governed the world through the Way; later ages merely kept it under control through laws.” Does not making these principles wondrously effective and illuminating them, then, depend upon the right person?

Second Session

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
論
聖人貴未然之防
張希舉
同考試官教諭鄧　批　是作疊疊千餘言初不露鋒
鋩而抑揚開闔機軸自別蓋非造理之精深者不能到此
同考試官教諭唐　批　精而核曲而中殆不可以
凡士目之也
同考試官教諭徐　批　說理精確而開闔起伏咸
中矩度是素有養者

===
考試官教授伍　批　博雅近於古作
天下之相尋而不窮者變也擬其變而豫爲之

punctuated:
論

聖人貴未然之防

張希舉

translation_en:
Discourse

Sages Value Prevention Before Events Occur

By Zhang Xiju

Comment by Associate Examiner Deng, Instructor: This composition unfolds layer upon layer through more than a thousand words, without initially displaying its sharp edge. Yet in its modulation, opening out, and drawing together, its organizing conception is distinctive. Surely only someone whose penetration of principle is profound and precise could attain this.

Comment by Associate Examiner Tang, Instructor: Subtle yet exact, intricate yet on target: its author can hardly be regarded as an ordinary scholar.

Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor: Its exposition of principle is precise, and its opening and closing, rising and falling, all conform to proper standards. This is someone who has long cultivated himself.

Comment by Examiner Ye, Instructor: The topic is clear enough in itself, but writers generally discuss it in terms of incipient signs, failing to understand that the sages’ preventive measures leave nothing unattended. What disorder, then, could have incipient signs [?]? This composition distinctly adduces the recorded deeds of ancient sages, explaining its meaning thoroughly and in detail. Moreover, it argues that Heaven cannot abolish principle, yet certainly cannot allow matters simply to cease; that sages, too, have something they seek to benefit through prevention [?]. Thus it comprehends the subtleties of both Heaven [?] and the sages.

Comment by Examiner Wu, Professor: Broad in learning and elegant, approaching the writings of antiquity.

What follows one thing after another without end in the world is change. Those who anticipate such changes and take preventive measures beforehand, so that they do not develop into upheaval, are the sages. Sages are not capable of standing outside change. When changes arrive in succession, sages and ordinary people alike cannot evade them, yet …

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
□人每無以豫防之是故積微以漸積漸以著
其端莫可禦而變是用成惟聖人者深思遠覽
識之於無事之時迎而遏之於朕兆莫窺之始
於是所謂相尋者有其理而無其應天下欣欣
然安於變之不作而不知其功則聖人有以防
之於未然也嗚呼防之而能使不至於變此聖
人所以貴未然之防歟蓋嘗讀易有以知邵子
之說矣夬之爲卦以五陽決一陰此陽極盛之
時也而姤次焉剝之爲卦以一陽乘五陰此陰
===
極盛之時也而復次焉非所謂　治一亂變之
相尋而不窮者乎然則是變也天實爲之顧有
責夫聖人之防之者何也蓋天之心非不欲世
之常治而於二氣五行亦不能廢其盈虛消息
之理其治與亂始有循環而代至者然其心不
容遂已也於是生聖人焉以救助於其間與之
聰明睿智之質所以使能察也與之剛健中正
之德所以使有爲也與之以位所以使得行其
志也而聖人者承天之命先民之憂者也此防
punctuated:
□人每無以豫防之，是故積微以漸，積漸以著，其端莫可禦，而變是用成。惟聖人者，深思遠覽，識之於無事之時，迎而遏之於朕兆莫窺之始。於是所謂相尋者，有其理而無其應。天下欣欣然安於變之不作，而不知其功，則聖人有以防之於未然也。嗚呼！防之而能使不至於變，此聖人所以貴未然之防歟！
蓋嘗讀《易》，有以知邵子之說矣。夬之爲卦，以五陽決一陰，此陽極盛之時也，而姤次焉；剝之爲卦，以一陽乘五陰，此陰極盛之時也，而復次焉。非所謂治一亂，變之相尋而不窮者乎？然則是變也，天實爲之，顧有責夫聖人之防之者，何也？
蓋天之心，非不欲世之常治，而於二氣五行，亦不能廢其盈虛消息之理。其治與亂，始有循環而代至者，然其心不容遂已也。於是生聖人焉，以救助於其間。與之聰明睿智之質，所以使能察也；與之剛健中正之德，所以使有爲也；與之以位，所以使得行其志也。而聖人者，承天之命，先民之憂者也。此防
translation_en:
…people [?] are often unable to guard against it beforehand. Thus minute developments accumulate by degrees, and gradual developments accumulate until they become manifest. Their beginnings can no longer be checked, and change consequently takes shape. Only the sage, through profound reflection and far-reaching vision, recognizes it while all is still calm and intercepts and arrests it at its inception, before any portent can be discerned. Thus what is said to follow in succession retains its underlying principle but produces no corresponding manifestation. All under Heaven rejoice in the security afforded by the absence of upheaval, unaware of the achievement behind it: the sage has guarded against it before it occurred. Ah! To guard against something and thereby keep it from developing into upheaval—is this why the sage values prevention before the event?
Having read the Book of Changes, I have come to understand Master Shao’s explanation. In the hexagram Guai (Resolution), five yang lines displace a single yin line. This is the moment when yang is at its fullest strength, yet Gou (Encounter) follows it. In the hexagram Bo (Stripping Away), one yang line rests above five yin lines. This is the moment when yin is at its fullest strength, yet Fu (Return) follows it. Is this not what is meant by order and disorder [?], changes following one another without end? If Heaven itself brings about these changes, why nevertheless require the sage to guard against them?
Heaven’s intention is certainly that the world should remain well ordered. Yet, with respect to the two vital forces and the Five Phases, even Heaven cannot abolish the principle of their fullness and emptiness, waning and waxing. Hence order and disorder come in cycles, alternating with one another. Yet Heaven’s intention does not permit it simply to leave matters there. It therefore brings forth sages to provide aid amid these changes. It endows them with intelligence, insight, sagacity, and wisdom so that they can discern; it endows them with the virtues of firmness, vigor, centrality, and rectitude so that they can act; and it grants them positions so that they can carry out their purposes. The sage receives Heaven’s mandate and anticipates the people’s troubles. This prevention…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
□人每無以豫防之是故積微以漸積漸以著
其端莫可禦而變是用成惟聖人者深思遠覽
謹之於無事之時迎而過之於朕兆莫窺之始
於是所謂相尋者有其理而無其應天下欣欣
然安於變之不作而不知其功則聖人有以防
之於未然也嗚呼防之而能使不至於變此聖
人所以貴未然之防歟蓋嘗讀易有以知邵子
之說矣夬之爲卦以五陽決一陰此陽極盛之
時也而姤次焉剝之爲卦以一陽乘五陰此陰
===
極盛之時也而復次焉非所謂一治一亂變之
相尋而不窮者乎然則是變也天實爲之顧有
責夫聖人之防之者何也蓋天之心非不欲世
之常治而於二氣五行亦不能廢其盈虛消息
之理其治與亂始有循環而代至者然其心不
容遂已也於是生聖人焉以救助於其間與之
聰明睿智之質所以使能察也與之剛健中正
之德所以使有爲也與之以位所以使得行其
志也而聖人者承天之命先民之憂者也比防
punctuated:
□人每無以豫防之，是故積微以漸，積漸以著，其端莫可禦，而變是用成。惟聖人者深思遠覽，謹之於無事之時，迎而過之於朕兆莫窺之始。於是所謂相尋者，有其理而無其應。天下欣欣然安於變之不作，而不知其功，則聖人有以防之於未然也。嗚呼！防之而能使不至於變，此聖人所以貴未然之防歟？

translation_en:
… people [?] generally have no means of guarding against it beforehand. Thus minute developments gradually accumulate, and gradual developments become manifest; their beginnings can no longer be checked, and upheaval consequently takes shape. Only the sage, thinking deeply and looking far ahead, takes precautions when all is still quiet and anticipates and forestalls it at its inception, before any signs can be discerned. Thus what is said to follow in succession retains its underlying principle but finds no actual manifestation. All under Heaven rejoice in the security of a world without upheaval, unaware of the sage’s achievement: he has found the means to prevent it before it occurs. Alas! To take precautions and thereby keep matters from reaching upheaval—is this why the sage values prevention before the event?

Having read the Book of Changes, I have come to understand Master Shao’s explanation. In the hexagram Guai (Breakthrough), five yang lines dislodge a single yin line: this is the moment when yang is at its fullest strength, yet Gou (Encounter) follows it. In the hexagram Bo (Stripping Away), a single yang line rests above five yin lines: this is the moment when yin is at its fullest strength, yet Fu (Return) follows it. Is this not what is meant by alternating order and disorder, changes following one another without end? Yet if Heaven itself brings about these changes, why is the sage charged with preventing them? It is not that Heaven’s heart does not desire lasting order in the world. But even with respect to the two vital forces and the Five Phases, it cannot abolish the principles of fullness and emptiness, waning and waxing. Hence order and disorder recur in cycles and arrive in alternation. Yet Heaven’s heart cannot simply leave matters there. It therefore brings forth sages to offer succor amid these changes. It gives them perceptiveness and wisdom so that they can discern; it gives them the virtues of strength, vigor, centrality, and uprightness so that they can act; and it gives them positions of authority so that they can carry out their purposes. The sage receives Heaven’s mandate and anticipates the people’s troubles. This [?] prevention …

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
之之責所以在聖人也聖人既知夫責之有在
又計以為變之在天下方相尋而不窮而吾無
以擬其至而豫為之防則將竭其力而無所用
也是故及其未然防之蓋其於民嘗導之而生
養遂矣而頒之職事通之貨泉資之國服以防
其匱者無弗至也嘗敎之而倫理明矣而戒之
用休董之用威勸之以九歌以防其壞者無弗
至也嘗治之而爭奪息矣而警之遒人糾之黨
正察之司救訶諫以防其入於刑者無弗至也
===
猶未也觀諸在朝賢人君子皆已登用矣而難
任人聖讒說殄行以防倖進之門者不敢懈也
觀諸四海皆已無虞矣而憂困窮畏勝寺以防
釁薛之萌者不敢懈也觀諸四夷皆已賓服矣
而戒怠荒審玩好以防窺伺之端者不敢懈也
猶未也帝德已罔愆矣而叢脞之防見於歌者
惕如也厥中已允執矣而荒亡之防載於訓者
昭如也聰明齊聖德則已至矣而勝義勝敬之
防著於銘者凜如也夫惟聖人內脩其身外脩
punctuated:
之之責，所以在聖人也。聖人既知夫責之有在，又計以為變之在天下，方相尋而不窮，而吾無以擬其至而豫為之防，則將竭其力而無所用也。是故及其未然防之。蓋其於民，嘗導之而生養遂矣，而頒之職事，通之貨泉，資之國服，以防其匱者，無弗至也；嘗敎之而倫理明矣，而戒之用休，董之用威，勸之以九歌，以防其壞者，無弗至也；嘗治之而爭奪息矣，而警之遒人，糾之黨正，察之司救訶諫，以防其入於刑者，無弗至也。
猶未也。觀諸在朝，賢人君子皆已登用矣，而難任人，聖讒說殄行，以防倖進之門者，不敢懈也；觀諸四海，皆已無虞矣，而憂困窮，畏勝寺，以防釁薛之萌者，不敢懈也；觀諸四夷，皆已賓服矣，而戒怠荒，審玩好，以防窺伺之端者，不敢懈也。
猶未也。帝德已罔愆矣，而叢脞之防見於歌者，惕如也；厥中已允執矣，而荒亡之防載於訓者，昭如也；聰明齊聖，德則已至矣，而勝義勝敬之防著於銘者，凜如也。夫惟聖人內脩其身，外脩
translation_en:
…the responsibility for guarding against them therefore rests with the sage. Knowing where this responsibility lies, the sage further reflects that upheavals throughout the realm follow one another without end. If he cannot anticipate their arrival and take precautions beforehand, he will exhaust his strength to no purpose. Thus he guards against them before they occur. He has already guided the people so that their livelihoods and nurture are assured; yet he assigns them occupations and duties, facilitates the circulation of goods and currency, and supplies them through the state's services [?], leaving nothing undone to guard against want. He has already taught them so that ethical relationships are clear; yet he exhorts them with blessings, supervises them with awe-inspiring authority, and encourages them through the Nine Songs, leaving nothing undone to guard against moral decay. He has already governed them so that contention and strife have ceased; yet he has them admonished by heralds, corrected by neighborhood heads, and scrutinized and reproved by the officials charged with rescue from wrongdoing, leaving nothing undone to prevent their incurring punishment.
Nor is this all. Looking at the court, he sees that worthy men and gentlemen have all been appointed to office; yet he rejects flatterers and counters slanderous words and ruinous conduct [?], never daring to relax his guard against avenues to advancement through undue favor. Looking within the Four Seas, he sees that all is free from danger; yet he worries about those in distress and poverty and fears “sheng si” [?], never daring to relax his guard against the first stirrings of trouble [?]. Looking at the peoples of the four quarters, he sees that all have submitted; yet he guards against indolence and neglect and carefully scrutinizes objects of amusement, never daring to relax his guard against occasions for others to spy out opportunities against him.
Nor is this all. Imperial virtue is already without fault, yet the warning against preoccupation with petty matters expressed in song remains a source of vigilance. The mean is already faithfully upheld, yet the warning against dissipation and ruin recorded in the Instructions remains clear. Intelligence and sagely understanding have already brought virtue to its utmost, yet the warning in the inscription concerning that which overcomes righteousness and reverence remains a source of solemn apprehension. Thus the sage inwardly cultivates his person and outwardly cultivates…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
其政所以爲防者若是乎豫也是故以德則日
新以業則富有以神化則上下與天地同流而
所謂變者卒不得以其相尋之常爲聖人病天
下徒見夫聖人之在御歷數十年治安如一日
而其垂統於後或數百年或過其歷以爲是何
時之無變也又見夫後世亂日之多傳世之促
以爲是偶值其變也不知循環迭至之運聖人
所不能違者與夫人同而擬其至而豫爲之防
者聖人與夫人異故聖人之治始以奉天其終
===
也勝天後世之立國其始也幸而得天而其終
也無以祈天而永命譬之人之身生死壯老有
必至之時善養生者以延其年不善養者反是
皆人也非天也故曰防乎其防邦家其長子孫
其昌聖人貴未然之防也雖然聖人所以防未
然者非其心冀得夫邦家之長子孫之昌也冀
得之則是利焉而已利可以保治乎是故聖人
本之天德達之王道曰天德王道而內脩其身
外脩其政防乎其防者畢舉之矣〔然則欲事畢〕
punctuated: 其政，所以爲防者若是乎豫也。是故以德則日新，以業則富有，以神化則上下與天地同流，而所謂變者，卒不得以其相尋之常爲聖人病。天下徒見夫聖人之在御，歷數十年，治安如一日，而其垂統於後，或數百年，或過其歷，以爲是何時之無變也；又見夫後世亂日之多，傳世之促，以爲是偶值其變也。不知循環迭至之運，聖人所不能違者，與夫人同；而擬其至而豫爲之防者，聖人與夫人異。故聖人之治，始以奉天，其終也勝天。後世之立國，其始也幸而得天，而其終也無以祈天而永命。譬之人之身，生死壯老，有必至之時；善養生者以延其年，不善養者反是。皆人也，非天也。故曰：「防乎其防，邦家其長，子孫其昌。」聖人貴未然之防也。雖然，聖人所以防未然者，非其心冀得夫邦家之長、子孫之昌也。冀得之，則是利焉而已。利可以保治乎？是故聖人本之天德，達之王道。曰天德王道，而內脩其身，外脩其政，防乎其防者畢舉之矣。〔然則欲事畢〕
translation_en:
…his government: thus far in advance does he take precautions. Hence his virtue is renewed daily, his achievements grow abundant, and in his wondrous transforming influence he moves in the same current as Heaven and Earth, above and below. What are called changes, despite their constant succession, ultimately cannot afflict the sage. People throughout the realm merely see that, during the sage’s reign, peace and good order remain unchanged for several decades, and that the dynastic succession he bequeaths lasts for several hundred years, or even beyond its allotted span. They suppose that his must have been a time without change. Then, seeing how numerous the days of disorder and how brief the succession of rulers were in later ages, they suppose that these merely happened to encounter change. They do not understand that, in being unable to escape the cyclical course of events as they arrive in succession, sages are no different from ordinary people. Where sages differ is in anticipating their arrival and taking precautions beforehand. Thus the sage’s government begins by serving Heaven and ultimately prevails over Heaven. When later ages establish states, they are fortunate at first to gain Heaven’s favor, but in the end have no means of entreating Heaven to prolong their mandate.

Consider the human body: birth and death, vigor and old age each have their inevitable time. Those skilled in nurturing life prolong their years; those who nurture it poorly do the reverse. This all rests with human beings, not Heaven. Thus it is said: “Take precautions where precautions are due: the state shall endure, and descendants shall flourish.” The sage prizes precautions taken before trouble arises. Yet his reason for taking such precautions is not that he hopes in his heart to secure the endurance of his state and the flourishing of his descendants. To hope to obtain these would be nothing more than seeking advantage. Can advantage preserve good government? Thus the sage takes the virtue of Heaven as his foundation and gives it expression through the Kingly Way. In speaking of the virtue of Heaven and the Kingly Way, we mean that he cultivates himself inwardly and orders his government outwardly, putting into practice every precaution that ought to be taken. 〔If, then, one wishes to carry out fully [?]…〕

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
人之防者其尚求聖人之爲心
同前
江鯤
同考試官教諭李　批〔一氣呵成絕無窒礙且反覆治亂未然之防曲盡聖人心事子亦可與幾矣〕
同考試官教諭林　批〔邵子本易論作戒場中類能言之非泛則迂是作發揮詳盡且中矩矱可以爲難矣〕
考試官教諭葉　批〔說理精而馳騁頓挫𡙇異諸作葢邃於理學者〕
===
考試官教授伍　批〔學博而識遠詞達而氣昌錄之〕
聖人有見於天下之幾而預爲之所焉此所以
能通其變於未窮也夫天下之幾其所由來者
漸也而其終至於不可過是雖天地自然之理
然究而論之其治亂興衰之所以然者未始不
由人以致之是其幾又在我而不在天也夫以
不可測之數動舉而歸諸天而於吾所當爲者
則忽焉不加脩省而其成與否一聽其幾之自
punctuated:
人之防者，其尚求聖人之爲心。

同前。
江鯤。
同考試官教諭李，批〔一氣呵成，絕無窒礙，且反覆治亂未然之防，曲盡聖人心事，子亦可與幾矣〕。
同考試官教諭林，批〔邵子本易論作戒，場中類能言之，非泛則迂。是作發揮詳盡，且中矩矱，可以爲難矣〕。
考試官教諭葉，批〔說理精，而馳騁頓挫𡙇異諸作，葢邃於理學者〕。
考試官教授伍，批〔學博而識遠，詞達而氣昌，錄之〕。

聖人有見於天下之幾，而預爲之所焉，此所以能通其變於未窮也。夫天下之幾，其所由來者漸也，而其終至於不可過，是雖天地自然之理，然究而論之，其治亂興衰之所以然者，未始不由人以致之，是其幾又在我而不在天也。夫以不可測之數，動舉而歸諸天，而於吾所當爲者，則忽焉不加脩省，而其成與否，一聽其幾之自
translation_en:
…those who would take human precautions should seek to understand the intentions of the sages.

Same topic as above.
By Jiang Kun.

Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: 〔Written in a single sustained breath, without the slightest obstruction. Moreover, its repeated examination of precautions taken before order or disorder emerges fully conveys every subtlety of the sages’ concerns. You, too, may be counted among those who understand incipient developments.〕

Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: 〔Master Shao based his admonition on the Book of Changes. Candidates in the examination hall can generally discuss this, but their treatments are either vague or far-fetched. This composition develops the subject thoroughly and in detail, while also conforming to the proper standards: a difficult accomplishment indeed.〕

Examiner Ye, Instructor, comments: 〔Its exposition of principle is precise, and the sweep and rhythmic turns of its writing distinguish it markedly [?] from the other compositions. Its author is evidently deeply versed in the Learning of Principle.〕

Examiner Wu, Professor, comments: 〔Broad in learning and far-reaching in judgment, clear in expression and vigorous in spirit. Select it for inclusion.〕

The sages discern the incipient developments of the world and make provision for them in advance. This is how they can respond effectively to change before circumstances reach an impasse. The incipient developments of the world arise gradually, yet ultimately reach a point beyond which they cannot proceed. Although this is the natural principle of Heaven and Earth, upon examining the matter fully, the causes of order and disorder, flourishing and decline, invariably prove to be human actions. Thus these incipient developments lie with us, rather than with Heaven. If, treating them as an inscrutable destiny, we constantly attribute everything to Heaven, while carelessly neglecting cultivation and self-examination in matters that we ourselves ought to undertake, and leave success or failure entirely to the incipient developments themselves to…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
定則其始也夫天下之大可畏者隱于若不足畏
之中而其終遂至于極重而不可返者凡以不
能預爲之所也惟聖人者有見夫天下之治不
生于治之日蓋必有所由基天下之亂不生于
亂之日亦必有由兆其將治也則爲之闢其幾
使之日長而能善其治于未窮也其將亂也則
爲之闘其幾使之日消而能遏其亂于未窮也
此聖人所以貴未然之防也甞觀諸易矣夫
復一陽之卦也起震歷臨兌以至于乾而六陽
皆長焉蓋言天下極治之有漸也然乾遇于巽
而一陰生是治固亂之所伏也夫姤一陰之卦
也起巽歷坎艮以至于坤而六陰皆長焉蓋言
天下極亂之有漸也然坤遇于震而一陽生是
亂又治之所倚也此天地陰陽消息之機人事
物理盛衰之數其運不息其來不禦也故自復
至乾其間則有否矣而聖人於否之上爻則繫
之曰否終則傾何可長也所以示傾否之有道
也自姤至坤其間則有泰矣而聖人於泰之□
punctuated:
定，則其始也，夫天下之大可畏者，隱于若不足畏之中，而其終遂至于極重而不可返者，凡以不能預爲之所也。惟聖人者有見，夫天下之治不生于治之日，蓋必有所由基；天下之亂不生于亂之日，亦必有由兆。其將治也，則爲之闢其幾，使之日長，而能善其治于未窮也；其將亂也，則爲之闘其幾，使之日消，而能遏其亂于未窮也。此聖人所以貴未然之防也。
甞觀諸《易》矣。夫復，一陽之卦也，起震，歷臨、兌，以至于乾，而六陽皆長焉，蓋言天下極治之有漸也。然乾遇于巽而一陰生，是治固亂之所伏也。夫姤，一陰之卦也，起巽，歷坎、艮，以至于坤，而六陰皆長焉，蓋言天下極亂之有漸也。然坤遇于震而一陽生，是亂又治之所倚也。此天地陰陽消息之機，人事物理盛衰之數，其運不息，其來不禦也。故自復至乾，其間則有否矣，而聖人於否之上爻則繫之曰：「否終則傾，何可長也？」所以示傾否之有道也。自姤至坤，其間則有泰矣，而聖人於泰之□
translation_en:
…settle itself, then at its beginning [?]. The most fearsome things in the world lie concealed within what seems unworthy of fear. That they ultimately become overwhelmingly grave and irreversible is entirely due to the failure to make provision for them beforehand. Only the sage perceives that order in the world does not originate on the day when order prevails: it must have foundations laid earlier. Disorder in the world does not originate on the day when disorder prevails either: it too must have earlier portents. When order is about to arise, he opens the way for its incipient tendencies, allowing them to grow daily, and can thus perfect that order before its course is exhausted. When disorder is about to arise, he combats its incipient tendencies [?], allowing them to diminish daily, and can thus check that disorder before it reaches its utmost extent. This is why the sage values precautions against what has not yet happened.
I have examined this in the Book of Changes. Return (Fu) is a hexagram with one yang line. Beginning with Zhen, passing through Lin and Dui, and reaching Qian, all six yang lines grow to fullness. This speaks of the gradual development of supreme order in the world. Yet when Qian encounters Xun, one yin line is born: thus disorder indeed lies hidden within order. Encounter (Gou) is a hexagram with one yin line. Beginning with Xun, passing through Kan and Gen, and reaching Kun, all six yin lines grow to fullness. This speaks of the gradual development of extreme disorder in the world. Yet when Kun encounters Zhen, one yang line is born: thus order, in turn, rests upon disorder. These are the workings of the waxing and waning of yin and yang in Heaven and Earth, and the patterns of flourishing and decline in human affairs and the principles of things. Their movement never ceases; their coming cannot be resisted.
Thus, between Fu and Qian there is Stagnation (Pi). To the top line of Pi the sage appended these words: “When stagnation reaches its end, it is overturned. How could it endure?” This shows that there is a way to overturn stagnation. Between Gou and Kun there is Peace (Tai), and the sage, concerning Tai’s □ [illegible]…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
久則繫之曰城復于隍其命亂也所以示保泰
之有道也蓋聖人之於天下也當其積衰至
於開必先也非不知時之方來而未已也然豈
其徐徐然聽其自治而不預爲之所哉是故紀
綱之未振必思所以振之法制之未齊必思所
以齊之君子之未用必思所以用之中國之未
尊必思所以尊之凡所以培埴長養調停宣洩
夫天地之陽和者靡不爲未然之防也及夫薰
蒸既久時之將極也則又爲之勑天之命惟時
===
惟幾焉神而化之使民宜之焉凡此皆所以迎
治平之盛保有道之長也當其治極思亂其幾
已見也非不知其亂之方來而莫遏也然豈忍
泄泄然聽其自亂而不預爲之所哉是故紀綱
將蠱必思所以飭之法制將解必思所以聯之
小人將進必思所以抑之夷狄將乘必思所以
驅之凡所以芟刈祈除摧陷廓清夫天地之陰
慝者靡不爲未然之防也不幸遭時之極勢不
可返也則亦爲之周旋委曲以弘濟于艱難焉
punctuated:
久，則繫之曰：「城復于隍，其命亂也。」所以示保泰之有道也。蓋聖人之於天下也，當其積衰至於開必先也，非不知時之方來而未已也，然豈其徐徐然聽其自治而不預爲之所哉？是故紀綱之未振，必思所以振之；法制之未齊，必思所以齊之；君子之未用，必思所以用之；中國之未尊，必思所以尊之。凡所以培埴長養、調停宣洩夫天地之陽和者，靡不爲未然之防也。及夫薰蒸既久，時之將極也，則又爲之勑天之命，惟時惟幾焉，神而化之，使民宜之焉。凡此皆所以迎治平之盛，保有道之長也。
當其治極思亂，其幾已見也，非不知其亂之方來而莫遏也，然豈忍泄泄然聽其自亂而不預爲之所哉？是故紀綱將蠱，必思所以飭之；法制將解，必思所以聯之；小人將進，必思所以抑之；夷狄將乘，必思所以驅之。凡所以芟刈祈除、摧陷廓清夫天地之陰慝者，靡不爲未然之防也。不幸遭時之極，勢不可返也，則亦爲之周旋委曲，以弘濟于艱難焉。
translation_en:
…[The opening character 久 is doubtful here.] He then appends these words: “The city wall falls back into the moat; its commands are in disorder.” This shows that there is a way to preserve peace. In dealing with the world, when accumulated decline reaches the point where an opening must first appear [?], the sage is not unaware that the coming turn of the times is still unfolding. Yet how could he leisurely leave the world to put itself in order without making provision beforehand? Thus, if the guiding principles of government have not been restored, he must consider how to restore them; if laws and institutions have not been brought into order, he must consider how to order them; if gentlemen have not been employed, he must consider how to employ them; if the central realm has not been accorded due honor, he must consider how to secure that honor. Every means of cultivating and nourishing, regulating and giving free passage to the harmonious yang of Heaven and Earth serves as a precaution against troubles before they arise. Once its warming influence has long permeated the world and the times approach their culmination, he further attends reverently to Heaven’s mandate, considering the proper moment and the first subtle signs of change. He brings about transformation with wondrous efficacy, enabling the people to live as is fitting. All these measures welcome the flourishing of peaceful government and preserve the enduring rule of the Way.
When order reaches its height, he considers disorder, whose first subtle signs have already appeared. He is not unaware that disorder is approaching and cannot be checked. Yet how could he bear to remain idle, leaving the world to fall into disorder without making provision beforehand? Thus, when the guiding principles of government are about to decay, he must consider how to put them in order; when laws and institutions are about to come apart, he must consider how to hold them together; when petty men are about to advance, he must consider how to restrain them; when the Yi and Di are about to exploit an opportunity, he must consider how to drive them away. Every means of cutting away and removing [?], breaking down and thoroughly clearing away the malign yin of Heaven and Earth serves as a precaution against troubles before they arise. If, unfortunately, he encounters the utmost extremity of the times, when the course of events cannot be reversed, he nevertheless adapts his actions to circumstances with flexibility, so as to bring far-reaching relief amid hardship…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
遏其變使民不倦焉凡此皆所以絶致禍之源
反乎康之治也故聖人于豐則曰豐亨王假之
勿憂宜日中于臨則曰至于八月有凶若此者
何莫非聖人有見于天下之幾而預爲之所耶
是故其天下之將治也則逆爲致治之圖而治
日以長也如木之有萌蘖也條達滋長勢不可
已也其天下之將亂也則逆爲弭亂之慮而亂
日以銷也如農夫之去草也芟夷薀崇絶其根
芟也由是紀綱振而勿壞也天下綏於治矣禮
===
制齊而勿解也天下執於物矣君子在位小人
在野而朝廷無可乘之釁矣中國道長夷狄道
消而邊鄙無可乘之釁矣此聖人之治所以歷
萬年而勿壞者也故曰聖人能通其變于未窮
也幾微故幽神應故妙非天下之至聖其孰能
與于此哉雖然心普萬物而無心者其天乎情
順萬事而無情者其聖乎聖人所以往往貴未
然之防初豈揣摩億度天下之變于未來之先
而假術以濟之哉蓋天人之理本無二致
punctuated: 遏其變，使民不倦焉。凡此皆所以絶致禍之源，反乎康之治也。故聖人于豐則曰：「豐，亨，王假之，勿憂，宜日中。」于臨則曰：「至于八月有凶。」若此者，何莫非聖人有見于天下之幾，而預爲之所耶？是故其天下之將治也，則逆爲致治之圖，而治日以長也。如木之有萌蘖也，條達滋長，勢不可已也。其天下之將亂也，則逆爲弭亂之慮，而亂日以銷也。如農夫之去草也，芟夷薀崇，絶其根芟也。由是紀綱振而勿壞也，天下綏於治矣；禮制齊而勿解也，天下執於物矣；君子在位，小人在野，而朝廷無可乘之釁矣；中國道長，夷狄道消，而邊鄙無可乘之釁矣。此聖人之治所以歷萬年而勿壞者也。故曰：「聖人能通其變于未窮也。」幾微故幽，神應故妙，非天下之至聖，其孰能與于此哉？雖然，心普萬物而無心者，其天乎？情順萬事而無情者，其聖乎？聖人所以往往貴未然之防，初豈揣摩億度天下之變于未來之先，而假術以濟之哉？蓋天人之理，本無二致。
translation_en:
…check these changes and keep the people from growing weary. All these measures serve to cut off the sources of calamity and restore peaceful government. Thus, in the Book of Changes, under Abundance (Feng), the sage says: “Abundance brings success. The king attains it. Do not be anxious; be like the sun at midday.” Under Approach (Lin), he says: “When the eighth month comes, there will be misfortune.” Are not all such statements instances of the sage discerning the incipient tendencies of the world and making provision for them beforehand?

Thus, when the world is about to attain order, he prepares plans in advance to bring about good government, so that order grows daily. It is like a tree putting forth shoots: its branches spread and flourish with an unstoppable momentum. When the world is about to fall into disorder, he considers in advance how to quell it, so that disorder diminishes daily. It is like a farmer removing weeds: he cuts them down, heaps them up, and eradicates their roots [?]. Consequently, the guiding principles of government are invigorated and do not deteriorate, and the world rests securely in good order. Ritual institutions are set in order and do not fall slack, and the world is held to its proper observances [?]. Exemplary men hold office, while petty men remain outside government, leaving no opening at court that can be exploited. The Way of the Central Kingdom flourishes, while that of the Yi and Di declines, leaving no opening on the frontiers that can be exploited. This is why the sage’s government endures for ten thousand years without deteriorating.

Hence it is said: “The sage can accommodate change before circumstances reach an impasse.” Incipient tendencies are subtle and therefore hidden; the response is numinous and therefore wondrous. Who but the utmost sage in the world could participate in this? Yet is it not Heaven whose mind encompasses all things while having no deliberate intent? Is it not the sage whose feelings accord with all affairs while remaining free of partial feeling? In repeatedly valuing precautions against what has yet to happen, could the sage ever be merely conjecturing and guessing at changes in the world before their arrival, and borrowing techniques to deal with them? For the principles of Heaven and humanity are fundamentally one.

We humbly consider: the Son of Heaven establishes equilibrium and harmony, diligently setting right the supreme standard for the four quarters; the great ruler promotes rites and music, thereby illuminating the source of all transformation. Thus mutual responsiveness is fully expressed in both feeling and outward form, and the work of composition truly depends upon enlightened sageliness. Bringing peaceful and joyous music to completion, we thereby make harmony and tranquility manifest. Your servants Kai and the others, in utmost fear and trembling, bow our heads to the ground and repeatedly kowtow, presenting these words:

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
來也雖皆本于天地陰陽闔闢之數然吾心之
混乎太極而聖人之幾非在外也故闔之自
我闢之自我則天地之終始鬼神之消息有不
能外焉者矣所謂範圍天地之化而不過者也
嘗觀堯舜之治天下也萬邦已協和矣四方已
無虞矣日月星辰之變昆虫草木之妖亦皆已
銷息矣顧安所用其心哉然猶觀變巽命以先
天下之防也放逐凶奸以先朝廷之防也徂征
苗頑以先外夷之防也封山濬川脩五考度以
===
先萬世之防也此聖人之治所以至今不廢也
嗚嘑天下勢而已矣勢輕重也方其漸之萌也
識之早則反之易也乃姑徐徐焉而不爲之所
至于極重然後起而議之則已無及矣秦之柯
天下之不潰且亂也然則如漢七國之反唐□□
鎮之變宋西夏之憂豈非後世之永監也哉
表
擬禮部尚書陶凱等進宴饗九奏樂□
洪武四年
punctuated:
來也，雖皆本于天地陰陽闔闢之數，然吾心之混乎太極，而聖人之幾非在外也。故闔之自我，闢之自我，則天地之終始、鬼神之消息，有不能外焉者矣。所謂範圍天地之化而不過者也。嘗觀堯舜之治天下也，萬邦已協和矣，四方已無虞矣，日月星辰之變、昆虫草木之妖，亦皆已銷息矣。顧安所用其心哉？然猶觀變巽命，以先天下之防也；放逐凶奸，以先朝廷之防也；徂征苗頑，以先外夷之防也；封山濬川，脩五考度，以先萬世之防也。此聖人之治所以至今不廢也。嗚嘑！天下勢而已矣，勢輕重也。方其漸之萌也，識之早則反之易也，乃姑徐徐焉，而不爲之所。至于極重，然後起而議之，則已無及矣。秦之柯，天下之不潰且亂也。然則如漢七國之反、唐□□鎮之變、宋西夏之憂，豈非後世之永監也哉？

表
擬禮部尚書陶凱等進宴饗九奏樂□。
洪武四年。
translation_en:
…comes. Although all are rooted in the patterns of Heaven and Earth, yin and yang, closing and opening, my mind is united with the Supreme Ultimate, and the incipient impulses apprehended by the sage are not external to it. Thus closing proceeds from me, and opening proceeds from me; the endings and beginnings of Heaven and Earth, and the waning and waxing of spirits, cannot lie outside it. This is what is meant by encompassing the transformations of Heaven and Earth without exceeding them.

I have considered how Yao and Shun governed the realm. The myriad states were already harmonious, the four quarters already free from anxiety, and anomalies of the sun, moon, and stars, as well as uncanny manifestations among insects, plants, and trees, had all subsided. What, then, still required their attention? Yet they continued to observe changes and issue commands, taking precautions for the realm in advance; they banished the wicked and treacherous, taking precautions for the court in advance; they marched against the recalcitrant Miao, taking precautions against foreign peoples in advance; and they established boundaries at mountains, dredged rivers, and attended to the five matters and examined standards [?], taking precautions for ten thousand generations in advance. This is why the government of the sages has not fallen into disuse even today.

Alas! The affairs of the realm are simply a matter of the configuration of circumstances, which may be slight or weighty. When a gradual development first begins to emerge, recognizing it early makes it easy to reverse. Yet people merely dawdle and make no provision for it. Once it has become extremely grave, they finally rise to discuss it, but by then it is too late. Qin’s ke [?]—the realm did not collapse and yet fell into disorder [?]. Thus, were not the rebellion of the Seven Kingdoms under the Han, the upheaval of the Tang’s □□ garrisons [?], and the trouble caused by Xixia under the Song enduring warnings for later generations?

Memorial
A model memorial in the voice of Minister of Rites Tao Kai and others, presenting the music for nine performances at court banquets [final character illegible].
Fourth year of Hongwu [1371].

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
地同流肇啓虞廷賡歌載始繼隆周室豈
樂交孚授几席於臣工被論倫於管籥情

而令德欣欣相告肅肅是聽慨自雅頌之

免於歡哀陳閣酣歌臨春竟淫於豔麗泣

耳雜部盈庭匪能飾貌合情祇以增悲導

皇帝陛下
體道凝醇

夷仰
punctuated:
地同流，肇啓虞廷，賡歌載始；繼隆周室，豈樂交孚。授几席於臣工，被論倫於管籥。情周禮備，度廣倫清。戛擊鳴球，虞賓在位；登歌鼓棟，君子來朝。或示事以示情，終令儀而令德。欣欣相告，肅肅是聽。慨自雅頌之風微，馴致聲音之道晦。沛鄉醉酒，大風未免於歡哀；陳閣酣歌，臨春竟淫於豔麗。泣玄武而錫宴，七德誇功；集紫宸而肆筵，羣僊列仗。播合無關於作則，揚干何取於端儀？朱鷺鐃歌，旋競心於侈瑞；黃驄疊曲，曾罔意於思勳。比及胡元，盡隳樂化，吹笳充耳，雜部盈庭。匪能飾貌合情，祇以增悲導欲。聿追大雅，宜俟明時。
恭惟皇帝陛下，體道凝醇，綏猷致豫。戎商纘服，本太古之初風；用夏變夷，仰
translation_en:
…flowing together with the earth. First inaugurated at the court of Yu, the exchange of songs began; subsequently flourishing in the house of Zhou, joyful music inspired mutual trust. Seats and tables were bestowed upon the ministers, and ordered relationships were expressed through pipes and flutes [?]. Sentiments were fully expressed and ritual complete; measures were ample and relationships clear. Sounding jade chimes were struck, and the guest of Yu stood in his place; singers ascended and drums sounded [?], as noble men came to court. Sometimes deeds were displayed to reveal feelings, culminating in fine deportment and admirable virtue. Joyfully they told one another; reverently they listened.
Alas, as the influence of the Odes and Hymns waned, the Way of music gradually became obscured. At drunken revels in Pei, the Song of the Great Wind could not escape mingled joy and sorrow; amid intoxicated singing in the towers of Chen, Linchun ultimately sank into sensuous extravagance. Tears at Xuanwu accompanied the bestowal of a banquet, and the Dance of the Seven Virtues vaunted achievements; guests gathered at Zichen for a lavish feast, with ranks of immortals arrayed in attendance. Such musical performances [?] had no bearing on establishing exemplary standards; what did the brandishing of shields contribute to proper deportment? The martial song White Egret turned men's ambitions toward extravagant celebration of auspicious signs; repeated renditions of Yellow Bay Horse gave no thought to commemorating meritorious service. By the time of the non-Han Yuan dynasty, music's transforming influence had been wholly destroyed. The blowing of reed pipes filled the ears, and miscellaneous musical ensembles crowded the court. Far from refining outward conduct and harmonizing feelings, these merely increased sorrow and encouraged desire. A return to the great elegance of antiquity had to await an enlightened age.
We reverently consider that Your Majesty the Emperor embodies the Way and concentrates its purity, brings repose through your plans, and achieves harmonious joy. Through warfare against Shang [?], you succeeded to the sovereign charge, taking as your foundation the pristine customs of highest antiquity; using the ways of Xia to transform the barbarians, we look up to…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
大明之盛治民生初蕃膏澤涵濡品物咸亨欽
天廣復羽儀入表鼓動三才
六龍御而北極尊嚴
一統大而泰階平定虞絃解阜咸歌
若德之成武亂投戈共比
聖謨之顯歆居緝輯樂只清寧遹成物育時和
坐見風移俗易歷覽前朝之什殊多訣說
之詞渙啓
淵衷誕敷
===
睿旨命儒臣以稽古正
昭代之遺音爰慶敦龐軌儀赫奕溥臣
主同遊之善慶明良喜起之交百禮壬林饗餼
大烹於鼎實九儀辯等衣冠萃止於臨軒
珍薦嘉魚興鳴呦鹿晉接被晝三之日謙
光近尺五之天饗及一朝遙錫彤弓之貺
聞非三月頓忘肉味之廿訓恭儉以同心
極天神而觀德臣凱等遭逢盛典莫罄揄
揚醞藉
punctuated:
大明之盛治。民生初蕃，膏澤涵濡；品物咸亨，欽天廣復，羽儀入表，鼓動三才。六龍御而北極尊嚴，一統大而泰階平定。虞絃解阜，咸歌若德之成；武亂投戈，共比聖謨之顯。歆居緝輯，樂只清寧，遹成物育時和，坐見風移俗易。歷覽前朝之什，殊多訣說之詞。渙啓淵衷，誕敷睿旨，命儒臣以稽古，正昭代之遺音。爰慶敦龐，軌儀赫奕，溥臣主同遊之善，慶明良喜起之交。百禮壬林，饗餼大烹於鼎實；九儀辯等，衣冠萃止於臨軒。珍薦嘉魚，興鳴呦鹿。晉接被晝三之日，謙光近尺五之天。饗及一朝，遙錫彤弓之貺；聞非三月，頓忘肉味之廿。訓恭儉以同心，極天神而觀德。
臣凱等遭逢盛典，莫罄揄揚，醞藉
translation_en:
…the flourishing government of the Great Ming. The people begin to multiply, steeped in the richness of imperial beneficence; all things prosper. Reverence for Heaven spreads and returns [?]; feathered ceremonial emblems enter into display [?], stirring the Three Powers—Heaven, Earth, and humankind. As the six dragons bear the imperial chariot, the northern pole stands august; as the unified realm expands, the celestial Steps of Supreme Peace become tranquil and settled. The strings of Shun dispel distress and enrich the people: all sing of the fulfillment of your virtue. At the closing movement of the Martial Dance, weapons are laid aside: all alike attest to the manifest brilliance of your sagely counsels. Joyfully dwelling in concord [?], all rejoice in purity and peace. Thus living things flourish and the seasons are harmonious; without effort, you see customs transformed and popular ways improved.
Surveying the poems of former dynasties, one finds many expressions of farewell [?]. You have generously disclosed your profound thoughts and broadly proclaimed your sagely purpose, commanding scholarly officials to investigate antiquity and rectify the music inherited by this illustrious age. We therefore celebrate ample simplicity and splendid ceremonial forms, extending everywhere the goodness of ruler and subjects rejoicing together and celebrating the accord of an enlightened sovereign and worthy ministers, joyfully rousing one another to action. The hundred rites stand in profusion [?]; banquet offerings and provisions fill the cauldrons with sumptuous dishes. The nine ceremonial forms distinguish ranks, and officials in caps and robes gather before the imperial throne. Choice offerings evoke “Fine Fish,” and inspiration sounds in the deer’s gentle calls. Received in audience, we enjoy the favor of being admitted three times in a day; beneath your modest radiance, we draw within a mere foot and five inches of Heaven. A single morning’s feast brings the far-reaching gift of the vermilion bow; hearing the music, we immediately forget the sweetness [?] of meat, without waiting three months. You teach reverence and frugality, bringing hearts into unity; reaching even the heavenly spirits, you display your virtue [?].
Your servant Kai and the others have encountered this splendid ceremony, yet cannot exhaust its praises, cherishing within ourselves…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
徽猷徒深說繹顧職司器數而性之直溫勉
期操縵而安絃豈曰審音而知樂仰睹同
和之蹟用聲合愛之文章德象功受成
復定陳詞繹義僃竭愚誠遠孚洛鎬之情悉屏
沛汾之習濟同五味諧克八音依永和聲
竊附后夔之教舞簫替德願從季札之觀
同樂廣於閭閻協氣充於宇宙六變而致
象物豈徒降福於百神九成而來鳳儀巳
見允諧於庶尹臣凱等無任瞻
===
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹以所撰宴饗九奏樂章隨
表上
進以
聞
第叁場
策五道
第一問
張希皋
punctuated:
徽猷，徒深說繹。顧職司器數，而性之直溫，勉期操縵而安絃，豈曰審音而知樂？仰睹同和之蹟，用聲合愛之文，章德象功，受成復定。陳詞繹義，僃竭愚誠，遠孚洛鎬之情，悉屏沛汾之習。濟同五味，諧克八音。依永和聲，竊附后夔之教；舞簫替德，願從季札之觀。同樂廣於閭閻，協氣充於宇宙。六變而致象物，豈徒降福於百神？九成而來鳳儀，巳見允諧於庶尹。臣凱等無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹以所撰宴饗九奏樂章隨表上進以聞。
第叁場
策五道
第一問
張希皋
translation_en:
…your illustrious designs, which we can only discuss and expound with ever deeper appreciation. Our duties concern musical instruments and their prescribed arrangements, and our disposition is upright and gentle [?]. We strive merely to handle the strings and tune them properly; how could we claim to discern tones and understand music? Reverently we behold the achievements of shared harmony and the compositions that use sound to unite people in affection: they display virtue and represent accomplishments, receiving what has been achieved and establishing it anew [?]. In setting forth words and elucidating their meaning, we exhaust our humble sincerity, seeking to accord from afar with the spirit of Luo and Hao and entirely to banish the practices of Pei and Fen. Let the five flavors complement one another, and the eight classes of musical sound achieve harmony. In following the sustained singing and harmonizing the sounds, we venture to adhere to the teachings of Hou Kui; in the dances, flutes, and transmission of virtue [?], we wish to follow the example of Ji Zha’s viewing of the performances.
May shared enjoyment spread through the neighborhoods, and harmonious vitality fill the universe. When the music’s six transformations summon the beings represented by images, would this merely bring blessings from the hundred spirits? When its nine completions bring phoenixes to dance in stately array, we already see true concord among the many officials. Your servants Kai and the others, gazing toward Heaven and looking up to Your Sagely Majesty, are overcome with fervent emotion and trembling awe. We respectfully submit with this memorial the texts we have composed for the nine musical performances at ceremonial banquets, for Your Majesty’s hearing.
Third Session
Five Policy Questions
First Question
Zhang Xigao

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭鄧　批〔五策敷答無遺而據事考〕
〔衷皆犂然精當不但博洽而已錄此以例其餘〕
同考試官教諭唐　批〔善言豫教本之身忠哉〕
同考試官教諭徐　批〔忠愛之情溢於言表取之〕
〔不但以其文而已〕
考試官教諭葉　批〔老與法立論非他卷所及〕
考試官教授伍　批〔教太子法古今漸備而能〕
〔以身教者惟古帝王與我〕
祖宗而已是作能發揚之且用意忠愛措辭溫潤不獨策士也
===
對帝王所以教其子孫者有濂焉有本焉
何謂濂早諭教與選左右是也何謂本率
之以其所躬行是也濂雖教之所不可廢
然猶維其外也未若有本者之以身教也
是故濂之所在能使人從不能使樂於從
其本立則不令而行矣教以其濂能使人
善不能使必於善植其本則不言而化矣
嗚呼此古帝王之爲教所以非漢唐宋可
及而惟我
punctuated:
同考試官教諭鄧，批〔五策敷答無遺，而據事考〕〔衷，皆犂然精當，不但博洽而已。錄此以例其餘。〕
同考試官教諭唐，批〔善言豫教，本之身，忠哉！〕
同考試官教諭徐，批〔忠愛之情溢於言表，取之〕〔不但以其文而已。〕
考試官教諭葉，批〔老與法立論，非他卷所及。〕
考試官教授伍，批〔教太子法，古今漸備，而能〕〔以身教者，惟古帝王與我〕祖宗而已。是作能發揚之，且用意忠愛，措辭溫潤，不獨策士也。

對：帝王所以教其子孫者，有濂焉，有本焉。何謂濂？早諭教與選左右是也。何謂本？率之以其所躬行是也。濂雖教之所不可廢，然猶維其外也，未若有本者之以身教也。是故濂之所在，能使人從，不能使樂於從；其本立，則不令而行矣。教以其濂，能使人善，不能使必於善；植其本，則不言而化矣。嗚呼！此古帝王之爲教，所以非漢唐宋可及，而惟我
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Deng, Instructor, comments: “All five policy essays give full answers, leaving nothing out. Their examination of the facts and weighing of what is right are consistently clear, precise, and apt: they display more than extensive learning alone. This essay is recorded as representative of the others.”

Associate Examiner Tang, Instructor, comments: “He speaks well of education begun in advance, grounding it in personal example. How loyal!”

Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor, comments: “Loyalty and affection overflow his words. We select this essay for more than its literary qualities alone.”

Examiner Ye, Instructor, comments: “Its argument [the phrase 老與法 is unclear: ?] is beyond what the other papers achieve.”

Examiner Wu, Professor, comments: “Methods for educating the heir apparent have gradually become more comprehensive from antiquity to the present. Yet only the ancient emperors and kings and our imperial ancestors have been able to teach through personal example. This essay brings that out fully. Moreover, its intent is loyal and affectionate, and its language gentle and polished. Its author is more than merely a candidate writing policy essays.”

Answer: The means by which emperors and kings educate their descendants comprise safeguards [?] and a foundation. What are safeguards [?]? They are early instruction and the selection of those who attend them. What is the foundation? It is leading them through one’s own conduct. Although safeguards [?] cannot be dispensed with in education, they still provide only external restraint; they cannot compare with teaching through personal example, which supplies a foundation. Thus, safeguards [?] can make people obey, but cannot make them take pleasure in obedience. Once the foundation is established, however, people act without being commanded. Education through safeguards [?] can make people good, but cannot ensure their steadfastness in goodness. Once the foundation is planted, however, they are transformed without a word being spoken. Ah! This is why the education provided by the ancient emperors and kings was beyond the reach of the Han, Tang, and Song, and only our…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
太祖
太宗能繼其盛歟執事發策秋闈首以
皇上本支日蕃預求教
皇太子及
諸王之術以獻甚盛心也愚何能知之然而
太祖
太宗佑啓之功
皇上光裕之德則在臣子不可以無言也敢因
明問揄揚其萬一且古帝王教子孫之澧
何始乎自舜命夔教胄子而其澧以啓禹
有典則貽子孫而其澧漸詳周人貽孫謀
燕翼子而其澧□備其見於記則文王世
子之篇有曰學世子及學士必時春夏學
干戈秋冬學羽籥〔又曰〕〔三〕王教世子必以
===
禮樂有曰立太傅少傅以養之太傅審父
子君臣之道以示之少傅奉世子以觀太
傅之德行而審喻之太傅在前少傅在後
入則有保出則有師是以教喻而德成有
punctuated:
太祖、太宗能繼其盛歟？執事發策秋闈，首以皇上本支日蕃，預求教皇太子及諸王之術以獻，甚盛心也。愚何能知之？然而太祖、太宗佑啓之功，皇上光裕之德，則在臣子不可以無言也。敢因明問，揄揚其萬一。
且古帝王教子孫之澧，何始乎？自舜命夔教胄子，而其澧以啓；禹有典則貽子孫，而其澧漸詳；周人貽孫謀，燕翼子，而其澧□備。其見於記，則《文王世子》之篇有曰：「學世子及學士，必時。春夏學干戈，秋冬學羽籥。」〔又曰〕：「〔三〕王教世子，必以禮樂。」有曰：「立太傅、少傅以養之。太傅審父子君臣之道以示之，少傅奉世子以觀太傅之德行而審喻之。太傅在前，少傅在後；入則有保，出則有師。是以教喻而德成。」有
translation_en:
…could our Taizu and Taizong alone perpetuate that flourishing legacy? In issuing the policy questions for the autumn Provincial Examination, you gentlemen began with the daily increase of His Majesty’s principal and collateral descendants, seeking in advance methods for educating the Imperial Heir Apparent and the princes to present to the throne. Your concern is most admirable. How could someone as ignorant as I understand this? Yet, as a subject, I cannot remain silent about Taizu and Taizong’s achievements in protecting and establishing the dynasty, or His Majesty’s virtue in gloriously enriching their legacy. I venture, therefore, in response to your illuminating question, to extol some tiny part of these accomplishments.
Now, where did the rites [?] by which ancient emperors and kings educated their descendants begin? When Shun commanded Kui to educate the sons of the nobility, these rites [?] had their inception. Yu had statutes and rules to bequeath to his descendants, and these rites [?] gradually became more detailed. The rulers of Zhou devised plans for their grandsons, providing security and assistance for their sons, and these rites [?] became □ complete. As for their appearance in the Book of Rites, the chapter “King Wen as Heir Apparent” says: “Instruction of the heir apparent and the students must accord with the seasons. In spring and summer they learn the use of shields and spears; in autumn and winter they learn the feather and flute dances.” 〔It also says:〕 “The 〔Three〕 Kings invariably educated their heirs apparent through rites and music.” It says: “A Grand Preceptor and a Junior Preceptor were appointed to nurture him. The Grand Preceptor carefully examined the proper relations between father and son and between ruler and subject, and demonstrated them to him. The Junior Preceptor accompanied the heir apparent to observe the Grand Preceptor’s virtuous conduct and carefully explained it to him. The Grand Preceptor was before him and the Junior Preceptor behind him. Within, he had a guardian; outside, he had a teacher. Thus, through instruction and explanation, his virtue was perfected.” There is also…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
曰世子齒於學樂正司業父師司成今皆
可稽也其見於史則賈誼治安之策有曰
太子始生固舉以禮使士負之有司齋肅
端冕見之南郊有曰成王幼在襁褓之中
召公爲太保周公爲太傅太公爲太師有
曰選天下之端士孝悌博聞有道術者以
衛翼之有曰太子既冠成人免於保傅之
嚴則有記過之史徹膳之宰進善之旌誹
謗之木敢諫之鼓瞽史誦詩工誦箴諫大
===
夫進謀士傳民語今皆可稽也而執事有
疑於書及周禮之未載愚則以爲此無足
疑也蓋胄子之教既載於舜典而虞夏商
周師保疑丞四輔三公不必備惟其人則
其敎祄未嘗廢三公三孤既載於周官而
三公無官不隷六卿則其事固無由見於
周禮耳執事又謂帝王典則燕翼別有所
在而深慨夫漢唐宋治效之衰愚則以
此執事之卓識而實愚所謂□本□
punctuated: 曰：「世子齒於學，樂正司業，父師司成。」今皆可稽也。其見於史，則賈誼治安之策有曰：「太子始生，固舉以禮，使士負之，有司齋肅端冕，見之南郊。」有曰：「成王幼在襁褓之中，召公爲太保，周公爲太傅，太公爲太師。」有曰：「選天下之端士孝悌博聞有道術者，以衛翼之。」有曰：「太子既冠成人，免於保傅之嚴，則有記過之史、徹膳之宰、進善之旌、誹謗之木、敢諫之鼓；瞽史誦詩，工誦箴諫，大夫進謀，士傳民語。」今皆可稽也。而執事有疑於《書》及《周禮》之未載，愚則以爲此無足疑也。蓋胄子之教既載於《舜典》，而虞夏商周師保疑丞、四輔三公，不必備，惟其人，則其敎祄未嘗廢。三公三孤既載於《周官》，而三公無官，不隷六卿，則其事固無由見於《周禮》耳。執事又謂帝王典則燕翼別有所所在，而深慨夫漢唐宋治效之衰，愚則以此執事之卓識，而實愚所謂□本□
translation_en:
…it says: “At school, the heir apparent takes his place according to age. The Director of Music oversees instruction, and the fatherly master oversees its completion.” All these statements can now be verified. As for evidence in historical writings, Jia Yi’s policy essay on securing peace says: “When the crown prince is first born, he is duly lifted up according to ritual, and a gentleman is made to carry him. The responsible officials purify themselves and, solemnly wearing ceremonial robes and caps, present him in the southern suburbs.” It also says: “When King Cheng was an infant still in swaddling clothes, the Duke of Shao served as Grand Guardian, the Duke of Zhou as Grand Mentor, and the Grand Duke as Grand Preceptor.” It also says: “Upright gentlemen from throughout the realm, filial and respectful toward their elders, widely learned and versed in the Way and its arts, were selected to protect and assist him.” It also says: “Once the crown prince has undergone capping and reached adulthood, he is released from the strict supervision of his guardians and mentors. There are then scribes to record his faults, stewards to withdraw his meals, banners for presenting good counsel, wooden posts for criticism, and drums for bold remonstrance. Blind musicians and scribes recite poems, musicians recite admonitions and remonstrances, grandees offer counsel, and gentlemen convey the people’s words.” All these statements can now be verified.
Yet you entertain doubts because these matters are not recorded in the Book of Documents or the Rites of Zhou. In my humble opinion, there is nothing here to doubt. The education of the sons of the nobility is already recorded in the “Canon of Shun.” Under Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou, there were the master, guardian, counselor, and assistant—the Four Aides—and the Three Dukes. It was not necessary to fill every post; what mattered was finding the right men. Thus their educational work [?] was never abandoned. The Three Dukes and Three Vice Dukes are already recorded in the “Offices of Zhou” chapter of the Book of Documents. But the Three Dukes had no specific administrative offices and were not subordinate to the Six Ministers; hence there was naturally no occasion for their activities to appear in the Rites of Zhou.
You further argue that the true basis of the emperors’ and kings’ exemplary standards and their provision for their descendants lies elsewhere, and you deeply lament the decline in effective government under the Han, Tang, and Song. I humbly consider this an instance of your penetrating insight [?], and indeed what I have called ‘□ foundation □’ …

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
蓋帝王之爲典則于其身不于其言貽
謀燕翼于其道不于其總而漢唐宋諸君
乃闊畧於身心之間而徒致飾於言語事
爲之末故雖六傳之設賓客等官之設崇
文崇賢桂坊諸館局之設名位日繁帝範
之作戒子篇之作元良述承華要畧之作
後先相望而善在太子卒不免如楚士亹
所云耳洪惟我
太祖高皇帝道冠百王見高千古踐位之初旣
建大本堂取古今圖書充其中延四方名
===
儒教
皇太子及
諸王矣又著
祖訓錄
儲君昭鑑錄以賜而其爲書或紬繹六年始
克成編或采經傳格言以示訓戒天下之
至文也
太宗文皇帝入正大統益篤前烈嗣位之後既
punctuated:
蓋帝王之爲典則，于其身，不于其言；貽謀燕翼，于其道，不于其總。而漢唐宋諸君乃闊畧於身心之間，而徒致飾於言語事爲之末。故雖六傳之設，賓客等官之設，崇文、崇賢、桂坊諸館局之設，名位日繁；《帝範》之作，《戒子篇》之作，《元良述》《承華要畧》之作，後先相望，而善在太子，卒不免如楚士亹所云耳。
洪惟我太祖高皇帝，道冠百王，見高千古。踐位之初，旣建大本堂，取古今圖書充其中，延四方名儒教皇太子及諸王矣。又著《祖訓錄》《儲君昭鑑錄》以賜，而其爲書，或紬繹六年始克成編，或采經傳格言以示訓戒，天下之至文也。
太宗文皇帝入正大統，益篤前烈。嗣位之後，既
translation_en:
For emperors and kings establish exemplary standards through their own conduct, not their words; they bequeath plans for their descendants’ security through their Way, not through their outward arrangements [?]. Yet the rulers of the Han, Tang, and Song neglected the cultivation of their persons and minds, merely embellishing the superficial details of speech and action. Thus, although they established the six tutors [?], officials such as the Guests of the Heir Apparent, and institutions such as the Chongwen and Chongxian Academies and the Guifang Office, with titles and ranks growing ever more numerous; and although works such as the Model for Emperors, Admonitions to a Son, Account of the Heir Apparent, and Essentials for the Heir Apparent appeared in succession, goodness still depended upon the crown prince himself. Ultimately, matters could not escape being as Shi Wei of Chu had said.
We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao surpassed a hundred kings in the Way, and his insight excelled that of all antiquity. At the beginning of his reign, he established the Hall of the Great Foundation, filled it with books ancient and modern, and invited renowned Confucian scholars from all regions to instruct the imperial crown prince and the other princes. He also compiled the Record of Ancestral Instructions and the Record of Illuminating Examples for the Heir Apparent and bestowed them upon them. Of these works, one required six years of sustained examination before it could be completed; another selected maxims from the classics and their commentaries to provide instruction and admonition. These were writings of the highest order under Heaven.
Emperor Taizong Wen assumed the legitimate imperial succession and further strengthened the illustrious achievements of his predecessor. After succeeding to the throne, he had already …

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
命翰林諸臣舉老成正大儒者得禮部侍
郎儀智以傳
皇太孫矣又輯
文華寶鑑
聖學心法賜
皇太子而其爲書或克廣
昭鑒之義而重戒夫秦皇晉元之失或推極
帝王之學而深懲夫秦漢以下之非聖者
之謨訓也至若
===
太祖於
東宮不設府僚以廷臣兼領其職非有忽於
教諭德成之任也觀其示詹同等以良匠
拙工之喻示李善長等以恐生嫌疑之說
則其爲慮至深而不獨祖述於周召保傅
之制如執事所云矣
太祖屬輔臣敎
皇太子以兵事
太宗以
punctuated:
命翰林諸臣舉老成正大儒者，得禮部侍郎儀智以傳皇太孫矣。又輯《文華寶鑑》、《聖學心法》賜皇太子，而其爲書，或克廣《昭鑒》之義，而重戒夫秦皇、晉元之失；或推極帝王之學，而深懲夫秦漢以下之非，聖者之謨訓也。
至若太祖於東宮不設府僚，以廷臣兼領其職，非有忽於教諭德成之任也。觀其示詹同等以良匠拙工之喻，示李善長等以恐生嫌疑之說，則其爲慮至深，而不獨祖述於周召保傅之制，如執事所云矣。
太祖屬輔臣敎皇太子以兵事，太宗以
translation_en:
…commanded the Hanlin officials to recommend a mature, upright, and principled Confucian scholar, and obtained Yi Zhi, Vice Minister of Rites, to tutor the imperial grandson. He also compiled the Precious Mirror of Literary Brilliance (Wenhua baojian) and the Essential Methods of Sagely Learning (Shengxue xinfa), and bestowed them upon the crown prince. Of these works, one expanded the meaning of the Mirror of Illumination, emphatically warning against the failings of the First Emperor of Qin and Emperor Yuan of Jin; the other explored the learning of emperors and kings to its fullest extent, sternly condemning the errors committed from the Qin and Han onward. These were the counsels and instructions of a sage.
As for Taizu’s not establishing a separate staff for the Eastern Palace, instead assigning court officials to hold its posts concurrently, this did not mean that he neglected the responsibility of instruction and the cultivation of virtue. Consider how he presented Zhan Tong and others with the analogy of a skilled craftsman and a clumsy worker, and explained to Li Shanzhang and others his fear that suspicion might arise. His concerns were therefore profoundly considered; he was not merely following the precedent of the protector and preceptor system of the Dukes of Zhou and Shao, as you, sir, have stated.
Taizu charged his assisting ministers with teaching the crown prince military affairs; Taizong had…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
皇太孫從征北庭非有昧於長恩明仁之道
也觀其諭李善長等以居安慮危不忘武
備諭楊榮以俾知用兵之瀵及知將士勞
苦則其爲謀至遠而不獨有取於春夏干
戈之學如執事所云矣然此愚以爲特其
瀵也乃如其本則
太祖
太宗之德猶之天地日月雖非繪畫之工所能
形容摹擬而愚也莊誦
===
聖訓亦間獲窺其精藴之所存矣蓋
太祖嘗謂侍郎曾魯曰朕求古帝王之治莫盛
於堯舜觀其授受其要在允執厥中謂學士
宋濂曰人心虛靈乘氣機出入操而存之爲
難又曰朕之爲君上畏天地下畏兆民兢兢
業業不敢自逸又曰人君能淸心寡慾勤於
政事不作無益害有益使民安田里足衣食
熙熙皞皞而不自知此卽神僊也功業垂
簡册聲名流於後世此卽長生不死也
punctuated:
皇太孫從征北庭，非有昧於長恩明仁之道也。觀其諭李善長等以居安慮危、不忘武備，諭楊榮以俾知用兵之瀵及知將士勞苦，則其爲謀至遠，而不獨有取於春夏干戈之學，如執事所云矣。然此愚以爲特其瀵也，乃如其本，則太祖、太宗之德猶之天地日月，雖非繪畫之工所能形容摹擬，而愚也莊誦聖訓，亦間獲窺其精藴之所存矣。
蓋太祖嘗謂侍郎曾魯曰：「朕求古帝王之治，莫盛於堯舜。觀其授受，其要在允執厥中。」謂學士宋濂曰：「人心虛靈，乘氣機出入，操而存之爲難。」又曰：「朕之爲君，上畏天地，下畏兆民，兢兢業業，不敢自逸。」又曰：「人君能淸心寡慾，勤於政事，不作無益害有益，使民安田里，足衣食，熙熙皞皞而不自知，此卽神僊也。功業垂簡册，聲名流於後世，此卽長生不死也。」
translation_en:
…the imperial grandson accompany the expedition to the northern regions: this did not mean that he failed to understand the way of nurturing kindness and manifesting benevolence. Consider his admonition to Li Shanzhang and others to anticipate danger while dwelling in security and never neglect military preparedness, and his instruction to Yang Rong that the grandson should learn the intricacies [?] of employing troops and understand the hardships of officers and soldiers. His planning was thus exceedingly far-sighted; it did not merely draw upon the spring and summer instruction in shields and spears, as you have said. Yet I humbly consider these to be only its secondary aspects [?]. As for its foundation, the virtue of Taizu and Taizong resembled Heaven and Earth, the sun and moon. Although no painter’s skill could portray or reproduce it, through reverently reciting their sagely instructions I have occasionally gained a glimpse of their profound essence.
Taizu once said to Vice Minister Zeng Lu: “When I examine the government of ancient emperors and kings, none surpasses that of Yao and Shun. Looking at their transmission and reception of rule, its essential principle was sincerely to hold fast to the Mean.” He said to Academician Song Lian: “The human mind is empty and numinous; it comes and goes with the movements of vital energy. To grasp and preserve it is difficult.” He also said: “As ruler, above I stand in awe of Heaven and Earth; below I stand in awe of the countless people. Vigilant and conscientious, I dare not indulge in ease.” He further said: “If a ruler can purify his mind and lessen his desires, attend diligently to government, and refrain from undertaking useless things that harm what is useful, so that the people dwell securely among their fields and villages, with sufficient clothing and food, living in harmony and contentment without knowing how this has come about—this is what it means to be an immortal. To have one’s achievements recorded in the histories and one’s renown transmitted to later generations—this is longevity without death.”

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
□唐同曰聲色乃伐性之斧斤易以溺人一
有溺焉則禍敗隨之嗚呼茲數言也帝王正
心脩身之學漢唐宋所未有也
太宗嘗諭學士解縉等曰人君一有好樂泥而
不返則慾必勝理朕每退朝默坐未嘗不思
管束此心爲切要諭巡視監察御史曰朕居
深宮一飲一食未嘗不念及軍民斤獻道經
者曰朕所用治天下者五經耳道經何用諭
皇太子曰堯舜相傳惟曰允執厥中帝王之
===
道貴乎知要郤永春侯王寧飯僧奉佛之請
曰天子以四海爲家能思天位者親之所傳
大業者親之所建天下生民親之所保而敬
以奉天勤以守業仁以臨民使萬物得所四
夷咸賓光昭祖宗傳之子孫可以爲孝何必
事佛乃爲孝乎嗚呼茲數言也帝王正心脩
身之學漢唐宋所未有也
聖子神孫得諸觀感其與起善端成就令德信
當有潛移默化而不自知者百七十年
punctuated:
□唐同曰：「聲色乃伐性之斧斤，易以溺人，一有溺焉，則禍敗隨之。」嗚呼！茲數言也，帝王正心脩身之學，漢唐宋所未有也。

太宗嘗諭學士解縉等曰：「人君一有好樂，泥而不返，則慾必勝理。朕每退朝默坐，未嘗不思管束此心爲切要。」諭巡視監察御史曰：「朕居深宮，一飲一食，未嘗不念及軍民。」斤獻道經者曰：「朕所用治天下者，五經耳，道經何用？」諭皇太子曰：「堯舜相傳，惟曰允執厥中。帝王之道，貴乎知要。」郤永春侯王寧飯僧奉佛之請，曰：「天子以四海爲家，能思天位者親之所傳，大業者親之所建，天下生民親之所保，而敬以奉天，勤以守業，仁以臨民，使萬物得所，四夷咸賓，光昭祖宗，傳之子孫，可以爲孝。何必事佛乃爲孝乎？」嗚呼！茲數言也，帝王正心脩身之學，漢唐宋所未有也。

聖子神孫得諸觀感，其與起善端、成就令德，信當有潛移默化而不自知者。百七十年
translation_en:
…[He] said to Tang Tong [?]: “Sensual pleasures are axes that cut away at one’s moral nature and readily engulf a person. Once one becomes immersed in them, disaster and ruin follow.” Alas! These few sayings express a learning devoted to rectifying the ruler’s mind and cultivating his person such as the Han, Tang, and Song dynasties never possessed.

Taizong once instructed Academician Xie Jin and others: “Once a ruler develops a fondness for something and becomes so absorbed that he cannot turn back, desire will inevitably overcome principle. Whenever I withdraw from court and sit quietly, I invariably reflect that keeping this mind under control is of the utmost importance.” He instructed the touring Investigating Censors: “Though I dwell deep within the palace, whenever I drink or eat, I never fail to think of the soldiers and the common people.” He rebuked [?] someone who presented Daoist scriptures, saying: “What I use to govern the realm is simply the Five Classics. What use have I for Daoist scriptures?” He instructed the heir apparent: “What Yao and Shun transmitted to one another was simply this: ‘Sincerely hold fast to the Mean.’ In the Way of emperors and kings, what matters is knowing the essentials.” He rejected the request of Wang Ning, Marquis of Yongchun, to feed Buddhist monks and worship the Buddha, saying: “The Son of Heaven takes all within the four seas as his home. If he can reflect that his heavenly throne was handed down by his parents, that his great undertaking was established by his parents, and that the people of the realm were protected by his parents; if he reverently serves Heaven, diligently preserves that undertaking, and benevolently governs the people, enabling all beings to find their proper place and the barbarians of the four quarters all to submit; and if he brings glory to his ancestors and transmits his inheritance to his descendants—this may be called filial piety. Why must one serve the Buddha to be filial?” Alas! These few sayings express a learning devoted to rectifying the ruler’s mind and cultivating his person such as the Han, Tang, and Song dynasties never possessed.

Their sagely sons and divinely gifted grandsons learned through observing and being moved by these examples. In awakening the beginnings of goodness [?] and bringing excellent virtue to fruition, they surely underwent a gradual, silent transformation without themselves being aware of it. For one hundred and seventy years…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
聖聖相承天下乂安和氣឵洋溢豈偶然之故哉
乃今
皇上
仁孝聰明得之天縱凡古今所謂曠典旣次
第舉之而恭默思道至誠無息緝熙敬止
聖學日新是卽
太祖
太宗之爲德也
天章縟藻出自性成凡古今所謂大製作旣兼
===
有之而
敬一一箴獨遡心學之源星變一
勑曲盡時幾之義是卽
太祖
太宗之爲文也然則今日敎
皇太子及
諸王之術亦奚必求之遠哉
皇上建極綏猷本已立矣乃其灋則
太祖
punctuated: 聖聖相承，天下乂安，和氣឵洋溢，豈偶然之故哉？乃今皇上，仁孝聰明，得之天縱。凡古今所謂曠典，旣次第舉之，而恭默思道，至誠無息，緝熙敬止，聖學日新，是卽太祖、太宗之爲德也。天章縟藻，出自性成。凡古今所謂大製作，旣兼有之，而《敬一》一箴，獨遡心學之源；星變一勑，曲盡時幾之義，是卽太祖、太宗之爲文也。然則今日敎皇太子及諸王之術，亦奚必求之遠哉？皇上建極綏猷，本已立矣。乃其灋則太祖
translation_en:
…sage sovereign has succeeded sage sovereign; all under Heaven is well governed and at peace, and harmonious influences abound. Could this have happened by chance? Now His Majesty possesses benevolence, filial devotion, intelligence, and discernment as gifts of Heaven. He has successively performed all those exceptional ceremonies spoken of in ancient and modern times. Reverent and silent, he contemplates the Way; his utmost sincerity never ceases. Continuing in luminous virtue and abiding in reverence, he daily renews his sagely learning. These are precisely the virtues practiced by Taizu and Taizong.

The rich ornament of his imperial writings springs from his innate nature. He has mastered all the great forms of composition spoken of in ancient and modern times. His single Admonition on Reverent Unity (Jingyi) uniquely traces learning of the mind to its source; his edict concerning celestial anomalies fully explores the significance of the incipient tendencies of the times. This is precisely how Taizu and Taizong practiced literary composition.

Why, then, need one seek far afield today for methods of educating the Imperial Heir Apparent and the princes? His Majesty has established the supreme standard and secured the proper course of government: the foundation is already laid. As for his taking Taizu as his model…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
宗成憲具存奉而循之雖萬世可也愚也遭
逢
聖明涵濡大化覩
元良之有賴而益以篤
宗社靈長之休計屏翰之有眷而益以知磐石
奠安之慶蓋有不勝其欣忭者執事倘與
其進尚當爲
聖天子頌之謹對
第二問
熊□臣
===
同考試官教諭李 批 朱子論仁深得孔門遺□
而好異者或持其說以亂之是作考據折衷確有定見□
可與言仁矣
同考試官教諭王 批 說學者求仁處詞旨婉而意
足必有得於仁者
同考試官教諭孫 批 考據詳而議論正可式
考試官教諭葉 批 論仁折衷於朱子深意有見
考試官教授伍 批 得朱子學旨
punctuated:
宗成憲具存，奉而循之，雖萬世可也。愚也遭逢聖明，涵濡大化，覩元良之有賴，而益以篤宗社靈長之休；計屏翰之有眷，而益以知磐石奠安之慶。蓋有不勝其欣忭者。執事倘與其進，尚當爲聖天子頌之。謹對。

第二問
熊□臣

同考試官教諭李批：朱子論仁，深得孔門遺□，而好異者或持其說以亂之。是作考據折衷，確有定見，□可與言仁矣。

同考試官教諭王批：說學者求仁處，詞旨婉而意足，必有得於仁者。

同考試官教諭孫批：考據詳而議論正，可式。

考試官教諭葉批：論仁折衷於朱子，深意有見。

考試官教授伍批：得朱子學旨。
translation_en:
…the established statutes of the imperial ancestors remain fully preserved. By reverently following them, one could govern even for ten thousand generations. In my humble station, I have encountered an enlightened sovereign and been steeped in his great transforming influence. Seeing that the Crown Prince has support, I am all the more confident in the blessing of enduring prosperity for the ancestral temples and altars of state. Reflecting that the princes who serve as the dynasty’s bulwarks receive imperial care, I recognize all the more the joy of security founded firm as rock. Indeed, my delight is beyond restraint. If you, honored examiners, should approve my advancement, I shall further celebrate these blessings in praise of the sage Son of Heaven. Respectfully submitted in reply.

Second Question
Xiong □chen

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: Master Zhu’s discussion of benevolence profoundly grasped the legacy [?] of Confucius’s school. Yet those who delight in novelty sometimes advance their own doctrines to throw it into confusion. This essay examines the evidence and weighs the interpretations, arriving at a firm judgment. [Illegible] one may discuss benevolence with its author.

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: In explaining how students should seek benevolence, the wording and purport are graceful, and the meaning is fully expressed. The author must have attained some understanding of benevolence.

Comment by Associate Examiner Sun, Instructor: The examination of evidence is detailed, and the argument is sound. It can serve as a model.

Comment by Examiner Ye, Instructor: In discussing benevolence, the author takes Master Zhu as the standard for weighing interpretations. The meaning is profound and shows insight.

Comment by Examiner Wu, Professor: The author has grasped the essential meaning of Master Zhu’s learning.

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
學有正傳而失焉者說之者之好爲異也
道有定論而晦焉者學之者之不知求也
道莫大於仁君子之學莫先於求仁然是
學也在聖人有正傳矣苟說之者無乘之
以好異之心則於學當有獲得而益見其
傳之不容廢是仁也在大儒有定論矣苟
學之者能持之以必求之志則於道當有
所契而益見其論之不可易夫惟不然也
是故傳而或失焉論而或晦焉其始也非
===
