有意於病道與學而卒不免爲之病嗚呼
是豈非君子之大戒哉執事於此思救正
之以詢承學愚也於求仁之學嘗得之孔
子論仁之言嘗得之朱子矣請執以復焉
何如蓋昔堯舜之爲治莫非仁也然其見
諸授受者不過曰人心惟危道心惟微惟
精惟一允執厥中而已於仁未始及也是
豈有所遺而然哉道心即仁人心即慾惟
從事精一之間則仁在是矣孔門之爲教
punctuated:
學有正傳，而失焉者，說之者之好爲異也；道有定論，而晦焉者，學之者之不知求也。道莫大於仁，君子之學莫先於求仁。然是學也，在聖人有正傳矣。苟說之者無乘之以好異之心，則於學當有獲得，而益見其傳之不容廢。是仁也，在大儒有定論矣。苟學之者能持之以必求之志，則於道當有所契，而益見其論之不可易。夫惟不然也，是故傳而或失焉，論而或晦焉。其始也，非有意於病道與學，而卒不免爲之病。嗚呼！是豈非君子之大戒哉？執事於此思救正之，以詢承學。愚也，於求仁之學，嘗得之孔子；論仁之言，嘗得之朱子矣。請執以復焉，何如？

蓋昔堯舜之爲治，莫非仁也。然其見諸授受者，不過曰：「人心惟危，道心惟微，惟精惟一，允執厥中。」而已，於仁未始及也。是豈有所遺而然哉？道心即仁，人心即慾。惟從事精一之間，則仁在是矣。孔門之爲教
translation_en:
Learning has an orthodox transmission; when this is lost, it is because its interpreters delight in advancing novel views. The Way has an established exposition; when this is obscured, it is because those who study it do not know how to seek it. Nothing in the Way is greater than benevolence, and nothing takes precedence over seeking benevolence in the gentleman’s learning. This learning has an orthodox transmission from the sages. If its interpreters do not allow a taste for novelty to intrude upon it, they should gain something through their learning and see still more clearly that this transmission must not be abandoned. Benevolence has an established exposition in the writings of the great Confucian masters. If those who study it can persevere with a resolve to seek it out, they should attain some accord with the Way and see still more clearly that this exposition cannot be altered. Yet precisely because they fail to do so, what is transmitted is sometimes lost, and what is expounded is sometimes obscured. At the outset they have no intention of harming the Way and learning, but in the end they cannot avoid doing them harm. Alas! Is this not a grave warning for the gentleman? You, honored examiners, seek to remedy and correct this, and therefore question us who have received this learning. In my humble study of the pursuit of benevolence, I have learned from Kongzi; for statements expounding benevolence, I have learned from Zhuzi. May I draw upon these to offer my reply?

In ancient times, the government of Yao and Shun was benevolent in every respect. Yet what appeared in the teaching handed down from one to the other amounted only to this: “The human mind is precarious; the mind of the Way is subtle. Be discerning, be single-minded; sincerely hold fast to the mean.” Benevolence was never mentioned. Could this have been because something was omitted? The mind of the Way is itself benevolence; the human mind is itself desire. Only apply yourself to discernment and single-mindedness, and benevolence is to be found therein. As for the teaching of the school of Kongzi…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
莫非仁也然其見諸問荅者不過曰克己
復禮主敬行恕先難後獲言之能訒而已
於仁殆罕言也夫豈有所隱而然哉仁固
難言在於心會惟從事數者之中則仁可
求矣至若子思得傳於夫子而著於中庸
者曰脩身以道脩道以仁夫身以道脩道
以仁脩則仁與道固非兩物而脩道之責
實存乎人也孟子得傳於子思而著於七
篇者曰仁者人也合而言之道也夫人而
具此仁則爲人人而體此仁則爲道是道
與仁誠非二致而體仁之功乃繫於人也
是不可見聖人立教之意而學之正傳在
是乎夫何說之者之好爲異以爲聖人之
言未盡也而思以足之於是競求所以釋
夫仁者蓋自漢世以兼愛爲仁至唐韓愈
主之之過遂以博愛名之今原道所言是
也又至謝良佐矯之之過遂以知覺名之
今桃仁杏仁之喻是也殊不知仁體也愛
punctuated: 莫非仁也，然其見諸問荅者，不過曰克己復禮、主敬行恕、先難後獲、言之能訒而已，於仁殆罕言也。夫豈有所隱而然哉？仁固難言，在於心會，惟從事數者之中，則仁可求矣。至若子思得傳於夫子，而著於中庸者曰：「脩身以道，脩道以仁。」夫身以道脩，道以仁脩，則仁與道固非兩物，而脩道之責實存乎人也。孟子得傳於子思，而著於七篇者曰：「仁者，人也，合而言之，道也。」夫人而具此仁則爲人，人而體此仁則爲道，是道與仁誠非二致，而體仁之功乃繫於人也。是不可見聖人立教之意，而學之正傳在是乎？夫何說之者之好爲異，以爲聖人之言未盡也，而思以足之？於是競求所以釋夫仁者，蓋自漢世以兼愛爲仁，至唐韓愈主之之過，遂以博愛名之，今《原道》所言是也。又至謝良佐矯之之過，遂以知覺名之，今桃仁杏仁之喻是也。殊不知仁，體也；愛，
translation_en:
…was concerned entirely with benevolence. Yet what appeared in his questions and answers amounted only to overcoming the self and returning to ritual propriety, holding fast to reverence and practicing reciprocity, putting difficult tasks before rewards, and being restrained in speech. He seldom spoke directly of benevolence. Could this have been because he was concealing something? Benevolence is indeed difficult to express in words; it must be apprehended in the heart. Only by working at these several practices can benevolence be sought.

Zisi received the transmission from the Master and set it down in the Doctrine of the Mean: “Cultivate the person through the Way; cultivate the Way through benevolence.” Since the person is cultivated through the Way, and the Way through benevolence, benevolence and the Way are certainly not two separate things; yet responsibility for cultivating the Way rests with the person. Mengzi received the transmission from Zisi and set it down in his Seven Books: “Benevolence is being human. Taken together, this is the Way.” A person is human by possessing this benevolence, and embodies the Way by giving bodily realization to this benevolence. Thus the Way and benevolence are indeed of one purport, while the work of embodying benevolence depends upon the person. Can we not see here the sages’ intention in establishing their teachings, and that the orthodox transmission of learning lies in this?

Why, then, do interpreters delight in devising divergent explanations, believing that the sages’ words were incomplete and seeking to supplement them? They consequently compete to find ways of explaining benevolence. Beginning in the Han, indiscriminate love was taken to be benevolence. In the Tang, Han Yu went too far in endorsing this view and accordingly designated benevolence as universal love; this is what his Inquiry into the Way (Yuan dao), available today, says. Later, Xie Liangzuo went too far in correcting this and accordingly designated benevolence as awareness; the analogy of peach and apricot kernels is an instance of this. They entirely fail to understand that benevolence is the substance, while love …

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
用也仁者物無不愛雖可以徵其爲用之
廣而直謂之仁則是不究夫體用之辯惻
隱之心仁也是非之心智也仁者心有知
覺雖可以見其包智之用而直謂之仁則
是不審夫仁智之殊獨尹焞所謂公者庶
幾近之然公所以體仁不可以言仁善乎
程子之言曰仁者必愛指愛爲仁則不可
不仁者無所知覺指知覺爲仁則不可又
曰公只是仁之理不可將公便喚做仁蓋
===
有以斷乎此矣愚故曰學有不傳而失焉
者說之者之好爲異也朱子集諸儒之大
成闡四德之名義其於仁曰心之德愛之
理蓋孔子所未發也然仁者天地生物之
心而人得之以爲心方其未發四德具焉
曰仁義禮智而仁無不統及其已發四端
著焉曰惻隱羞惡辭遜是非而惻隱之心
無不通則其指以爲心之德而義禮智不
得竝焉宜矣仁以言乎其理渾然在中而
punctuated: 用也。仁者物無不愛，雖可以徵其爲用之廣，而直謂之仁，則是不究夫體用之辯。惻隱之心，仁也；是非之心，智也。仁者心有知覺，雖可以見其包智之用，而直謂之仁，則是不審夫仁智之殊。獨尹焞所謂公者，庶幾近之。然公所以體仁，不可以言仁。善乎程子之言曰：「仁者必愛，指愛爲仁則不可；不仁者無所知覺，指知覺爲仁則不可。」又曰：「公只是仁之理，不可將公便喚做仁。」蓋有以斷乎此矣。愚故曰：「學有不傳而失焉者，說之者之好爲異也。」朱子集諸儒之大成，闡四德之名義，其於仁曰：「心之德，愛之理。」蓋孔子所未發也。然仁者，天地生物之心，而人得之以爲心。方其未發，四德具焉，曰仁義禮智，而仁無不統；及其已發，四端著焉，曰惻隱、羞惡、辭遜、是非，而惻隱之心無不通。則其指以爲心之德，而義禮智不得竝焉，宜矣。仁以言乎其理，渾然在中而
translation_en: …is its function. A benevolent person loves all things without exception. Although this attests to the breadth of benevolence’s functioning, to identify love outright with benevolence is to leave the distinction between substance and function unexamined. The heart of compassion is benevolence; the heart that distinguishes right from wrong is wisdom. Although the benevolent heart’s awareness shows that its functioning encompasses wisdom, to identify awareness outright with benevolence is to fail to discern the difference between benevolence and wisdom. Only what Yin Tun called impartiality comes close. Yet impartiality is the means of embodying benevolence; it cannot itself be called benevolence. How well Master Cheng put it: “The benevolent necessarily love, but one cannot identify love with benevolence. Those who lack benevolence have no awareness, but one cannot identify awareness with benevolence.” He also said: “Impartiality is simply the principle of benevolence; one cannot simply call impartiality benevolence.” These statements surely provide a basis for settling the matter. Thus I humbly say: “Where learning fails to be transmitted and is lost, it is because its interpreters delight in advancing divergent views.” Master Zhu brought the learning of the various Confucian scholars to its fullest expression and elucidated the names and meanings of the four virtues. Of benevolence he said: “The virtue of the heart and the principle of love.” This was something Confucius had not explicitly articulated. Yet benevolence is the heart through which Heaven and Earth give life to things, and human beings receive it as their own heart. Before it is aroused, the four virtues are fully present—benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom—and benevolence encompasses them all. Once it is aroused, the four beginnings become manifest—compassion, shame and aversion, deference and yielding, and discernment of right and wrong—and the heart of compassion pervades them all. It is therefore fitting that he designated benevolence as the virtue of the heart, with which righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom cannot rank equally. Speaking of benevolence in terms of its principle, it resides within as an undivided whole, and…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
所謂愛者出焉而不窮愛以言乎其事充
然各足而所謂仁者資之而無盡則其指
以爲愛之理對夫義之宜禮之敬智之知
而言之宜矣是不可見朱子精義之極而
道之定論在是乎夫何學之者之不知求
以爲朱子之言未然也而思以易之於是
復取昔人之論仁者或進而托於程子一
體之說以爲仁之惻怛慈愛必如是乃可
以名也或近而守夫謝氏知覺之說以爲
===
仁之周流貫徹必如是乃可以名也殊不
知愛之在人其理雖一而其分則殊專主
夫愛則於所謂分之殊者有未明而將淪
於兼愛之失心之在人其覺雖同而理慾
則異專主夫覺則於所謂理與慾者有不
察而將昧夫精一之宗善乎朱子之言曰
泛言同體者使人含胡昏緩而無警切之
功其弊或至認物爲己者有之專言知覺
者使人張皇躁迫而無沉潛之味其弊或
punctuated: 所謂愛者出焉而不窮。愛以言乎其事，充然各足，而所謂仁者資之而無盡，則其指以爲愛之理，對夫義之宜、禮之敬、智之知而言之，宜矣。是不可見朱子精義之極，而道之定論在是乎？夫何學之者之不知求，以爲朱子之言未然也，而思以易之？於是復取昔人之論仁者，或進而托於程子一體之說，以爲仁之惻怛慈愛，必如是乃可以名也；或近而守夫謝氏知覺之說，以爲仁之周流貫徹，必如是乃可以名也。殊不知愛之在人，其理雖一，而其分則殊；專主夫愛，則於所謂分之殊者有未明，而將淪於兼愛之失。心之在人，其覺雖同，而理慾則異；專主夫覺，則於所謂理與慾者有不察，而將昧夫精一之宗。善乎朱子之言曰：「泛言同體者，使人含胡昏緩，而無警切之功，其弊或至認物爲己者有之；專言知覺者，使人張皇躁迫，而無沉潛之味，其弊或
translation_en:
…what is called love issues from it without exhaustion. Speaking of love in its actual workings, it is abundantly sufficient in each instance, while what is called humaneness supplies it without end. Thus it is fitting to identify humaneness as the principle of love, speaking of it alongside the appropriateness of righteousness, the reverence of ritual propriety, and the knowing of wisdom. Can we not see from this the utmost refinement of Master Zhu’s understanding of moral principles, and that here lies the definitive account of the Way? Why, then, do learners fail to investigate it, consider Master Zhu’s words unsound, and seek to replace them? They consequently return to earlier discussions of humaneness. Some reach further and invoke Master Cheng’s doctrine of forming one body, maintaining that the compassion and loving care of humaneness can be named only in these terms. Others stay closer and adhere to Master Xie’s doctrine of awareness, maintaining that the universal circulation and penetration of humaneness can be named only in these terms.

They fail entirely to understand that, although the principle of love in human beings is one, its proper allotments differ. If one takes love alone as the governing consideration, one fails to understand these differences and will fall into the error of indiscriminate love. Although the mind’s awareness is common to human beings, moral principle and desire are distinct. If one takes awareness alone as the governing consideration, one fails to discern moral principle and desire and will obscure the essential teaching of refinement and single-mindedness.

How well Master Zhu put it: “Those who speak vaguely of forming one body make people muddled, benighted, and lax, without the effort of vigilant attention. In some cases, this error even leads them to identify things as the self. Those who speak exclusively of awareness make people agitated, restless, and impatient, without any savor of deep contemplation. This error may…”

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
至認欲爲理者有之矣已預憂乎此矣愚
故曰道有定論而悔焉者學之者之不知
求也然則執事爲今之計將若之何請戒
於衆曰爾欲求仁有孔子之正傳在焉愼
毋侮聖人守之可也爾欲言仁有朱子之
定論存焉愼毋小朱子信之可也如是而
日申飭之士固當畋其趨矣由是而又申
飭之則士貞積之久將自有以識夫仁體
而所謂定論者不至於侮體驗之深將自
===
不能已於求仁而所謂正傳者不至於亡
交養而互發執事之愿庶幾其免夫狂瞽
之言未知是否惟進教之幸甚
第三問
同考試官教諭胡　批　數篇辭明吾子之學之識
可概見矣
同考試官教諭葉　批　葉能□
景行先哲而愼厥瀋所著□錄之
〔□士之良論□□□策務求〕
punctuated:
至認欲爲理者有之矣。」已預憂乎此矣。愚故曰：「道有定論，而悔焉者，學之者之不知求也。」然則執事爲今之計，將若之何？請戒於衆曰：「爾欲求仁，有孔子之正傳在焉，愼毋侮聖人，守之可也；爾欲言仁，有朱子之定論存焉，愼毋小朱子，信之可也。」如是而日申飭之，士固當畋其趨矣。由是而又申飭之，則士貞積之久，將自有以識夫仁體，而所謂定論者不至於侮；體驗之深，將自不能已於求仁，而所謂正傳者不至於亡。交養而互發，執事之愿，庶幾其免夫！狂瞽之言，未知是否，惟進教之，幸甚。

第三問

同考試官教諭胡，批：「數篇辭明，吾子之學之識，可概見矣。」

同考試官教諭葉，批：「葉能□，景行先哲，而愼厥瀋，所著□錄之。」〔□士之良論□□□策務求〕
translation_en:
…some even go so far as to mistake desire for principle.” He had already foreseen this danger. Thus I humbly say: “There is a settled understanding of the Way; those who have misgivings about it do so because, as students, they do not know how to seek it.” What, then, should you do in present circumstances? I ask that you admonish everyone: “If you wish to seek benevolence, Confucius’s authentic transmission is there. Take care not to slight the sage; hold fast to it. If you wish to discuss benevolence, Master Zhu’s settled conclusions remain. Take care not to belittle Master Zhu; trust in them.” If you reiterate this admonition daily, scholars should surely direct their efforts accordingly [?]. If you continue to reinforce it, then, through long accumulation of steadfast practice, scholars will themselves come to recognize the substance of benevolence, and those settled conclusions will not be slighted. Through profound personal experience, they will become unable to cease seeking benevolence, and the authentic transmission will not be lost. The two nourish and illuminate each other; perhaps what you wish to avert may thus be avoided [?]. These are rash and ignorant words; I do not know whether they are correct. I would be most grateful for your further instruction.

Third Question

Associate Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: “The wording of these several essays is clear; from them one can gain a general view of your learning and discernment.”

Associate Examiner Ye, Instructor, comments: “Ye is able to □ [?], to look up to the worthy thinkers of the past and to be cautious concerning his ‘ink’ [?]; what is written □, record it [?].” 〔□ sound arguments of scholars □□□; policy essays must seek … [?]〕

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭葉　批　於經之學精確〔不〕見無踰
于者宜置前列
論封建於三代之下師其意而已矣求人
才於封建之外取其志而已矣封建其起
於理乎緣於情乎成於勢乎理與賢者共
而不及惡德情先乎九族而後萬邦勢則
宜於古而尼於今吾見封建之難復也雖
然後世之封建已與古意異矣後世之封
===
考試官教授伍　批　考事尚賢可以風矣
建之科目又與封建之意異矣封建之科
目之不究其用又與科目之意異矣勢不
同而理同理同而已遑恤乎其他是
故不車服而榮不爵賞而勸隨其所遭而
吾無與焉豈不誠志士哉南宋之諸趙是
已於戲彼皆江右之產而科目之良也孰
事舉以為問豈欲求才於封建之外而論
治於三代之上乎愚竊以為非封建意也
是故知勢者則不必襲古以為瀆知情者
punctuated:
考試官教諭葉批：於經之學精確〔不〕見無踰于者，宜置前列。

論封建於三代之下，師其意而已矣；求人才於封建之外，取其志而已矣。封建，其起於理乎？緣於情乎？成於勢乎？理，與賢者共而不及惡德；情，先乎九族而後萬邦；勢，則宜於古而尼於今。吾見封建之難復也。雖然，後世之封建已與古意異矣，後世之封

考試官教授伍批：考事尚賢，可以風矣。

建之科目，又與封建之意異矣；封建之科目之不究其用，又與科目之意異矣。勢不同而理同，理同而已，遑恤乎其他？是故不車服而榮，不爵賞而勸，隨其所遭而吾無與焉，豈不誠志士哉？南宋之諸趙是已。於戲！彼皆江右之產，而科目之良也。孰事舉以為問，豈欲求才於封建之外，而論治於三代之上乎？愚竊以為非封建意也。是故知勢者，則不必襲古以為瀆；知情者，
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Ye, Instructor: His learning in the Classics is precise; none appears to surpass him [?; the small annotation reads “not”]. He should be placed among the foremost.

To discuss enfeoffment after the Three Dynasties is simply to emulate its intent; to seek talented men outside enfeoffment is simply to value their aspirations. Did enfeoffment arise from principle, derive from human affections, or take shape through circumstances? As a matter of principle, rule is shared with the worthy, excluding those of wicked character. As a matter of affection, the nine degrees of kinship come before the myriad states. As a matter of circumstances, it was suitable in antiquity but encounters obstacles today. I see how difficult it would be to restore enfeoffment. Nevertheless, the enfeoffment of later ages already differed from the ancient intent.

Comment by Examiner Wu, Professor: He examines affairs and esteems the worthy; this may serve as an example.

The examination system associated with enfeoffment in later ages [?] differed in turn from the intent of enfeoffment; and its failure to realize its usefulness differed yet again from the intent of the examination system. Circumstances differ, but principle remains the same. It is enough that principle is the same: why trouble oneself about anything else? Thus, to feel honored without carriages and robes of rank, and encouraged without titles and rewards, accepting whatever one encounters without personally seeking a part in it—is this not truly to be a man of high purpose? Such were the various Zhao of the Southern Song. Ah! They were all natives of Jiangyou and outstanding men of the examination system. You have raised their deeds as a question [?]: do you wish to seek talent outside enfeoffment and discuss government surpassing that of the Three Dynasties? In my humble view, this is not the intent of enfeoffment. Thus, those who understand circumstances need not imitate antiquity and thereby bring about disorder [?]; those who understand human affections …

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
則不必易令以爲治知理者則不必違天
以病民合是三者神而明之無封建無郡
縣而同歸於治無世官無科目而同歸於
才亦何庸心其間必爲此而不爲彼哉且
秦取天下而郡縣之而守令不以賢聞漢
更郡國而分置之而諸侯王數至僭叛人
才之不係於封建與否也明矣唐猶漢也
而隴西未嘗無賢士宋猶唐也而南渡未
嘗無善人人才之不係於世官與否也亦
===
明矣姑以江右論之昌邑肇封於漢世遠
而莫究元嬰胙土于唐枝散而日微可考
者其惟南宋之宗室乎時則有若善應之
刺血和藥崇憲之表明父心事雖不同而
同爲孝良淳之死守孫城時倚之以身殉
主地雖不同而同爲忠人稱趙母則有彥
端力變士風則有與清其政事何如也師
晦菴而究心理學則有汝靚請漕舉而苦
志詩賦則有希晉其文學何如也至若必
punctuated:
則不必易令以爲治；知理者，則不必違天以病民。合是三者，神而明之，無封建，無郡縣，而同歸於治；無世官，無科目，而同歸於才。亦何庸心其間，必爲此而不爲彼哉？且秦取天下而郡縣之，而守令不以賢聞；漢更郡國而分置之，而諸侯王數至僭叛。人才之不係於封建與否也，明矣。唐猶漢也，而隴西未嘗無賢士；宋猶唐也，而南渡未嘗無善人。人才之不係於世官與否也，亦明矣。

姑以江右論之：昌邑肇封於漢，世遠而莫究；元嬰胙土于唐，枝散而日微。可考者，其惟南宋之宗室乎？時則有若善應之刺血和藥、崇憲之表明父心，事雖不同，而同爲孝；良淳之死守孫城、時倚之以身殉主，地雖不同，而同爲忠。人稱趙母，則有彥端；力變士風，則有與清。其政事何如也？師晦菴而究心理學，則有汝靚；請漕舉而苦志詩賦，則有希晉。其文學何如也？至若必
translation_en:
…then there is no need to change ordinances to achieve good government; those who understand principle need not contravene Heaven and thereby afflict the people. Combine these three kinds of understanding and apply them with inspired discernment: whether through enfeoffment or through commanderies and counties, both may lead to good government; whether through hereditary office or through the examinations, both may lead to the discovery of talent. Why, then, trouble oneself over the choice, insisting on adopting one and rejecting the other? Qin conquered the realm and organized it into commanderies and counties, yet its governors and magistrates were not renowned for worthiness. Han reorganized the commanderies and kingdoms, establishing them separately, yet its feudatory kings repeatedly resorted to usurpation and rebellion. Clearly, the presence of talented men does not depend on whether enfeoffment is practiced. Tang was like Han, yet Longxi never lacked worthy men; Song was like Tang, yet after the court’s southward migration there was never a lack of good men. It is likewise clear that talent does not depend on whether offices are hereditary.

Let us consider Jiangyou alone. The Prince of Changyi first received his fief under Han, but that age is too remote for thorough investigation. Yuanying received a territorial grant under Tang, but his lineage’s branches dispersed and grew steadily less prominent. Are those whose deeds can be investigated perhaps chiefly the members of the Southern Song imperial clan? Among them were Shanying, who drew his own blood to mix with medicine, and Chongxian, who made his father’s true intentions known in a memorial. Their deeds differed, but both exemplified filial devotion. Liangchun defended Suncheng [?] to the death, while Shiyi sacrificed his life for his sovereign. Their locations differed, but both exemplified loyalty. There was Yanduan, whom people called “Mother Zhao,” and Yuqing, who worked vigorously to transform the conduct of scholars. What does this tell us of their achievements in government? There was Rujing, who studied under Hui’an and devoted himself to investigating the learning of principle, and Xijin, who sought examination through the Transport Commission and applied himself diligently to poetry and rhapsodies. What does this tell us of their literary learning? As for Bi…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
願早聞忠義之訓善堅勵志之節可
以語行誼矣不黜退居錦水而以樂善名
汝偵廾守布衣而以固窮著可以語清脩
矣之數人者或起於科目或老于山林而
其立身行事之節有如此而吾所尊仰之
者則惟丞相汝愚而已好善忘勢有仕優
則學之風正色立朝有國爾忘家之節其
期待也則以司馬光富弼韓琦范仲淹爲
己任其淵源也則以朱熹張栻呂祖謙王
===
十朋汪應辰爲師友忠結人主而有文武
威風之稱行孚于朝而有忠孝大節之薦
是蓋不徒誓志於功名而實任道之器也
豈直一鄉之望而已哉使寧宗而竟其用
則其施爲氣象將必有可觀者而中興之
功易與也夫以韓侂胄爲之搆讒京鏜爲
之傳議李沐爲之疏詆正謂市虎三人能
保其不爲永之行乎雖然吾惜其辭相之
不力也宗室不爲宰執高宗之訓也而衎
punctuated: 願早聞忠義之訓，善堅勵志之節，可以語行誼矣。不黜退居錦水而以樂善名，汝偵廾守布衣而以固窮著，可以語清脩矣。之數人者，或起於科目，或老于山林，而其立身行事之節有如此。而吾所尊仰之者，則惟丞相汝愚而已。好善忘勢，有仕優則學之風；正色立朝，有國爾忘家之節。其期待也，則以司馬光、富弼、韓琦、范仲淹爲己任；其淵源也，則以朱熹、張栻、呂祖謙、王十朋、汪應辰爲師友。忠結人主，而有文武威風之稱；行孚于朝，而有忠孝大節之薦。是蓋不徒誓志於功名，而實任道之器也，豈直一鄉之望而已哉！使寧宗而竟其用，則其施爲氣象將必有可觀者，而中興之功易與也。夫以韓侂胄爲之搆讒，京鏜爲之傳議，李沐爲之疏詆，正謂市虎三人，能保其不爲永之行乎？雖然，吾惜其辭相之不力也。宗室不爲宰執，高宗之訓也，而衎
translation_en:
…[Bi]yuan received instruction in loyalty and righteousness early in life, and Shanjian displayed steadfast resolve: these are examples worthy of discussion for their moral conduct. Buchu retired to Jinshui and became known for delighting in goodness; Ruzhen remained a commoner [?] and became renowned for maintaining his principles in poverty: these are examples worthy of discussion for their purity and cultivation of character. These men either rose through the examinations or grew old in woodland retirement, yet such was the integrity with which they conducted their lives and affairs. The one whom I revere and admire, however, is Chief Councillor Ruyu alone.

He loved goodness and forgot his powerful position, embodying the principle that one who has strength to spare after official service should study. He stood at court with an upright bearing, displaying the integrity of one who forgets his family in devotion to the state. In his aspirations, he took it upon himself to emulate Sima Guang, Fu Bi, Han Qi, and Fan Zhongyan; in the sources of his learning, he took Zhu Xi, Zhang Shi, Lü Zuqian, Wang Shipeng, and Wang Yingchen as teachers and friends. His loyalty bound him to his sovereign, and he was praised for his commanding presence in both civil and military affairs. His conduct won the court’s trust, and he was recommended for his outstanding loyalty and filial devotion. Surely he was not merely someone resolved to win achievement and fame, but a man truly capable of bearing responsibility for the Way. How could he have been merely the pride of a single locality?

Had Ningzong employed him to the fullest, his accomplishments and the character of his administration would surely have been remarkable, and the achievement of dynastic restoration would have been readily attainable. But Han Tuozhou fabricated slanders against him, Jing Tang circulated accusations against him, and Li Mu submitted a memorial vilifying him. This was precisely the case of three men reporting a tiger in the marketplace: could anyone have guaranteed that he would escape the journey to Yong? Even so, I regret that he did not decline the chief councillorship more firmly. That members of the imperial clan should not serve as chief councillors or other chief ministers was Gaozong’s injunction; yet Kan [?] …

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
昧此乎然趙氏者又豈特一時之盛而已
抑使宋室而世其官則其夾輔忠貞又將
有可觀者而世臣之功可收也夫以崇憲
爲之子必愿爲之孫良淳爲之曾孫可謂
四世名德而獨無有知之者乎雖然吾惜
其逢時之不偶也人衆則能勝天往事之
監也而又何論乎方是時也晦菴十里命
駕註騷以洩不平蓋不待良淳之身而已
決矣君子以是知忠賢之進退而百年之
===
氣運係之一門之盛衰而終宋之命脉係
之彼小人者所自爲謀則巧矣而其流至
于禍人家國而不悟亦獨何哉蓋嘗即宋
事而論之宋之亡國也始於公天下而成
於私其身故其初也兄弟之太恩而其後
也子姓之不保其仁也優於養士而其廑
也畧於懿親羣臣任于九族不免乎編氓
罷政乞祠諸宗顧以之應舉儗之以先王
親睦之風誠無以望其後求諸大易通變
punctuated:
昧此乎？然趙氏者，又豈特一時之盛而已？抑使宋室而世其官，則其夾輔忠貞又將有可觀者，而世臣之功可收也。夫以崇憲爲之子，必愿爲之孫，良淳爲之曾孫，可謂四世名德，而獨無有知之者乎？雖然，吾惜其逢時之不偶也。人衆則能勝天，往事之監也，而又何論乎？方是時也，晦菴十里命駕，註騷以洩不平，蓋不待良淳之身而已決矣。君子以是知忠賢之進退，而百年之氣運係之；一門之盛衰，而終宋之命脉係之。彼小人者，所自爲謀則巧矣，而其流至于禍人家國而不悟，亦獨何哉？
蓋嘗即宋事而論之，宋之亡國也，始於公天下，而成於私其身。故其初也，兄弟之太恩；而其後也，子姓之不保。其仁也，優於養士；而其廑也，畧於懿親。羣臣任于，九族不免乎編氓。罷政乞祠，諸宗顧以之應舉。儗之以先王親睦之風，誠無以望其後；求諸大易通變
translation_en:
…was he unaware of this? Yet was the Zhao family's eminence confined to a single generation? Had the Song ruling house allowed this family to hold office generation after generation, its loyal and steadfast assistance to the throne would likewise have been worthy of admiration, and the benefits of service by hereditary ministers could have been secured. With Chongxian as his son, Biyuan as his grandson, and Liangchun as his great-grandson, there were surely four generations renowned for virtue. Was there really no one who recognized them? Even so, I lament their ill fortune in the times they encountered. When enough people combine, they can overcome Heaven: past events offer this warning. What more is there to say? At that time, Hui'an ordered his carriage for a journey of ten li [?] and annotated Encountering Sorrow to vent his indignation. The outcome was already decided, without waiting for Liangchun's lifetime. From this the gentleman understands that the fortunes of a hundred years depended on the advancement or withdrawal of loyal and worthy men, and that the lifeblood of the Song down to its end depended on the rise or decline of a single family. Those petty men were clever indeed in scheming for themselves. Yet their actions ultimately brought disaster upon another's family and the state, and they never understood it. Why was this so?
I have considered the affairs of the Song in these terms: the dynasty's loss of its realm began with treating All-under-Heaven as a public trust and was consummated by rulers pursuing their own private interests. Thus, at the beginning, excessive favor was shown between brothers; afterward, their descendants could not be protected. Their benevolence was generous in nurturing scholars, but their solicitude was scant toward their close imperial kin. Ministers were entrusted with office [?], while members of the nine degrees of kinship could not escape the status of registered commoners. Retirement from government and requests for temple sinecures were, paradoxically, what members of the imperial clan sought through the examinations [?]. Measured against the former kings' practice of fostering affection and harmony among kin, this could scarcely follow even in their footsteps. If one seeks in the great Book of Changes the principle of adapting to changing circumstances…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
之道彼固以爲得之矣然而豪傑之才固
無恃乎門第神明之胄終弗類乎寒微卒
能以其忠孝之姿而赴功名之會入而爲
良相出而爲賢牧生而爲善士死而爲忠
臣炳炳乎起而爲中原文獻之傳此豈爵
祿名寵之所能勸而封建科目之所能限
者哉愚以是知有志之士無所待而猶興
者雖以宋之宗室猶能自飭其身自淑其
政以爲國家之重則凡爲今日之
===
藩國者
祖宗之富貴若此
朝廷之親愛若此又將何以爲報哉然非欲
其舉成法而棄之讀書業科舉効儒生輩
爲也亦曰
祖訓者
皇祖之家灋也守之以不越則自有餘貴矣境
內者
天子之子民也居之以不擾則自有餘富矣該
punctuated:
之道，彼固以爲得之矣。然而豪傑之才，固無恃乎門第；神明之胄，終弗類乎寒微。卒能以其忠孝之姿，而赴功名之會，入而爲良相，出而爲賢牧，生而爲善士，死而爲忠臣，炳炳乎起而爲中原文獻之傳。此豈爵祿名寵之所能勸，而封建科目之所能限者哉？愚以是知有志之士，無所待而猶興者。雖以宋之宗室，猶能自飭其身，自淑其政，以爲國家之重。則凡爲今日之藩國者，祖宗之富貴若此，朝廷之親愛若此，又將何以爲報哉？

然非欲其舉成法而棄之，讀書業科舉，効儒生輩爲也。亦曰：《祖訓》者，皇祖之家灋也，守之以不越，則自有餘貴矣；境內者，天子之子民也，居之以不擾，則自有餘富矣。該
translation_en:
…the Way of adapting to change: they certainly believed they had grasped it. Yet exceptional talent assuredly does not depend upon pedigree, and the descendants of illustrious sovereigns are, in the end, unlike those of humble origins. Ultimately, with their qualities of loyalty and filial devotion, they could seize opportunities for achievement and renown: serving at court as worthy chief councilors and in the provinces as worthy governors, living as good men and dying as loyal ministers. They rose resplendent to transmit the cultural heritage of the Central Plains. Could rank, emoluments, fame, and favor have been what spurred them on? Could systems of enfeoffment and examination categories have confined them? From this I, in my humble judgment, know that men of resolve rise even without waiting for external encouragement. Even members of the Song imperial clan could discipline themselves and improve their governance, becoming pillars of the state. How, then, shall all those who hold princely fiefs today repay such wealth and honor bestowed by their ancestors, and such affection shown by the court?

Yet I do not wish them to cast aside the established regulations, study books and pursue the examinations, or imitate the conduct of Confucian students. I say only this: the Ancestral Injunctions (Zuxun) are the household laws of the imperial founding ancestor. Observe them without transgression, and there will naturally be honor in abundance. Those within your domains are the people whom the Son of Heaven cherishes as his children. Dwell among them without troubling them, and there will naturally be wealth in abundance. It is stated [?]…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
曰居上不驕高而不危所以長守貴也制
節謹度滿而不溢所以長守富也是謂無
所事事而有利於國與民夫無所事事之
利與有所事事而未必利者其勞逸難易
奚啻十百千萬莫之禁而弗爲豈不大有
負於時乎於戲此義行則不惟爵封茲土
者之知所以勸而凡天下之爲王國者靡
不竭忠夾輔以綿我
國家無疆之休矣故曰師其意也以此
===
第四問　　　　　　　　　　　　江鯤
同考試官教諭李　批〔五策條答無遺而皆有大下之慮此篇拔其尤者〕
同考試官教諭林　批〔談錢幣有違變之術可謂識時務者〕
考試官教諭葉　批〔考古而不遺酌今而合宜有用之才也〕
考試官教授伍　批〔論李言圜法與夫利弊〕
punctuated:
曰：「居上不驕，高而不危，所以長守貴也；制節謹度，滿而不溢，所以長守富也。」是謂無所事事而有利於國與民。夫無所事事之利，與有所事事而未必利者，其勞逸難易，奚啻十百千萬！莫之禁而弗爲，豈不大有負於時乎？於戲！此義行，則不惟爵封茲土者之知所以勸，而凡天下之爲王國者，靡不竭忠夾輔，以綿我國家無疆之休矣。故曰「師其意也」，以此。

第四問　江鯤
同考試官教諭李　批〔五策條答無遺而皆有大下之慮此篇拔其尤者〕
同考試官教諭林　批〔談錢幣有違變之術可謂識時務者〕
考試官教諭葉　批〔考古而不遺酌今而合宜有用之才也〕
考試官教授伍　批〔論李言圜法與夫利弊〕
translation_en:
… says: “To occupy a superior position without arrogance, to stand high without danger: this is how one long preserves nobility. To observe restraint and carefully follow the prescribed measures, to be full without overflowing: this is how one long preserves wealth.” This is what is meant by undertaking no affairs yet benefiting the state and the people. Between benefiting them by undertaking no affairs and undertaking affairs that may not benefit them, the difference in exertion and ease, difficulty and simplicity, is surely more than tenfold, a hundredfold, a thousandfold, or ten thousandfold! If nothing prohibits this course, yet one fails to pursue it, does one not greatly fail the needs of the times? Alas! If this principle is put into practice, not only will those enfeoffed in this territory know what should encourage them; all who rule princely domains throughout the realm will exhaust their loyalty in supporting the throne, perpetuating the boundless blessings of our state. This is why I said, “Take its intent as your model.”

Fourth Policy Question — Jiang Kun

Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “All five policy essays answer every point without omission, and all show concern for the realm [?]. This essay has been selected as the most outstanding.”

Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: “In discussing currency, he offers methods of adaptation [?]; he may be called someone who understands the needs of the times.”

Examiner Ye, Instructor, comments: “He examines antiquity without omissions and weighs present circumstances appropriately. He is a man of useful ability.”

Examiner Wu, Professor, comments: “Discusses Li [?], the currency system, and its benefits and drawbacks.”

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
人君欲制用以足國則不可不通變以裕
民蓋天之立君本以治民而君之足國亦
惟以利民耳以利民爲心則用之詘也不
可不善其道以處之濟之弊也不可不通
其變以宜之民宜則百姓足君孰與不足
君足則百度舉天下又焉有不治哉愚讀
明問及此作而嘆曰是欲修政非爲理財
也欲裕民非爲足國也敢不掇拾以對嘗
昔民之有生易於困也天必生財以資之
===
財之爲用易於乏也君必立法以理之是
故稻黍稷麥菽之五穀珠玉金刀布之三
幣非財之生於天者乎錢以濟穀幣之不
通鈔以補錢幣之不足非法之立於君者
乎蓋五穀可以取用而不可以致遠三幣
可以致遠而不可以常得則其勢不得不
趨於錢鈔矣夫三品之金銅爲下以之鑄
錢爲最宜是物也在陶唐氏謂之泉商人
謂之布齊人莒人謂之刀周人兼謂之帛
punctuated: 人君欲制用以足國，則不可不通變以裕民。蓋天之立君，本以治民，而君之足國，亦惟以利民耳。以利民爲心，則用之詘也，不可不善其道以處之；濟之弊也，不可不通其變以宜之。民宜則百姓足，君孰與不足？君足則百度舉，天下又焉有不治哉？愚讀明問及此，作而嘆曰：「是欲修政，非爲理財也；欲裕民，非爲足國也。」敢不掇拾以對？嘗昔民之有生，易於困也，天必生財以資之；財之爲用，易於乏也，君必立法以理之。是故稻、黍、稷、麥、菽之五穀，珠玉、金、刀布之三幣，非財之生於天者乎？錢以濟穀幣之不通，鈔以補錢幣之不足，非法之立於君者乎？蓋五穀可以取用，而不可以致遠；三幣可以致遠，而不可以常得，則其勢不得不趨於錢鈔矣。夫三品之金，銅爲下，以之鑄錢爲最宜。是物也，在陶唐氏謂之泉，商人謂之布，齊人、莒人謂之刀，周人兼謂之帛。
translation_en:
If a ruler wishes to regulate expenditure and make the state's resources sufficient, he must adapt to changing circumstances so as to enrich the people. Heaven established rulers originally to govern the people; a ruler's provision of sufficient resources for the state likewise serves only to benefit the people. With their benefit at heart, when resources for expenditure fall short, he must find sound methods of dealing with this; when measures of relief develop defects [?], he must adapt them to make them appropriate. When the people's circumstances are favorable, the common people have enough: with whom, then, could the ruler share insufficiency? When the ruler has enough, all the affairs of government are carried out. How, then, could the realm fail to be well governed? Upon reading your illuminating question to this point, I rose and exclaimed: “This seeks to improve government, not merely to manage wealth; to enrich the people, not merely to make the state's resources sufficient.” How could I fail to gather what I know in reply?

In former times [?], the people were readily beset by hardship in sustaining their lives, so Heaven necessarily produced wealth to support them. Wealth was readily exhausted through use, so rulers necessarily established regulations to manage it. Thus, the five grains—rice, glutinous millet, common millet, wheat, and beans—and the three kinds of currency—pearls and jade, gold, and knife and spade money—are these not wealth produced by Heaven? Coins remedy the difficulties in circulating grain and other currencies, while paper notes supplement an insufficient supply of coins: are these not arrangements established by rulers? The five grains can be put to use but cannot readily be conveyed over great distances; the three kinds of currency can be conveyed over great distances but cannot always be obtained. Circumstances therefore necessarily lead to the use of coins and paper notes.

Of the three grades of metal, copper ranks lowest, yet it is the most suitable for casting coins. This object was called quan under Taotang; the people of Shang called it bu; the people of Qi and Ju called it dao; and the people of Zhou also called it bo, “silk” [?]…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
至景王鑄錢則謂之寳貨而錢始有□入矣
後是或爲八銖四銖或爲開元通寳或爲
皇宋通寳及其弊也則有榆莢鵝眼二銖
四分而失之太輕又有赤仄半兩直百當
千而失之太重求其得中者其惟漢之五
銖唐之開元乎然孰若我
朝通寳爲最善夫百物之質楮爲輕以之制
鈔爲尤便是物也在漢謂之皮幣在唐謂
之飛錢在宋謂之便錢至寇瑊守蜀則謂
===
之交子而始用楮矣後是或爲錢引或爲
交鈔或爲關會或爲會子及其衍也有一
界印一千百萬一界印三千萬萬而多寡
之不同有至元一貫準中統五貫有至大
一貫準至元五貫而貴賤之不同未有適
均者其惟宋之天聖元之中統乎然孰若
我
朝寳鈔爲最良夫錢之制既善則通之天下
而可行而何周□之都餘地鈔之制既良
punctuated:
至景王鑄錢，則謂之寳貨，而錢始有□入矣。後是，或爲八銖、四銖，或爲開元通寳，或爲皇宋通寳。及其弊也，則有榆莢、鵝眼、二銖、四分，而失之太輕；又有赤仄、半兩、直百、當千，而失之太重。求其得中者，其惟漢之五銖、唐之開元乎？然孰若我朝通寳爲最善？

夫百物之質，楮爲輕，以之制鈔爲尤便。是物也，在漢謂之皮幣，在唐謂之飛錢，在宋謂之便錢。至寇瑊守蜀，則謂之交子，而始用楮矣。後是，或爲錢引，或爲交鈔，或爲關會，或爲會子。及其衍也，有一界印一千百萬、一界印三千萬萬，而多寡之不同；有至元一貫準中統五貫，有至大一貫準至元五貫，而貴賤之不同。未有適均者，其惟宋之天聖、元之中統乎？然孰若我朝寳鈔爲最良？

夫錢之制既善，則通之天下而可行，而何周□之都餘地？鈔之制既良，
translation_en:
…When King Jing cast coins, they were called “precious currency,” and coins first had □入 [?]. Thereafter there were eight-zhu and four-zhu coins, Kaiyuan tongbao coins, and Huang Song tongbao coins. When abuses arose, there were “elm-pod” and “goose-eye” coins, two-zhu coins, and four-fen coins, which erred by being too light; there were also red-rim coins, half-liang coins, coins worth one hundred, and coins worth one thousand, which erred by being too heavy. If we seek those that struck the proper balance, were they not the Han five-zhu coins and the Tang Kaiyuan coins? Yet which could compare with our dynasty’s tongbao coins, the best of all?

Among the materials of all things, paper is light, making it especially convenient for producing banknotes. This form of currency was called “hide currency” under the Han, “flying cash” under the Tang, and “convenience money” under the Song. When Kou Jian governed Shu, it was called jiaozi, and paper first came into use. Thereafter there were qianyin, jiaochao, guanhui, and huizi notes. As their issuance expanded, one issue might comprise eleven million [?], while another comprised three hundred billion [?], so quantities varied. One guan of Zhiyuan notes was equivalent to five guan of Zhongtong notes, and one guan of Zhida notes was equivalent to five guan of Zhiyuan notes, so values varied. None achieved a proper balance—unless perhaps those of the Song Tiansheng and Yuan Zhongtong eras? Yet which could compare with our dynasty’s precious banknotes, the finest of all?

Once the system of coinage is sound, its currency can circulate throughout the realm; why then [distinguish between?] the capital and other places [?]? Once the system of banknotes is sound…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
則推之後世而皆準而何分於草昧承平
然而猶有不能盡如立法之始而多積於
無用者此無他不能通其變於未窮焉耳
且錢之稱爲泉布以其流通而無滯也鈔
而稱爲楮幣以其輕便均爲寶也今世之
用者惟銀幣是資自官府之催科以至民
間之貿易率惟是之售至於錢之用獨居
常小費而已錢安得不滯鈔之用特論功
議辟而已鈔安得可行錢鈔既輕則銀幣
益重銀重則用之者日不足而取之者盡
錙銖于是乎有輸粟之計有發礦之謀是
亦不得已而爲是權宜以紓
宵旰之憂以濟用度之急耳然輸粟若可也
而名器濫其或濫發礦若可也而採取未
免殃民二者誠非足國裕民之要道其惟
於錢鈔之用救其弊而使之不匱通其變
而使之宜民可矣何者錢不患其滯也立
法以疏之則通鈔不患其輕也立法以反
punctuated: 則推之後世而皆準，而何分於草昧承平？然而猶有不能盡如立法之始，而多積於無用者，此無他，不能通其變於未窮焉耳。且錢之稱爲泉布，以其流通而無滯也；鈔而稱爲楮幣，以其輕便，均爲寶也。今世之用者，惟銀幣是資，自官府之催科，以至民間之貿易，率惟是之售。至於錢之用，獨居常小費而已，錢安得不滯？鈔之用，特論功議辟而已，鈔安得可行？錢鈔既輕，則銀幣益重；銀重，則用之者日不足，而取之者盡錙銖。于是乎有輸粟之計，有發礦之謀，是亦不得已而爲是權宜，以紓宵旰之憂，以濟用度之急耳。然輸粟若可也，而名器濫其或濫；發礦若可也，而採取未免殃民。二者誠非足國裕民之要道。其惟於錢鈔之用，救其弊而使之不匱，通其變而使之宜民，可矣。何者？錢不患其滯也，立法以疏之則通；鈔不患其輕也，立法以反
translation_en:
…then it can be extended to later generations and serve as a standard for them all; why distinguish between times of founding turmoil and settled peace? Yet its operation still cannot fully match the intentions at the establishment of the laws, and much currency accumulates unused. This is for no other reason than a failure to adapt it to changing circumstances before its possibilities are exhausted.

Coins are called quanbu, “flowing currency,” because they circulate without obstruction; notes are called “paper currency” because they are light and convenient. Both are treasures. In present-day transactions, however, silver alone is relied upon. From government collection of taxes to trade among the people, virtually all payments are made with it. Coins are used only for small everyday expenses: how could they fail to stagnate? Notes are used only in assessing rewards for merit and deliberating penalties: how could they circulate? Once coins and notes lose value, silver becomes still more valuable. As silver grows dearer, those who need to use it find their supply increasingly inadequate, while those who collect it exact every last fraction of an ounce.

Hence the plans for grain contributions and proposals to open mines. These are merely expedients adopted out of necessity, to relieve the sovereign’s anxieties that keep him occupied before dawn and after nightfall, and to meet urgent expenditure. Grain contributions may seem acceptable, but official ranks and honors are bestowed indiscriminately [?]; opening mines may seem acceptable, but extraction inevitably brings suffering upon the people. Neither is truly the essential means of making the state adequately supplied and the people prosperous. Rather, in the use of coins and notes, we should remedy their defects so that supplies do not run short, and adapt them to changing circumstances so that they serve the people’s needs. This would suffice. Why? There is no need to fear the stagnation of coins: establish laws to clear their channels, and they will circulate. There is no need to fear the low value of notes: establish laws to reverse…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
之則重蓋錢之鑄本以濟幣之窮鈔之制
又以濟錢之乏茲欲錢鈔之行必別其大
小之分權其子母之勢於錢則分古今以
今之一而當古之二濫惡者不得雜於其
間於鈔則分新舊以舊之二而當新之一
折壞者不得預以爲算二者又皆以銀爲
準銀一分而準錢十文鈔十張而準銀一
分由是立爲一定之則凡有行使大約以
三分爲率雖銀之多也不得專用銀銀一
===
而錢居其一雖錢之多也不得專用錢錢
二而鈔居其一上而科派徵收下而輸納
懋遷率守是瀍而罔俾踰易至於鈔重則
出錢以易鈔錢重則出鈔以易錢又必嚴
銅楮之禁絕僞造之奸謹關市之令杜減
境之私將見出於官者有以資於民入於
民者可以閉之官錢鈔尚何有不行哉或
謂銀銅並行未免爲穆則古今之矣周禮
內府掌邦之大用外府掌邦之小用準此
punctuated: 之則重。蓋錢之鑄，本以濟幣之窮；鈔之制，又以濟錢之乏。茲欲錢鈔之行，必別其大小之分，權其子母之勢。於錢則分古今，以今之一而當古之二，濫惡者不得雜於其間；於鈔則分新舊，以舊之二而當新之一，折壞者不得預以爲算。二者又皆以銀爲準：銀一分而準錢十文，鈔十張而準銀一分。由是立爲一定之則，凡有行使，大約以三分爲率。雖銀之多也，不得專用銀，銀一而錢居其一；雖錢之多也，不得專用錢，錢二而鈔居其一。上而科派徵收，下而輸納懋遷，率守是瀍，而罔俾踰易。至於鈔重則出錢以易鈔，錢重則出鈔以易錢。又必嚴銅楮之禁，絕僞造之奸；謹關市之令，杜減境之私。將見出於官者有以資於民，入於民者可以閉之官，錢鈔尚何有不行哉？或謂銀銅並行，未免爲穆，則古今之矣。《周禮》內府掌邦之大用，外府掌邦之小用。準此
translation_en: …it will regain its value. Coins were originally cast to remedy a shortage of currency, and paper notes were instituted in turn to remedy a shortage of coins. To ensure the circulation of coins and notes now, their greater and lesser denominations must be distinguished, and the relative weight of the “mother” and “child” currencies balanced. Coins should be divided into ancient and current issues, with one current coin equivalent to two ancient coins; inferior coins must not be mixed among them. Notes should be divided into new and old issues, with two old notes equivalent to one new note; torn or damaged notes must not be counted. Both should also be valued against silver: one fen of silver should equal ten cash, and ten notes should equal one fen of silver. These should be established as fixed rules. All payments should generally be apportioned in three shares. Even where silver is plentiful, silver alone must not be used: for one share of silver, coins should account for one share. Even where coins are plentiful, coins alone must not be used: for two shares of coins, notes should account for one share. Above, in assessments and collections, and below, in remittances and trade, all should observe this rule [?], with no departures or alterations permitted. When notes rise in value, coins should be issued to exchange for notes; when coins rise in value, notes should be issued to exchange for coins. Restrictions concerning copper and paper currency must also be strictly enforced to eliminate counterfeiting, and regulations at customs barriers and markets carefully upheld to prevent illicit movement across the borders [?]. Then currency issued by the authorities will provide resources for the people, and currency received by the people can return to the authorities [?]. How could coins and notes still fail to circulate? Some may say that the concurrent circulation of silver and copper inevitably produces confusion [?]; yet there is ancient precedent [?]. In the Rites of Zhou, the Inner Treasury administers the state's major expenditures, and the Outer Treasury its minor expenditures. On this basis…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
以銀爲大用錢爲小用又何不可乎又謂
銅楮錯用日見其勞則古又有之矣單穆
公曰民患輕則爲母權子而行民患重則
爲子權母而行準此以錢爲母以鈔爲子
又何不可乎行之旣利習之而安則錢鈔
與銀幣相兼相濟相補相洩不出三三年
之間國可使富而民亦有餘大則
朝廷之祭祀征伐營繕錫予隨用皆充小則
閭閻之衣食用度致遠輕齎隨在各足所
===
謂制用裕民誠莫有要於此矣雖然此特
語其末耳又有其本在焉傳曰官之失職
寵賂章也抑孰知古人之制用其意固已
嚴乎夫錢之名曰流曰泉以言清也清斯
惠流矣曰利于刀以言決也決斯利辯矣
曰布于布以言德也德斯令布矣曰束于
帛以言約也約斯不濫潔斯不瀆矣
凡以爲用錢者言也鈔之名其制取諸券
義取諸交易上之交下而補助行焉否則
punctuated:
以銀爲大用，錢爲小用，又何不可乎？又謂銅楮錯用，日見其勞，則古又有之矣。單穆公曰：「民患輕，則爲母權子而行；民患重，則爲子權母而行。」準此，以錢爲母，以鈔爲子，又何不可乎？行之旣利，習之而安，則錢鈔與銀幣相兼相濟，相補相洩，不出三三年之間，國可使富，而民亦有餘。大則朝廷之祭祀、征伐、營繕、錫予，隨用皆充；小則閭閻之衣食用度、致遠輕齎，隨在各足。所謂制用裕民，誠莫有要於此矣。
雖然，此特語其末耳，又有其本在焉。傳曰：「官之失職，寵賂章也。」抑孰知古人之制用，其意固已嚴乎！夫錢之名，曰流，曰泉，以言清也，清斯惠流矣；曰利于刀，以言決也，決斯利辯矣；曰布于布，以言德也，德斯令布矣；曰束于帛，以言約也，約斯不濫，潔斯不瀆矣。凡以爲用錢者言也。鈔之名，其制取諸券，義取諸交易。上之交下，而補助行焉，否則
translation_en:
…use silver for major expenditures and copper cash for minor expenditures: why should this not be permissible? Some further say that using copper cash and paper currency together brings daily trouble. Yet this, too, has an ancient precedent. Duke Mu of Shan said: “When the people suffer from currency being too light, make the mother to balance the child and circulate it; when the people suffer from currency being too heavy, make the child to balance the mother and circulate it.” Following this principle, why should we not make copper cash the mother and paper currency the child? Once their circulation proves beneficial and familiarity makes their use comfortable, copper cash, paper currency, and silver currency will work together and sustain one another, supplying deficiencies and draining surpluses. Within ‘three-three’ years [?], the state could be made wealthy and the people would also have a surplus. At the greater level, the court’s sacrifices, military campaigns, construction and repairs, and grants and gifts would all be amply supplied as needs arose. At the lesser level, ordinary households would have enough everywhere for clothing, food, and daily expenses, and could convey wealth over long distances with light loads. For what is called regulating expenditure and enriching the people, surely nothing is more essential than this.
Nevertheless, this speaks only of the peripheral aspects; there is also a fundamental principle. The Commentary says: “Officials neglect their duties when favoritism and bribery are conspicuous.” Yet who recognizes how strict the ancients’ intentions already were in regulating expenditure? Among the names for money are ‘flow’ and ‘spring,’ expressing clarity: with clarity, benefits flow. The phrase ‘benefit through the knife’ expresses decisiveness: with decisiveness, benefits are distinguished [?]. The phrase ‘spread through cloth’ expresses virtue: with virtue, commands spread. The phrase ‘bind through silk’ expresses restraint: with restraint, there is no excess; with purity, there is no defilement. All these sayings address those who use money. As for paper currency, its form derives from certificates, and its meaning derives from exchange. When those above engage with those below, aid and assistance are put into effect; otherwise …

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
於天下之交上而貢賦輸焉否則畔矣凡
以爲用鈔者言也若私與公交遠臣與近
臣交正與奇之流通補者是謂不泉不刀
不布不帛而已失其制用之本而又益之
以非道之交其不傷財而害民也者幾希
此後世之財所以日見其告匱而理財之
難於昔之人無惑也故曰其本則在
朝廷而不在有司
第五問
===
江一川
考試官教諭葉　批〔經畫備荒弭盜之畧咸〕〔中時宜而結尤有餘味有用之才也〕
考試官教授伍　批〔敷陳詳盡是有見者〕
善爲政者不恃無盜而恃吾有弭盜之術
不恃無荒而恃吾有備荒之術蓋有備無
患爲政之大經也荒與盜之無同不足恃
而吾備荒之術弭盜之方豈可不豫爲之
所乎誠能於豐登有餘之日恒爲荒歉不
punctuated:
於天。下之交上，而貢賦輸焉，否則畔矣。凡以爲用鈔者言也。若私與公交，遠臣與近臣交，正與奇之流通補者，是謂不泉、不刀、不布、不帛，而已失其制用之本，而又益之以非道之交，其不傷財而害民也者幾希。此後世之財所以日見其告匱，而理財之難於昔之人，無惑也。故曰：其本則在朝廷，而不在有司。

第五問

江一川

考試官教諭葉，批〔經畫備荒弭盜之畧咸〕〔中時宜而結尤有餘味有用之才也〕

考試官教授伍，批〔敷陳詳盡是有見者〕

善爲政者，不恃無盜，而恃吾有弭盜之術；不恃無荒，而恃吾有備荒之術。蓋有備無患，爲政之大經也。荒與盜之無，同不足恃，而吾備荒之術、弭盜之方，豈可不豫爲之所乎？誠能於豐登有餘之日，恒爲荒歉不
translation_en:
…against Heaven [?]. When those below deal with those above, tribute and taxes are remitted; otherwise, there is rebellion. All this is said with reference to those who use paper currency. But when private interests enter into dealings with public authority, distant officials with officials close to the throne, and regular and irregular channels circulate and supplement one another [?], this amounts to having neither the spring, nor the knife, nor the cloth, nor the silk. The fundamental principles governing their use have already been lost, and improper dealings are added to this. There is scarcely any chance that such practices will not deplete resources and harm the people. This explains why, in later ages, financial resources increasingly prove insufficient; it is no wonder that managing finances is harder than it was for the people of antiquity. Thus I say: the root of the matter lies with the imperial court, not with the responsible officials.

Fifth Question

Jiang Yichuan

Comment by Examiner Ye, Instructor: 〔His plans for preparing against famine and suppressing banditry all〕〔accord with the needs of the time, and the conclusion is especially thought-provoking. He is a man of practical ability.〕

Comment by Examiner Wu, Professor: 〔The exposition is thorough and detailed. This is someone with insight.〕

Those skilled in government rely not on the absence of bandits, but on possessing methods for suppressing banditry; they rely not on the absence of famine, but on possessing methods for preparing against famine. Preparedness averts calamity: this is a cardinal principle of government. Neither the absence of famine nor the absence of banditry can be relied upon. How, then, could we fail to make advance provision through our methods of preparing against famine and suppressing banditry? If, in days of abundant harvests and surpluses, we could constantly remain concerned about famine and insufficient supplies…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
給之憂夫平無事之時毎懷反側擾擾之
慮則荒歉盜皆有其備斯善爲政矣請復
明問饑饉薦臻國家代有葢天時之不常
地利人事之不及也顧吾所以備之何如
耳觀諸成周荒政十二以及遺人廩人所
掌則所以慮災防患也至矣盜賊竊發古
今皆然葢其困於饑寒而弄兵山海以爲
假息之計也亦顧吾所以弭之何如耳觀
諸成周聯比什伍以爲追逐胥伺之備則
所以思患預防也深矣此三代之民所以
===
遇災無患承平無事也先王往矣成濾具
在乃若江西則目前之近固難辛以周濾
行之而亦不可不爲之深思遠慮也是故
地狹矣而猶有曠土民稠矣而類多游民
是無惟乎蓄積寡而荒易見也執事固嘗
慮及此矣而今者南贛之水泛濫瀰漫又
得無爲地方之患乎民財窮矣而賦歛愈
繁民力竭矣而征役不息是無惟乎姦宄
punctuated:
給之憂，夫平無事之時，毎懷反側擾擾之慮，則荒歉、盜皆有其備，斯善爲政矣。請復明問：饑饉薦臻，國家代有，葢天時之不常，地利人事之不及也，顧吾所以備之何如耳。觀諸成周荒政十二，以及遺人、廩人所掌，則所以慮災防患也至矣。盜賊竊發，古今皆然，葢其困於饑寒，而弄兵山海，以爲假息之計也，亦顧吾所以弭之何如耳。觀諸成周聯比什伍，以爲追逐胥伺之備，則所以思患預防也深矣。此三代之民所以遇災無患、承平無事也。
先王往矣，成濾具在。乃若江西，則目前之近，固難辛以周濾行之，而亦不可不爲之深思遠慮也。是故地狹矣，而猶有曠土；民稠矣，而類多游民。是無惟乎蓄積寡而荒易見也？執事固嘗慮及此矣。而今者南贛之水泛濫瀰漫，又得無爲地方之患乎？民財窮矣，而賦歛愈繁；民力竭矣，而征役不息。是無惟乎姦宄
translation_en:
…the fear of insufficient provisions; if, in times of peace [?] when nothing is amiss, one constantly considers the danger of unrest and turmoil, then preparations will exist against both famine and banditry. This is good government. Allow me to respond to your discerning question. Repeated famines have occurred under every dynasty. They arise from irregular weather and shortcomings in the use of the land and in human efforts. What matters is how we prepare for them. Consider the twelve famine-relief measures of the Zhou and the responsibilities of its Provisioners and Granary Directors: their provisions for anticipating disasters and preventing calamities were indeed comprehensive. Sudden outbreaks of banditry have occurred in ancient and modern times alike. Driven by hunger and cold, people take up arms in the mountains and along the seas as a means of prolonging their precarious lives. Here too, what matters is how we suppress such troubles. Consider how the Zhou linked households into groups of ten and five, preparing them to pursue offenders and keep watch over one another: their foresight in anticipating and preventing trouble was indeed profound. This is why the people of the Three Dynasties suffered no distress when disasters struck and enjoyed undisturbed peace in settled times.
The former kings are gone, but their established plans [?] remain fully available. As for Jiangxi, given the immediate circumstances, it is certainly difficult to implement comprehensive plans [?]; yet we cannot fail to give the matter deep thought and consider the long term. Thus, although land is scarce, some still lies uncultivated; although the population is dense, many people lack settled occupations. Is it any wonder [?] that reserves are scant and famine readily appears? You, sir, have surely considered this already. Now, moreover, the waters of Nangan have overflowed and spread far and wide: can they fail to bring distress to the locality? The people's resources are exhausted, yet taxes and exactions grow ever more numerous; their strength is depleted, yet levies and compulsory service never cease. Is it any wonder [?] that evildoers…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
生而盜易作也執事亦嘗加之慮矣如向
者姚源之賊出沒剽掠又得無爲今日之
防乎然嘗求之古人如中饑則發中熟之
所斂大饑則發大熟之所斂此平糴之濟
李悝嘗行於魏矣穀賤則增價而糴穀貴
則減價而糶此常平之濟耿壽昌嘗行於
漢矣至若隋之開皇則有長孫平之爲義
倉取之於民不厚而置之當社爲近宋之
孝宗則有朱熹之爲社倉始則請官米以
===
加息而終則止息米以加耗凡此皆備荒
之術也然地有遠近戶有多寡人有老幼
强弱自不能以皆同以今論之平糴慮有
拘泥之失常平恐失斂散之宜義倉委之
社司或非人以長吏奸胥社倉則官無所
責民有所刺識鄉閭無窮之計也使郡邑
皆倣而行而又斟酌以適中焉庶備荒其
有濟乎在漢武帝則作從命之濮盜起不
發發而捕弗滿品主者皆死在魏李悝則
punctuated: 生而盜易作也。執事亦嘗加之慮矣。如向者姚源之賊出沒剽掠，又得無爲今日之防乎？然嘗求之古人，如中饑則發中熟之所斂，大饑則發大熟之所斂，此平糴之濟，李悝嘗行於魏矣。穀賤則增價而糴，穀貴則減價而糶，此常平之濟，耿壽昌嘗行於漢矣。至若隋之開皇，則有長孫平之爲義倉，取之於民不厚，而置之當社爲近。宋之孝宗，則有朱熹之爲社倉，始則請官米以加息，而終則止息米以加耗。凡此皆備荒之術也。然地有遠近，戶有多寡，人有老幼强弱，自不能以皆同。以今論之，平糴慮有拘泥之失，常平恐失斂散之宜，義倉委之社司，或非人以長吏奸胥；社倉則官無所責，民有所刺，識鄉閭無窮之計也。使郡邑皆倣而行，而又斟酌以適中焉，庶備荒其有濟乎？在漢武帝則作從命之濮，盜起不發，發而捕弗滿品，主者皆死；在魏李悝則
translation_en:
… arise, and banditry readily breaks out. You, too, have given thought to this. For example, when the bandits of Yaoyuan formerly appeared and disappeared, plundering as they went, ought this not to prompt precautions today?

Yet I have sought precedents among the ancients. In a moderate famine, they released what had been collected during a moderately good harvest; in a great famine, they released what had been collected during a very abundant harvest. Such was the relief provided by equitable grain purchasing, which Li Kui once practiced in Wei. When grain was cheap, the purchase price was raised; when grain was dear, the selling price was lowered. Such was the relief provided by the ever-normal granary system, which Geng Shouchang once implemented under the Han. Then, during the Kaihuang reign of the Sui, Zhangsun Ping established charity granaries: contributions exacted from the people were light, and the granaries were conveniently located within their local communities. Under Emperor Xiaozong of the Song, Zhu Xi established community granaries. Initially, he requested government grain to lend at interest; ultimately, he discontinued the interest charge, retaining an additional allowance for wastage. All these were methods of preparing against famine.

Yet places are near or distant, households numerous or few, and people old or young, strong or weak; naturally, they cannot all be treated alike. Judged in present circumstances, equitable grain purchasing risks excessive rigidity; the ever-normal system may fail to collect and distribute grain appropriately. Charity granaries are entrusted to community administrators, who may be unsuitable and thereby encourage corrupt officials and clerks [?]. With community granaries, officials have no responsibility to exact contributions, and the people have something to criticize [?]; this is an enduring plan for local communities [?]. If prefectures and counties all followed these examples, weighing and adapting them to attain a proper balance, might preparations against famine then prove effective?

Under Emperor Wu of the Han, a statute called “Obeying Orders” [?] was enacted: if bandits arose and were not reported, or if they were reported but arrests fell short of the prescribed quota, all those responsible were put to death. In Wei, Li Kui, for his part, …

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
設樓鼓之防盜發而擊鼓則四村皆集
之而聲布百里義營之爲行之者實徵也
一户爲盜累其一村一户被盜累其一將
懸賞之濫爲之者崔安潛也告捕一盜賞
錢伍百同侶捕之賞同平人此皆弭盜之
方也然地有險易勢有强弱情有向背順
逆亦不能以相一自今觀之况命誠禁之
太嚴樓鼓止用之有警懸賞所費官錢亦
可暫而不可久惟義營則村自相保盜無
===
所脫實獨清一境之效也使郡邑皆行而
濫而又變通以宜民庶弭盜其或得乎雖
然此特蘉時之宜而非探本之論求其本
于備荒則荀卿所謂田野縣鄙者財之本
垣窌倉廩者財之末百姓時和事業得敘
者貨之源等賦府庫者貨之流而欲人君
養其和節其流開其源則上下俱富乃國
計之極故禹十年水湯七年旱而民無菜
色者以此故也知此則平糴諸濫又似□
punctuated: 設樓鼓之防，盜發而擊鼓，則四村皆集之，而聲布百里。義營之爲，行之者實徵也：一户爲盜，累其一村；一户被盜，累其一將。懸賞之濫，爲之者崔安潛也：告捕一盜，賞錢伍百；同侶捕之，賞同平人。此皆弭盜之方也。然地有險易，勢有强弱，情有向背順逆，亦不能以相一。自今觀之，况命誠禁之太嚴，樓鼓止用之有警，懸賞所費官錢，亦可暫而不可久。惟義營則村自相保，盜無所脫，實獨清一境之效也。使郡邑皆行而濫，而又變通以宜民，庶弭盜其或得乎？雖然，此特蘉時之宜，而非探本之論。求其本于備荒，則荀卿所謂「田野縣鄙者，財之本；垣窌倉廩者，財之末；百姓時和，事業得敘者，貨之源；等賦府庫者，貨之流」，而欲人君養其和，節其流，開其源，則上下俱富，乃國計之極。故禹十年水，湯七年旱，而民無菜色者，以此故也。知此，則平糴諸濫又似□
translation_en:
…set up watchtowers and drums as a defense. When bandits appeared and the drums were struck, the four surrounding villages would all assemble, and the sound would spread a hundred li. As for organizing community defense camps, the person who implemented this was Shi Zheng [?]: if one household engaged in banditry, its entire village was held accountable; if one household suffered a bandit attack, its commander was held accountable. The system of offering rewards [?] was instituted by Cui Anqian: reporting and capturing one bandit earned a reward of five hundred cash; an accomplice who captured him received the same reward as an ordinary person. These were all methods of suppressing banditry.

Yet terrain varies in difficulty, forces in strength, and popular sentiments in allegiance and opposition, obedience and defiance; these, too, cannot be made uniform. Viewed from the present, the kuangming measure [?] was indeed excessively harsh in its prohibitions. Watchtowers and drums are useful only when there is an alarm. Offering rewards consumes government funds and can be sustained temporarily, but not indefinitely. Only community defense camps, through which villagers protect one another and bandits have no means of escape, truly have the distinctive capacity to clear an entire district of banditry. If prefectures and counties all implemented this measure [?], adapting it to suit the people, might they not achieve some success in suppressing banditry?

Nevertheless, these are merely expedients suited to the times [?], rather than arguments that investigate the foundations. To seek the foundations of famine preparedness, consider what Xun Qing said: “Fields and outlying settlements are the roots of wealth; enclosed storage pits and granaries are its branches. The people's living in seasonal harmony and their occupations proceeding in proper order are the source of goods; graded levies and treasuries are their flow.” The ruler should nurture this harmony, regulate the flow, and open up the source. Then both those above and those below will be prosperous: this is the highest achievement of managing the state's resources. This is why, despite ten years of flooding under Yu and seven years of drought under Tang, the people showed no signs of hunger in their faces. Once this is understood, the various measures [?], such as purchasing grain at fair prices, would also seem … [illegible]

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
□矣求其本□□□則洪範箕禹所謂□
□食之源立教化之官示之以節儉示之
以純朴而欲人君不舍其本而專□其末
必如唐太宗之使民衣食有餘不必如宋
興寧別立盜賊重法焉則邪僻不作乃邪
成之至故路不拾遺外戶不閉商旅野
宿者坐是焉耳知此則流命諸法又似不
必用矣雖然猶未也三年耕必有一年之
食九年耕必有三年之食此王制之儲畜
===
之慮不使其非國也苟子之不欲雖賞之
不竊子欲善而民善此聖人主教化之意
不欲以徒慮也而蘇□□古之聖人上
盜以義使天下皆知父子君臣而誰與爲
亂朱熹入曰爲政者當順五行脩五事以
安百姓又荀范之所不及也特此而往雖
措之天下可也豈獨江西然哉昔人有云
勢不同而理同又云有治人而無治法歟
事以爲何如
punctuated:
□矣。求其本□□□，則洪範箕禹所謂□□食之源，立教化之官，示之以節儉，示之以純朴，而欲人君不舍其本而專□其末。必如唐太宗之使民衣食有餘，不必如宋興寧別立盜賊重法焉，則邪僻不作，乃邪成之至。故路不拾遺，外戶不閉，商旅野宿者，坐是焉耳。知此，則流命諸法又似不必用矣。

雖然，猶未也。三年耕必有一年之食，九年耕必有三年之食，此王制之儲畜之慮，不使其非國也。苟子之不欲，雖賞之不竊；子欲善而民善，此聖人主教化之意，不欲以徒慮也。而蘇□□古之聖人上盜以義，使天下皆知父子君臣，而誰與爲亂？朱熹入曰：「爲政者當順五行，脩五事，以安百姓。」又荀范之所不及也。特此而往，雖措之天下可也，豈獨江西然哉？昔人有云：「勢不同而理同。」又云：「有治人而無治法。」歟事以爲何如？
translation_en:
…[illegible]. Seeking its root in [illegible], there is what Ji[zi] and Yu said in the Great Plan (Hongfan) concerning … the source of food [?]: establish officials responsible for moral instruction, set examples of frugality and simplicity, and require the ruler not to abandon the root and devote himself exclusively to [illegible] its branches. One must follow Emperor Taizong of the Tang in ensuring that the people have clothing and food to spare; one need not follow the Song in separately establishing severe laws against robbers during the Xingning era [?]. Then depravity will not arise, and this constitutes the highest achievement of [corrupt text]. Thus, people did not pick up things lost on the roads, outer doors were left unbarred, and traveling merchants slept in the open: all this was simply because of these measures. Understanding this, one sees that the various laws concerning “liuming” [?] likewise seem unnecessary.

Yet this is still not enough. Three years of cultivation must yield one year’s food in reserve, and nine years of cultivation must yield three years’ food in reserve. Such is the concern for storing provisions expressed in Royal Regulations (Wangzhi), lest it cease to be a state [?]. “If you yourself were free of desire, they would not steal even if rewarded for doing so”; “If you desire goodness, the people will be good.” Such is the sage’s intention in giving priority to moral instruction, unwilling to rely on mere deliberation [?]. And Su [two illegible characters] … the sages of antiquity [restrained?] robbers through righteousness, ensuring that everyone under Heaven understood the relationships between father and son, ruler and subject. Who, then, would join in disorder? Zhu Xi further [?] said: “Those who govern should accord with the Five Phases and cultivate the Five Duties, thereby bringing peace to the common people.” This, moreover, goes beyond what Xun and Fan [?] attained. Proceeding on this basis [?], these measures could be applied throughout the realm; how could they apply only to Jiangxi? Someone of old said, “Circumstances differ, but the principle is the same.” It was also said, “There are people who bring about good government, but no laws that do so of themselves.” What do you think of these matters [?]?

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試錄後序
凡試事成有司爲錄以
獻錄成序之皆
制也而序以爲戒也禮也序其後
中戒之也士之始進也猶女
子之嫁也禮女子之嫁也父
醮而戒之母送之階而又戒
===
之蓋慎其始也江西之試至
是爲錄凡幾序凡幾其主司
之得士與否其士之貞不貞
皆可觀已於其始也敢弗慎
與雖然彼爲是者徒以文焉
耳文果足恃耶我
國家體道爲治文出于一壹
punctuated:
江西鄉試錄後序

凡試事成，有司爲錄以獻。錄成，序之，皆制也。而序以爲戒也，禮也。序其後，中戒之也。士之始進也，猶女子之嫁也。禮，女子之嫁也，父醮而戒之，母送之階而又戒之，蓋慎其始也。江西之試至是，爲錄凡幾，序凡幾？其主司之得士與否，其士之貞不貞，皆可觀已。於其始也，敢弗慎與？雖然，彼爲是者，徒以文焉耳。文果足恃耶？我國家體道爲治，文出于一壹
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination

Whenever an examination is completed, the responsible officials compile a record for presentation to the throne. Once the record is completed, a preface is written: these are all prescribed procedures. That the preface should serve as an admonition accords with ritual propriety. A postface likewise conveys admonition [?]. A scholar’s first entry into official life resembles a woman’s marriage. According to ritual, when a woman marries, her father offers her a ceremonial cup of wine and admonishes her; her mother accompanies her to the steps and admonishes her again. This expresses care for the beginning.

By now, how many records have been compiled for the Jiangxi examinations, and how many prefaces written? Whether the presiding examiners have secured worthy scholars, and whether those scholars remain steadfast, can all be observed. At this beginning, dare we fail to exercise care? Nevertheless, those who undertake this selection rely solely on literary composition. Can literary composition truly be relied upon? Our dynasty embodies the Way in its governance, and literary expression proceeds from unity [?]…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
又曰似司馬遷似陸贄韓愈
也今試求之非似之間而其
所見者則一矣脩之言曰三
代之上政出于一而禮樂達
於天下是也知一則知文矣
於是則有本論濮議知一則
知士矣於是則有蘇軾曾鞏
===
固脩之所自得於文者是不
寧鄉士之濮而天下公言之
矣雖然昔脩起五季排佛老
爲功矣而今得無進之以爲
博乎脩變鉤棘黜靠軋稱復
古矣而今得無目之以爲古
乎彼其主司士之相遭也有
punctuated: 又曰：「似司馬遷，似陸贄、韓愈也。」今試求之非似之間，而其所見者則一矣。脩之言曰：「三代之上，政出于一，而禮樂達於天下。」是也。知一則知文矣，於是則有《本論》《濮議》；知一則知士矣，於是則有蘇軾、曾鞏。固脩之所自得於文者，是不寧鄉士之濮，而天下公言之矣。雖然，昔脩起五季，排佛老爲功矣，而今得無進之以爲博乎？脩變鉤棘，黜靠軋，稱復古矣，而今得無目之以爲古乎？彼其主司、士之相遭也，有
translation_en:
…It is also said: “He resembles Sima Qian; he resembles Lu Zhi and Han Yu.” Now, if we seek what lies beyond these resemblances, what we discover is unity. As Ouyang Xiu said, “In the age of the Three Dynasties and before, government issued from a single source, and rites and music extended throughout the realm.” This is the point. Understanding unity means understanding literary composition: hence his Discourse on Fundamentals (Ben lun) and Deliberations on the Prince of Pu (Pu yi). Understanding unity means understanding men of talent: hence Su Shi and Zeng Gong. This was indeed what Xiu grasped for himself in literary composition. It was not merely [the judgment of local scholars?—the transcription is unclear]; the whole realm publicly affirmed it.
Nevertheless, Xiu arose after the Five Dynasties and earned distinction by opposing Buddhism and Daoism. Yet today, might people promote these teachings in the name of breadth of learning? Xiu reformed a thorny, convoluted style and rejected strained writing [?], winning acclaim for restoring antiquity. Yet today, might people dismiss him as antiquated? In such encounters between examiners and candidates, there are…

title: 嘉靖十六年江西鄉試錄
text:
不爲今弊也者幾希夫豈以
脩爲不美哉不變則不奇不
利則不變固世之恒者比其
後也而習成焉習而厭生
焉習而厭厭而奇吾不知文
所止矣是故文也者變而未
始變者也至奇而易簡者也
===
此脩之謂一或者其有遺志
於斯哉
祖宗朝用少師楊士奇言特取脩
之文顯行之士奇之文固脩
之瀷也而後之作者漸以異
須者禮官之論又以正文體
請禮官之請又士奇之意也
punctuated:
不爲今弊也者幾希，夫豈以脩爲不美哉？不變則不奇，不利則不變，固世之恒者。比其後也，而習成焉；習而厭生焉。習而厭，厭而奇，吾不知文所止矣。是故文也者，變而未始變者也，至奇而易簡者也。此脩之謂一，或者其有遺志於斯哉！
祖宗朝，用少師楊士奇言，特取脩之文，顯行之。士奇之文，固脩之瀷也。而後之作者漸以異，須者，禮官之論又以正文體請。禮官之請，又士奇之意也。
translation_en:
…very few have not become abuses in our own day. But does this mean that Xiu’s achievement was not admirable? Without change there is no novelty; without advantage there is no change: this is indeed the constant way of the world. In time, habits form, and familiarity breeds weariness. Familiarity leads to weariness, and weariness to the pursuit of novelty; I do not know where writing will finally come to rest. Thus writing changes yet has never truly changed; at its most extraordinary, it is easy and simple. This is what is meant by Xiu’s unity [?]; perhaps he left us an aspiration in this regard!
During the reigns of our imperial ancestors, acting on the advice of Junior Preceptor Yang Shiqi, the court specially selected Xiu’s writings and gave them prominent circulation. Shiqi’s own writing was indeed an offshoot of Xiu’s [?]. Later writers gradually diverged. Subsequently [?], the officials responsible for ritual again requested that literary style be rectified. Their request likewise expressed Shiqi’s intent.
